Alex Halper (Managing Director, PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP)
Harsha Desai (Consumer and Commercial Lead, PepsiCo, Inc.)

title: 4 primitives to evaluate your on-call agent's autonomy (sponsored by ResolveAI)
abstract: AI that handles on-call autonomously requires agents to take on alert triage, investigations, acting on production, and learning from what happened. Autonomy progresses unevenly as investigations are bottlenecked on quality while actions are limited by trust. In this session we will walk through how we build each primitive of our autonomous agents at ResolveAI, and how we help engineering teams handle on-call and incident resolutions. This presentation is brought to you by ResolveAI, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Varun Krovvidi (Product Marketing, Resolve AI)
Steven Karis (Chief Architect, Resolve AI (clouddatalabs.io))

title: Your AI agent gets a budget when Agentic AIOps meets FinOps (sponsored by ManageEngine)
abstract: AI agents can now detect, diagnose, and act in seconds. Observability tells them what is happening. The harder question is how they decide. What is an action worth, and what should an agent optimize for? The intersection of Agentic AIOps and FinOps answers both. The result is a blueprint for business-aware autonomous operations, and three practical steps to apply it in your own environment. This presentation is brought to you by ManageEngine, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Ananthkumar KS (Director of Engineering ( MLS ), Zoho Corporation Pvt. Ltd.)

title: Machines on Call for Humans: Agents to run and fix your prod (sponsored by ResolveAI)
abstract: We're entering a new era of software operations where the question is no longer whether intelligent agents have a role in production, but whether humans should still be the first responder. As production environments continue to grow more complex, agents are becoming part of the operations team, handling the repetitive work of operating production while engineers focus on the decisions that require judgment, creativity, and experience. This session explores how leading enterprises are rethinking on-call, improving reliability, and reshaping the way production is operated by putting machines on call for humans. This presentation is brought to you by ResolveAI, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Manveer Sahota (Head of Product Marketing, Resolve AI)
Claire Yin (Member of Technical Staff, ResolveAI)

title: Making Enterprise Data AI-Ready Without the Data Engineering Overhead (sponsored by Eon)
abstract: Enterprise data is spread across databases, object stores, and compute, but making it usable by AI often requires months of data engineering and a growing web of pipelines to build and maintain. In this session, we’ll show how Eon continuously discovers, connects to, classifies, and transforms data across Amazon RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, EC2, S3, and more into a unified, AI-ready data layer. We’ll walk through the architecture and semantic layer on AWS, then share how agents can use Amazon Bedrock to query that governed context in natural language through MCP, with Claude, Amazon Quick, and other AI clients. This presentation is brought to you by Eon, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Yaniv Ehrlich (VP AI & FDE, Eon.io)
Gonen Stein (Co-founder and President, Eon)

title: 3 a.m. and Already Fixed: How PagerDuty’s SRE Agent Is Rewriting Incident Response (sponsored by PagerDuty)
abstract: Every SRE knows the pattern: an alert fires, and the next 20 minutes disappear into triage before you've even confirmed what's broken. Context is scattered across dashboards, runbooks, and tribal knowledge, and much of incident response is just reconstructing what already happened. This session explores how autonomous operations changes that story. PagerDuty’s SRE Agent investigates before a human is even involved and proposes fixes you simply approve. See it firsthand through PD Labs, a hands-on site for trying autonomous workflows, and SRE Workbench, launching in early access, where humans, agents, and automation meet in order to investigate, diagnose, and remediate issues. This presentation is brought to you by PagerDuty, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Samrat Ghosh (Staff Technical Lead Manager, Quality Engineering & Incident Management, Liveramp)
Alice McElroy (Director, Global Application Support and Operations, Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd.)

title: Closing the Loop: How Cognition’s AI Continuously Improves Itself (sponsored by Datadog)
abstract: As AI accelerates software development, production systems are changing faster than teams can understand manually. Cognition is closing that gap by giving Devin, its software engineering AI agent running on AWS, access to its own production telemetry through Datadog. Devin uses that context to reason about its production behavior and take action when needed. That feedback loop turns production insights into improvements to Devin’s reliability and future task performance. In this session, we’ll show how Devin investigates alerts, correlates metrics and logs, distinguishes real issues from noise, and uses those insights to improve its harness and workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: Scaling Pharma Transformation Through Data-Driven Agentic AI (sponsored by Tech Mahindra)
abstract: Hear from a leading U.S. pharmaceutical company on its journey to transforming enterprise AI from isolated experiments into a scalable business capability. Discover how Tech Mahindra helped establish trusted data foundations, harness Agentic AI to enrich product and customer master data, unlock semantic intelligence, and create governed data products that power enterprise-wide insights, including drug demand forecasting. This session will explore the architectural principles, governance strategies, and leadership decisions required to scale compliant, trusted, and value-driven AI. Join Tech Mahindra and a pharma industry leader to learn how data-driven Agentic AI is reshaping the future of the intelligent pharma enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by Tech Mahindra, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: The Infrastructure Behind AI: Scaling Access to Web Data (sponsored by Oxylabs)
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence directly mirrors the continuous evolution of web intelligence infrastructure. As machine learning models demand exponentially richer datasets, web data extraction has transformed from simple parsing into a sophisticated, mission-critical engineering discipline. In this session, explore how modern web scraping infrastructure actively evolves alongside artificial intelligence to solve live data bottlenecks and complex anti-automation challenges. Discover high-throughput extraction architectures, real-world pipeline designs, and strategic business use cases that turn dynamic web data into production-ready intelligence. Learn how advanced web data infrastructure fuels current artificial intelligence capabilities and shapes the future of automated enterprise decision-making. This presentation is brought to you by Oxylabs, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Patricija Zemaityte

title: 4 foundations for building the agentic enterprise on AWS​ (sponsored by IBM)
abstract: Agentic AI is moving fast—but isolated agents and one-off experiments won’t transform the enterprise. To create value at scale, companies need a foundation that helps them build and modernize applications faster, orchestration across systems and workflows, governed execution, and control over the infrastructure, performance and cost behind them.​ Join IBM and industry leaders to discover what’s new from IBM on AWS. Hear real-world lessons and measurable business outcomes while exploring the four foundations organizations need to move from disconnected agents to secure, governed, enterprise-wide execution.​ This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Neel Sundaresan (GM, IBM)

title: The Capability Overhang: Ask More of the Frontier (sponsored by Anthropic)
abstract: Frontier models can do more than anyone asks of them. At Anthropic, the hardest part of testing a new model is finding work hard enough to make it fail. Outside, most teams hand Claude the tasks they gave last year's model. This session closes that gap: what the newest Claude models do on AWS when you delegate the job, not the task. Multi-day autonomous work, large migrations end to end, agents that verify their results and keep going. Evals, live demos, and how our researchers keep raising the bar. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Matt Bleifer (Product Manager, Research, Anthropic)

title: Build, run, and improve: inside a production AI inference platform (sponsored by Baseten)
abstract: Getting a model to work is the easy part. Keeping it fast, cheap, and reliable in production is the hard part. Sai Maddali, Product Manager at Baseten, walks through the platform behind some of the highest-volume inference workloads running today: how GPU capacity is sourced and managed across clouds, how runtimes are tuned per workload, and how dedicated inference, model APIs, and training sit on one pool of compute. He shows why the teams pulling ahead treat build, run, and improve as a single loop, and what that changes about latency, cost, and model quality. This presentation is brought to you by Baseten, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater

title: Solving Problems Faster with AI SRE​ (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
abstract: The complexity of problems continues to grow, and smart organizations know that leveraging AI is the quickest way to get this complexity under control and keep customers happy.​ In this session, you’ll see a demo of and learn how to use AI SRE in Splunk Observability Cloud to troubleshoot and remediate problems faster no matter how complex or distributed your operating environment is, all powered by OpenTelemetry. ​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Aaron Schifman (Product Marketing Manager, Cisco)

title: Stop Building Agents Without Unified Enterprise Context (sponsored by Glean)
abstract: Many AI programs start with a model, a prompt, and a narrow workflow. They stall when agents need to understand permissions, people, policies, past decisions, and data spread across AWS and SaaS systems. This session shows a different path: establish a governed enterprise context layer and scale the enterprise workflows that prove value. Attendees will learn the elements that make up a robust context platform, what to keep open and flexible, and how to measure whether agents improve real work. This presentation is brought to you by Glean, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater

title: Modernize the data layer, then scale the AI: A Cisco Case Study
abstract: Enterprise AI agents depend on applications running on data layers built for a different era. So, how do enterprises modernize applications at scale? Cisco migrated a workflow automation platform running tens of millions of workflows a month—and the AI support assistant built on it—to MongoDB on Amazon EKS without disrupting live operations. The assistant has since resolved 1M+ support cases on its own and is on track to handle most of Cisco’s support volume. Discover: • Modernization patterns MongoDB sees across enterprises on AWS, from tool-assisted migration to targeted rewrites, and how to choose between them • How Cisco’s distinguished engineer sequenced the migration and what had to change in the data model • What the AI assistant can do now that it couldn’t before Leave with a practical checklist for planning a modernization that supports AI and agentic workloads.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Srikrishna Srinivasan (Director, AI Engineering, T-Mobile)

title: AI at Lennar: Driving 80,000 Home Deliveries with Bedrock & Coralogix (sponsored by Coralogix)
abstract: Lennar is bringing AI into the everyday work behind more than 80,000 home deliveries a year, from land research and acquisition to construction, customer engagement, and sales. Join Ralph Gootee, CTO of Lennar, and Ariel Assaraf, CEO of Coralogix, for a practical look at moving AI from experimentation into production. They’ll share how Lennar is building and scaling AI agents on Amazon Bedrock, using AWS inference services and open-source models, and how Coralogix helps teams understand adoption, performance, cost, and business impact. This presentation is brought to you by Coralogix, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Ralph Gootee (CTO, Lennar)
Isaac Gabay (VP Data and AI, Lennar Corporation)

title: 3-step blueprint for scaling AI with a modern enterprise core (sponsored by IBM)
abstract: AI is a catalyst for growth and innovation, yet only 17% of AI initiatives reach full-scale production. Join IBM and AI trailblazers to explore the three-step blueprint for scaling AI on AWS: modernizing the enterprise core across applications, data and infrastructure; fostering a culture that moves innovation forward; and putting digital labor to work in real workflows. Discover how IBM Consulting helps organizations move beyond isolated use cases, accelerate ideas into production and make AI work inside the enterprise, not around it. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Kristen Bennie (Group Head of Innovation and Partnerships, Barclays)
Dan Kusel (Global Managing Partner, General Manager, & Global Practice Leader, IBM)
Laxman Challa (Director, Application Services, Southwest Gas)
Brian Bohan (Director, WW Partner Growth & Strategy, AWS)

title: FinOps for AI: Open the black box on AI spend (sponsored by Apptio)
abstract: AI spend often arrives as a black box: a rising bill with little clarity into which teams, models or features drove it. In this breakout, learn how Cloudability helps teams apply FinOps discipline to AI on AWS by categorizing costs, connecting spend to business goals and identifying waste. Discover how we turn that visibility into action for AI workloads running on Amazon EKS, improving GPU efficiency, Kubernetes workload right-sizing and application performance. Then apply the same cost discipline to Amazon Bedrock, including smarter provisioned throughput decisions, so teams can explain, defend and optimize AI spend. This presentation is brought to you by Apptio, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Andrew Midgley (Principal Product Marketing Manager, IBM)

title: How YipitData Builds AI-Native Analytics with AWS, Databricks, and OpenAI (sponsored by Databricks)
abstract: YipitData gives customers a self-service way to answer analytical questions using agents grounded in its data, completing custom requests in 30 minutes compared with the two weeks previously needed. This session walks through the production architecture behind that experience, combining Databricks for data governance and observability, OpenAI for reasoning and intelligence, and AWS for application resiliency and hosting. Learn how a custom agent harness connects OpenAI frontier models to Databricks SQL Warehouses, with Amazon ECS and ElastiCache supporting the application and asynchronous agent execution. We cover Unity Catalog access boundaries, dedicated agent identities, durable session state in Lakebase, and evaluations that check SQL, tool use, and answer consistency. This presentation is brought to you by Databricks, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Sully Clark (Senior Partner Engineer, Databricks)
Ankith Ede (Applied AI Engineer, OpenAI)
Anup Segu (Chief Architect, YipitData)

title: Securing the Bedrock: A Strong API Foundation for AI Innovation (sponsored by Kong)
abstract: AI moves fast until it hits production. Then agents that looked solid in a POC start making calls they shouldn't, hammering the vector database, or failing quietly under load, because the API layer underneath wasn't built for it. This session covers what a strong API foundation does for AI at scale: fine-grained authorization keeps context retrieval inside its data privacy boundaries, touching only what it's permitted to touch; rate limiting protects vector databases from resource exhaustion; edge caching cuts query latency without extra engineering; and circuit breaking plus canary deployments let teams ship changes without compromising security or compliance. You'll leave with architectural blueprints and real enterprise examples showing how the right API foundation turns governance from a blocker into what lets AI teams move faster. Presented by Kong an AWS Partner, alongside FanDuel. This presentation is brought to you by Kong, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Amit Shah (Director, Product Marketing, Kong)
Bryce Macher (VP, AI Engineering, FanDuel Inc)
Jonathan Kindberg (Sr. Director, AI Platform and Ops, FanDuel)

title: Everyone is a Coder. Govern what they build. (sponsored by Coder)
abstract: Suddenly, everyone is a coder. People who never wrote code now build apps, dashboards, and prototypes with AI, faster than most teams can govern them. The result is shadow AI, ungoverned data, and IP risk. See how a leading global private investment firm gave citizen developers a governed place to build on its existing AWS infrastructure, replacing scattered, unmanaged tools. Learn how approved models, scoped templates, centralized container management, and a complete audit trail let hundreds of builders move fast inside guardrails. Attendees leave with a practical model for governing AI adoption on their own AWS environment. This presentation is brought to you by Coder, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Abhipal Singh (Development Director, Capital Markets IT, Bain Capital, LP)
Nicky Pike (Field CTO, Coder)
John Zink (Director, Software Development & Data Engineering, Bain Capital)

title: At Petabyte Scale: Building an AI Telemetry Lake with Coralogix (sponsored by Coralogix)
abstract: The Access Group is turning petabytes of telemetry from hundreds of teams into an engine for business performance. Its telemetry lake gives teams a clearer view of product health, helping them spot risks sooner, solve problems faster, and understand how technology shapes the customer experience. Join The Access Group CTO Thad Széll and Coralogix CEO Ariel Assaraf to learn how unified telemetry is moving the business from reactive troubleshooting to continuous product improvement. Hear how it is sharpening decisions, focusing teams on what matters most, and creating the trusted data foundation needed to advance The Access Group’s AI ambitions. This presentation is brought to you by Coralogix, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater

title: 1 Customer, 1 Context, From all the Channels: (sponsored by Redis)
abstract: Join Toshish Jawale, Head of AI Engineering at Invoca, to learn how his team is putting context at the center of the business’ customer journeys. Hear how Invoca and Redis are delivering real-time, mutli-source context for Invoca’s agents, how they’re helping customers interact with their brand in exciting ways, and how they’re delivering complete pictures of user brand experiences. This presentation is brought to you by Redis, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Toshish Jawale (Head of AI Engineering, Invoca (fka RingRevenue, Inc.))
Jon Fritz (Chief Product Officer, Redis (Redis Labs))

title: Inside the Agentic Engineering Org of the Future (sponsored by Harness)
abstract: What does it actually take to become an AI-native engineering organization? A senior technology executive from a Fortune 500 enterprise sits down with Harness Field CTO Nick Durkin to talk through what it's really taken to go all in on agentic software delivery, orchestrating agents across the entire SDLC instead of one-off automations. They'll get into what that transformation actually looks like end to end, how they decide when an agent runs on its own versus when a human stays in the loop, how agentic engineering has affected cloud migration and consumption, and what it takes to do this at the scale of a Fortune 500 engineering org. This presentation is brought to you by Harness, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Nick Durkin (Global Field CTO, Harness, Inc.)

title: Ask the News: Making Decades of Publisher Content Instantly Searchable (sponsored by MongoDB)
abstract: TPublishers sit on enormous archives: decades of articles, millions of photos, entire histories of coverage. Most of it is invisible the moment someone needs more than a keyword match. ArcXP built Ask the News to close that gap: a standalone, API-first product giving publishers natural-language access to their own content, powered by MongoDB Atlas Vector Search. The system combines lexical and vector search so results reflect what was meant, not what was said. One of the hardest parts was visual: a pipeline that generated descriptions and embeddings for roughly five million historical images, making decades of archives searchable by meaning for the first time. You'll leave understanding a working pattern for combining lexical and vector search, and a model for exposing natural-language search as an API-first product, not a bolt-on feature. Featuring ArcXP, presented by MongoDB. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: Agents demand context. Build them a Streamhouse. (sponsored by Confluent)
abstract: Your agents can't act on yesterday's data. In this session, see how to connect streaming events, governed data, and agent orchestration into one production-ready streamhouse architecture on AWS. Learn how to build a complete, performant, and open streamhouse that delivers real-time context, elastic scale, and mission-critical reliability across every cloud and private environment without data silos. You'll leave with practical patterns for moving from brittle data pipelines to AI built on data streams, designed for speed, trust, and scale. This presentation is brought to you by Confluent, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Sean Falconer (Vice President of Product, AI Products and Strategy, Confluent)

title: The Frontier Doesn't Hold Still: Running Claude Agents at Scale on AWS (sponsored by Anthropic)
abstract: Enterprises are moving faster with AI than ever. And they're falling further behind. Once the first agents land and the numbers look good, most teams turn to cost control while the frontier keeps moving. This session covers how to do both with Claude on AWS: the security and compliance controls enterprises require, execution inside your own boundary, observability and cost governance, and the safeguards that let you trust agents with more. Then how to keep expanding what agents do as new models arrive, so efficiency doesn't become the ceiling. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Lauren Polansky (Head of Cloud Product, Anthropic)

title: Scaling inference compute across clusters (sponsored by Baseten)
abstract: Your traffic outgrows a single cluster long before you expect it to. Colin McGrath explains how Baseten runs inference across more than 80 GPU clusters and roughly 15 cloud providers as one system: how capacity gets found and claimed, how requests get routed to the right region under real load, how large models get delivered to new clusters quickly, and how autoscaling behaves when traffic is bursty and cold starts are expensive. He covers what happens when a whole region goes down, and the patterns that matter most for teams scaling past one cluster. This presentation is brought to you by Baseten, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Colin McGrath (Head of Infrastructure, Baseten)

title: One Control Plane for Every Agent: Architecture Patterns for Cost, Risk, and ROI (sponsored by Boomi)
abstract: Every agent call carries cost, permission, and blast radius, and as agents multiply across tools, frameworks, and SaaS, the gaps compound: uncapped spend, unapproved permissions, no shared record. This session breaks down an AI infrastructure layer, running on AWS, that governs every model, agent, and system. A design-time layer publishes an approved catalog of agents, tools, and MCP servers; a runtime layer routes, meters, and enforces policy on every call before it executes. See how spend caps, in-tenant SLMs, and governed APIs turn cost into a controlled input, while one trace gives finance, security, and engineering a shared, audit-ready record. This presentation is brought to you by Boomi, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Mani Gill (SVP, Product, Boomi)
Patricia Moore (AI Field CTO & Innovation Lead, Boomi)

title: Why Multi-Agent Systems Fail in Production (And How to Fix It) (sponsored by MongoDB)
abstract: Most AI agents don't fall apart in production because the model isn't smart enough. They fail because state is fragmented: one agent can't see what another already learned, and nobody can reconstruct what was retrieved, decided, or handed off. In a multi-tenant setting, that's a governance problem, not just a debugging one. This session shows an architecture that fixes it by giving every layer a clear job: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore manages session context and end-to-end tracing, MongoDB Atlas handles durable memory, tenant-aware vector search, and audit history, and the MongoDB MCP Server connects the two so access stays governed. You'll watch agents share state, retrieve tenant-scoped data, and leave a replayable decision trail. Leave with a reference architecture for multi-agent state sharing and a model for what audit-ready really looks like. A MongoDB & AWS technical session. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Nina Lopatina (Staff AI Developer Advocate, MongoDB)
Lydia Eichelberg (Strategic Events, MongoDB)

title: Benchmarking Bedrock knowledge bases for agents in production (sponsored by Braintrust)
abstract: In this talk, we’ll walk through an independent eval of Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, which manages the ingestion, parsing, and retrieval steps in a RAG application. In the first half, we’ll cover our methodology, including how we developed a dataset that queries documents such as tickets, wiki pages, and product docs, and what we decided to score: latency, cost, relevance, and citation support. We’ll also cover how we analyzed the results with research rigor, including p50 and p95 latency and confidence intervals around our metrics. In the second half, we’ll expand this into a conceptual understanding of evals and observability: why they’re important, how other companies are implementing them in production, and the terminology you need to know. This presentation is brought to you by Braintrust, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater

title: How Observability Evolved From Dashboards to Agents Writing Code (sponsored by Honeycomb)
abstract: Observability's real job has always been closing the feedback loop between what you ship and what happens next. We'll trace how that loop evolved at Honeycomb: from dashboards you stared at, to SLOs that quantified what mattered, to Canvas, agents that investigate with you, and now MCP tools feeding production reality straight back into software written by agents This presentation is brought to you by Honeycomb, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Martin Thwaites (Principal Developer Advocate, Honeycomb.io)

title: The Governance Gap Keeping AI Agents Out of Production (sponsored by WSO2)
abstract: Every leader is under pressure to show AI value now. Some move fast, and agents sprawl across teams with no shared controls. Others lock everything down, and pilots never reach production. Both point to the same gap: governance maturity hasn't kept pace with agent speed. This talk covers how governance becomes an accelerator, not a blocker, to production AI. You’ll learn how to design identity, policy, and guardrails from day one, so agents ship with the same controls whether they run on AWS Bedrock, hybrid, or otherwise. Get the principles right early, and agents move from pilot to production without every team reinventing governance on their own. Takeaways: Why AI programs sprawl or stall, and what governance maturity looks like in between. How trusted AI governance turns into speed instead of slowing teams down. What governance principles to design in from day one, on AWS & beyond. This presentation is brought to you by WSO2, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Rania Khalaf (Chief AI Officer, WSO2)

title: Tokenomics: Understanding What Your AI Actually Costs (sponsored by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
abstract: Your AI pilot ran smoothly and stayed on budget. Then you launched, and the invoice was much higher than the estimate. This session breaks down why that happens and what to do about it. We'll walk through where AI spend actually goes once a system leaves the demo stage, why agentic AI costs differently than a simple chatbot, and how choosing the right model for each task, not just the flagship model for everything, can cut spend dramatically without hurting quality. You'll leave with a practical framework for tracking cost, avoiding common budgeting traps, and having a more confident conversation with finance the next time AI spend comes up. This presentation is brought to you by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: ryan ries (Chief AI and Data Scientist, Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)

title: Setting up the Right AI Architecture: Bringing Together Agents, Teams, and Context (sponsored by Notion)
abstract: Every organization is building their AI architecture in real-time: deciding which agents to use, which data sources to connect them to, and figuring how to get teams to collaborate across it all. These different layers have been arranged over many years of procuring tools, but can sometimes feel like a jumbled mess in the AI era. This session offers a practical way to reexamine your tech architecture. We'll cover four patterns that recur across organizations as they try to structure their business for the AI era, plus pitfalls to avoid to ensure your tech stack is optimized for AI. This presentation is brought to you by Notion, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: Ship agents, not chaos: a 90-day pattern for production on AWS. (sponsored by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
abstract: AI agents are moving from pilots into production faster than most organizations can govern them, and independent teams building in parallel are creating what practitioners now call agent sprawl. This session presents a repeatable 90-day pattern that converts sprawl into governed agents ready for production, using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Guardrails, and Kiro alongside NIST AI RMF and the Well-Architected Generative AI Lens. Architects, platform owners, and public-sector leaders see how a governed runtime, evidence-based mission KPIs, and cost discipline turn compliance into an accelerator. Audit-ready patterns from CDW customer engagements across regulated commercial and public-sector missions are included This presentation is brought to you by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater

title: Deepfakes, Deception, and the New Rules of Reality (sponsored by KnowBe4)
abstract: Deepfakes are transforming the rules of trust. As AI-generated voice, video, and imagery become easier to create, attackers use synthetic media to make deception feel familiar, urgent, and credible. In this session, KnowBe4 shows how deepfakes fit into broader social engineering campaigns built around narrative, timing, and cross-channel reinforcement. The fake clip is rarely the whole attack; it is one piece of a larger story designed to short-circuit judgment when it matters most. Attendees will learn what separates an interesting tech demo from a nation-state-level attack. They will see how these attacks work and why convincing stories and cognitive biases override technical skepticism even in well-trained people. Perry Carpenter will also cover how organizations can prepare for high-stakes moments when trust is under pressure—before the call comes in, not after This presentation is brought to you by KnowBe4, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Perry Carpenter (Chief Deception Strategist, KnowBe4, Inc.)

title: Every Flight Has a Story. Here’s What It Takes to Power It. (sponsored by ZS)
abstract: United and ZS go behind the scenes of the data, AI and technology powering personalized flight stories for travelers at scale. This presentation is brought to you by ZS, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: FinOps for AI: Scale Investments That Work. Stop Ones That Don't. (sponsored by Kion)
abstract: Most organizations can tell you what they spend on AI. Fewer can tell you what they're getting for it. FinOps for AI closes that gap, but it takes three things: visibility into spend by use case; controls that act on what the data tells you instead of just surfacing it; and value tracking that connects spend to outcomes your stakeholders can evaluate. This session includes real examples of token attribution, guardrail patterns that respond to data, and a model for turning ROI signals into corrective action. This presentation is brought to you by Kion, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Tatum Tummins (Senior Product Manager, Kion)

title: Enabling agentic development loops with a local cloud validation layer (sponsored by LocalStack)
abstract: Agentic coding loops let AI develop, test, and iterate on code autonomously. But agents often lack the permissions required to validate how code behaves in the cloud, stalling the cycle and holding back velocity. This session will show how simulating your AWS application environments locally can enable AI agents to identify and fix bugs faster, more securely, and more effectively than human engineers can when building in live cloud development environments. This presentation is brought to you by LocalStack, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater

title: The Next Phase of AI for SRE: Distributed Reasoning for Enterprise Operations (sponsored by Ciroos)
abstract: AI for SRE isn’t just a speed or accuracy problem; it’s a problem of deeper understanding. This session explores how team members across different domains in an enterprise can use a shared AI reasoning layer to operate production systems and collaborate effectively to increase reliability. We’ll show how this AI reasoning layer handles the extremes of alert storms and alert silence, catching deployment-triggered anomalies before they cause production impact. Learn how teams are moving beyond reactive dashboards, using state-of-the-art techniques to instantly correlate cross-domain telemetry, execute complex investigations, and achieve proactive reliability in dynamic cloud and hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by Ciroos, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Ananda Rajagopal (Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Ciroos, Inc.)

title: Beyond the Buy Button: Cisco on AWS Marketplace, a Partner-Led AI Win (sponsored by Cisco)
abstract: AWS Marketplace isn't just a procurement channel, it's a financial lever. A typical ISV saves a procurement cycle. Cisco draws down committed spend against the infrastructure your agents run on: connectivity from cloud to edge, visibility into agent behavior, and protection for models, identities, and data. Partners add the expertise to deploy it right, turning a procurement decision into an architectural one, a true better together win with AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cisco, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Dave Gervon (Global Partner Sales Leader, Cisco Systems, Inc.)

title: Running Vercel in Your Own AWS Account (sponsored by Vercel)
abstract: This session explores how Vercel Enterprise customers can run workloads in their own AWS account while continuing to use the Vercel developer experience. You’ll learn about the separation between the Vercel control plane and customer runtime, and why this model can help organizations meet data privacy, security, and compliance requirements. You’ll see how the setup works through a live walkthrough and demo, and how this architecture can support broader access to tools like v0, Amazon Q, and other coding agents. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Glenn Phillips (Senior Solutions Architect, Vercel)
Brandon Tuttle (Member of Technical Staff, Vercel)

title: Open source agent observability and evals with AgentCore and Langfuse (sponsored by ClickHouse)
abstract: Production agents need more than infrastructure. They need an open source foundation for understanding behavior, evaluating quality, and improving continuously without sacrificing control of their data. In this session, learn how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Langfuse combine secure agent infrastructure with open source observability and evaluation, powered by ClickHouse. See how teams capture OpenTelemetry traces, debug trajectories and tool calls, evaluate production quality, turn failures into datasets, and prevent regressions before deployment. We will share a practical architecture for unifying policy and telemetry across AgentCore, EKS, and other runtimes so teams can ship trustworthy agents faster. This presentation is brought to you by ClickHouse, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Marc Klingen (Co-Founder, Langfuse (by ClickHouse))

title: Pushing AI Boundaries: Transform Marketing with Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker and AWS (sponsored by Adobe)
abstract: As generative AI matures into autonomous ecosystems, enterprise marketing demands a new era of collaboration. In this session, discover how Adobe and Amazon co-innovate to deliver next-generation AI capabilities for marketers, business practitioners, and developers. At the center of this revolution is Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker, an advanced AI teammate powered by Adobe Harness. We will showcase how Coworker and its flexible, headless capabilities seamlessly unite Adobe’s deep customer experience expertise with the power of AWS. Attendees will discover how this combined innovation enables teams to transition from manual execution to goal-based, automated workflows with built-in governance. Join us to learn how this partnership helps enterprise organizations take a massive leap forward in operational effectiveness and unlock entirely new business outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Adobe, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Siddhartha Srivastava (Sr Product Manager, Adobe Inc)

title: Elasticsearch - the Search database for Context Engineering and AI (sponsored by Elastic)
abstract: Your agentic applications have an accuracy and cost problem, and it's not your model choice. Sound familiar? If you're a developer trying to get LLMs to work effectively with your business context, this session is for you. Come learn how we rearchitected Elasticsearch as the database of choice for the different data types your enterprise knowledge is buried in — docs, logs, metrics, tickets, sales call transcripts, and more. From foundational innovations like Columnar and VectorDB mode with no ETL, to best-in-class retrieval that combines vector search, Jina embedding models, and native inference, Elastic is the context database for your production needs. Join this session to learn the best practices, from optimizing data preparation to retrieval patterns, to make your agents a production reality. This presentation is brought to you by Elastic, an AWS Partner.

title: Build the Right Next Thing: A Forward Deployed Approach to AI ROI (sponsored by Slalom)
abstract: Two years ago, standing up generative AI technology was the hard part. Today, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore make the path to production more straightforward—but technology alone does not create value. AI initiatives often stall because ROI is undefined and business, user, and technical priorities are disconnected. Learn how Slalom’s Forward Deployed Expertise (FDX) model places a cross-functional team spanning product, business, industry, UX, and technology alongside customers. Using real data, these teams compare opportunities, prioritize the highest-value use cases, and co-build the right next thing through production, adoption, and measurable outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Slalom, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Mike Ostrowski (Director - AWS AI, Slalom)

title: Tokenomics for AI on AWS: Local inference plus Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by Spectro Cloud)
abstract: Power users in AI teams building on AWS face the challenge of frontier models delivering the best answers and token costs scaling with adoption. Not every prompt requires frontier models. The ones that do, belong on the best endpoint. This talk covers a working pattern for enterprise inference on AWS: PaletteAI Inference Launchpad running local open-weight models for routine requests, Amazon Bedrock as the burst target to extend capacity, and frontier models as needed for complex work. We will show how routing, quotas, and per-team attribution keep tokenomics predictable, so platform teams can enable AI adoption without inheriting the bill. This presentation is brought to you by Spectro Cloud, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: Fresh Threats, Stale Defenses: The Race for Real‑Time Security (sponsored by Booz Allen)
abstract: Cyber conflict has entered a new phase, accelerated by AI that increases the volume, velocity, and sophistication of attacks. The shift is not that attackers are unstoppable — it is that they operate on a faster clock than the systems meant to contain them. Their advantage is freshness: exploiting what changed before defenders reconcile it, exploiting uncertainty before it becomes understanding, and exploiting stale proof before records drift from reality. AI compresses discovery and action, scaling tasks that once required teams. In this session, learn how defense can be rebuilt around real‑time truth, continuous visibility, and inspectable, defensible action. This presentation is brought to you by Booz Allen, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Emilio Rodas (Solutions Engineer, Booz Allen)

title: Enterprise AI is missing a key ingredient: The knowledge layer (sponsored by Neo4j)
abstract: You don't need another post-mortem to know why enterprise AI projects fail. Organizations that have moved AI from pilot to production know it runs on context. A knowledge layer shows AI how facts relate, what's changed, and what's already been decided. Trained on siloed data, a model sees disconnected records, not relationships, and can't reason well without that context. The knowledge layer connects GenAI and agentic systems to data that's organized and accessible. In this session, we'll cover why the knowledge layer is the missing piece your enterprise AI needs, and what your organization gains from implementing one: Trust every AI answer, back to your source data. Prove every AI decision with a complete audit trail. Synthesize intelligence across disparate systems and teams. Use your existing data investments instead of replacing them. This presentation is brought to you by Neo4j, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Mike Worthington (Product Marketing, Mike Worthington)

title: When Guardrails Break: Defense in Depth for Non-Deterministic AI (sponsored by Darktrace)
abstract: Organizations are deploying copilots, AI agents, and LLM-driven workflows faster than governance and security can adapt. Non-deterministic AI creates a new attack surface across prompts, agents, data, and runtime behavior, and acts as both defensive force multiplier and adversarial accelerant. Static guardrails are necessary but insufficient: they miss novel behavior, unsafe tool use, and risk that only surfaces when AI interacts with identities and downstream systems. This session presents a defense-in-depth model for securing AI at runtime, using NIST's Secure/Defend/Thwart framing: an identity control plane for agents, least-privilege and JIT access, runtime observability, behavior detection, and autonomous investigation and containment. We'll share a blueprint for a minimum viable AI security baseline, and why behavioral oversight is the decisive layer for securing AI at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Darktrace, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Margaret Cunningham (VP Security & AI Strategy
Head of Americas Field CISO Operations, Darktrace)

title: How to run parallel coding agents without sitting in the loop (sponsored by Cursor)
abstract: Running multiple coding agents in parallel can increase throughput, but only if technical leads and engineers avoid being pulled into every agent’s execution loop. Join this session to learn how Grok Bot is an orchestration layer for technical knowledge work, coordinating workflows while saving time and mitigating costs. Through live demos, see Grok Bot operate from its own VM and browser, maintain authenticated tool access, monitor usage, and provision cloud agents on demand. We’ll be joined by a customer in production as well as SpaceXAI engineers as they share the workflows they run today. This presentation is brought to you by Cursor, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater

title: How the most advanced teams manage the full SDLC on an agentic stack (sponsored by Cursor)
abstract: This 201 technical deep dive covers the AI Software Development Lifecycle featuring the Grok product family. SpaceXAI experts and customers in production will demo proven patterns, covering which parts of the SDLC to delegate to agents first, how to structure review and testing when agents write most of the code, and where the Grok API and Grok Voice fit a production workflow. This presentation is brought to you by Cursor, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater

title: Mapping and Securing the Enterprise AI Attack Surface (sponsored by Zscaler)
abstract: AI is racing across the enterprise—showing up in endpoints, apps, workflows, agents, and data paths faster than most security teams can track. But securing AI takes more than knowing where it exists; it requires understanding how data flows, where it comes from, where it goes, and which users, devices, apps, and AI endpoints interact with it along the way. In this session, we’ll explore how to map the AI attack surface and its data lineage while securing the AI endpoints where innovation actually happens. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Mark Ryan (Vice President, AI Strategy & Architecture, Zscaler, Inc.)

title: Architecting Intelligent Omni-Channel Communication Workflows with Twilio + AWS
abstract: Orchestrating AI conversations across channels requires more than just connecting APIs. Learn how to build agents that understand context, respond instantly, and adapt to channel constraints. Explore Twilio Agent Connect and Amazon Bedrock integration patterns, plus the operational playbook for deploying engagement AI at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Twilio, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Safdar Jaffari (Partner Solutions Engineer, Twilio)

title: Securing the Enterprise in the Age of AI Agents: From Zero Trust to Agentic Security (sponsored by Zscaler)
abstract: AI isn’t just another workload—it’s introducing agents that act, connect, and make decisions at machine speed. This session reframes Zero Trust for an agent-driven world: how to govern agent-to-agent communication, constrain access to sensitive data, and reduce risk without slowing the business. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Dhawal Sharma (Executive VP- Product Strategy, Zscaler, Inc.)

title: Data & AI Security, Resilience and Recovery in AWS  (sponsored by Veeam)
abstract: As AI adoption accelerates on AWS, cloud and platform teams need to know exactly what Veeam can do to keep their data secure and their environments resilient. This session takes you on a tour of Veeam's capabilities built for the AWS developer and cloud practitioner: discovering sensitive data, monitoring AI agent activity, and closing visibility gaps before they become incidents. You'll see how security posture and backup protection work together in practice, giving teams confidence in what's protected. And when something does go wrong, precise, granular recovery means restoring exactly what changed, nothing more. This presentation is brought to you by Veeam, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Johan Huttenga (Senior PM Manager, Veeam Software)
Roy Adiel (Cloud Solutions Architect, Veeam)

title: Snowflake: Build a Multi-Engine Architecture on A single AI Ready Governed Data Copy (sponsored by Snowflake)
abstract: Delivering enterprise analytics and AI requires an architecture designed for operational flexibility not forcing complex data movement. Snowflake's interoperable lakehouse gives teams total agency to query and write to data where it lives using the right engine for every job. This session explores how organizations establish universal open metadata governance powered by Apache Polaris while preserving rich semantic business context across tools. Learn how the Snowflake AI Data Cloud simplifies data management, lowers total cost of ownership, and accelerates time to insight for every team, and agent, across your AWS cloud environment. This presentation is brought to you by Snowflake, an AWS Partner.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: David Mitchell (Sr Director Engineering, Cox Automotive)
Matt Sidley (Senior Manager, Prod. Mgmt., Snowflake Computing Inc)

title: Build an Agentic Enterprise to Enable Autonomous Action (sponsored by Snowflake)
abstract: Building an agentic enterprise empowers organizations to automate complex work and drive measurable business outcomes. True transformation happens when autonomous AI operates across systems using trusted data, flexible models, connected applications, and a unified, agentic control plane. By bringing knowledge workers and technical builders into a shared agentic environment, teams move faster without sacrificing governance. Learn how the Snowflake AI Data Cloud unifies enterprise context, model choice, and app connections into a single architecture. Discover how to turn enterprise data into reliable, autonomous action and long-term competitive advantage in your AWS cloud environment. This presentation is brought to you by Snowflake, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Santiago Giraldo (Sr. Director Product Marketing - AI, Snowflake)
John Pulikkottil (Director Data Engineering, Hyatt)

title: When tags run out: cost allocation for AI and multi-tenant workloads (sponsored by DoiT)
abstract: Tag-based allocation works until the resource stops belonging to anyone. A multi-tenant EKS cluster, a shared inference endpoint, a queue five services write to: each lands on the bill once, charged to whoever provisioned it. No amount of tagging discipline fixes that, because there is nothing to tag. This session covers where tag coverage structurally breaks down, and the alternative: measuring the running system to attribute shared spend to the team, feature, and customer that caused it, then reconciling back to the bill so the allocation still foots. Includes what this looks like in production on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by DoiT, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Amit Kinha (Field CTO, DoIT International Ltd)

title: Build Agentic AI That Understands Your Business with SAP and AWS (sponsored by SAP)
abstract: Enterprise AI falls short when agents lack live business context. See how SAP's Business AI Platform and AWS solve this: Joule Studio enables developers and business users to build and deploy custom AI agents grounded in SAP's process knowledge, while bidirectional, zero-copy integration between SAP Business Data Cloud and Amazon Athena gives AWS services secure access to trusted SAP data. Watch a live demo of building agents that reason with business context, collaborate across SAP and AWS, and act across enterprise processes with governance.​ This presentation is brought to you by SAP, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Haridas Nair (Global Head Ecosystem Integrations, BDC, SAP)
Ted Way (VP and Chief Product Officer, SAP Business AI Product Engineering, SAP)

title: Teaching agents to pay with Stripe (sponsored by Stripe)
abstract: AI agents can already search, reason, and call tools. What changes when they can spend money, too? This talk explores the shift from human checkout to machine-native commerce, where payments become part of an agent's reasoning loop. We will look at how agents can discover and purchase products today, then explore Stripe’s Machine Payments Protocol and a future where agents autonomously pay for APIs, compute, data, and other capabilities needed to complete a task. When software becomes the buyer, developers may need to rethink not only checkout, but also how software itself is discovered, priced, and consumed. This presentation is brought to you by Stripe, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Ben Smith (Staff Developer Advocate, Stripe)

title: How In-Context Learning Delivers Interpretable AI at 90% Lower Cost
abstract: Enterprises have spent years building institutional knowledge, but AI agents still struggle to apply that expertise to complex business tasks. This session explores how scaling in-context learning (ICL) enables organizations to train AI on their existing work, allowing agents to reason and make decisions with the judgment of an organization's experts. We’ll examine how this approach makes institutional knowledge portable across models, achieves 95%+ accuracy and performance while reducing inference costs by 90%+ with the ability to swap to smaller models. Through real-world examples, we’ll demonstrate how organizations can customize AI for their business without costly fine-tuning while maintaining full interpretability into what agents learn, how that knowledge influences their outputs, and how errors can be corrected.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater

title: Application Archeology: Digging up lost knowledge with Kiro
abstract: Every organization bleeds knowledge when people leave. For mission-driven teams, a single departure can erase years of context from codebases, runbooks, and integrations. In this builder session, use Kiro — AWS's AI-powered development environment — to reverse that loss. Configure steering files that encode your team's conventions, connect MCP servers to pull context from docs and APIs, and deploy subagents that generate living architecture diagrams and knowledge bases as your code evolves. Walk away with a Kiro workspace that turns any new hire into a productive contributor from day one — no more tribal knowledge walking out the door.

title: Six Ways AI Fails Who Your Nonprofit Serves — And How to Stop Each One
abstract: Every AI application touching real people can fail in ways that cause harm. In this chalk talk, we walk one application through six failure modes — PII exposure, phantom citations, out-of-scope advice, unreviewed judgments, hidden bias, and unaccountable decisions — and whiteboard a defense-in-depth architecture using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, AgentCore, Automated Reasoning, and human-in-the-loop patterns. Leave with a responsible AI stack applicable to any form factor — chatbot, agent, RAG pipeline, or model call — whether you serve donors, patients, customers, or citizens.
speakers: Sam Grace (Solutions Architect,, Amazon Web Services)
Annie Cimack (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Building enterprise agent platform on AgentCore
abstract: As agents multiply across teams, platform owners need control without becoming a bottleneck. In this session, learn best practices for building a governance foundation for your agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Use gateway as a central control point for all agent-to-tool traffic, enforce authorization with policies at the infrastructure layer that agents cannot bypass, and propagate identity end to end for a complete audit trail. Use the Agent Registry to catalog, discover, and approve agents and tools across the organization, and end-to-end tracing for fleet-wide visibility. Includes a demo. Leave with a governance blueprint teams can adopt.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Chaitra Mathur (Principal Solutions Architect GenAI, AWS)
Anubhav Mangal (Principal Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Deploy and optimize world models with agentic AI workflows
abstract: World models generate real-time video by learning environment dynamics, which powers interactive simulation for gaming, robotics, and autonomous driving, but deploying these latency-sensitive pipelines is complex. In this builders session, we deploy and optimize a real-time video world model on AWS Trainium using AWS Neuron Agentic Development skills that automate compilation, profiling, and kernel optimization through natural-language interaction. See the agent identify bottlenecks, then select optimized kernels from Hugging Face or write custom kernels from scratch. You will apply these agentic tools yourself to reach optimized, real-time inference on silicon built specifically for AI.

title: Hands-on training world models and deploying agents for Physical AI
abstract: Physical AI is transforming robotics and autonomous systems with world models that enable agents to understand and interact with their environments. Training and deploying these large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) models requires complex distributed infrastructure. AWS Trainium and AWS Neuron simplify this with PyTorch integration: apply standard distributed training techniques using familiar APIs while the software stack handles multi-device coordination, compilation, and optimization. In this hands-on session, fine-tune a transformer-based world model, implement parameter-efficient training strategies, and deploy trained agents for real-time inference. You will build the skills to adapt Physical AI models and deploy robotic agents across large clusters.
speakers: Jianying Lang (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: Turn your coding agent into an always-on dev team with AgentCore
abstract: Claude Code, Kiro, and Codex are impressive individually, but in an enterprise they run stateless, isolated from team context, and invisible to governance. AgentCore turns any coding agent into a production system: shared memory so the agent understands your architecture across sessions, microVM isolation so jobs run in parallel without interference, identity propagation so agents access only what they should, and full trace observability so you know what every agent did and why. This session shows what changes when you pair popular coding agents with a production platform, and how our customer deployed this across hundreds of developers.
speakers: Abhimanyu Siwach (Principal Engineer, Amazon)
Eashank Kaushik (Specialist SA, AI/ML, AWS)

title: Put your data to work: build a knowledge assistant on Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Your data lives in documents, images, databases, warehouses, and relationships between entities. In this builders session, build a knowledge assistant that works across all of it on Amazon Bedrock. Use Managed Knowledge Bases with multimodal ingestion to handle PDFs and images, add natural-language querying over structured data, and wire in GraphRAG for questions that span connected entities. Then make it enterprise-ready: secure tenant isolation, concurrency-aware ingestion, and the Agentic Retrieval API for multi-hop, cited answers. Leave with a deployed stack and retrieval patterns you can reuse across your organization.

title: Put your data to work: build a knowledge assistant on Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Your data lives in documents, images, databases, warehouses, and relationships between entities. In this builders session, build a knowledge assistant that works across all of it on Amazon Bedrock. Use Managed Knowledge Bases with multimodal ingestion to handle PDFs and images, add natural-language querying over structured data, and wire in GraphRAG for questions that span connected entities. Then make it enterprise-ready: secure tenant isolation, concurrency-aware ingestion, and the Agentic Retrieval API for multi-hop, cited answers. Leave with a deployed stack and retrieval patterns you can reuse across your organization.

title: Making foundation models performant on AWS Trainium3
abstract: Many of today's largest foundation models are mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, and modern MoE models place several performance demands on AI chips and their HPC systems. This session walks through those demands and how AWS Trainium3 and the Trn3 UltraServer respond. See how to train and serve with PyTorch, TorchTitan, and vLLM, then profile with Neuron Explorer and choose between a config change, an NKI Library kernel, or a custom NKI kernel. Two customers share their experience running on Trainium3.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Matthew McClean (Sr Manager, AWS)

title: From 1 to 20,000: Scale reliably on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS
abstract: As AI workloads scale, infrastructure failures become inevitable, causing stalled jobs, degraded throughput, and wasted accelerator capacity. In this chalk talk, we'll show how to build resilient AI workloads on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS. We'll whiteboard the full resiliency stack: Neuron DRA Driver for topology-aware scheduling; UltraServer Operator for provisioning UltraServer workloads; Neuron Observer for sub-second fault detection; and Device Taint for automated recovery. These patterns support fault-tolerant distributed training and inference from a single accelerator to 20,000. You will leave able to assemble this resiliency stack yourself and keep training and inference running through hardware failures.
speakers: Chelsie Zhang (Pr. PMT-Platform and ML Infra, Amazon)

title: Beyond fine-tuning: RL for reasoning agents with AWS Trainium
abstract: Supervised fine-tuning enables your model to follow instructions, but teaching it to reason requires reinforcement learning. RL workflows demand iterative loops that multiply compute costs, making the price performance of AWS Trainium, a chip built specifically for deep learning AI, critical. In this chalk talk, we explore what techniques like RLHF and GRPO bring to the table and how to run them on Trainium with the AWS Neuron software stack, Torchtitan, HuggingFace TRL, vLLM, and native PyTorch. We compare co-located and disaggregated RL architectures. You'll leave ready to implement cost-effective RL loops that train agents to reason.
speakers: Hiroshi Tokoyo (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Japan)
Maen Suleiman (Head of Neuron Product Management, Annapurna Labs)

title: When AI agents make high-stakes decisions: Build governance on AWS
abstract: When AI agents approve aid applications, triage patients, or allocate resources, failure isn't a bug — it's a harm. In this workshop, build a production governance layer for high-stakes agentic workflows using AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock, and AgentCore. Implement human approval gates that don't kill velocity, audit trails that satisfy regulators, cost budgets with automatic circuit-breakers, and guardrails for consistent enforcement of policies. Test your governance stack against adversarial scenarios. Leave with a deployable framework applicable anywhere AI decisions affect people — social services, healthcare, finance, or government.
speakers: Sabrina Petruzzo (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Sophie Bacon (Associate Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Evaluating AI Agents for your Nonprofit: From Vibes to Metrics on AWS
abstract: You shipped an agent. How do you know it works? For organizations where AI decisions affect people's lives, rigorous evaluation isn't optional — it's ethical. This chalk talk introduces a structured evaluation framework combining Amazon Bedrock model evaluation, AgentCore observability, and CloudWatch metrics. We cover building eval datasets, measuring tool-use accuracy, detecting hallucination in agentic chains, benchmarking latency and cost, and setting up automated regression testing. Leave with a repeatable eval pipeline you can plug into CI/CD — turning agent quality from subjective to measurable.
speakers: Krutika Khinvasara (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc.)
Omar Tabbakha (Solution Architect, AWS)

abstract: New to Bedrock, or considering it for your next workload? In this hands-on workshop, you go from your first API call to a working application in a single sitting. You choose a model, ground it with Managed Knowledge Bases, apply Guardrails, pick a service tier, then deploy and monitor what you built. Along the way you learn the core building blocks and how they fit together. You leave with an application you built yourself and a repeatable path your team can follow to build the next one.

title: Resilient VLM Training at Scale on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
abstract: Training vision-language models at scale fails in predictable ways — node crashes mid-epoch, checkpoints corrupt, and GPU clusters sit idle during recovery. In this hands-on workshop, build resilient VLM training pipelines on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod that survive real-world failures. Configure automatic health monitoring and node replacement, implement fault-tolerant checkpointing strategies, and design distributed training topologies that resume without losing progress. Using open-source frameworks on multi-node GPU clusters, you'll train a VLM end-to-end while simulating and recovering from infrastructure failures. Leave with battle-tested patterns for keeping large-scale training runs alive.
speakers: Roy Allela (Sr. WW Specialist SA GenAI, AWS)
Aravind Neelakantan (WW Specialist Solution Architect, AWS)

title: Token Counts to Business Impact: Measurable AI Architectures at Scale
abstract: As AI workloads scale, the question shifts from "what does this cost?" to "is this delivering real value?" The answer depends on your workload, architecture, and adoption maturity. We present progressive architecture patterns using agentic software development — from vibe-coding to cloud agents to self-hosted inference to custom models — with a live demo across the AWS AI Stack, including Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker HyperPod, and Trainium, showing how the right metrics evolve with your architecture. You'll leave with cost-per-outcome comparisons, spend controls that work at scale, and an ROI measurement framework with architecture patterns to implement across any AI workload.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Pranav Sharma (Principal Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)
John Masci (Principal Optimization Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Alex Iankoulski (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Making sense of messy enterprise data with AI on AWS
abstract: Organizations struggle to make sense of their data when it's scattered across inconsistent formats, ad-hoc naming conventions, and incomplete records. In this workshop, you will build a scalable pipeline that uses generative AI to transform product descriptions into structured data ready for downstream analysis. Inspired by how AWS tackles life cycle assessment across its data center fleet in the AWS Sustainability Console, you will use Amazon Bedrock and other AWS services to ingest, classify, and contextualize data to deliver sustainability intelligence. You'll then deploy AI agents to orchestrate queries and execute analysis tasks, providing you patterns for any domain.
speakers: Ryan Bradley (Sr. Manager, AWS Sustainability - Science, Services, Infrastructure, and Innovation, AWS)
Thomas Coombs (Principal TAM, Amazon)

title: From carbon data to action: Optimize AI workloads on AWS
abstract: Not all workloads are equal in carbon impact, but how do you know which choices matter most? In this chalk talk, we pull back the curtain on how AWS measures and allocates cloud emissions, balancing scientific rigor with practical usability. Through real-world examples, you'll see how this data reveals meaningful differences across diverse AI workloads. You'll leave with an understanding of the methodology behind your carbon data and how to apply those insights to build AI workloads with a lower environmental footprint, and, often, lower cost.
speakers: Benoit de Chateauvieux (Climate Tech Solutions Architect, AWS)
Fabio Grimaldi (Senior Sustainability Scientist, AWS)

title: Build an AI navigator that makes every frontline worker an expert
abstract: A member is on the line, a regulation changed last week, and the answer isn't in any manual yet. Frontline staff don't need a search box — they need a guide that surfaces the next right action in the moment. In this builder session, build a self-improving frontline navigator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness: ground it in your policies with a Managed Knowledge Base, keep it current with live rule changes via AgentCore Web Search, and close the loop with AgentCore Optimization so it measurably improves from every real interaction. Unlike a static knowledge base, this agent recommends actions, adapts as policies shift, and learns on the job. Whether you serve members, patients, or beneficiaries, leave with a deployed self-improving navigator and the architecture behind it.
speakers: Paul Mietz Egli (Specialist Solutions Architect, Data & AI, AWS)
vtbloise Bloise (Solutions Architect Manager, Amazon)

title: Serving world models on AWS Trainium with native PyTorch
abstract: The next major leap in AI is predicting and interacting with the physical world. World models bridge digital reasoning with real-world execution, introducing new infrastructure demands for video generation, robotics, and gaming workloads. We'll explore the emerging architecture of world models and why AWS Trainium, purpose-built for better price-performance, is well suited to serve them. Learn how native PyTorch support with torch.compile fuses operations into optimized device graphs, and how NKI custom kernels accelerate critical operators like attention. You'll leave able to move world model inference from eager prototyping to compiled deployment using familiar PyTorch workflows.
speakers: Josh Longenecker (Annapurna ML Solutions Architect, AWS)
Diwakar Bansal (Principal GenAI Specialist, Amazon Web Services)

title: From chatbot to proactive agent: Connect AI to your nonprofit systems
abstract: Agents stall at the demo stage because core enterprise systems — ERPs, legacy databases, and internal APIs — were never built for AI. In this session, we whiteboard two patterns to bridge the gap: request-driven integration via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with access-control interceptors, and event-driven routing via Amazon EventBridge with confidence-based human-in-the-loop fallback. We trace both approaches using a legacy system with no modern API surface — wrapping its interfaces as MCP tools without modifying the original code. The patterns apply whether your blocker is a SOAP endpoint, a stored-procedure layer, or a REST API with no auth story for agents. Leave with a maturity rubric and two practical reference architectures.
speakers: Madhu Bussa (Sr Manager, Solutions Architecture, Amazon)
Mike George (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Fine-Tune Agents That Reason: Multi-Turn RL on SageMaker AI
abstract: AI agents that do real work, such as financial advising, coding, and customer operations, reason across turns, call tools, and recover when steps fail mid-conversation. Prompting won't get you there, and building multi turn RL from scratch takes weeks. We'll whiteboard how SageMaker AI's managed MTRL connects your Strands, LangChain, or CrewAI agent under 10 lines of code, handling rollouts, trajectories, and checkpointing, auto cataloged in SageMaker AI catalog. We'll cover reward design, rollouts in managed gym environments, decoupled training compute keeping GPUs from idling, and smaller specialized models outperforming larger ones at lower inference cost. Bring your agent use case and we'll sketch how to train it.
speakers: Ruchi Bhatia (Product Marketing Manager, Tech, AWS)
Sandeep Raveesh (Senior GenAI Specialist AI, AWS)

title: Scaling Frontier AI model inference on AWS Trainium
abstract: Every team moving AI to production hits the same wall: scaling frontier model inference against growing token demand, tighter latency budgets, and spiraling compute costs. This workshop tackles that problem head-on. See how purpose-built chips change the inference economics equation as you deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium, apply optimization techniques, and connect the Neuron software stack to familiar open-source frameworks without rewrites to achieve superior tokenomics. You will leave able to run performant, cost-effective frontier model inference in production on AWS Trainium yourself.
speakers: Pinak Panigrahi (Making LLMs go Brrr..., Annapurna ML, AWS)
Achintya Pinninti (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Andre Gomes (Frontier AI Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Secure AI the same way you secure everything else on AWS
abstract: You already run security and governance on AWS with IAM, CloudTrail, KMS, and VPC boundaries, and AI workloads on Amazon Bedrock inherit all of it. This chalk talk shows how: IAM scoping for model access, data perimeter policies, full prompt and response logging in CloudTrail, and KMS encryption at rest and in transit. There is no separate governance stack to learn and no new tools to onboard. Apply the security patterns your organization already trusts to AI workloads on Bedrock.
speakers: J.D. Bean (Principal Architect, Amazon)

title: Optimizing model performance with agentic loops on AWS Trainium
abstract: Extracting peak performance from AI accelerators requires optimization at every level, from framework configuration down to individual kernels, and the complexity grows with every new workload. Agentic loops replace this manual work with autonomous profiling, diagnosis, and code generation, iterating toward performance targets without human intervention. In this session, we demonstrate this workflow on AWS Trainium, purpose-built to deliver better price-performance for AI workloads. Explore how these loops identify bottlenecks, how persistent memory prevents repeated failures, and how long-running campaigns uncover optimizations for different inference shapes. You will leave able to run agentic optimization loops yourself on AWS Trainium.
speakers: Esha Lakhotia (Technical Product, Annapurna Labs)
Adam Stanley (Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Champagne AI on a beer budget: Cost-optimized AI architectures live
abstract: A surprise cloud bill can wipe out a nonprofit's budget, but running frontier-quality generative AI doesn't have to cost frontier prices. In this code talk, we build an architecture that gets premium model output on a fraction of the spend. Starting with a naïve workload where every request hits the same large model, we layer in routing to send requests to the lowest-cost model meeting the quality bar, caching to reduce token counts, and token budgets with kill switches that gracefully degrade. You'll leave with working code your engineers can implement, and your finance team won't panic over.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Shawn Abdi (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
