title: Defending the Three Lanes: Preventing Toxic Agentic Combinations with Cyera and AWS (sponsored by Cyera)
abstract: Agentic AI is entering production faster than enterprise authorization models can keep up, and most access decisions are made without regard to the sensitivity of the data agents can reach, turning over-permissioned agents into high-value targets. This session introduces the three lanes: the data agents touch, the identity they act as, and the actions they take, as the framework for defending agentic AI on AWS. See how Cyera's Agent Guardian extends Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity with data-aware authorization to enforce least privilege, monitor agent-to-data activity, and prove it to auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Sean Cordero (Chief AI Security Officer, Cyera)

title: Make every GPU count: Maximizing GPU efficiency for inference at scale
abstract: When an inference fleet spans thousands of interconnected NVIDIA GPUs in NVL72 racks, scheduling decisions cascade. Place a job wrong, and it fragments a capacity block, starves NVLink bandwidth, or strands GPUs behind a topology boundary. In this session, AWS and OpenAI will share scheduling and bin-packing strategies developed for production inference on Amazon EC2 UltraServers. Explore rack-aware placement that respects 72-GPU NVLink domains, approaches for mixed workload profiles (prefill vs. decode vs. batch), capacity block utilization maximization, and Kubernetes scheduling primitives that enforce topology constraints. Leave with actionable blueprints to efficiently schedule GPU inference at scale.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Erik Anderson (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Archana Balakrishnan (Principal Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Evaluate, select, optimize your AI model
abstract: Most teams pick a model on instinct. In this hands-on workshop, you'll build a structured evaluation pipeline for your own use case, run it against multiple model candidates (frontier and open-weight), and learn exactly when customization is worth the investment vs. when prompt engineering or RAG is enough. You'll leave with a working evaluation harness, a decision framework for technique selection (SFT vs. RFT vs. CPT), and a trained model you can take home.

title: Building end-to-end agentic IDP Pipelines
abstract: Learn how to build an end-to-end intelligent document processing (IDP) pipeline with specialized agents and Amazon Bedrock Data Automation. This session walks through document classification, data extraction, and validation, showing how agents coordinate across each stage. You’ll learn how to connect these steps into a complete workflow that transforms documents into structured, validated data for downstream applications.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Babu KP (Senior Solution Architect AI/ML, Amazon)

title: What's next in SageMaker AI, how to make data your differentiator for AI.
abstract: Customers are building working agentic applications on their own data, wiring open weight or frontier models through serverless inference, prompt optimization, and retrieval. The first version of your model is close to your accuracy needs, but you run into challenges with preparing data and governance. Governed data and models are hard to access, and inconsistent data quality impacts your accuracy. In this session, learn how new SageMaker AI capabilities help solve these challenges.

title: What's new: SageMaker HyperPod, with learnings from Multiverse
abstract: Building specialized intelligence demands clusters that stay reliable under the heaviest training and inference loads. Learn what's new across SageMaker HyperPod running on EKS and Slurm. Maximize every GPU hour when building models such as BioFMs, World Models, and Sovereign AI, and run the full lifecycle from notebook to production across training, serving, and observability

title: Reimagining how you build AI on SageMaker AI: the idea to AI flywheel
abstract: Building a high-performing generative AI application isn't a one-time model selection. Teams prepare and evolve data, measure quality, decide when customization is needed, compare alternatives, deploy the best candidate, and keep learning from production evaluations. Today those activities live in disconnected tools. In this chalk talk we'll whiteboard and demo new SageMaker experiences, some of it shown publicly for the first time. Bring your questions.

title: Gatekeepers & guardrails: Secure AI agents across your nonprofit stack
abstract: AI agents that reach across your tools via MCP are a force multiplier — but letting an agent call OAuth-protected APIs means handling credentials, identity, and blast radius. Get it wrong and you expose sensitive data. In this code talk, deploy an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and walk through three-legged OAuth live: secure token storage via AgentCore Identity, identity propagation across agent chains, confused-deputy prevention, and guardrails on tool results. Whether you're a 5-person nonprofit team or a 5,000-person enterprise, leave with deployable IaC for your own environment.
speakers: Jason Rodriguez (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Ramanathan Muralidhar (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Stop the bleed: control and optimize agent costs on AgentCore
abstract: Your agent cost $0.02 per session in testing. In production it's $0.14 and climbing. Token consumption grows unpredictably as agents retry, loop, and fan out across tools, and most teams have no visibility into where the money goes. This chalk talk breaks down where agent costs actually hide and how to control them on AgentCore: per-session budgets that kill runaway loops, model routing that drops to cheaper models for simple subtasks, cost attribution at the team and workload level, prompt caching strategies, and how to measure the tradeoff between cost and quality with evaluations.

Willie Lee (Senior WW Specialist, AWS)

title: See where every AI dollar goes on Amazon Bedrock
abstract: AI spend scales fast, and you can't optimize what you can't attribute. In this code talk, build Bedrock cost visibility live: combine CloudWatch metrics and supported invocation logs for timely usage signals with Cost Explorer and CUR 2.0 for billing reporting. Add attribution by IAM principal and cost-allocation tags, then assemble a dashboard that maps spend to teams, workloads, and models while accounting for each source's freshness and granularity. Turn that visibility into action: match steady workloads to Reserved Tier, choose models for price-performance, and set budgets and alerts. Use these signals to reconcile engineering usage with finance reports.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk

title: Accelerate analytics with GPUs at lower cost: Spark, DuckDB, and more
abstract: Feature engineering, ETL, and interactive analytics for AI push CPU-based clusters to their limits. In this session, learn how Amazon EMR with the NVIDIA cuDF Plugin for Apache Spark runs workloads up to 3.7x faster on Amazon EC2 G7 instances with no code changes. The session also covers DuckDB on GPU, presents benchmarks and tuning patterns, and shows how faster jobs lower cost per run, even at a higher hourly rate.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Karthik Prabhakar (Principal Big Data Specialist, EMR, Amazon Web Services)
Vidish Mehta (Senior Technical Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Optimize agentic AI costs with EC2 Capacity Blocks and Spot Instances
abstract: Agentic AI turns ML infrastructure into a dynamic scheduling problem, where the goal is cost per accepted outcome. In this lightning talk, watch a self-managed agentic workflow run financial services portfolio stress testing on Amazon EC2, with telecom and media content generation as bonus patterns. EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML reserve capacity for deadline-critical stages, while EC2 Spot Instances add elastic, checkpointable capacity for parallel work. A bounded agentic planner proposes placement across NVIDIA GPUs and AWS silicon while deterministic controls enforce budget and deadline limits, keeping cost per accepted outcome low as workloads shift.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Sherif AbdElGawad (AI Strategist, Amazon)

title: Koa: NVIDIA Nemotron-Powered CRM Reasoning Inside Salesforce’s AWS Trust Boundary (sponsored by NVIDIA)
abstract: Salesforce Koa is a family of CRM reasoning models post-trained from NVIDIA Nemotron open models. Koa is in production on AWS, inside Salesforce's trust boundary. This session covers technical insights on how Koa was built and how Salesforce serves the model on AWS. Additionally, attendees will learn how Salesforce enforces trust and safety controls in the serving layer outside the model. This session is relevant to any team building and deploying custom open models for the enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Shubham Mehrotra (Lead Applied Scientist, Salesforce)
Petro Junior Milan (Sr. Solutions Architect, Gen AI, NVIDIA)

title: How Datadog optimizes cost per token for GenAI at scale
abstract: Datadog embeds AI across its product portfolio, and every product team has different needs for cost, latency, and model capability. Serving GenAI at production scale requires an architecture that flexibly routes across frontier models, open-weight models, fine-tuned variants, and Datadog's own specialized models — without runaway spend. In this session, Datadog shares how it built a multi-tenant serving platform on AWS to power dozens of AI workloads. Learn the patterns for model routing and fallback, the techniques that reduced cost per token, and the platform-and-product team operating model that lets Datadog ship AI features quickly and reliably.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater

title: Agentic fairness: Practical methods to detect bias in AI-driven decisions
abstract: AI agents are increasingly making real-world decisions — approving loans, issuing refunds, offering discounts — yet most fairness testing still focuses on whether chatbots use offensive language. This gap creates real business and regulatory risk. Join this session to explore how to assess whether your agentic AI systems apply equitable treatment across chosen demographic attributes using defined fairness criteria. Through hands-on examples spanning financial services, customer support, and commerce, discover how to move from language-level toxicity checks to decision-level fairness audits. Learn to identify disparate treatment, choose appropriate fairness metrics for your use case, and implement testing frameworks that catch bias where it matters most: in the outcomes that affect people's lives.
speakers: Bharathi Srinivasan (GenAI Data Scientist, AWS)
Denis V Batalov (WW Tech Leader, AI/ML, Amazon Web Services)

title: The Agent Harness: Unifying Fragmented Tools for Mission AI Advisors
abstract: Advisors across mission-driven organizations—financial advisors, benefits navigators, program coordinators—juggle fragmented tools, manual research, and delayed plan delivery while clients go underserved. AI agents change this equation. See how to collapse this fragmentation into configuration using the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness. Learn to securely plug domain-specific skills and disparate Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers directly into the harness to generate tailored action plans in real time. Then, deploy the agent to isolated microVM sessions utilizing native memory strategies and Bedrock Guardrails. Leave with sample configurations, deployment patterns, and blueprints for building production advisors that scale.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Mrudhula Balasubramanyan (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Praveen Nerellapalli (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Hands-on distributed training with AWS Trainium and PyTorch
abstract: Get hands-on with AWS Trainium and PyTorch's TorchTitan to train models using a fully native PyTorch workflow. This workshop walks you through distributed training on Trainium, covering cluster setup, parallelism strategies, and performance optimization, all through familiar PyTorch APIs. Whether you're training LLMs or fine-tuning domain models, you'll learn how Trainium and TorchTitan simplify scaling without sacrificing native PyTorch flexibility. You will leave able to scale model training on Trainium without changing your PyTorch workflow.
speakers: Samir Araujo (AI/ML Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Build Provable Zero-Trust Agents with Automated Reasoning checks
abstract: Neurosymbolic AI pairs the language understanding of LLMs with the mathematical rigor of automated reasoning, enabling agent decisions that are provably correct, not just statistically likely. In this hands-on workshop, you'll take real-world business rules (e.g. insurance eligibility or financial compliance) and formalize them into Automated Reasoning policies that agents invoke at decision time. Starting from natural-language documents, you'll translate requirements into verifiable logic, then integrate your policies with agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, validating outputs at inference time. Leave able to build Automated Reasoning policies that guarantee correctness, where every decision is logically grounded, traceable, and auditable.
speakers: Nafi Diallo (Senior Automated Reasoning Applied Scientist, Amazon)
Wale Akinfaderin (Sr. Data Scientist - Generative AI, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: A responsible AI challenge: Audit your agentic AI before the regulator does
abstract: Accuracy is necessary, but it isn't enough for agentic systems. Your agents can handle most requests correctly and still fail when someone asks how a decision was made, who approved it, or how to override it. In this hands-on workshop, you inherit a multi-agent claims system seeded with responsible AI gaps. Using the Well-Architected Responsible AI governance skill in your IDE, you audit the code against responsible AI dimensions like fairness, transparency, and accountability, investigate what you find, fix it, and generate an evidence-backed report. Walk away with a repeatable audit workflow you can run on your own agentic systems.
speakers: Rachna Chadha (Principal Technologist, AI, AWS)
Isha Dalal (Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: Four agents, one answer: multi-agent synthesis on AWS
abstract: We live-build a multi-agent system where specialized agents — a document searcher, a data analyst, a claims verifier, and a synthesizer — collaborate to produce evidence-backed summaries from unstructured sources. Using Bedrock's multi-model routing, each agent selects the optimal foundation model for its task. Along the way we solve hard coordination problems: message routing, shared state, deadlock avoidance, and cost control. One presenter codes; the other narrates architecture decisions. Whether you synthesize research literature, member feedback, grant requirements, or compliance updates — leave with replicable patterns for your domain.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Matt Bollinger (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Aneel Murari (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Open-weights at work: Scaling AI without scaling the bill
abstract: Agentic and coding workloads are multiplying token consumption, and paying frontier prices on every call adds up fast. This chalk talk shows how open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock let you scale that growth affordably without giving up quality or security. We walk through multi-model strategies for agentic and code generation workloads, the unit economics of open-weight versus frontier, and how Bedrock's inference engine design keeps security strong regardless of where a model came from. You leave with a practical path to cost-efficient inference at scale.
speakers: Alex Thewsey (WW Specialist SA - AI/ML and Open Source, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build nanochat models with PyTorch and Trainium-Easier than you think
abstract: Can you train an LLM on AWS Trainium, our purpose-built AI chip for better price performance, using PyTorch with minimal code changes? We'll show you with nanochat, a 560M-parameter GPT you can train in about two hours on a single Trainium instance using familiar PyTorch workflows. We cover end-to-end training across data preparation, distributed configuration, and model test practices with interactive chat, showing what works out of the box and what few changes are required. You'll walk away with knowledge to train your own LLM on Trainium with PyTorch.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Josh Longenecker (Annapurna ML Solutions Architect, AWS)
Pinak Panigrahi (Making LLMs go Brrr..., Annapurna ML, AWS)

title: Build agents that take orders like your best sales reps, with PepsiCo
abstract: Your best sales reps understand what a customer means, remember the conversation, check the right systems, and close the order in one exchange. This session shows how to build conversational agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that work the same way: stateful sessions on runtime, memory for multi-turn context, enterprise APIs as tools, and deterministic controls that keep the agent accurate and on task. PepsiCo shares how it built a WhatsApp ordering agent for roughly one million retailers in India, where a shopkeeper can order by text, voice note, or a photo of a handwritten list in their own language.
speakers: Bharathi Srinivasan (GenAI Data Scientist, AWS)
Ganapathi Krishnamoorthi (Principal GenAI Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Murali Ambekar (Sr Director  - Engineering, Pepsico)

title: Migrating a Managed Assistant API to Strands Agents SDK
abstract: As organizations scale AI agent deployments, the gap between managed APIs and production-grade frameworks becomes a migration challenge. This talk describes a large-scale migration from a managed assistant API serving hundreds of agent projects to Strands Agents, selected for its deterministic orchestration, multi-provider portability, and open-source extensibility. The migration replaced three subsystems (orchestration, conversation persistence, and observability) while preserving all existing tool implementations. This session details the architectural decisions, backward-compatible tool migration, security constraints for production deployment, and evaluation methodology that validated quality parity. These patterns generalize to any organization migrating from managed AI APIs to open-source agent frameworks.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Dharamendra Kumar (Agent Platform Software Engineer, Netflix)
Ryan Coleman (Principal Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Kyle Ahn (Distributed Systems Engineer, Netflix)

title: One Service, Every Workload: Build, Customize, and Deploy with SageMaker AI
abstract: AI/ML teams want to move fast - experiment with models, fine-tune them on their data, and serve them in production, without stitching together separate tools at every step. In this session, see how Amazon SageMaker AI lets you build, customize, deploy, and run inference, all within one service. Learn how to match the right approach to each stage: serverless experimentation for fast iteration, fully managed environments for custom frameworks and training, persistent clusters for large-scale research, and optimized inference for real-time and batch serving in production. Walk away with a practical decision framework and a reference architecture to start simple and scale without switching platforms.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Sumedha Swamy (Senior Manager, Product Management, Amazon Web Services)
Kanwaljit Khurmi (Sr Mgr, Solutions Architecture, AMAZON WEB SERVICES INC)

title: Data Prep to Deployment: How Tencent Games Scaled to 1,000 GPUs on SageMaker HyperPod
abstract: Join us to see how Amazon SageMaker HyperPod lets teams build complete training pipelines, from data prep and transformations through distributed training to seamless model deployment, all on one resilient, self-healing platform with no re-platforming required. Then, hear how Tencent Games, a game AI team (not an infra team), went from first cluster to thousand-GPU training in weeks for their VISVISE engine powering 90+ titles including PUBG Mobile. Walk away with lessons learned from real production workloads and best practices for EFA networking, FSx storage, and GPU fault tolerance.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Shreyas Adiyodi (Sr Product Manager - Technical, Amazon Web Services)
Xulong Gao (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Haoming Li (Senior Researcher, Tencent)

title: GPU cluster failure patterns on AWS: observe, diagnose, recover
abstract: At scale, GPU clusters fail in ways that single-node debugging does not reveal: NCCL timeouts that are actually storage problems, DataLoader forks that silently hang collectives, and GPUs that pass health checks yet corrupt results. In this hands-on builders session, diagnose these failures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic Fabric Adapter. Read NCCL debug logs, interpret all-reduce bus bandwidth against per-instance baselines, and run open-source health checks that catch faults early. The session provides a failure-signature runbook and a triage method drawn from operating large GPU fleets on AWS.
speakers: Harish Rao (senior solutions architect, Amazon)
SooJung Lee (Sr.Technical Account Manager, AWS)
Keita Watanabe (Pr. WW Solutions Architect – GenAI, Amazon Web Services)
Natarajan Chennimalai Kumar (Senior Manager, AWS)
Daisuke Miyamoto (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect, HPC, Amazon Web Services Japan)

title: Disaggregated inference at scale: when to split prefill from decode
abstract: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto independent GPU pools, eliminating the interference that lets one long prompt stall active generations and letting each phase scale independently. There is a trade-off: the KV cache must cross the network, and a well-cached unified deployment can still perform better depending on traffic. In this hands-on builders session, run both architectures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances, move the KV cache between pools over Elastic Fabric Adapter, and benchmark them against realistic agentic traffic. Learn a decision framework based on input length, prefix reuse, and latency targets, with runnable configurations.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Keita Watanabe (Pr. WW Solutions Architect – GenAI, Amazon Web Services)
Toshinobu Akazawa (ISV/SaaS Solutions Architect, AWS Japan)

title: Deploy, scale, and tune AI model serving with self-managed agents
abstract: Setting up AI infrastructure, tuning model performance, and benchmarking throughput could mean navigating brittle tooling, context rot in long sessions, irrelevant retrieval, missing guardrails for irreversible actions, bursty GPU and CPU demands, and observability gaps. In this chalk talk, explore how to set up, manage, and scale self-managed autonomous agents on AWS to address these challenges with built-in memory, safety boundaries, and audit trails. We will walk through how to quickly deploy a reference architecture on Amazon EKS, tune a 550B-parameter model for inference using disaggregated serving with NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM, and scale with Elastic Fabric Adapter for cross-node KV cache transfer.
speakers: Aniruddha Deodhar (Principal Specialist, Accelerated Computing, AWS)
Alex Iankoulski (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: AI Systems Performance Engineering on AWS: A practitioner's deep dive
abstract: Extracting useful throughput from GPU clusters is a discipline: profiling kernels, tuning collectives, keeping the GPUs fed, and handling the failures that grow with scale. In this hands-on workshop, work through the full stack on Slurm-managed NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances, covering compute, network, storage, and the ML software stack from drivers to distributed frameworks. Set up the observability that ties them together, from GPU, EFA, and Lustre counters to training throughput and MFU. At each layer, measure, attribute, and fix with the right tool. The workshop concludes with self-built dashboards and a goodput methodology for training clusters.
speakers: Keita Watanabe (Pr. WW Solutions Architect – GenAI, Amazon Web Services)
Aravind Neelakantan (WW Specialist Solution Architect, AWS)

title: Governed ModelOps: From customization to deployment with SageMaker AI
abstract: Join us in working through the ModelOps lifecycle, starting with experiment, train, register, approve, to deploy, anchored by the Amazon SageMaker catalog system of record. Using SageMaker managed MLflow and the catalog within SageMaker AI Studio, you'll build governance in as you go with no end-of-cycle compliance scramble. Training runs auto-catalog with model cards, lineage, and audit trails; you'll discover assets with semantic search, trace lineage with OpenLineage, configure access control, gate promotion on quality and compliance, and publish models across accounts. You'll leave able to trace any endpoint to its dataset, experiment, and approval in seconds.

title: Build production AI assistant with Hugging Face Libraries and models
abstract: Every product team wants an embedded AI assistant, but closed APIs erode margins and limit customization. In this chalk talk, we architect a production solution using open building blocks: retrieval, reranking, and generation models working together in real time. We diagram how to fine-tune for your domain, orchestrate multi-model pipelines, and serve thousands of concurrent users cost-efficiently. You will leave able to run native Hugging Face models and libraries on AWS Trainium and own your AI stack end to end.
speakers: Jeff Boudier (CPGO, Hugging Face)

abstract: Stand up a continuous evaluation pipeline for your generative AI applications. In this hands-on workshop, you'll build an end-to-end evals infrastructure using Amazon Bedrock and open-source tooling. We cover designing evaluation datasets, implementing automated scoring (LLM-as-judge and programmatic metrics), tracking model performance over time, and triggering alerts on quality regressions. Leave with a working pipeline you can adapt for your organization's models and prompts.

abstract: Build and deploy a voice agent with Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic. Learn how to build and deploy a voice agent using Nova 2.5 Sonic, Strands BidiAgent, AgentCore, and customized Skills. The session covers both bidirectional streaming architecture (Nova 2.5 Sonic) and cascading architectures using Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Polly. Attendees will learn reference architectures, implementation patterns, deployment steps, and best practices for building scalable, production-ready voice agents using AI coding tools.

title: Full-stack data agents using Box MCP and AWS
abstract: Organizations struggle to assess contract compliance as terms live in unstructured documents while structured financial and risk data sit in operational databases across the enterprise. In this session, build an AI agent that performs real-time contract compliance analysis, bridging unstructured content stored in Box with operational structured data on AWS. Using Box MCP in AWS Marketplace, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon Aurora, you implement a multi-MCP architecture, routing to Box for contract extraction and to AWS databases for operational data, producing auditable compliance determinations citing both unstructured content and structured data. You must bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Gopal Surapaneni (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Designing  AI Agents with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and Voice AI
abstract: Multimodal AI agents need to understand more than text and interact through more than a screen. In this interactive chalk talk, we’ll explore how Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings connects knowledge across text, documents, images, video, and audio, including semantic search over spoken content and sound, while voice AI enables natural conversational interaction. We’ll examine cross-modal retrieval, audio and video segmentation, multimodal context, conversational orchestration, latency, and grounding tradeoffs for building responsive agents that can listen, understand, retrieve, and converse across modalities.
speakers: Anuj Jauhari (Senior Product Marketing Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Nitin Eusebius (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Strengthen identity verification with Amazon Rekognition
abstract: Learn how to use Amazon Rekognition Face Liveness to help confirm a real person is present during digital onboarding. This session explores how to integrate liveness checks into your application, detect spoofing attempts, and support identity verification workflows.

title: Build voice-enabled applications with Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe
abstract: We'll use Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe to add natural speech and accurate transcription to your applications. With Polly, you'll build expressive, emotionally engaged voices using its generative and long-form engines, covering streaming audio, speech marks for word-level timing, and newscaster styles. With Transcribe, you'll turn speech into text for captions, search, and analytics, handling real-time streaming and batch workloads. We'll show how these services work together to power voice agents, accessibility features, and conversational experiences, giving your applications the ability to both speak and listen naturally across a wide range of use cases and customer scenarios.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Venkat Gomatham (Sr. Partner Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Deepthi Devanira (Software Development Manager, AWS)

title: Cross-modal search with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings
abstract: Build search and RAG that understand more than text. In this hands-on workshop, you'll use Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings that embeds text, documents, images, video, and audio into one semantic space for cross-modal retrieval. You'll generate embeddings across modalities, load them into a vector store, and build a working app that searches with text, an image, or an audio clip and retrieves relevant results from any modality. We'll cover indexing strategies, query routing, and accuracy tuning for production agentic RAG. Bring your laptop.
speakers: Gowtham Shankar (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Wale Akinfaderin (Sr. Data Scientist - Generative AI, Amazon Web Services (AWS))
Sapeksha Vemulapati (Principal PMT, Amazon)

title: Build agentic observability workflows with AI tools from AWS Marketplace
abstract: In this workshop, discover how to create an AI agent that takes a single user prompt, finds anomalies using observability and monitoring tools, and takes proper actions on your behalf. Using solutions available in AWS Marketplace, you can incorporate leading generative AI models into your agentic AI workflows while maintaining privacy leveraging stands agents. Deploy third-party products in your AWS account, ensuring that prompts, data, and model responses stay within the boundaries of your account and are not shared with model providers. This is important for business use cases where competitive or confidential information may be used with models. You must bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: George Maroulakos (Sr. Leader - AWS Marketplace Center of Excellence, AWS)
Tuan Vo (Specialist Senior Solution Architect, Amazon Inc.)

title: Customize open-weight models for accuracy, cost, and latency on SageMaker AI
abstract: An off-the-shelf frontier model may not meet the accuracy, cost, or latency requirements of your specialized business task. Across businesses from retail to financial services, organizations are customizing open-weight models to unlock higher value, including for domain-specific workflows and agents. In this session, learn why and how to customize open-weight models with Amazon SageMaker AI using features including serverless model customization and techniques such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Intuit shares how it customizes models on SageMaker AI with its proprietary financial datasets to deliver personalized customer experiences. See how Intuit is achieving up to 5% improved accuracy and 50% reduced latency compared to general-purpose LLMs, while delivering cost efficiency for certain accounting workloads.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Michael Oguike (Senior Technical Product Manager, AWS)
Ganesh Hegde (Sr. WW Specialist, GenAI, Amazon)
Oded Vainas (AI & Engineering Leader, Intuit)

title: Which customization path? A decision framework for fine-tuning on AWS
abstract: Off the shelf models work for prototyping, but production forces a choice of technique and service. In this chalk talk, we work through that choice live. See when Supervised Fine Tuning is enough, when Direct Preference Optimization or Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback earns its added cost, when Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards or multi turn reinforcement learning is the right call, and what data each needs. Compare Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization, SageMaker AI training jobs, Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, and Amazon Bedrock Custom Model Import by cost and control. Bring a real use case and we'll work through where it fits.
speakers: Kanwaljit Khurmi (Sr Mgr, Solutions Architecture, AMAZON WEB SERVICES INC)
Jason Berkowitz (Head of Product Marketing for AI Model Development and Inference, Amazon Web Services)

title: Your data is your AI advantage: From foundation to business value
abstract: Your AI is only as good as the data underneath it. Most teams treat data preparation and model serving as separate problems, then wonder why costs spike and quality drops at scale. This chalk talk connects the two. We whiteboard how to design governed data products that feed customization, inference on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and agent workloads on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Then apply cost levers like prompt caching, distillation, and batch inference that compound when built on clean, governed data. You leave with the design decisions that let you scale AI with confidence and control.
speakers: Anastasia Tzeveleka (Principal AI/ML Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Ram Vittal (Principal WW GenAI/ML SA, Amazon)

title: Your data is your AI advantage: From foundation to business value
abstract: Your AI is only as good as the data underneath it. Most teams treat data preparation and model serving as separate problems, then wonder why costs spike and quality drops at scale. This chalk talk connects the two. We whiteboard how to design governed data products that feed customization, inference on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and agent workloads on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Then apply cost levers like prompt caching, distillation, and batch inference that compound when built on clean, governed data. You leave with the design decisions that let you scale AI with confidence and control.
speakers: Ram Vittal (Principal WW GenAI/ML SA, Amazon)
Anastasia Tzeveleka (Principal AI/ML Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Architect for production AI: A decision framework that scales
abstract: Organizations deploying AI workloads face a critical decision at every step: which AI service handles which job, and will it hold up at scale? This chalk talk delivers an opinionated framework for choosing between Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and when to use them together. We'll ground it in a real example: an agentic coding system pairing a Bedrock frontier model for complex coding with a fine-tuned open weight model on SageMaker AI for high-volume automated PR reviews. It runs on AgentCore, which supports any model or provider mix, including Bedrock and SageMaker AI, for cost- and performance-optimized architectures.
speakers: Brent Rabowsky (AWS WWSO, AWS)
Hazim Qudah (SOLUTIONS ARCHITECT, AI/ML WWSO, AWS)

title: Architect for production AI: A decision framework that scales
abstract: Organizations deploying AI face a critical decision at every step. Which service handles which job, and will those decisions hold up as you scale? This chalk talk delivers an opinionated decision framework for choosing between Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and when to combine both for unified security, governance, and models that move between services without rearchitecting. We cover model access patterns (API, custom model import, marketplace), deployment trade-offs between self-managed and fully managed inference, and cost-performance optimization at production scale.
speakers: Hazim Qudah (SOLUTIONS ARCHITECT, AI/ML WWSO, AWS)
Brent Rabowsky (AWS WWSO, AWS)

title: Innovating with agentic AI inside Amazon, powered by AgentCore
abstract: Amazon runs thousands of AI agents internally, built on the same AgentCore platform available to every AWS customer. Teams across the company have replaced manual workflows with agents that act autonomously, cutting process times from weeks to hours and eliminating thousands of lines of custom orchestration code. This session brings together the Amazon builders behind these transformations to share the AgentCore capabilities that made it possible, the failure modes they hit at scale, and the design patterns that separate agents that demo well from agents that survive production. Every pattern discussed is one you can adopt today.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Amanda Lester (Principal WW Gen AI GTM Specialist, AWS)
Mihir Patel (GM, AWS Field Experiences, Amazon)

title: How ISVs ship agent products faster: Twilio and Typeform on AgentCore
abstract: Customers now expect AI agents inside the software they buy. For an ISV, shipping agents to many customers means solving multi-tenancy, per-customer isolation, identity delegation, and cost attribution before writing any agent logic. This session shows how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore handles that undifferentiated work. Twilio and Typeform join on stage to share how they built agent products on AgentCore and serve large numbers of end users without building custom infrastructure. Both stayed framework-neutral and spent their engineering effort on the agent experience rather than the plumbing beneath it. Expect specific isolation, identity, and cost-attribution patterns that move an ISV's agent product from prototype into production.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Veena Vasudevan (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Peter Janovsky (Chief Architect of Conversational AI, Twilio)
Andy Kuszyk (Staff Engineer, Typeform)

title: Automate your business processes with workflow agents on AgentCore
abstract: The agents with the clearest ROI don't wait for a prompt. They wake on an event and run a process to completion. A new lead triggers a prospecting agent, a filed ticket triggers IT resolution, a spend threshold triggers a campaign adjustment. This session covers best practices for building workflow agents on AgentCore: triggering agents from event sources, running long tasks asynchronously on Runtime, connecting to systems of record through gateway, holding state with memory, adding human-in-the-loop approvals, and enforcing actions with policies the agent cannot bypass.
speakers: Daniela Kinsella (Principal Engineer, The New York Times)
Will Matos (Principal Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)
Heeki Park (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Trusting agents in production: end-to-end security with AgentCore
abstract: AI agents call APIs, access databases, and act on behalf of users, making security non-negotiable before you go to production. But they introduce new attack surfaces: persistent sessions, autonomous tool execution, and permissions that compound across steps. This session shows how to secure agents end to end with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: microVM isolation so sessions can't leak into each other, identity propagation so every action traces back to a user, Gateway policies that control which tools agents can reach, and Cedar authorization for least-privilege at every call. Leave with a blueprint for production.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Fei Yuan (Principal Engineer, AWS Identity, Amazon Web Services)
Guilherme Greco (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Open for Business: OpenAI on AWS
abstract: There is more than one way to put OpenAI to work on AWS, from coding agents that ship production code to knowledge workflows and custom agents. This session tours OpenAI on AWS, starting with the latest OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock. Put them to work through two agentic surfaces: Codex for coding and ChatGPT Work for knowledge work. Then explore Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents for OpenAI to deploy OpenAI-powered agents in your AWS environment. The session maps OpenAI on AWS and helps you decide which path fits your needs.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Nick McCarthy (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect (GenAI), AWS)

title: Claude It Your Way: Anthropic on AWS
abstract: Your teams want Claude for coding, agents, and knowledge work, and there are more ways than ever to reach it. This session maps every path to Anthropic on AWS. Start with the models, served two ways: Amazon Bedrock, with Haiku for speed, Sonnet for balance, and Opus for long-running agentic work, or Claude Platform on AWS for Anthropic's first-party API. Add applications on top: Claude Code for agentic development, Claude Desktop for broader knowledge work. Govern both with the Claude apps gateway, one control plane across them. See how these layers fit your teams' needs.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Ayan Ray (Worldwide Tech Lead, Anthropic Partnership, AWS, Amazon Web Services)

title: What happens in Bedrock stays in Bedrock
abstract: You want to ship AI, but your compliance team won't sign off until the solution meets their regulatory requirements. This session shows how Bedrock protects data from the hardware up, with zero operator access enforced at the chip so no one, not even AWS operators, can access your prompts and completions. See how data residency controls and strict workload separation extend that protection, and how those guarantees map to the compliance frameworks your teams already use. Use what you learn to make the security case for approving your AI workload.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Steve Kendrex (Sr. Manager, Product, Amazon)
Chase Kernan (Principal Engineer, AWS)

title: It's live. Now what? Operating AI on Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Your AI workload is live. You own three questions: what broke, whose spend is it, and are you still running the right model. Answer the first two with Amazon Bedrock metrics: why latency alone cannot tell you what broke, how output tokens per second separates a slower model from a longer answer, why throttling starts before you reach your quota, and how to attribute spend by caller identity and request metadata. Answer the third with evals: see how Airbnb sets a model and reasoning effort per workload across 3,000 engineers.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Alan Yao (Senior Staff Software Engineer, Airbnb)
Rashim Gupta (Senior Manager, Product Management, Amazon Web Services)
Jayadev Vadakkanmarveettil (Principal Product Manager, AWS)

title: Building the Intelligent Health System, CXO blueprint for the agentic era (sponsored by PwC)
abstract: The health systems that will lead the next decade are not simply digitizing existing processes. They are reimagining what a health system looks like with AI native to every layer. On AWS that means a unified data foundation across electornic health records, claims, images, devices, and genomics; real-time AI at the point of decision; agentic workflows that absorb entire categories of administrative burden; and governance that holds up to audit at scale. Chief Information, Digital, and AI Officers building this now share what worked and what they would do differently. Attendees leave with a practical sequence, from data foundation to agentic deployment. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Geoffry Hook (Chief Information Officer - Northern Market, Northwell Health)
Abbas Mooraj (Partner, PwC)

title: How Rail Operators Are Using Agentic AI to Improve Service Reliability (sponsored by PwC)
abstract: Many organizations successfully pilot generative AI but struggle to scale adoption. Rail operators worldwide are now exploring how agentic AI can transform mission-critical operations and improve service reliability. Deutsche Bahn (DB) and Norfolk Southern are among the organizations leading this journey. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, they are transforming rail operations through AI agents embedded into the systems that support daily operations across their transportation networks. The solution combines AI agents and human oversight to automate incident resolution, support operations teams, and improve service reliability. This session explores the journey from proof of concept to production, the governance and safety guardrails required for adoption, and how lighthouse programs are becoming blueprints for enterprise-wide agentic process transformation. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Morten Wetjen (Director | Cloud & AI Transformation, PwC Germany)
Leila Fathallah (Cloud Solutions Architect, PwC)
Tobias Hackbarth (Head of, Deutsche Bahn AG)
Marc Schulmeyer (Product Owner, Deutsche Bahn AG)
Srikanth Dola (Chief Technology Strategy Officer, Norfolk Southern Corporation)

title: Agentic platform design engineering: scaling AI agents across the enterprise.
abstract: Your teams are building AI agents in every line of business and also using third-party agents. How do you evolve them into an enterprise agentic platform where you know what exists, reuse it instead of rebuilding, keep it secure, and control what agents spend? This hands-on workshop applies agentic platform design engineering for enterprises. Learn how AWS Agent Registry and an open-source registry let teams discover and reuse agents. Secure cross-account calls with short-lived tokens, trace each request end to end, and let agents pay for data within limits they can't override. Leave with a blueprint for your platform.
speakers: Rajeswari Malladi (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Manuj Arora (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: MCP and A2A for SaaS: making your product agent-ready
abstract: Agentic AI is reshaping how SaaS products reach end customers. Alongside browser and API interactions, exposing capabilities through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and distributing agents via the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol is fast becoming the norm. In this session, build the two pieces every multi-tenant, agent-ready SaaS needs: an MCP server exposing your tools and resources, and an A2A endpoint with agent cards for inter-agent calls. Discover reference architectures for MCP in front of existing APIs, A2A agent cards, and authentication and authorization on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Leave with a blueprint for being a citizen in the agentic ecosystem.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Alexander Pogorielov (Senior Solutions Architect, ISV, CEE, Amazon Web Services)
Rohith Vijayasankar (Enterprise Support Lead, Amazon Web Services)
Luca Guida (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Gaurav Acharya (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Frederic Schoenberger (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Scale reinforcement learning globally with sparse weight updates (sponsored by Modal)
abstract: Reinforcement learning post training usually keeps trainers and rollout workers in one tightly coupled GPU cluster. This talk shows how to keep backpropagation on fast local fabric while moving independent rollout workers to elastic GPU capacity across regions and clouds. The key is to diff weights in the precision actually served, then publish lossless sparse version transitions instead of full checkpoints. Attendees will learn why Adam/Muon updates often disappear under BF16 rounding, how version aware sidecars commit exact weight versions, and how this architecture turns globally available inference capacity into practical reinforcement learning capacity. This presentation is brought to you by Modal, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Nan Jiang (Member of Technical Stuff, Modal Labs)

title: Clinical Trials, Reimagined at the Speed of AI (sponsored by PwC)
abstract: Bringing a new drug to market takes over a decade, and much of that time is lost to paperwork rather than science. This session tells how pharma leaders are transforming clinical development with agentic AI on AWS. Attendees will hear how PwC’s Digital Trial Core turns clinical protocols into structured, machine-readable data, powering AI agents that draw on historical insights and reusable, modular content to streamline study startup activities such as vendor selection, budgeting, negotiations, and trial documentation. Industry leaders will share how these solutions move from proof of concept into live studies, bringing treatments to patients sooner. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Chuck Liu (Vice President, Neuroscience CSL & Global Study Start Up, AbbVie)
Terry Morris (AVP Clinical Tech, Lilly)

title: Build Production Grade Agents with OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by OpenAI)
abstract: Learn how to ship agents for your applications with Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents, powered by OpenAI, and accelerate development with Codex agents. Explore architecture patterns for reliable, governable workflows across enterprise systems, covering tool use, evaluations, observability, identity, and permissions. See how to keep agent behavior measurable, access secure, and actions aligned with organizational policies. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Chris Dickens (Product Lead, OpenAI)

title: End-to-End Voice Agents with AWS and Deepgram (sponsored by Deepgram)
abstract: Voice agents are growing in popularity, but most fall apart the first time a caller interrupts or asks a hard question. In this session, Deepgram builds one live on AWS: the Deepgram Voice Agent API streams speech in and out within minutes, with Amazon Bedrock as the reasoning layer. You'll see natural, expressive voices, sub-second responses, and barge-in handling that actually works. Compliance requirements? The same models deploy via Amazon SageMaker inside your own VPC, so audio never leaves your AWS perimeter. Leave with running code and an architecture your security team can approve. This presentation is brought to you by Deepgram, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Ed Charbeneau (Sr. Developer Advocate, Deepgram)

title: The Control Plane for Your Agent Workforce: Governance, Cost and ROI at Scale (sponsored by Cognition)
abstract: Cognition has rolled out Devin, the autonomous software engineer, at the world's largest Fortune 500 companies. Along the way, we learned that scaling an agent workforce hinges on three questions every enterprise asks: How do we onboard agents? How do we know they're delivering value? How do we ensure they only do what they're supposed to? Drawing from real deployments, this session introduces the practical patterns we developed to answer them — governance, cost controls, ROI measurement, and federated configurations. You'll leave with a playbook for turning agents from a promising pilot into a trusted, scaled workforce. This presentation is brought to you by Cognition, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater

title: Build Your Defense Factory for Continuous Defense with OpenAI (sponsored by OpenAI)
abstract: Put agents to work discovering vulnerabilities and driving fixes autonomously with OpenAI and AWS. Learn how to implement continuous defense with OpenAI tooling, Daybreak cyber models, and AWS infrastructure including Amazon Bedrock, drawing on lessons from OpenAI's internal Defense Factory. Explore routing findings to the right owners, reducing duplicate findings, and using development environments to validate vulnerabilities and test fixes. As broadly available cyber models help threat actors find decade-old vulnerabilities, this session focuses on how defenders can put continuous defense into practice. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Matt Boyle (Head of Cyber Engineering, OpenAI)
Shikhar Kwatra (Head of Partner Applied AI Engineering, Open AI)

title: Small Language Models, Total Control: Sovereign AI Agents, Lower Cost (sponsored by Boomi)
abstract: Enterprises are waking up to a hard truth: the AI their business now depends on runs on infrastructure, models, and pricing they don't control. In this session, Boomi's engineering and AI leadership show a different path — AI agents that run anywhere you choose (your Amazon VPC, your data center, behind your firewall) powered by small language models fine-tuned to each agent's job and served entirely on infrastructure you govern. You'll see the full architecture on AWS — Amazon EKS, EC2 GPU instances, Amazon S3, Aurora, MSK, and Amazon Bedrock as a governed escalation path — plus the fine-tuning pipeline (LoRA SFT + DPO), the evaluation gate that decides when a small model is ready, and a live demo of an agent reasoning locally at a fraction of the latency and cost of a frontier LLM. This presentation is brought to you by Boomi, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Thomas Benjamin (SVP Product Development & Engineering, Boomi)
Chris Hallenbeck (SVP and GM, AI & Platform, Boomi)

title: Build durable AI agents with AgentCore and Temporal (sponsored by Temporal)
abstract: An AI agent completes five steps, waits for approval, and then its runtime is replaced. How does it recover without repeating costly tool calls or losing the business process? In this session, learn how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, and Temporal combine AWS-native agent infrastructure with durable execution. We’ll build a production agent that preserves progress across failures, coordinates tools, agents, and people, and safely evolves while work is still running. You'll see how Temporal natively supports serverless compute infrastructure, complementing AgentCore Runtime with durable execution, preserving workflow progress across failures, approvals, runtime changes, and scale to zero, without pushing recovery and coordination logic into application code. This presentation is brought to you by Temporal, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Cornelia Davis (Principal Technologist, Temporal)

title: Rethinking Agentic Security: How Cyera Scaled AI Securely in Days (sponsored by Cyera)
abstract: As AI shifts from assistive systems to autonomous agents, data becomes the control surface. Agents need a goldilocks balance of data, identity, and process access: enough to be effective, too much and you end up on Twitter. Cyera solved this internally, reaching 88% weekly AI usage across engineering and non-engineering teams in 17 days. Adoption was not the hard part. The wiring was. How do you govern access and give builders a permit path so they ship instead of wait? Join us for what we learned, and what it means on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: AWSome Automation: From Project Brief Prompt to Landing Page (sponsored by Storyblok)
abstract: Building a product-launch agent means solving several problems at once: assembling content from approved components, enforcing brand guidelines, localizing across markets, and ensuring a human has final say before anything reaches production. This session examines how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and Storyblok handle each of those concerns without requiring a separate governance layer. Explore why a custom Strands agent made more sense than the no-code harness, how Cedar policies, Storyblok's component whitelist, brand guidelines, and publishing workflows form complementary guardrail layers, and how the architecture takes a brief to a reviewed, localized landing page in minutes. This presentation is brought to you by Storyblok, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Daniel Mendoza (Senior Developer Relations Engineer, Storyblok)

title: Fine-tune and evaluate NVIDIA Open models on Amazon SageMaker (sponsored by NVIDIA)
abstract: Learn how to customize NVIDIA Open models using Amazon SageMaker without managing training infrastructure. This session walks through preparing a dataset, fine-tuning the model, and evaluating the customized model against the base model to measure improvements in quality. Attendees will leave with a practical workflow for adapting NVIDIA's open models to domain-specific use cases on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Curt Lockhart (Sr. AI Solutions Architect, NVIDIA)
Sandeep Raveesh (Senior GenAI Specialist AI, AWS)

title: Automate AI governance and risk management with John Deere
abstract: Governance frameworks designed for static deployments struggle to keep pace with AI systems that learn, adapt, and act autonomously. Walk through AWS Responsible AI best practices for governing AI across the full development lifecycle. Then see how John Deere applied these principles through AI Risk Intelligence (AIRI) to automate risk management. Learn how static checks verify controls at code and documentation level while dynamic checks analyze APIs and traces in real time, achieving over 30% reduction in assessment time and continuous visibility into AI risk posture. Learn what it takes to move from periodic manual assessments to continuous, automated governance.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Segolene Dessertine-Panhard (Sr Science Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Carl Kubalsky (IT Director, Enterprise Data & Architecture, John Deere)

title: Expand your GPU playbook: Amazon EC2 G7e/G7 for inference and training
abstract: Not every ML workload needs the same GPU. Amazon EC2 G7e and G7 instances, powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with GDDR7 and native FP4 support, deliver strong price-performance for inference and select training use cases. This session breaks down where G7e and G7 fit: inference prefill (competitive FLOPS per dollar) and decode (FP4 and higher concurrency help close the HBM gap), and training via pipeline parallelism. The session covers the toolchain (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, TransformerEngine, CUTLASS FP4 kernels), a TCO comparison, and a decision framework for choosing G7e and G7 versus P-series instances.
speakers: Theo Wu (Senior Business Development Manager, Graviton WW GTM, Amazon Web Services)
Leah Tucker (Sr. AI/ML Specialist SA, AWS)

title: Open weights to production: How Salesforce built and served Koa models
abstract: Learn how to turn open-weight models into specialized, production-grade models for enterprise AI. Using Salesforce's Koa models as a real-world example, this session shows how the team built and served classifier, text, and voice agent evaluation models at scale. You'll learn how to choose training techniques for each use case, curate high-quality training environments, and prove accuracy gains against base models. For serving, you'll see how the team selected the serving engine, configuration, and instance type for better price-performance. Salesforce trained on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod and serves on SageMaker AI managed inference, keeping enterprise data within its trust boundary.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: James Zhu (Senior Manager, Salesforce)
Amit Gupta (Senior Director AI/ML, Salesforce)
Hrushikesh Gangur (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Agents run at the edge. The blast radius lives in the cloud (sponsored by Sysdig)
abstract: Every agent your company runs, on a developer laptop, in a CI runner, or in an Amazon EKS pod, ends its work the same way, with an API call against your AWS account using a credential nobody reviewed. Endpoint tools stop at the laptop. The credentials that matter live in the cluster. This year's worst agent incidents involved no attacker. An agent did what it was permitted to do, and nobody rendered a decision at the moment a permitted step became an incident. In fifteen minutes, Sysdig follows one person's agents from their laptop into EKS, shows what each action would reach in your account, and stops the one whose reach includes admin-equivalent permissions before it executes. Bring your own agents. Ask us what they can reach. This presentation is brought to you by Sysdig, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Eric Carter (Product Marketing Director, Sysdig)

title: Kiro Writes the PR. Nobody Validates the App. (sponsored by TestMu)
abstract: Kiro can now build a whole feature on its own: write the spec, implement it, and open the PR without anyone sitting in the loop. That’s real progress. But nothing in that pipeline actually runs the app and checks it against what the spec promised. The checks that gate the PR look at the code, not the behavior. So the PR arrives looking done, and “done” is still just a guess someone has to trust. The good news is Kiro already produces the one thing a testing agent needs to close that gap: a clear, structured spec of what the feature is supposed to do. We’ll show Kane-CLI plugged in as a Kiro Power, reading that spec, actually running the app the way a user would, and reporting back proof, not just a checkmark, before the PR merges. This presentation is brought to you by TestMu, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater

title: Build a Live App in Under 20 Minutes, Then See How It Actually Worked (sponsored by MongoDB)
abstract: Most teams know what they want to build long before they have something they can show someone. This workshop gets you there fast, then shows you what's behind that build. First, you'll build a real app. Using MongoDB Build Lab from your laptop, turn an idea (a search tool, an AI assistant, a dashboard, anything) into a working, deployed app backed by MongoDB Atlas. No repo setup, no infrastructure work. You'll touch the full stack, generation, database, and deployment, and walk away with a functional prototype. Then we open up the system behind it: planning, safety checks, a durable job queue, containerized workers on Amazon EC2, automated testing, targeted repairs, and deployment. We'll unpack what makes it repeatable, like isolating generated code, keeping credentials at trusted boundaries, and preserving state across restarts with Atlas. A MongoDB Build Lab workshop, with AWS. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Nina Lopatina (Staff AI Developer Advocate, MongoDB)

title: Customer paths to production grade domain-specific AI with Forge
abstract: Domain-specific AI delivers accuracy that is difficult for general models to match. In this session, see how real customers use Amazon Nova Forge to accelerate the path from idea to production..
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Deepak Rupakula (Principal Specialist: Gen AI GTM, Amazon Web Services)
Sharlina Keshava (Applied Science Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Inside UK AISI: stress-testing frontier AI safety on Amazon Bedrock
abstract: The UK AI Security Institute leads global research into harmful AI capabilities, assessing frontier models for risks like offensive cybersecurity, bioweapon design, and psychological manipulation. In this talk, UK AISI representatives walk through how they built their evaluation infrastructure on Amazon Bedrock, from model access and prompt orchestration to result analysis. Hear highlights from recent research projects and the engineering decisions that make safety evaluation repeatable at scale. Together, these examples show how rigorous AI safety research runs in production on AWS.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Kyle McMaster (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Agents that train themselves: autonomous reinforcement learning on AWS
abstract: Can an AI agent teach itself to land a spacecraft? In this hands-on Builders' session you hand a Strands agent one goal: land the lunar lander gently. Then you watch it write its own reward, run reinforcement learning, and grade the result, looping until it sticks the landing. You'll catch it cheating, then watch it diagnose and fix its reward. When a run stalls, you fan out parallel agents and let a sealed judge crown the winner before shipping it to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Give an agent a goal and a judge it can't game, and it trains itself.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

Arron Bailiss (Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Bryan Lu (Applied Scientist, Amazon Web Services)

title: From dataset to a deployed fine-tuned LLM in hours on SageMaker AI
abstract: ​Customize a foundation model on your own dataset in hours, with no infrastructure to provision and no GPUs to manage. In this workshop, fine tune LLMs using the Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization APIs. Work through five techniques, including Supervised Fine Tuning for task specific behavior, Direct Preference Optimization for alignment, Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards for reasoning, Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback for scalable feedback, and multi turn reinforcement learning for agentic tasks. Prepare datasets, launch training jobs, register models in the SageMaker AI Registry, evaluate with LLM as a judge, and deploy to a real time endpoint.
speakers: Christian Kamwangala (Sr SA Specialist AIML GenAI, AWS)
Bruno Pistone (WW Sr. Specialist SA Gen AI/ML, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build and Optimize AI Pipelines with Ray on SageMaker HyperPod
abstract: Ray provides a unified Python framework for petabyte-scale data processing, large-model training, and low-latency inference. In this hands-on workshop, you will use Ray on SageMaker HyperPod to a model and set up endpoints. Create a Ray cluster from SageMaker Studio and attach a JupyterLab notebook to build the pipeline from Ray train to Ray Serve. Simulate a node failure and watch training auto-resume in seconds. Experience HyperPod's native Ray integration with embedded observability, tiered checkpointing, hung-job detection, and managed KV cache for inference. You leave with a working endpoint and patterns you can apply to your own workloads.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Ioan CATANA (AIML GenAI Specialist SA, AWS)
Varun Rajan (Sol Architect, Amazon)

title: Build optimized, resilient inference endpoints on Amazon SageMaker AI
abstract: Deploy, optimize, and monitor an LLM inference endpoint end to end on Amazon SageMaker AI. In this hands on workshop, use GenAI Inference Recommender to discover optimal configurations, cutting model deployment time to days instead of weeks, learn how to train EAGLE speculative decoding heads on your own data for up to 2.5× throughput gains, and benchmark results. Then, configure capacity aware instance pools with priority based GPU fallback and weighted autoscaling for production resilience. Throughout, interact with endpoints via OpenAI compatible APIs. You keep the working notebooks to reuse on your own endpoints.
speakers: Dmitry Soldatkin (Sr WW Specialist SA - GenAI, Amazon)
Apoorva Chandra (Sr PMT-ES, AWS)

abstract: Stop paying frontier-model prices for agentic workloads. In this hands-on session, build production-ready AI agents powered by open-source models like Qwen3 and Gemma4 running entirely on Amazon SageMaker AI. You'll deploy models with optimized serving, connect them to multi-turn tool-use workflows through OpenAI-compatible APIs, and enable real-time bi-directional streaming for responsive agent interactions. Leave with a working cost-optimized agent stack you fully control — fast inference, zero vendor lock-in, and patterns for scaling agentic workloads on your own terms.
speakers: Dan Ferguson (Sr WW Specialist SA - GenAI, AWS)
Piyush Daftary (Principal Software Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: End-to-end foundation model pipelines on SageMaker HyperPod with EKS
abstract: Train, deploy, and serve a foundation model end-to-end on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod with on Kubernetes. In this hands-on workshop, prepare training data at scale leveraging high speed storage, launch distributed fine-tuning across multi-node GPU clusters with auto-healing and checkpointless recovery that maximizes goodput, and transition seamlessly to production inference on the same cluster— eliminating re-platforming. Throughout, monitor cluster health and inference latency. Leave with working notebooks and production-ready patterns you can deploy immediately.

Harsh Asnani (Sr. Worldwide Specialist SA - GenAI, Amazon Web Services, Inc.)

title: Build a production multi-Agent Systems with Strands
abstract: Build, deploy, and scale agents with re-usable multi-agent patterns in Strands Agents. You will create an agentic system that is capable of decomposing complex tasks and delegating sub-tasks to specialized worker agents. These agents will manage shared state and memory across boundaries, gracefully handle failures, and enforce quality guardrails. Subsequently, these agents will be deployed to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for production scaling and observability, featuring harness capabilities for checkpointing and long-running multi-agent workflow capabilities. Upon completion, you will be equipped with reusable design patterns and industry best practices to construct production-grade multi-agent systems utilizing the Strands Agent SDK.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1

title: End-to-End ModelOps on SageMaker AI: Experiment to Production
abstract: Hands-on workshop where practitioners experiment with SageMaker AI end-to-end ModelOps capabilities: onboard, build, govern, deploy, monitor. Attendees track experiments with managed MLflow, orchestrate repeatable training workflows with SageMaker Pipelines and built-in lineage tracking, register and version models in Model Registry with model cards and approval gates, deploy through CI/CD promotion pipelines, and monitor for drift and quality with Model Monitor. Governance such as access control, validation, approvals, and Responsible AI guardrails is embedded into every step. Attendees leave with a repeatable, governed path from experiment to production they can stand up within a week
speakers: Paolo Di Francesco (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Nisha Gambhir (Senior Delivery Consultant, AWS Proserve)

title: Build a cost optimization playbook for your AI workload
abstract: Learn how to cut the cost of your AI workloads without sacrificing quality. In this builders session, you work through a curated set of representative prompts and apply three high-impact levers: prompt caching, Intelligent Prompt Routing, and right-sizing model choice. You measure token cost before and after each change, so you see exactly which levers move the needle and which do not. You're welcome to bring a prompt from your own workload to test alongside the guided examples. Leave with a repeatable cost optimization playbook and the evidence to support each decision.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

title: Scale AI-powered software development securely with Bedrock
abstract: Your dev teams are adopting AI coding agents fast: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, open-source agents, and more. Without a shared platform, every team rolls its own auth, its own cost tracking, its own rules. In this builders session, build one platform on Amazon Bedrock that manages all of them. Package your security policies, coding standards, and delivery practices as reusable plugins, agent skills, and MCP servers, then apply consistent identity, sandboxing, observability, and cost controls across every agent. Use the platform to turn an issue into a tested change, then adapt the architecture across your organization.

title: Visualize and interpret domain knowledge graphs using AI
abstract: Complex systems like supply chains, energy grids, and decarbonization efforts are difficult to model because relationships between actors are hidden across siloed data. A knowledge graph can surface these connections, helping organizations simulate what-if scenarios and act on high impact opportunities. In this builder session, use Amazon Neptune to construct an ontology-typed knowledge graph that maps stakeholder dependencies and sustainability regulatory impacts. Then simulate competing interventions and use an Amazon Bedrock agent to interpret which action drives the broadest impact. Leave with a reusable pattern for modeling complex systems and identifying high-leverage intervention points.
speakers: Colin Marden (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Kenta Sato (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Japan G.K.)
Marco Masciola (Sr. Research Scientist, Amazon Web Services)
Jun Zhang (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build a Physical AI Model Factory on SageMaker HyperPod
abstract: Physical AI teams in robotics and autonomous vehicles can't collect enough real data for the rare edge cases that dominate risk. The answer is a continuous data flywheel: generate synthetic scenarios, post-train policies, evaluate, repeat. Running that at scale is GPU-hungry and orchestration-heavy. This chalk talk shows how to run the full Physical AI model factory on SageMaker HyperPod with EKS: provision heterogeneous GPU pools, schedule multi-stage jobs, and leverage auto-healing infrastructure.
speakers: Nicolas Jourdan (Sr. Specialist Solution Architect AI/ML/GenAI EMEA, AWS)
Nathan Arnold (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Scale your coding agents beyond the laptop with AgentCore
abstract: Developers want Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro with laptop-like feel but without laptop limits: no parallelism, no persistence, no isolation. In this hands-on workshop, you will deploy a coding agent to AgentCore's runtime in three commands, then build real workflows: a code review agent, PR automation, and a repo consolidation job. You will run agents in parallel across isolated microVMs, persist and share state with BYO S3 and EFS, connect models through Bedrock, and wire an agent to wake on GitHub events and work in the background. Leave with working code you can drop straight into your own repos.
speakers: Aravind Subramanian (Specialist Sr. SA, GenAI/ML, Amazon Web Services)
Sanghwa Na (Sr. Specialist SA, Gen AI, AWS)

title: Best practices for AI-powered software development on Amazon Bedrock
abstract: You already use a coding agent for software development. It touches your codebase, infrastructure, and production environment and needs guardrails, permissions, and rules to operate safely. In this workshop, you connect an agent of your choice, such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex, to Amazon Bedrock and deliver a real application from brief to production. You define specs the agent can act on, wire in automated test gates, apply Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and lock down permissions before anything reaches infrastructure. The app serves as a tested reference implementation your team can adapt to its own development workflows. Laptop required.
speakers: Ajit Mahareddy (Bedrock Product/GTM Lead, Amazon Web Services)
Alfredo Castillo (Sr WW Specialist SA - GenAI, AWS)

title: Build and deploy agents to Lambda and EKS with Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Bring an agent idea and leave with it deployed. In this workshop you use the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock to build an agent from scratch, give it tools and memory, and add guardrails, permissions, and observability. There are multiple ways to deploy agents in production, including Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Lambda MicroVMs, and Amazon EKS. In this lab you deploy to Lambda and EKS. Leave with a reference architecture for agents you can actually ship. Laptop required.

title: From prompts to loops: inference best practices for agents
abstract: Every layer of an agent, from context and harness to planning loops, places additional demand on the inference engine. Each model turn created by planning, tool use, retrieval, reflection, or retry shapes cost, latency, and reliability. This chalk talk traces that evolution on Amazon Bedrock and shows the inference impact of each layer, with best practices to get them right: versioning prompts, grounding context, engineering a reliable harness, setting verifiable goal conditions, and designing loops that know when to stop. Leave knowing how each layer shapes cost, latency, and reliability.
speakers: Nathan Jones (Sr. Manager, Bedrock, Amazon Web Services)
Aris Tsakpinis (Sr WW Specialist SA, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Web Services)
