title: Maximize GPU utilization across training and inference on HyperPod
abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore how SageMaker HyperPod serves as a unified GPU pool for data processing, training, post-training, and inference without re-platforming. Through live whiteboarding, demos, and production architectures; we'll cover how customers are maximizing GPU utilization across workloads, regions, and multiple teams with shared architectures and GPUs. Then learn how SageMaker Studio gives give data scientists, AI researchers, and machine learning engineers an easy way to to iterate on jobs all on the shared pool of resources. We'll also see how Humain has optimized utilization of compute resources across two large HyperPod clusters, onboarding multiple teams of researchers with team isolation and advanced task submission strategies. Participants will walk away with practical patterns for running the full model lifecycle on resilient, shared infrastructure
speakers: Giuseppe Angelo Porcelli (Principal ML Solutions Architect, AWS)
Rama Thamman (Sr. Manager, Amazon)

title: From raw data to custom model: Dataset prep with Amazon SageMaker AI
abstract: Great models start with great data. In this hands-on workshop, use SageMaker AI Agent skills to profile, curate, and validate datasets for the full model customization lifecycle — no infrastructure to manage. Assess data completeness and distribution, apply auto-labeling at scale, run human-in-the-loop review for edge cases, and fix quality issues like deduplication and toxicity filtering. Generate synthetic data to fill coverage gaps, then prepare datasets for Supervised Fine-Tuning, Direct Preference Optimization, Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, and RLAIF. Launch training, evaluate with LLM-as-a-Judge, and deploy. Walk away ready to go from raw data to custom model in hours.
speakers: Amin Dashti (Sr. Data Scientist, AWS)
gzappia Zappia (Principal AI/ML Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: On-Policy Distillation on HyperPod EKS: Train Smarter Small Models
abstract: Frontier models are powerful but costly to deploy. On-policy distillation, adopted by Qwen3, MiMo, and GLM-5, lets you compress a large teacher into a lean, domain-specialized student by training on the student's own rollouts with dense token-level feedback. Unlike Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, it's cheaper, more stable, and doesn't require a verifier. In this code talk, walk through a working implementation on HyperPod EKS: orchestrate teacher inference and student training across GPU pools, manage the rollout buffer, and evaluate convergence.
speakers: Eric Borland (Senior Solutions Developer, Amazon Web Services)
Chakravarthy Nagarajan (Sr Mgr, WW Spec SA - GenAI, AWS)

title: Scale production agents reliably with AgentCore
abstract: What changes when you go from ten agent sessions to ten thousand? In this chalk talk, whiteboard the architectural and operational patterns that determine whether your agents perform reliably at scale. Discuss microVM isolation for secure multi-tenancy, elastic scaling that handles traffic spikes without capacity planning, and long-running task handling with human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Cover resiliency patterns: what happens when a tool call fails, how to handle model timeouts, and designing for graceful degradation. Walk through the infrastructure decisions you make once and benefit from forever. Bring your scaling scenarios and we architect solutions together.
speakers: Shishir Bharathi (Principal Engineer, AWS)
Satveer Khurpa (Sr WW Specialist SA - GenAI, AWS)

title: Route, cache, and batch: a multi-model decision framework on Bedrock
abstract: Treating every request the same is what makes inference expensive at scale, and most of that cost is repeat work you already paid for. This chalk talk whiteboards how prompt caching on Amazon Bedrock eliminates redundant computation across system prompts, shared context, and multi-turn conversations, then shows where Intelligent Prompt Routing and batch inference extend the savings further. We walk through cache-hit economics, how to structure prompts for maximum reuse, and when routing or batching is the better lever. Bring your traffic patterns and questions, and leave with a caching-first cost strategy tuned to your workloads.
speakers: Aswath Ram A Srinivasan (Sr. WW Specialist Solutions Architect- Bedrock, Amazon Web Services)
Chris Greenwood (Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: Switch models in production without disrupting customers on Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Your application is working in production, and then a newer model arrives with better benchmarks or lower cost. You need to decide whether moving is worth the risk. A switch can change outputs, break prompts, raise costs, and create weeks of retesting. This session shows how to reduce that disruption on Amazon Bedrock. Test candidate models against your own use cases, compare quality, latency, and cost, and update prompts without rewriting them by hand. See how Advanced Prompt Optimization scores your current model against candidates on your own data, giving each candidate a fair prompt, so you can measure the impact before rollout. Leave with a practical plan for switching models without disrupting customers.
speakers: Shash Sapre (Sr. Product Manager, AWS)
Claudio Mazzoni (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Getting Started with AgentCore: ship an agent to production in 2 hours
abstract: You can build an agent in an afternoon. Getting it to production takes months. Not because the AI is hard, but because the infrastructure around it is: memory, tool access, identity, policy, observability, evaluation. This workshop closes that gap in two hours. Build a customer support agent from scratch and progressively add each production capability using the AgentCore CLI: runtime, memory, gateway, identity, policy, observability, and evaluation. AgentCore is framework and model agnostic, so everything applies whether you use LangGraph, CrewAI, Strands, or your own stack. Leave ready to ship.
speakers: Madhu Samhitha Vangara (Specialist Solution Architect - GenAI, Amazon)
Robert Belson (Senior Developer Advocate, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build the full agent optimization loop on AgentCore
abstract: How do you know your agent is still performing? Stop guessing. This workshop walks you through the full optimization loop on AgentCore: instrument with OpenTelemetry traces, score with built-in and custom evaluators, generate data-backed recommendations that rewrite your system prompt or tool descriptions, validate offline with batch evaluation, then split live traffic with A/B testing through AgentCore Gateway until you have statistical confidence to promote. You will run every step hands-on, ship a measurably better agent configuration, and leave with a repeatable process that replaces guess-and-check prompt iteration with evidence.
speakers: Rajesh Kumar Ravi (Sr. Solutions Architect, WWSO Agentic AI, Amazon Web Services)
Abhinav Krishna (Principal Product Manager (Technical), External Services, AWS)

title: First principles at LLM scale: Architecting Forge
abstract: When we set out to build Forge, Amazon's foundation model customization platform, we assumed the hardest problems would be ML problems. They weren't. They were classical problems Amazon's been solving for years, at a new scale. Same Well-Architected principles, evolved techniques. We will deep-dive into three workloads from the team behind Forge. First, serverless training of large language models on AWS. Second, enterprise-grade inference serving. Third, observability and evaluation tools optimizing toward smaller, performant models. Leave with lessons for your own AI platform.
speakers: Omid Razavi (Principal Technical Program Manager, Amazon)
Anjali Narayan-Chen (Principal Applied Scientist, Amazon)

title: Intelligent document processing with generative AI on AWS
abstract: Description: In this workshop, you build an intelligent document processing pipeline on AWS that turns unstructured documents into structured, verifiable data. First, extract text, tables, and layout in the format and granularity your downstream application expects. Then configure a pipeline that splits a multi-document package, matches each document to the right schema, and extracts the fields you need. Each value comes with a confidence score and its source location, so you can decide what to automate and what to send for human review. You leave with a working pipeline you can adapt to your own documents. Bring your laptop.
speakers: Niklas Breuer (Senior Product Manager, Technical, Amazon.com)
Roop Bains (Sr. GenAI/ML SA, AWS)

title: Train and deploy large-scale models with governance at every step
abstract: Training a large-scale model is the easy part. Getting it into production with the right data flowing in, governance enforced, and multiple deployment paths ready is where most teams stall. This chalk talk works through how to build one training pipeline on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, bring in enterprise data that amplifies model value while respecting data protection policies, and deploy the same model into Amazon Bedrock for inference or Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for agent orchestration. Governance follows the model at every step. No bolted-on compliance. You leave with an architecture you can build against immediately.
speakers: Paulo Pontes Vieira de Aragao (Principal WW Specialist SA GenAI, Amazon Web Services)
Amin Dashti (Sr. Data Scientist, AWS)

title: Beyond Prompt Engineering: Optimize the Agent Harness
abstract: An agent’s performance depends on far more than its model or system prompt. Tools, instructions, context management, memory, orchestration, and runtime policies form an agent harness that can determine whether the same model succeeds or fails. This session introduces harness optimization: a systematic, evaluation-driven approach to improving the complete agent system. Learn how to identify high-leverage changes, design controlled experiments, optimize for quality, latency, and cost, and avoid overfitting to benchmarks. Leave with a repeatable method for turning agent development into an engineering discipline.
speakers: Jonathan Buck (Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Po-Shin Chen (Software Developer Engineer, AWS)

speakers: Jonathan Buck (Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Po-Shin Chen (Software Developer Engineer, AWS)

title: Build the right inference strategy on Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Generative AI workloads place very different demands on inference. Customer support chatbots and coding assistants may prioritize responsiveness, while large-scale document processing can favor greater cost efficiency. Some workloads can tolerate flexible processing times, while others need predictable capacity and performance. Healthcare applications may also need inference processing to remain within a specific geography. Learn how to match Amazon Bedrock inference offerings to different workload needs, balancing performance and cost while meeting data residency requirements.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Aswath Ram A Srinivasan (Sr. WW Specialist Solutions Architect- Bedrock, Amazon Web Services)
Chintan Vyas (Principal Product Manager – Technical, Amazon Web Services)

title: One agent, any robot: building physical AI with Strands Robots
abstract: Physical AI puts agents in the real world. This chalk talk builds a robotics agent with the Strands Robots SDK: one Robot() call gives an agent hands — a MuJoCo simulation by default, real hardware with one code parameter change. We'll whiteboard the loop around the embodied agent: perception, a vision-language-action policy (GR00T, Cosmos 3, LeRobot), and low-level control. We'll cover the the edge-to-cloud intelligence split, the peer-to-peer mesh and AWS IoT bridge coordinating a fleet, and sim-to-real transfer.
speakers: Cagatay Cali (Research Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: Context engineering for production agents on AgentCore
abstract: An agent is only as good as what fills its context window. System prompts, skills, tool definitions, conversation history, retrieved documents, long-term memory, they all compete for limited space. Get the mix wrong and you waste tokens, degrade reasoning, or lose critical instructions mid-conversation. This chalk talk breaks down every layer of context that shapes agent behavior on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We cover how to structure system prompts, define skills effectively, manage tool context through gateway, retain the right conversation history, and use Memory strategies to persist what matters across sessions. Bring your agents, we optimize them live.
speakers: Akarsha Sehwag (Sr. GenAI Data Scientist - Agentcore Memory, Amazon Web Services)
Noor Randhawa (Sr. Software Engineer, Amazon)

title: Automated Reasoning as Agent Guardrails
abstract: Your agent is only as safe as the constraints it can’t bypass. This chalk talk covers how to enforce hard invariants on LLM-driven agents using formal policy languages: Cedar for stateless authorization, Dogwood for temporal reasoning over action history, and human-in-the-loop for the decisions machines shouldn’t make alone. We’ll look at different techniques for integrating this kind of enforcement with agents, including the Strands Agents intervention system and how deterministic policy can sit alongside a probabilistic model.
speakers: Mackenzie Zastrow (Software Development Engineer, Amazon Web Serv)
Liz Radway (SDE II, AWS Velocity Labs)

title: Build long-running agents that persist for days on AgentCore
abstract: Most agents handle a single request and forget everything. Production workloads are different — an incident investigation spans hours, a document review takes days, a customer onboarding stretches across weeks. These agents need to persist state, survive restarts, and pick up exactly where they left off. This session covers how to build long-running agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Runtime for durable execution and Memory for cross-session context. Learn checkpointing patterns, human-in-the-loop pause and resume, and cost strategies that keep idle agents from burning through your budget.
speakers: Prasanna Sridharan (Principal Gen AI Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Securing the agent loop with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
abstract: You screen the prompt on the way in and the answer on the way out. In between, tool results carry external content straight into the model's context and tool arguments carry the model's decisions out to your systems, without inspection. The middle of the loop is where indirect prompt injection lands. Where you place a guardrail inside the loop is a design decision. In this chalk talk, we place Bedrock Guardrails checks inside the agent loop. We examine ApplyGuardrail and InvokeGuardrailChecks, work through where each one belongs, and look at what risk remains when the checks are in place.
speakers: Shivani Singh (Data Scientist, Amazon)
Felipe Lopez (Principal AI Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Sreedhar Gade (VP Engineering, Freshworks)

title: Live-code inference patterns for agentic workloads on Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Agentic workloads are multi-step, tool-calling, and retrieval-augmented, which means they stress the inference layer differently than a single prompt. In this code talk, we build three patterns live: function calling, multi-step reasoning chains, and retrieval-augmented generation with Knowledge Bases. For each, you see how it behaves at the inference level, including token consumption, latency, and retry logic, and how to tune it for cost and speed. The completed code covers all three patterns and can be adapted to your own agents.
speakers: Bruno Pistone (WW Sr. Specialist SA Gen AI/ML, Amazon Web Services)
Daniel Wirjo (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Foundational Model Ops with Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Build a fine-tuning pipeline that proves its own results. In this workshop, run the full loop, baseline eval, fine-tune, RL, re-eval, against the same bar every time. Start with a benchmark baseline on a Hugging Face model. Then fine-tune with QLoRA on Amazon SageMaker AI Training Jobs, with full control over your training script and compute. Add an RL pass with RLAIF or RLVR to optimize against a reward signal the benchmark alone can't score, and re-evaluate against that same baseline to see whether the gain is real or just a lower loss number. Put the whole sequence into a SageMaker Pipeline so it reruns on new data without manual rework. Bedrock Guardrails sit at the deployment gate.
speakers: Mona Mona (Sr Gen AI Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Vinay Arora (Sr WW Specialist SA – GenAI, Amazon Web Services)

title: From reactive operations to autonomous resilience: How Agentic AI is redefining SRE (sponsored by HCLTech)
abstract: Traditional SRE was built to restore systems quickly, but today’s complex, distributed environments demand more than reactive operations. This lightning session explores how agentic AI is redefining SRE by enabling autonomous detection, decision-making, remediation, and continuous learning. It examines how observability can extend beyond infrastructure metrics to connect system health with customer experience and business outcomes. Attendees will learn how AI, observability, and operations are converging to create resilient, self-optimizing environments, why autonomous resilience is becoming a competitive advantage, and the practical steps organizations can take to progress toward Level 5 autonomous operations while retaining appropriate human oversight and governance This presentation is brought to you by HCLTech, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Ramesh Ramakrishnan (VP, Verizon)

title: The Physical AI Blueprint: A Full-Stack Solution with AWS and NVIDIA (sponsored by NVIDIA)
abstract: Get hands-on building a complete Physical AI pipeline using the AWS and NVIDIA toolchain. This workshop walks you through each stage—synthetic data generation with Isaac Sim, foundation model training with GR00T and Cosmos, digital twin simulation in Omniverse, edge deployment via IoT Greengrass, multi-robot orchestration with AgentCore, and continuous learning with SageMaker using NVIDIA OSMO. Walk away with a working blueprint you can apply to manufacturing, logistics, or autonomous systems. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Shaun Kirby (Principal ProServe Cloud Architect, AWS)
Ali Shahrokni (Sr. Developer Relations Manager, NVIDIA)
Abhishek Srivastav (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: From AI to Action: Powering Agentic Enterprises with AWS and Infosys (sponsored by Infosys)
abstract: As AI evolves from generating insights to driving action, leading organizations are adopting intelligent agents to transform how work gets done. Hear from enterprise leaders as they share their journeys to building agentic businesses with AWS and Infosys, accelerating decision making, improving productivity, and unlocking measurable business value at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Infosys, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: Unlock Secure Vibe Coding on AWS Today (sponsored by Superblocks)
abstract: Your business teams already build apps with AI, often on real company data. Most of those apps never make it to production. The rest run without guardrails, and IT can't see who built what or what data it touches. Blocking the tools doesn't stop the building. This session lays out a third option: a reference blueprint for governed vibe coding in your own AWS account. Learn how to set guardrails once for every AI-built app, catch vulnerable code before it ships, keep a full audit trail, and make sure every app still has an owner when its builder leaves. This presentation is brought to you by Superblocks, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater

title: Earned autonomy: handing production over to agents (sponsored by incident.io)
abstract: What does it take to trust an AI agent with production? This talk explores how agents earn increasing responsibility, from investigating problems and recommending fixes to taking action themselves. We’ll look at where human judgment matters and what gives us the confidence to hand over more of the work. This presentation is brought to you by incident.io, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Chris Evans (Co-founder, incident.io)

title: Get hands on with new SageMaker Inference performance features
abstract: SageMaker provides the full spectrum of dedicated inference infrastructure, from managed dedicated endpoints to self-healing EKS clusters managed by HyperPod for Kubernetes-native control. An inference endpoint that serves fine at 10 queries per second may buckle at 1k. It's requests landing on saturated GPUs or capacity stranded in the wrong region. In this workshop you'll get hands-on GPU access to build and test performance across both modes, solving four problems with new capabilities shown publicly for the first time: cutting time to first token, raising throughput, and keeping deployments healthy.
speakers: Deepak Singh (Sr GenAI/ML Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: From Infrastructure to Intelligence: Building the Full AI Stack in Saudi Arabia (sponsored by HUMAIN)
abstract: From Infrastructure to Intelligence: Building the Full AI Stack in Saudi Arabia Building AI at scale means bringing together far more than compute. This conversation will bring together HUMAIN, AWS and technology partners to explore how infrastructure, cloud, data, models and enterprise applications are being connected in Saudi Arabia, and what it takes to make those layers work as one system. The panel will look at partnerships at play across the stack, including the HUMAIN–AWS AI Zone, HUMAIN Fabric on AWS Marketplace and ALLAM on Amazon Bedrock, and discuss what this emerging ecosystem could enable for customers in MENA and around the world. Suggested Panelists: - Tareq Amin, HUMAIN - ⁠Tanuja Randery, AWS - ⁠Enterprise AI Customer (TBC) - Model Provider (TBC: Adobe/Cohere) This presentation is brought to you by HUMAIN, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Tanuja Randery (Managing Director / VP EMEA, AWS)

title: Lessons in Scale and Innovation Through the Deployment of AI Agents
abstract: AI agents on AWS are transforming how Amazon teams build, ship, and operate at velocity and scale. Discover how Amazon Finance Operations, supporting 6,000+ analysts across nine global service centers, deploys AI agents to resolve millions of contacts and hundreds of thousands of cases annually, automating low-value tasks and running autonomous workflows in a high-stakes finance environment. Then explore how Amazon Operation’s Workforce Intelligence & Scheduling Engine (WISE) enables them to orchestrate the operating, management, and adjustment of labor and flow across more than 1,200 facilities. When a gap in a tool, process, or service appears, it spins up autonomous coding agents on Bedrock AgentCore to build, test, and deploy solutions or mechanisms to close the gaps. Leaders will share the innovations that enabled them to stop managing systems and start orchestrating them.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Bruno Arnal (Director, AFT, Catalyst & Ops, Amazon Fulfillment Technology, Amazon)
Jeffrey Eckhaus (Principal Tech BD, AWS)
Junjie Tang (Sr. Principal ProServe, AWS)

title: Turn a Bee wearable into your re:Invent notetaking companion
abstract: re:Invent keynotes don't slow down for note-taking. Last year's CEO keynote announced roughly 28 launches in two hours. Careful notes still leave you with names, not links. So build an agent that does the finding. Participants in this workshop will get a Bee Pioneer wearable: it transcribes while you listen, and a double-press bookmarks anything worth a deep dive. Your agent (Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock) reads the transcript and researches each announcement through the AWS MCP Server, producing one markdown file linking every launch to its docs. Then make it yours: benchmark cheaper models, post to Slack, or run it in the cloud.
speakers: Kourtney Meiss (Developer Advocate, Amazon)
Emerson Sklar (Chief Evangelist, Amazon Alexa, Amazon Alexa)

title: The Art of the Impossible: How Amazon Builds on AWS
abstract: Discover how two Amazon teams tackled seemingly impossible problems with agentic AI running on AWS. Prime Video enabled content discovery at a scale where personalized curation was never feasible, building an AI discovery assistant powered by agentic search on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, vector-powered retrieval, and frontier and custom LLMs on SageMaker. Launched to millions of Fire TV customers, it replaced endless scrolling with conversation starters like "hidden gems from the '80s" and natural voice exploration. Amazon Pharmacy now autonomously resolves most of its hundreds of thousands of monthly customer contacts while staying HIPAA compliant. Specialized agents on Amazon Bedrock Agents and Amazon Connect handle billing, fulfillment, and pharmacist workflows, hand off to humans, increasing satisfaction. Learn to apply their approaches to your own seemingly impossible problems.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Tulip Gupta (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Naresh Narayanan (Principal Engineer, Amazon)

title: Zero-Trust by Design: How Bee Protects Personal Data Even from Itself on AWS
abstract: Personal agentic AI represents a new frontier; devices that understand you deeply enough to act on your behalf. Bee is Amazon's AI wearable that helps users capture and act on insights from their daily lives. But deep personalization demands deep trust and privacy. In this session, learn how the Bee team architected a zero-trust pipeline using AWS Nitro Enclaves and confidential computing to keep sensitive data cryptographically isolated at every stage. We'll share the attestation models, data minimization tradeoffs, and design principles you can apply to build AI-powered experiences your users trust from day one.
speakers: Gopinath Jagadesan (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Prime Video Financial Systems on the Road to 10x Velocity with Kiro
abstract: This chalk talk will deep-dive into Prime Video Financial Systems' journey toward 10x engineering velocity with Kiro. Starting at 3x through AI-assisted sprints, the team evolved to autonomous agent-driven delivery, where agents pick up tasks, implement code, raise code requests, address feedback, and merge 24/7 without human intervention. Each step compounds, enabling parallel execution, zero idle time, and freeing engineers to focus on design and review. This is an honest, in-progress story that demonstrates the concrete methodology, structured specs, persistent Kiro sessions, and architectural decisions required to move from acceleration toward order-of-magnitude transformation.
speakers: Tulip Gupta (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Robert Cicero (Senior Software Development Manager, Amazon)
Kannan Ekanath (Principal Engineer, Amazon)

title: Instant Play Demos on Twitch – Increasing Player Engagement
abstract: From game builds to live campaigns, take a deep dive into the best practices and constraints around launching Instant Play Demos on Twitch, powered by Amazon GameLift Streams. This innovative approach to game marketing enables developers to reach potential players and let them try your game before they buy it. No downloads or installs required, just a WebRTC enabled browser and an internet connection. Learn what kind of content makes for a great demo, engine-specific best practices, and the benefits of launching a campaign and how they perform compared to traditional marketing channels.
speakers: Todd Sharp (Principal Specialist Solutions Architect - GameLift, AWS)
Frank Zhu (Sr. Product Manager-Tech, Twitch Advertising)

title: How Amazon Ads Built a Service Mesh Without a Control Plane Service
abstract: Most service meshes require dedicated infrastructure just to manage the mesh itself. Amazon Ads took a different approach: a fully serverless xDS control plane built with AWS Lambda and S3 that manages hundreds of Envoy proxies serving 100K+ requests per second at 2ms p99 overhead with no long-running control plane servers. In this session, we walk through the architecture end to end: Envoy sidecars on Amazon ECS for service-to-service communication, an edge proxy for external ingress, and the serverless control plane that ties it together.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Yiwen Luo (Manager, Machine Learning Engineering, Amazon)
Garry Galinsky (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Soham Kale (Senior Software Developer, Amazon)

title: AI flight plan: How British Airways’ parent builds and measures AI ROI (sponsored by NTT DATA)
abstract: British Airways’ parent, International Airlines Group (IAG), has moved rapidly from AI experimentation to production deployments delivering measurable results. This session explores how IAG and its partner NTT DATA assess AI opportunities by giving business units ownership of value realization, build momentum by prioritizing high-impact use cases, and operationalize AI through scalable technology, operating models, governance and change management. Attendees will learn how to connect AI strategy to top- and bottom-line impact through real-world examples, including procurement optimization, contract leakage detection and citizen-developed agents that accelerate safe, responsible AI adoption across the enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by NTT DATA, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Luis Huerta (Group Head of GenAI, Agents & Atomation, IAG/BRITISH AIRWAYS PLC)
Charlie Doubek (Executive - Head Of Global AI Delivery, NTT DATA Deutschland GmbH)

title: AI Spreadsheets and the Modern Data Stack: An AWS Story (sponsored by Row Zero)
abstract: AWS relies on spreadsheets for planning, forecasting, business intelligence, and self service analytics. To improve self-serve data analysis, AWS rolled out Row Zero, a cloud-based AI spreadsheet that can open billion row datasets, connect directly to data warehouses, and provide enterprise grade security controls. This session covers how AWS solved their legacy spreadsheet problems that are constrained by the compute and memory resources of employee laptops and a 1 million row limit. By adopting Row Zero, business users can derive insights and have secure access to governed data in Amazon S3, Redshift, or Athena at massive scale. This presentation is brought to you by Row Zero, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater

title: Stop Moving AWS Data. Turn It into Action with Splunk​ (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
abstract: Machine data across AWS environments is growing faster than teams can move, normalize, and analyze it. What if you could stop moving all that data and start putting it to work? In this session, learn how Cisco Data Fabric, powered by Splunk, federates data across AWS and enterprise sources, correlates it at scale, and prepares it for AI and agentic workflows. Through practical architecture patterns and a live demonstration, you’ll see how to reduce data movement and operational cost while turning distributed telemetry into trusted context, faster decisions, and action.​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Heath Johnson (Sr Manager Technical Marketing, Splunk, a Cisco Company)
Adrian Acuna (TME, Splunk, a Cisco Company)

title: Accelerating Data Processing: GPU Accelerated Amazon EMR at the Enterprise Scale (sponsored by NVIDIA)
abstract: As AI agents ask increasingly complex and frequent questions, analytics systems must become more responsive, scalable, and efficient, over hundreds of Terabytes and trillions of rows. This session explores how GPU acceleration integrated with Amazon EMR can improve performance and efficiency, with the NVIDIA cuDF Router that enables seamless migration and simplifies adoption across a large enterprise setting. Applying operational metrics to AI-driven optimization, the smart router continuously directs workloads for better performance and cost efficiency. See how enterprises can operate this architecture over hundreds of jobs in a fraction of time and hear the practical lessons learned along the way. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater

abstract: Learn how ZS and AWS help pharma teams turn field insights into AI-powered intelligence. This presentation is brought to you by ZS, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: Graviton. Serverless. Apache Iceberg. Your guide to a modern data warehouse strategy
abstract: You need your data warehouse to be fast, open, and accessible to everyone on your team. This session shows you how to get there with Amazon Redshift. Take advantage of Graviton-powered RG instances for faster analytics at lower cost. Eliminate the complexity of managing infrastructure with Redshift Serverless. Query open data formats directly in your data lake with native Apache Iceberg support. And put insights in the hands of every team with natural language access. You'll also learn how multi-warehouse architectures let teams scale independently without duplicating data. Leave with a clear architecture strategy you can apply to your environment.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Raza Hafeez (Senior Product Manager Technical, Amazon Web Services)
Manikandan Paramasivan (Principal Architect - Data and ML/AI, KOHO Financial)
Divya Ananthanarayanan (Director Of Engineering, Amazon)

title: What's new in Amazon SageMaker platform
abstract: Amazon SageMaker platform is where data engineering, analytics, and AI come together. In this session, see what's new across the platform including innovations in lakehouse architecture that eliminates silos between data teams and AI teams, catalog capabilities for data discovery and governance, and streamlined development experiences that get you from raw data to production models faster. Whether you are building pipelines, running SQL analytics, or training models, learn how SageMaker platform delivers enterprise-grade governance with the flexibility to work the way your team needs.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Brian Ross (Head of Engineering: Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Web Services)
Shikha Verma (Head of Product - Data, Analytics, AI, AWS)
Derek Chau (Head of AI Center of Excellence, Cathay Pacific Airways)

title: Accelerate analytics and AI with an open lakehouse architecture on Apache Iceberg
abstract: Stop choosing between your data lake and data warehouse. Join this session to explore how to build a unified, open, and secure data lakehouse architecture, on Apache Iceberg. Learn how the lakehouse breaks down data silos and opens your data estate offering flexibility to use your preferred query engines and tools that accelerate time to insights. Learn about recent launches that improve data interoperability and performance, and enable large language models (LLMs) and AI agents to interact with your data. Discover robust security features, including consistent fine-grained access controls, attribute-based access control, and tag-based access control that help democratize data without compromises.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Brian Mitchell (Director, WW Data and Analytics, AWS)
Shruti Worlikar (Sr Mgr, Data & AI SA, Strategic Accounts, Amazon Web Services)

title: Real-time agentic architecture on AWS: from batch to real-time AI
abstract: Batch jobs and cron schedules fail silently and delay agentic AI outcomes: a missed run, a stuck lock, or a partial write goes unnoticed, adding lag between the moment an event occurs and the moment an agent responds. This advanced deep dive rethinks the architecture—loosely coupled services that deploy and fail independently, wired through events. We show how shifting transactional and analytical workloads to real-time, event-driven patterns fuels responsive agentic AI on AWS.
topics: amazon managed streaming for apache kafka (amazon msk)
speakers: Chinmayi Narasimhadevara (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Ankita Mishra (Senior Product Manager - Technical, Amazon)

title: What's new in AWS Data Processing
abstract: Explore the latest advancements in AWS Analytics designed to transform your data processing landscape. This session unveils powerful new capabilities across key services, including Amazon EMR for scalable big data processing, AWS Glue for seamless data integration, Amazon Athena for optimized querying, and Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA) for complex workflow orchestration. Discover how these innovations can supercharge performance, optimize costs, and streamline your entire data ecosystem. Whether you're looking to enhance scalability, improve data integration, accelerate queries, or refine workflow management, join us to gain actionable insights that will position your organization at the forefront of data processing innovation.

Anurag Singh (Engineering Manager, Netflix, Inc.)

title: Architect your metadata hub with AWS Glue Data Catalog
abstract: Your data is scattered across warehouses, lakes, databases, and streams. In this session, learn how AWS Glue Data Catalog serves as a single metadata hub that connects all of your data, enforces consistent governance across it, and makes it discoverable across engines and teams. See how to enrich, curate, and share metadata at scale, and give AI agents the context they need to get work done accurately and efficiently. Ideal for data engineers, architects, and platform teams.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Mihika Naik (Sr. PMT-ES, AWS)
Vidit Ochani (Principal Software Dev Eng, Amazon)

title: Accelerating data analytics on Apache Iceberg with Amazon S3 Tables
abstract: Every analytics query starts with how your data is stored. In this session, learn how Amazon S3 Tables deliver purpose-built Iceberg table storage that accelerates query performance, reduces storage costs, and eliminates table maintenance overhead. See how to pair S3 Tables with Athena, Redshift, and EMR to get faster results at lower cost, automate compaction and snapshot management, and simplify your lakehouse without changing your query engine or workflow.

title: Advanced Optimization & Cost-Saving Strategies for Amazon Athena
abstract: Dive deep into Amazon Athena's most powerful capabilities in this interactive chalk talk for experienced practitioners. We'll explore cost-saving techniques—CTAS for materializing expensive query results, partition projection to eliminate metadata lookups, and EXPLAIN-based tuning to minimize bytes scanned. Discuss workgroup budgets, provisioned capacity for predictable pricing, and query result reuse to avoid redundant scans. We'll cover Athena's latest innovations including Amazon S3 Tables integration for fully managed Iceberg tables and enhanced Spark notebooks.

Scott Rigney (Principal Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Data mesh on AWS: governance, identity, and end‑user attribution
abstract: Data mesh promises domain‑owned data as a product — but the hard part is governance: who can access what, and how you prove it after the fact. In this interactive chalk talk, we whiteboard two patterns for building a data mesh on AWS and debate when each one fits. The first is a centrally governed mesh using attribute‑based, fine‑grained access controls across separate producer, consumer, and governance accounts. The second is a peer‑to‑peer mesh where the producer directly approves each consumer's subscription. We'll follow a single data product through the AWS Glue Data Catalog from publication to subscription, wire enterprise identity (federated from your existing identity provider, such as Okta or Entra) all the way through to the query, and show how trusted identity propagation and end‑user attribution give you per‑user accountability you can audit end to end.
speakers: Mert Hocanin (Pr. Specialist Solution Architect - Analytics, Amazon Web Services)
Zach Mitchell (Sr. Big Data Architect, AWS)

abstract: Your telemetry is scattered across tools. Your storage costs keep climbing. Your AI agents are a black box. In this chalk talk, we'll tackle your problems head-on with Amazon OpenSearch Service. Bring your toughest scenarios. Ask how our purpose-built log analytics engine reduces cost while boosting query performance. Ask how to unify logs, traces, and metrics into a single OpenTelemetry-native pane of glass with cost efficiency. title: Build better agent retrieval with OpenSearch Service
abstract: Your AI agents and assistants are only as good as the answers they retrieve. Out-of-the-box frameworks get you started, but production-ready AI applications demand more from their search layer including higher relevance on complex queries, persistent memory across sessions, and tools the model can invoke reliably. Amazon OpenSearch Service delivers these capabilities natively. In this chalk talk, we dig into how to make OpenSearch Service the backbone of your AI agents and assistants, covering hybrid retrieval for better accuracy, MCP-based access to your data, and built-in conversation and long-term memory so your applications maintain context across interactions. Bring your architecture questions. Whether you're optimizing retrieval accuracy, adding persistent context, or connecting your agent to search via MCP, we work through it together and leave you with patterns you can apply.

title: Inside DuckDB and how AWS Analytics puts it to work
abstract: DuckDB has become one of the most talked-about innovations in analytics, and now the team behind it, DuckLabs, is part of AWS. In this session, dive deep into the architecture of DuckDB, the in-process analytical database that brings fast OLAP performance to laptops, serverless functions, and data pipelines. Learn how its vectorized execution engine, columnar storage, and zero-dependency design make it well suited for embedded analytics, local development, and edge processing. Explore real-world use cases, performance characteristics, and how DuckDB complements AWS analytics services, including Amazon S3, AWS Glue, Amazon Athena, and Amazon Redshift. Whether you're a data engineer, data scientist, or architect, gain the technical depth to put DuckDB to work.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: Your data, your engine: How open source and open standards power analytics on AWS
abstract: Open table formats and open-source engines like DuckDB give organizations the freedom to choose the right tool for each workload, from interactive dashboards and exploratory analytics to large-scale data processing, with no lock-in. In this session, learn how to capitalize these open tools to build on AWS and turn it into a competitive advantage for your business. We deep dive into the application of each engine, how they complement one another across the analytics lifecycle, and how data governance capabilities like catalog access, fine-grained governance, and consistent table management on AWS further simplify multi-engine architectures in production.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Ram Nottath (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Arun Shanmugam (Sr. Analytics SA, Amazon Web Services)

title: Cut your data lake and lakehouse bills: Cost and performance tuning best practices
abstract: Open data lakehouses and data lakes, built on open table formats such as Apache Iceberg, can quietly accumulate cost through uncompacted small files, over-partitioned tables, and inefficient scan patterns. In this session, learn advanced Iceberg cost savings and tuning techniques on AWS that cut storage and compute costs while improving performance. We cover partitioning strategies, predicate pushdown optimizations, compaction tradeoffs, Graviton efficiencies, Intelligent-Tiering storage and how to eliminate common anti-patterns that inflate your bill. Learn from practical examples on Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, Amazon EMR and leave with a comprehensive playbook to lower your analytics costs
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Red Theater

abstract: Delivering ROI for AI and ML at enterprise scale demands more than just great models — it requires a data and analytics foundation engineered for cost efficiency from day one. This session examines different cost efficiency levers that pair AWS data and analytics services with AI/ML workloads to maximize price-performance. We explore patterns including right-sizing your data infrastructure for training, inference, feature extraction, ETL pipelines and selecting optimal storage formats to minimize costs. You'll learn how to instrument cost observability across your analytics stack, apply tagging strategies for AI workload attribution, and implement governance guardrails that prevent runaway spend — turning your data foundation into a competitive advantage for ML and AI delivery.

abstract: AI agents are only as effective as the data they rely on. This chalk talk focuses on how to build and manage high-quality data products and contextual information for use by AI agents. You'll learn how to deliver accurate, up-to-date, and well-governed data for AI systems, including context engineering, RAG strategies, fine-tuning dataset curation, and automated quality checks. title: From human search to agent retrieval on OpenSearch Service
abstract: Agents don't search like humans. They fire hundreds of sub-queries per task, maintain stateful memory, and demand verified answers before acting. As organizations move agents into production, they hit the same walls: wrong retrieval cascades into wrong actions; without efficient memory, agents re-retrieve the same data, inflating cost and returning inconsistent results; and as agents become workloads of their own, teams need to keep them accountable. In this session, we show how Amazon OpenSearch Service addresses all three, find, remember, and observe, on one open engine, and how customers like Intuit are already running production AI agents on it.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Tia White (General Manager, OpenSearch, AWS)
Sohaib Katariwala (Sr. OpenSearch Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Archal Kumar (Director, Intuit)

We'll discuss the AWS performance-optimized runtime for Apache Spark—delivering up to 4.5x faster execution across Amazon EMR, Amazon Athena, and AWS Glue—meaning faster jobs and lower compute spend. Explore flexible deployment models—long-running clusters, on-demand elasticity with EMR Serverless, Kubernetes integration with EMR on EKS, and Graviton instances for up to 30% cost reduction. We'll also highlight how Glue's auto scaling, Flex execution class, and Iceberg integrations simplify pipelines while optimizing costs.
speakers: Kalyan Janaki (Senior STAM Big Data, Amazon Web Services)
Suthan Phillips (Sr. Analytics Architect, Amazon Web Services)

In this session, discover how Amazon MSK and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is making it easier and more affordable to build messaging and streaming applications at any scale. Learn how you can stop worrying about capacity planning and reduce costs automatically as your traffic scales up and down. See how you can land your streaming data directly into Amazon S3 and S3 Tables without building or managing separate pipelines so you can focus on deriving insights instead of maintaining infrastructure. Join us to see how these innovations come together to help you move faster, spend less, and eliminate operational overhead at any scale.

Learn which architecture fits your latency and cost requirements, how to keep Iceberg tables query-ready under continuous writes, and how these pipelines feed downstream analytics and AI workloads.
topics: amazon managed streaming for apache kafka (amazon msk)

title: What's new in AWS Glue Data Catalog for data and AI governance
abstract: Data spread across lakes, warehouses, and third-party platforms is hard to find, govern, and use. In this session, explore how AWS Glue Data Catalog embraces open standards and open table formats so your data stays portable and accessible across the tools and engines your teams already use. Learn how to discover and register data from a range of sources, govern and manage access from one place, and connect your catalog to Apache Iceberg-compatible engines, so you can avoid lock-in and keep the freedom to choose the right tool for each job. Ideal for data engineers, platform teams, and data architects building open, governed analytics across their data estate.

title: What's new with the Amazon SageMaker Data Agent
abstract: The Amazon SageMaker Data Agent helps data teams move from a plain-language request to results faster. In this session, learn how it helps you discover and understand your data, generate and run analysis, build and operationalize data workflows, and connect analytics work through to model development. See how it can take on the repetitive, time-consuming steps of data work so your team can focus on the questions that matter and the decisions that follow. Whether you're exploring a new dataset or building an end-to-end workflow, learn how the Data Agent brings governed, agentic development to every step of your data work.

title: What's new with Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
abstract: Organizations increasingly need to work with the same real-time data in different ways depending on the workload, and today that often means integrating services and building custom workarounds to make it fit. In this chalk talk, we head to the whiteboard to explore how Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is evolving to handle more of these patterns natively, so you can consolidate more of your real-time architecture onto one service. We work through how to design for the way your workload actually behaves, how scaling can adapt automatically as traffic rises and falls, and where teams can remove complexity and cost rather than adding another pipeline.

title: Cost-effective serverless data integrations and workflows for AI-ready data
abstract: AI is only as good as the data beneath it and building high-quality, well-integrated data products shouldn't break your budget. In this session, learn how to build cost-effective AI-ready datasets using AWS Glue, Amazon MWAA and Apache Iceberg. We'll show how Glue Data Quality and Glue serverless ETL, now with generative AI-assisted development, lets you ingest, transform, and prepare high-quality data at scale. We’ll demonstrate how Amazon MWAA serverless empowers a single DAG to coordinate workloads across AWS Glue, and other engines - all of this while paying only for what you use. Pairing this setup with Apache Iceberg further enhances your AI workloads with query-ready production data pipelines that move the needle without breaking the bank.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Sakti Mishra (Principal Data and AI Solutions Architect, Amazon.com Services, Inc.)
Raghuveer Reddy (Managing Director, Goldman Sachs)

title: Observe, investigate, act: smarter ops with Amazon OpenSearch Service
abstract: AI agents are becoming your best investigators, triaging alerts, correlating telemetry, and performing root-cause analysis across metrics, logs, and traces in seconds. And agents are a critical workload to observe: you need LLM trace monitoring, per-call cost attribution, and multi-agent workflow debugging to keep token spend and accuracy under control. Whether you're scaling an existing observability platform or modernizing your stack, Amazon OpenSearch Service addresses both sides. In this session, we present capabilities including native OpenTelemetry ingestion, MCP-based agent skills for natural-language issue investigation, and an optimized log-analytics engine delivering 4× price-performance at petabyte scale. Learn how to put AI agents to work on your observability data and how to keep them accountable in production.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater

Rohin Bhargava (Principal Product Manager Technical, AWS)

title: Introducing AWS Context: Build governed intelligence for agents at scale
abstract: AI agents need to understand what your data means, how it connects, and which definitions and rules apply to each use case. AWS Context automatically builds a governed knowledge graph by unifying structured and unstructured data, managed knowledge bases, and technical and business metadata from AWS and third-party sources. This shared foundation grounds agents in your organization’s data, business rules, relationships, and domain knowledge. In this session, dive into the reference architecture and learn best practices for integrating agents with AWS Context, including considerations for identity management, workload sizing, and production deployments.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Steve Ash (Senior Principal Engineer, Amazon AWS)
Aditya Krishnan (Director, AWS Agentic AI, Amazon Web Services)

title: Unlock Workday data with AWS: Building Trustworthy Agents (sponsored by Workday)
abstract: Generative AI agents and analytics in AWS are only as effective as the enterprise context behind them. While tools like Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Quick deliver powerful reasoning capabilities, grounding those models in authoritative, real-time HR and financial data traditionally requires complex ETL pipelines, custom integrations, and data duplication. In this session, we’ll demonstrate how Workday natively bridges this gap on AWS. Through live cross-system AI agent demos, you’ll see how to deliver unified, real-time enterprise insights without writing ETL code or moving data. This presentation is brought to you by Workday, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: Data governance for trustworthy AI: from raw data to trusted products
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, transform fictional retailer RetailMax's raw, ungoverned data into trusted, governed data products using Amazon SageMaker platform . Learn to build a business glossary and metadata forms, create an analysis-ready dataset with an ETL job, and trace end-to-end data lineage. Gain hands-on experience enforcing data quality rules, enriching and publishing a governed data product, and sharing it through a publish-and-subscribe model with approval workflows and least-privilege access. Discover how to deliver trustworthy, explainable answers with the Gen-AI data agent. Leave equipped to build the governance and metadata foundation that makes data — and the AI that runs on it — trustworthy across your organization. You must bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Jose Romero (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Kalyan Kumar Neelampudi (Sr Data & AI Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Reduce spend and data movement with Amazon Redshift Data Sharing and Graviton
abstract: Organizations sharing data across business units often rely on slow, error-prone ETL jobs that create costly duplication. Amazon Redshift Data Sharing enables secure, live access across provisioned and serverless warehouses — within or across accounts and regions — eliminating data movement entirely. Additionally, Graviton-powered Redshift RG instances accelerate workloads on Apache Iceberg tables through optimized columnar processing and parallel I/O. In this session, learn how to break down data silos with cross-warehouse data sharing and boost open data lakehouse performance with Redshift on Graviton.
speakers: Poulomi Dasgupta (Sr. Analytics Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Erika Nagamine (Sr. Specialist SA, Data & AI, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

abstract: AI agents generate SQL, surface insights, and take action on your data. Without governance guardrails, they hallucinate column meanings, query stale tables, and return wrong answers with high confidence. In this session, learn how to ground your AI agents in trusted metadata using AWS Glue Data Catalog. See how to flow business context like glossary terms, descriptions, and quality scores into agent workflows so they generate accurate, schema-aware queries instead of guessing. Walk away with practical patterns for governing AI-assisted analytics the same way you govern human analysts

title: From self-managed to AWS managed: agentic AI for Kafka and MQ migrations
abstract: Migrating self-managed Apache Kafka and RabbitMQ to Amazon MSK and Amazon MQ is hard. Topic mapping, offset translation, ACL migration, and the notoriously long cutover phase slow teams down for weeks. In this chalk talk, we walk through these challenges and show how agentic AI paired with AWS replication tooling compresses the longest migration phase from days to minutes. Watch a complete live migration executed end-to-end in under 60 minutes and leave with a repeatable playbook for your own migration.
topics: amazon managed streaming for apache kafka (amazon msk)
speakers: Mazrim Mehrtens (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Vignesh Selvam (Principal Product Manager - Technical (External Services), Amazon Web Services)

In this chalk talk, we explore how the AWS MCP Server paired with packaged AWS Analytics skills give agents like Claude Code, Kiro, and Cursor deep AWS service expertise — from SQL syntax and metadata discovery to migration planning and performance tuning. Bring your toughest questions — we'll cover setup, agent workflows, and best practices for your environments.
speakers: Avichay Marciano (Senior Analytics Specialist SA, Amazon)
Brandon Schur (Principal Database Engineer, AWS)

title: Simplify identity and security management in an open data architecture on AWS
abstract: As organizations unify data across Amazon S3 data lakes, S3 Tables, and Amazon Redshift using the open data lakehouse architecture, securing access at scale becomes critical. In this chalk talk, we dive deep into simplifying trusted identity propagation so end-user identities — not shared service roles — reach the data plane, designing multi-dimensional tag-based access control taxonomies that scale automatically through inheritance, enforcing column-level and cell-level security across federated catalogs, and auditing every access event to individual users.

Amir Bar-Or (Principal Engineer, Amazon)

title: Apache Iceberg V3 on AWS: Lower Costs, Better Lakehouse Performance
abstract: Apache Iceberg V3 is now production-ready, and adopting deletion vectors, row lineage, and new data types across your lakehouse requires careful planning. In this session, explore implementation patterns using Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, Amazon Athena, and Amazon S3 Tables. Learn when deletion vectors outperform copy-on-write, how row lineage enables compliance without extra pipelines, and how V3 incremental processing cuts batch costs. Leave with a practical migration strategy for your Iceberg upgrade.
speakers: Parul Saxena (Sr WW SSA Big Data, Amazon Web Services)
Sreeji Gopal (Sr. Solution Architect, Amazon)

title: Automating data pipelines with agentic AI and Apache Iceberg
abstract: Join this session to experience the power of agentic AI and Apache Iceberg coming together on AWS to build a self-correcting data pipeline. We will dive in to an agentic architecture for an Iceberg-based data pipeline - governed end-to-end through AWS Glue Data Catalog - where critical telemetry signals such as data loss, schema drift, cost spikes are not only detected and diagnosed but also remediated and verified - all in real time. title: Conversational AI to accelerate Apache Spark operations on Amazon EMR
abstract: Customers manage dozens of Apache Spark applications on Amazon EMR — and every major upgrade, unexpected failure, or performance regression pulls engineers away into reactive firefighting. In this workshop, experience a fundamentally different approach with AI-powered agents that handle the undifferentiated heavy lifting of Spark modernization and incident resolution. You'll work hands-on with conversational agents such as the Apache Spark Upgrade Agent and the Apache Spark Troubleshooting Agent across real-world scenarios on EMR Serverless and EMR on EC2 to simplify the operational burden through natural language, automated code transformation, workload analysis and data quality validation.

title: Build a grounded AI support assistant on Amazon OpenSearch Service
abstract: You want to build an AI assistant: where do you even start? A model alone is not the answer. The hard part is grounding it in your own data so it gives real answers, remembers the conversation, and holds up as that data grows, and grounding is a search problem. In this hands-on workshop, you build a customer support assistant grounded in Amazon OpenSearch Service. Starting from a pre-deployed base, you create an OpenSearch Serverless collection, add hybrid search for relevance, and add agentic memory so your assistant retains context across the conversation. You connect your tools and data with the OpenSearch MCP server, the AWS Knowledge MCP, and the AWS MCP. You leave with working code, an architecture that scales itself, and a clear path from a blank page to an assistant that answers from real data.
speakers: Arun Lakshmanan (Sr. WW SSA OpenSearch, AWS)
Gene Alpert (Analytics Specialist, AWS)

abstract: Transform your organization's data landscape and eliminate silos in this hands-on workshop with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Unify data management and design data interoperability across data lakes, data warehouses, and federated data sources. Through practical exercises, discover how to create a single source of truth while maintaining security and governance across your entire data estate. You'll implement real-time analytics, optimize query performance, and design scalable architectures. Perfect for data engineers, ML practitioners, and solution architects looking to modernize their data infrastructure for building agentic AI applications.

title: A practical guide to Apache Iceberg migration on AWS
abstract: Many organizations want to adopt Apache Iceberg but face a practical challenge: how do you migrate existing data lake tables — Hive-style, Apache Hudi, or Delta Lake — without disrupting production workloads? In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn and implement the full spectrum of migration techniques on AWS, from zero-copy in-place approaches to full data rewrites targeting both self-managed Iceberg tables in S3 and Amazon S3 Tables. Beyond the mechanics, you'll implement real-world migration strategies and learn how to choose among them based on downtime tolerance, writer constraints, and data volume. You'll leave with a repeatable playbook for migrating your data lake to Iceberg with minimal risk and zero data loss.
speakers: Stefano Sandonà (Big Data Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Salim Tutuncu (Sr. Specialist PSA, Data & AI, Amazon Web Services)

abstract: Enterprise data teams have distributed data catalogs across multiple cloud providers, each with partial visibility and no shared query surface. This hands-on workshop demonstrates how catalog federation unifies cross-cloud data silos into an open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Using Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation with Apache Iceberg as the open, engine-neutral table format for seamless interoperability and zero data duplication across AWS, Snowflake, and Databricks, you'll federate remote catalogs to build a unified lakehouse on AWS to run AI-assisted business analytics.
speakers: Shubham Purwar (Analytics Specialist Solution Architect, AWS)
Nidhi Nayak (Senior Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Power streaming analytics on AWS with AI-driven insights
abstract: Learn how to build a modern, streaming analytics solution for real-time data processing and power it with agentic AI capabilities to analyze events and extract patterns for actionable responses. This session will provide a hands-on experience on building a streaming solution using Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka for real-time data ingestion, using Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink for complex event processing, and Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock Agent Core to take immediate action. Further evolve this solution to demonstrate the integration with Amazon S3 Tables for deeper analysis.

title: Ground your agents with AWS Context and Amazon SageMaker
abstract: Agents are only as good as the context they're given. In this session, see how AWS Context makes the agentic experience in Amazon SageMaker more accurate and useful by grounding agents in business metadata. We'll show how context-aware agents like SageMaker Data Agent break complex requests into structured, multi-step plans, generate validated SQL, Python, and PySpark against your real data, and keep humans in the loop with built-in checkpoints. You'll learn practical techniques to feed the right context to your agents, connect additional sources, and turn a capable assistant into one that truly understands your environment.
speakers: Hari Thatavarthy (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Sandeep Adwankar (Sr. Product Manager, Amazon)

title: Accelerating Apache Spark 4.1 workloads with AWS Analytics
abstract: Apache Spark 4.1 is the latest engine upgrade, and AWS is the best place to run it. Learn best practices for building high-performing Spark 4.1 applications using Amazon EMR. Explore what's new, from the ANSI-compliant type system and Variant data type to Spark Connect and Python-first APIs, and how the AWS performance-optimized runtime amplifies these improvements at scale. See how the Spark Troubleshooting and Upgrade agent accelerates migration by automatically identifying deprecated APIs and recommending code fixes, and how AWS Glue and Apache Iceberg integrations simplify pipelines with open table formats.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Sekar Srinivasan (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Giovanni Matteo Fumarola (Sr. Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Simplify Data Analytics operations with AI-powered Apache Spark agents on AWS
abstract: Running analytics workloads at scale carries a hidden operational tax: teams commonly lose significant engineering time to debugging failures, leave performance and cost improvements on the table, and spend months on each version upgrade. In this talk, we walk through a family of AI-powered agents for AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, and Amazon Athena. The Spark Troubleshooting Agent finds the root cause of a failure and recommends the code or config fix - cutting debugging time from hours to minutes. The Spark Upgrade Agent plans an upgrade, transforms the code, and validates both runtime and data quality - turning months into hours. We share what worked in production for both agents - the design choices, failure modes, and validation strategies that made them reliable - and distill lessons that generalize to any team applying LLMs to complex infrastructure.
speakers: David Zhang (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Mohit Saxena (Senior Manager, AWS Data Analytics & Agentic Applications, Amazon Web Services)

title: Trace Lineage From AI Endpoints and Models to Data
abstract: Every number in a dashboard and every answer from an AI agent rests on a chain of data you may not be able to see. Can you prove where it came from? In this chalk talk, we whiteboard one lineage graph connecting endpoints, models, jobs, and tables across your pipelines on Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon Athena, anchored on the AWS Glue Data Catalog. We trace a production number back to the tables that fed it, work out what breaks before a schema change ships, and have an AI agent show the provenance of its own answer.
speakers: Nishchai JM (Sr Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Building a semantic layer with AWS Glue Data Catalog and AWS Context
abstract: In this chalk talk, we dive into how AWS Context assembles semantic data from multiple semantic stores to create a semantic layer, which is then turned into a unified context layer through a knowledge graph. This enables AI agents and analytics engines to understand business meaning, relationships, and intent — not just schema and location. We'll work through architecture patterns for defining semantic data annotations, propagating semantics across lakehouse tables, and exposing discoverable, agent-ready metadata at query time.
speakers: Syed Humair (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect (Analytics), Amazon Web Services (AWS))
Varshni Muralidharan (Product Manager - Technical, Amazon Web Services)

title: Design an open, cost-effective and high-performant lakehouse with Apache Iceberg on
abstract: What does it take to build a lakehouse that's open, fast, and cost-effective? In this chalk talk, we unpack real architectural decisions behind Apache Iceberg on AWS—from Amazon S3 Tables (delivering up to 3x faster queries and 10x higher TPS) to unified metadata management with the AWS Glue Data Catalog across Athena, EMR, and Glue ETL. Bring your questions as we whiteboard trade-offs around schema evolution, ACID transactions, time-travel queries, and avoiding vendor lock-in. Leave with actionable patterns tailored to your workload.
speakers: Radhika Jakkula (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect - Analytics, Amazon Web Services)
Saman Irfan (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Best practices for operating an Apache Iceberg lakehouse at scale
abstract: Operating an Iceberg lakehouse at scale means taming the operational overhead that grows with your data. In this chalk talk, we dive into table maintenance strategies—compaction, snapshot expiration, and orphan file cleanup—and discuss how Amazon S3 Tables automates these tasks. We'll whiteboard patterns for metadata management with AWS Glue Data Catalog, storage cost optimization through lifecycle-aware file pruning, and partition evolution without rewriting data. You will leave with battle-tested operational patterns for production Iceberg workloads.
speakers: Aditya Challa (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Priyanka Chaudhary (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Govern your context layer for AI agents with AWS Context
abstract: Learn how to carry your existing data permissions into a governed context layer your AI agents need to work accurately across structured and unstructured data. AWS Context assembles semantic data from your catalogs, glossaries, query logs, and access patterns into one governed context layer, honoring the governance contract placed on your data assets. Each user's identity flows through the agent so every answer is scoped to what they are authorized to see. We will whiteboard and interact on how identity propagates, how retrieval is filtered, and where permissions break.
speakers: Leonardo Gomez Virahonda (Principal Big Data Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Event-driven agents at scale: building agentic AI on Amazon MSK
abstract: Production agents need to dispatch long-running actions, wait on external systems, fan results out to analytics, and re-enter the conversation when work finishes — not sit in a synchronous loop. In this session, we present reusable patterns for building multi-tenant, event-driven agentic systems on Amazon MSK: dispatch-and-resume for long-running tool calls, topic and partition design keyed to tenant and conversation, decoupling the agent loop from channels and analytics, and durability and replay so in-flight work survives deploys and retries. Learn a practical approach for designing agentic SaaS that stays reliable as load, tools, and channels grow.
topics: amazon managed streaming for apache kafka (amazon msk)
speakers: Luca Perrozzi (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS)
Masudur Rahaman Sayem (Sr. WW SSA Streaming, AWS)

title: Powering your agentic AI experience with AWS streaming and messaging
abstract: Organizations are accelerating innovation with generative and agentic AI—and getting there depends on a handful of real-time data primitives: durable, high-throughput ingestion; stream processing and enrichment; low-latency, event-driven delivery; and a scalable place to land and serve data. In this session, learn how these primitives come together to power the real-time patterns behind agentic AI—and where each one fits: streaming into a real-time semantic layer for fresh retrieval context, event-driven agent invocation so agents act the instant something happens, and continuously sourcing agentic data stores with live data. We'll show how to satisfy each primitive—spanning multi-Region resilience, seamless migration off self-managed infrastructure, direct landing into open table formats and object storage, and simplified networking
topics: amazon managed streaming for apache kafka (amazon msk)
speakers: Sarang Bapat (Director Data & AI Engineering, United Airlines)
John Morkel (Director, Streaming and Messaging Services, Amazon Web Services)

abstract: Apache Iceberg Materialized Views on AWS store pre-computed query results as Iceberg tables on Amazon S3 or Amazon S3 Tables. Join this hands-on session to experience how Apache Iceberg Materialized Views on AWS simplify medallion architectures, lakehouse migrations, accelerate BI query transactions and complex joins.

title: Give your AI agents business context with AWS Glue Data Catalog
abstract: An AI agent pointed at a data catalog that has schema but no meaning will guess — and in a regulated environment, guessing is a compliance liability. In this builders' session, learn how to turn the AWS Glue Data Catalog into a trust layer for AI agents. Enrich the catalog with business context — Skill Assets, golden queries, business glossary terms, ownership, and access restrictions — then connect an MCP-compatible AI agent and watch its answers shift from hallucination to governed, data-literate reasoning. Use semantic search to discover data by business meaning, add queryable metadata forms at scale, and leave with architecture patterns to roll this out across your existing catalog. title: Build a well-governed natural language-to-SQL agentic solution for Amazon Redshift
abstract: The Amazon Redshift MCP Server enables AI agents to generate and execute SQL using natural language, but going from demo to production means answering critical security questions on preventing query hallucination, prompt injection, unbounded scans, and inadvertent PII exposure by the LLM. In this session, you will build a well-governed text-to-SQL agentic solution for Amazon Redshift with security gates that validate every AI-generated query before execution including schema allow-listing to constraining LLM context, authorized tables, columns and rows, SQL AST validation and enforced read-only access.

title: Make your vector search faster, more relevant, and cost-efficient
abstract: You have a vector workload running and questions piling up: How do I raise relevance? How do I control cost as I scale? Which ranking technique fits my data? We give you a quick tour of vector capabilities in Amazon OpenSearch Service, then spend the rest of the session working through your problems. Topics on the table include hybrid search combining lexical and vector results, ranking with reciprocal rank fusion, maximal marginal relevance, and filtering strategies, when to reach for Automatic Semantic Enrichment or neural sparse vectors instead of building your own embedding pipeline, and cost optimization techniques including quantization, tiered storage, GPU-accelerated indexing, and auto-optimization. Come with a workload in mind and leave with tuning direction for your specific situation.
speakers: Hajer Bouafif (Sr. Solutions Architect - OpenSearch, AWS)
prasadnu Mohan Prasad (Sr OpenSearch Specialist SA, AWS)

title: Build orchestration agents for AWS Glue ETL
abstract: What happens when you give an AI agent the keys to your ETL infrastructure? In this builder session, you'll build an agentic workflow using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that accepts natural language instructions and autonomously orchestrates ETL jobs on AWS Glue. Using MCP servers, your agent will reason job configurations, construct parameters, execute transformations, interact with the Glue Data Catalog, handle retries on failure, and surface results—all from a single conversational prompt.

abstract: Stop copying data just to query it. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use MCP server integration with Amazon Athena for fast conversational analytics where agents translate natural language to federated SQL queries across custom databases and a multi-vendor data store – without moving or copying data. You’ll learn how federated queries eliminate complex ETL pipelines, enable cross-source joins in a single SQL statement, and integrate with your lakehouse on AWS for unified governance.

Through guided exercises, implement critical features including fan-out architectures, FIFO queues, and hybrid patterns while optimizing for security, cost, and performance. Gain practical insights into how architectural decisions impact scalability, latency, and operational complexity in production systems.

abstract: Organizations need an operating layer where humans and agents can run critical workflows together. That’s Asana. As software development shifts toward work performed by agents in the cloud, engineering teams need the same connected approach at enterprise scale. Command brings Asana’s operating layer to engineering, giving developers one surface for project management and coding work—connecting planning, assignment, and execution across the organization. Command works with coding agents teams already use, including Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. See the challenges Command solves for product and engineering teams and how it works against real engineering workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Asana, an AWS Partner.

abstract: Join us to learn how to plan and automate your application modernization using agentic tools. We show how to reverse-engineer your applications and dependencies from existing code, then generate a event-driven cloud native target architecture. See how teams move from monoliths to event-driven microservices, deployed as containers or serverless applications, in weeks, and make your applications agent-ready in the process.
