title: Bring Oracle Databases to AWS Without Starting Over (sponsored by Oracle)
abstract: Organizations want the flexibility and innovation of AWS, but they cannot afford to rearchitect the mission-critical Oracle Database applications their businesses depend on. This session explains how Oracle AI Database@AWS provides a simpler path from on-premises Oracle Exadata and RAC environments to AWS with minimal to no database or application changes. Explore how customers can maintain full database capabilities and architectural compatibility, connect Oracle data to AWS applications with low latency, and unify data with AWS analytics, machine learning, and agentic AI services. We will also examine the operational value of familiar AWS tools, collaborative support, integrated security, and simplified purchasing. Attendees will learn how migration can reduce infrastructure constraints while creating a stronger foundation for innovation across Oracle and AWS. abstract: Scaling event-driven architectures across multiple AWS accounts has long meant managing fragmented buses, cross-account routing complexity, and developer friction. Whether you're consolidating existing event infrastructure or designing a new event-driven platform, you'll leave with a clearer picture of how to reduce operational complexity and ship faster.

Discover how durable functions simplify complex workflow orchestration by checkpointing progress, automatically recovering from failures, and pausing execution while waiting on long-running tasks—all without managing additional infrastructure or writing custom state management code. Discover how durable functions simplify complex workflow orchestration by checkpointing progress, automatically recovering from failures, and pausing execution while waiting on long-running tasks—all without managing additional infrastructure or writing custom state management code. Bring existing producers onboard by publishing events in open formats, configure Subscribers for each application independently to receive only the events it needs, recover from missed events with point-in-time replay, and keep related events in sequence with ordered delivery. title: Routing events at scale with Amazon EventBridge
abstract: Amazon EventBridge simplifies event routing for distributed applications. In this chalk talk, we show how to centralize multi-account event routing without custom infrastructure, using the enhanced custom event bus. We will discuss routing policies, event discovery with schema registry, and access controls that let platform teams govern while app teams move independently. We also explore rate limiting and backpressure so your applications gracefully handle traffic spikes and protect downstream systems without losing events. Along the way, we highlight new multi-account patterns the enhanced custom event bus enables.
speakers: Patrick Meiler (Solutions Architect, AWS)
David Roberts (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Amazon API Gateway: Migration strategies and agent-ready APIs
abstract: Unlock the full potential of Amazon API Gateway for modern workloads. In this chalk talk, we discuss migration strategies from legacy API platforms using OpenAPI extensions, schema validation, and Infrastructure as Code. Then we tackle the agentic era: how do you design APIs that AI agents can discover, authenticate against, and call reliably? We explore custom authorizers, mutual TLS, and exposing your endpoints as MCP-compatible tool definitions. Bring your questions—we'll work through them on the whiteboard.

Ronan Prenty (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

Working in small groups, you'll implement error handling, human approval gates, and cost controls for AI-powered pipelines. Walk away with reusable patterns for production-ready GenAI workflows. title: How event driven architectures go wrong and how to fix them
abstract: Event-driven architectures promise decoupling and scalability, but production systems reveal hard-won lessons. In this chalk talk, we dissect the most expensive anti-patterns teams encounter such as unbounded fan-out, missing dead-letter queues, chatty event schemas that drive up costs, and orchestration gaps that silently drop work. We whiteboard fixes using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Step Functions, and proven enterprise integration patterns, then walk through designs that keep event-driven systems reliable, cost-effective, and observable at scale.
speakers: Deepali Tandale (Migration & Modernization Solutions Architect, AWS)
Matthew Meckes (Principal Containers Specialist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Building event-driven, multi-agent swarms on serverless
abstract: Multi-agent AI systems need communication that is decoupled, observable, and scalable. In this chalk talk, we show how to coordinate swarms of independent agents through event choreography on Amazon EventBridge. Each agent reacts to events and emits new ones rather than being told what to do by a central controller. We discuss how to handle multi-agent failure modes like cascading hallucinations and runaway event loops (circular delegation), and how to prevent independent agents from taking conflicting actions.
speakers: Alexander Günsche (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Ben Freiberg (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Reliable data processing with AWS serverless services
abstract: In this chalk talk, learn how to optimize your serverless data processing workflows at scale. We cover AWS Step Functions Distributed Map for massive parallel batch processing and AWS Lambda durable functions for durable execution workflows. See how to combine these with Lambda event source mappings for stream and queue processing. We discuss cost optimization strategies and when to choose each approach for your data workload.
speakers: Ash Naik (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon/AWS)
Elizabeth Davis (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: A closer look at AWS Lambda durable functions
abstract: Lambda durable functions let you write reliable, long-running workflows as sequential code. We start with how durable execution works: checkpointing, replay-based recovery, and the programming model. Next, we explore production patterns including sagas, fan-out/fan-in, and human-in-the-loop waits. Finally, we cover observability, a decision framework to help you choose when to use durable functions versus AWS Step Functions, and operational considerations like concurrency, cost, and versioning.
speakers: Eric Johnson (Principal Developer Advocate, Amazon)

title: Coding high-throughput data pipelines with AWS Lambda durable functions
abstract: Processing large datasets usually means hand-wiring queues, coordinators, and state tracking. In this code talk, we live-build a high-throughput data pipeline with Lambda durable functions instead. You'll see the fan-out/fan-in pattern in code: split a large dataset across parallel durable executions, isolate and retry the branches that fail without reprocessing the ones that succeeded, and offload checkpoints to S3 so a job too big for a single invocation survives restarts. We'll tune concurrency to protect a downstream database from overload, then compare the durable-functions approach with other design patterns on both developer velocity and cost. Leave with patterns you can apply to your own data workloads immediately.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Tom Romano (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Matt Kahn (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Coding an AI agent from scratch with AWS Lambda durable functions
abstract: AI agents need multi-step reasoning, tool execution, human approvals, and long-running waits, all while keeping resilient state across failures. In this code talk, we build an AI agent from scratch using Lambda Durable Functions. You'll see how to implement a tool-use loop, add retries with exponential backoff, pause for human approval without paying for idle time, and recover cleanly from a mid-execution failure. We'll experiment with agent suspend and resume live, and watch it resume from a checkpoint deterministically. Leave with production-ready patterns for building stateful AI agents using familiar programming constructs.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Serda Kasaci Yildirim (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Rana Kiziltoprak German (Senior Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Coding event-driven retry patterns that prevent outages
abstract: In this code talk, you'll instrument an event-driven integration layer with the patterns that contain failure: exponential backoff with jitter, circuit breakers, poison-pill isolation, and replay-from-archive - all live, in code. See how jittered retries prevent thundering herds, how circuit breakers protect healthy services from impaired ones, and how idempotency makes every replay safe. By the end, you'll have hands-on patterns for EventBridge and Step Functions that shrink your blast radius from total outage to graceful degradation.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Dirk Fröhner (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Patrick Meiler (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Composing the right orchestration for serverless workflows
abstract: Both AWS Lambda durable functions and AWS Step Functions handle retries, long-running execution, and failure recovery - so how do you choose? In this session, we cut through the confusion with a clear decision framework across three scenarios: human-in-the-loop approvals, long-running AI agent workflows, and multi-service sagas. We'll also show a hybrid pattern where Durable Functions handle inner business logic while Step Functions orchestrate at the macro level - code-level flexibility inside, visual observability outside. Leave with a practical framework and a real production example to guide your next serverless workflow decision.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater

abstract: Production AI agents need orchestration that handles non-deterministic behavior, multi-hour workflows, human approvals, and multi-agent coordination. Learn how AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda durable functions provide the reliability layer that agents demand. We cover patterns for durable execution, human-in-the-loop controls, event-driven agent communication, and the scale-to-zero economics that make serverless the natural home for agentic workloads.

abstract: In this builders' session, transform a batch-oriented data processing pipeline into a real-time, event-driven architecture using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and AWS Step Functions. Working hands-on in small groups, you'll decompose a monolithic batch process into discrete event-driven steps, implement file-processing triggers, and design fan-out patterns for parallel execution. Learn when to keep batch and when to go event-driven, and leave with a working modernization pattern. You must bring your laptop to participate.

Learn how the patterns you already know, such as queues, events, and retries, evolve when your consumers are autonomous agents rather than just microservices.

title: Duck, Duck, Iceberg: Query Your Lake From Your Laptop (sponsored by Fivetran)
abstract: Vendor lock-in and rigid compute options prevent data teams from scaling efficiently, especially with AI agents added to the mix - Apache Iceberg fixes this. Join this session to see how a Fivetran Managed Data Lake automatically ingests data from your sources to open formats and also handles the table maintenance without manual overhead. Your data in your S3 bucket under your ownership. But landing data is just half the story though so we’ll also demonstrate querying the exact same dataset across multiple compute engines to show how open formats let you pair every workload with its ideal cost and performance profile. This presentation is brought to you by Fivetran, an AWS Partner.

title: Where do agents fit? A capability-first approach to agentic AI
abstract: Not every workflow needs an agent, and forcing agentic AI where it doesn't fit adds nondeterminism, cost, and failure modes a deterministic design would have avoided. This chalk talk introduces a capability-first methodology for architects and engineering leaders evaluating agentic paths in their workflows, manual or software-driven. At its core is the scoring framework that scores the inherent nature of the work across key dimensions to reveal where agents genuinely fit. You'll walk away with a repeatable rubric your teams can adopt immediately to decide whether agency is required in your workflows.
speakers: Mukund Rao (WW BCAP PSA, Amazon Web Services)
Sushanth Mangalore (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: What SOA taught us about building agents in production
abstract: You’ve taken AI agents from prototype to production, and now you own the hard parts: orchestration sprawl, brittle integrations, and behavior hard to test or observe. The patterns that hold up in production look a lot like ones SOA builders already know. This session explores what emerged: multi-agent orchestration mirroring service meshes, tool-use protocols (MCP) formalizing what APIs did for services, evaluation frameworks echoing contract testing, and hard-won lessons about agent observability and trust boundaries. You leave with concrete patterns from the SOA playbook, updated for the agentic era.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Andrew Baird (Sr. Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Architectural patterns for predictable multi-agent costs at scale
abstract: Agents consume several times more tokens than chat interactions, and multi-agent coordination pushes that higher. Monitoring alone isn't enough to manage costs, token economics must be considered when building agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architectural patterns that improve token economics for multi-agent applications, covering orchestration design decisions (orchestrator-subagent, generator-verifier, shared state) and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's temporal policies and cost optimization features improve cost-determinism. We'll illustrate these patterns with practical examples, then open the whiteboard for attendees to share their challenges and solutions.
speakers: Ayushi Goyal (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Aran Singh (UKI Startup Sales Leader, Amazon Web Services)

title: Keeping Your Lakehouse Fast: Optimization Methods for Performance & Cost (sponsored by Cloudera)
abstract: A common challenge with large-scale Apache Iceberg tables is keeping performance and costs under control as use and volumes grow. Optimizing tables is the solution, but it’s a tough problem to solve. As data volumes grow, querying effectively requires deliberate tuning and optimization strategies. Streaming ingestion, small files, delete files, aging metadata can gradually increase query latency and costs. In this session, you’ll learn the core optimization techniques that every Iceberg developer should understand, including partitioning, compaction, clustering, cleaning, and data skipping. You'll also learn how these techniques improve query planning and when to apply them. At the end of the session, you’ll see how these best practices can be automated using Cloudera Lakehouse Optimizer to improve performance and reduce costs. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Dipankar Mazumdar (Director, Data/AI Developers, Cloudera, Inc.)

By unifying simulation, data processing, and AI-driven research workflows, Pacific Fusion can accelerate scientific discovery while optimizing cost and resource utilization. Discover how AWS elasticity and AMD EPYC performance enable researchers to rapidly scale from compute-intensive simulations to data-rich analytics and intelligent automation, helping transform scientific data into actionable insights and accelerating the path toward commercially viable fusion energy. title: Build deeper into AWS with a traffic layer you own (sponsored by HAProxy Technologies)
abstract: Most teams on AWS accumulate separate systems for load balancing, WAF, bot management, rate limiting, and Kubernetes routing. Each brings its own config model and failure domain, another hop in the request path, and a configuration that does not travel. This session makes the case for one layer, on Graviton, benchmarked at over 2 million HTTPS requests per second, with no traffic leaving your VPC for inspection, managed and observed from one control plane. Because that layer runs unchanged in every environment you add, it becomes the one part of your architecture that never has to move. This presentation is brought to you by HAProxy Technologies, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Eric Martinson (Solutions Engineer, HAProxy Technologies)
Nathan Wehrman (Sr. Systems Engineer, HAProxy Technologies)

Hear how LSEG modernized a 7,500-system estate supporting 120 million financial instruments, achieved sub-4ms latency targets, and accelerated its cloud-native transformation. Discover how customers are improving price-performance, lowering infrastructure costs by more than 30%, and creating a scalable foundation for AI, analytics, and mission-critical workloads. Mike Thompson (Director - Cloud Product, AMD)

abstract: Real-time data loses value when it gets stuck in pipelines. In this session, learn how Confluent, IBM and AWS are helping make streaming data immediately usable for analytics and AI. See how Confluent Tableflow turns Kafka topics into Apache Iceberg tables and registers them in the AWS Glue Data Catalog—eliminating the need for custom streaming pipelines. Discover how this integration enables data engineers to reduce ingestion complexity, strengthen governance and put real-time data to work for analytics and AI with Amazon Athena. This presentation is brought to you by Confluent, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater

abstract: Today's organizations need infrastructure that can efficiently support everything from mission-critical databases to next-generation AI applications. Join AMD and AWS to explore how customers are leveraging Amazon EC2 instances powered by AMD EPYC processors across Amazon RDS, analytics, Agentic AI, HPC, and cloud-native applications. Learn how AMD-powered AWS infrastructure delivers compelling price-performance, scalability, and operational efficiency while helping organizations accelerate innovation, optimize costs, and meet growing compute demands. title: Rethinking the boundary between messaging and streaming
abstract: Modern event-driven architectures still separate cleanly into "queues" and "streams," but real workloads no longer do. Requirements like replay, ordering, high throughput and more, increasingly appear across both patterns, making the wrong service choice costly to unwind. This session explores the architectural spectrum across messaging and streaming systems, drawing on services such as Amazon SQS, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon MSK. Throughout the talk we will build a real world architecture and will provide guidance when to choose messaging, streaming or a hybrid approach, and which trade-offs matter most.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Stephan Schiller (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Building multi-tenant RAG: Isolation, cost, and scale
abstract: Customers building multi-tenant RAG platforms must balance tenant data isolation, cost, and operational scale. This chalk talk examines a production architecture serving thousands of tenants on Amazon Bedrock and compares multiple approaches. We whiteboard isolation patterns, tenant routing, per-knowledge-base scaling and limits, managed embedding models, and multimodal document parsing. We will discuss the tradeoffs that determine when to build your own retrieval stack and when to use a fully managed knowledge base.
speakers: Aakash Upadhyay (Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Hans Nesbitt (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Building multi-tenant RAG: Isolation, cost, and scale
abstract: Customers building multi-tenant RAG platforms must balance tenant data isolation, cost, and operational scale. This chalk talk examines a production architecture serving thousands of tenants on Amazon Bedrock and compares multiple approaches. We whiteboard isolation patterns, tenant routing, per-knowledge-base scaling and limits, managed embedding models, and multimodal document parsing. We will discuss the tradeoffs that determine when to build your own retrieval stack and when to use a fully managed knowledge base.
speakers: Aakash Upadhyay (Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Hans Nesbitt (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: One agent to thousands: Building for scale with Newforma
abstract: When every team builds agents independently, you get the same ungovernable sprawl that drove the shift from artisanal EC2 to container platforms. Agents are non-deterministic workloads that require deterministic governance, and this tension drives every platform decision, from dual orchestration for known vs. emergent topologies, to policy-based boundaries around soft reasoning, to defense layers that compose without coupling. We walk through how Newforma operationalized this architecture on AWS, and attendees leave understanding how to layer orchestration, policy, and defense into an enterprise agent platform that scales safely.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Benjamin Bazso (Chief Technology Officer, Newforma, Inc.)
Mahesh Biradar (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Vikrant Dhir (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: The cost of over-engineering: When your architecture fights you
abstract: Not every workload needs microservices, event-driven patterns, or serverless. Over-decomposed architectures create distributed monoliths, event spaghetti, and operational nightmares that cost more and move slower than the monolith they replaced. In this chalk talk, examine real-world anti-patterns: services split too small, queues added without purpose, and abstractions that add latency without value. We’ll whiteboard decision frameworks for right-sizing architecture, including the signals that tell you when decomposition earns its complexity and when it doesn’t. Bring your diagrams and discuss where simplification improves speed, reduces cost, and strengthens reliability. Leave able to right-size your own architecture with confidence.
speakers: Aman Raj (Big Data Consultant, Amazon Web Services)
Nitin Kumar (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Architecting for non-deterministic components
abstract: Our systems used to behave the same way every time. Now we give them judgment and agency, so they decide and act on their own, and the same inputs can produce different outcomes. Designing reliable architectures around that non-determinism comes down to three questions: where to enforce determinism around the model, when to verify behavior through automated evaluation and reasoning versus human judgment, and how to adapt the patterns (event flows, orchestration, automation) for components that don’t behave predictably. This session presents the design patterns for building systems that decide and act, while preserving the reliability your architecture depends on.
speakers: Kunle Adeleke (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
John Walker (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Find failure modes faster: AI-powered resilience assessments
abstract: Manual resilience reviews are slow, inconsistent, and routinely miss failure modes that don't surface until an incident occurs. In this workshop, you'll use the generative AI-driven assessment engine in AWS Resilience Hub to automatically discover dependencies across AWS services, internal endpoints, and third-party systems. You'll evaluate workloads against the Well-Architected Framework and your own defined resilience policies including availability SLOs, RTO, and RPO targets, then receive prioritized, actionable recommendations tied to business impact. Working with a reference architecture, you'll build a complete end-to-end assessment and leave with a repeatable framework you can run against any workload as your architecture evolves. Bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Matt Lanza (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Ricardo Piqueras Bonet (Senior Well-Architected Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Queue-based decoupling trade-offs for event-driven workloads
abstract: Every decoupling pattern makes trade-offs, and the right one depends on your workload's constraints. In this session, you work through scenarios with competing demands: exactly-once processing, tenant isolation, back pressure, and ordering. Using SQS and Lambda, you configure queue types and concurrency controls, tune batching behavior, and observe how your consumer scales under each configuration. Each scenario forces a trade-off between throughput, ordering, isolation, and cost. You leave knowing which trade-offs to accept for your workload and why. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Michael Orman (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
NS Sabah (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
John Lee (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Bailey (Sohyeon) Cho (Solutions Architect, GenAI Startups, Amazon Web Services)
Justin McGinnity (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Break it to prove It: Fault-isolated architecture built to recover
abstract: Your recovery plan is only as good as the architecture backing it. This workshop presents single-Region and multi-Region resilience patterns built along fault isolation boundaries, where failure scope dictates which recovery mechanism to engage. Using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC), you architect for discrete blast radii, then validate each boundary through fault injection with AWS Fault Injection Service. Observability surfaces the failure, alarms classify scope, and automated recovery executes without intervention. The result: proof that your architecture recovers the way you designed it to. Bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Serafin Sedano Arenas (Principal Engineer, AWS)
Shivani Sharma (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Well-Architected in your AI coding agent: Find gaps before you commit
abstract: Architecture reviews happen at milestones: a design review here, an operational readiness check there. But AI coding agents make architectural decisions dozens of times a day, and governance that runs at milestone pace can't keep up. In this session, you will configure open-source Well-Architected skills in your coding agent, run a full Well-Architected review and catch resilience, security, and operational gaps in minutes. Then author a custom skill that encodes your team's standards and trade-offs. You leave with a review loop that runs every commit. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

Swapnil Singh (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: When agents disagree: Resolving competing goals in cloud operations
abstract: When two agents manage the same workload, each optimizing a different objective, conflicting actions are the default, not the exception. A consensus layer changes the pattern: pillar-aligned agents carry workload goals and live signals as context, reason toward agreement, and produce a single decision playbook before any action executes. In this session, you build one pillar agent from scratch, configure its context layer, connect it to the consensus flow, and watch shared context resolve a live disagreement without rules or priority overrides. Bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Asal Shams (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Storm Manterola Guijt (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Multi-agent AI: Orchestration and choreography, compared
abstract: Every multi-agent AI system needs a coordination layer. The hard question is who decides what happens next: a central orchestrator or the agents themselves. In this session, you deploy the same five-agent travel booking pipeline through both orchestration (Step Functions) and choreography (EventBridge). Run identical load tests, inject the same failures, and add a sixth agent to each. Measure blast radius, extensibility cost, and debugging speed to see where the two approaches diverge. Leave knowing when to orchestrate, when to choreograph, and how to combine both in one architecture. Bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Dimple Dhar (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Archana Ambavane (Sr Solution Architect, AWS)

title: Red, green, re-architect: Test-driven infrastructure
abstract: AI can write your infrastructure in seconds — but did it build what you asked for? In this workshop, you'll apply test-driven development to AI-generated infrastructure. Describe your architecture in plain English, then use Kiro's spec-driven development to decompose it into discrete, testable behaviors. Kiro iterates through each one: writing a failing CDK assertion that encodes it (red), generating minimal infrastructure to pass it (green), then advancing to the next. Once green, refactor toward production readiness using cdk-nag rule packs to enforce Well-Architected practices. Leave with meaningful test coverage and a repeatable pattern for raising your organization's infrastructure coding standards. Bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Aoife Egan (Well-Architected Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))
Sanket Nasre (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc.)

title: Architect resilient agentic systems: Patterns beyond the happy path
abstract: Every agentic system works on the happy path. The real test is what happens when your AI agent times out mid-reasoning, returns a malformed action, or cascades a single failure across an entire chain. In this session, you implement four resilience patterns built for non-deterministic agents: circuit breakers that trip on semantic failure, fallback hierarchies from AI to rules to human, bulkhead isolation between agents, and timeout budgets for chain-of-thought latency. Leave with a decision framework mapping failure modes to pattern combinations you can implement immediately. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Folarin Alamu (Solutions Architect II, Amazon Web Services)

title: Where embeddings live: Designing production retrieval on AWS
abstract: Where should vector embeddings live? In your operational database, a dedicated vector store, or across several? In this session you evaluate the trade-offs across latency, data freshness, cost, and retrieval quality. You implement the same retrieval pattern across three engines: Amazon OpenSearch Service for combined lexical and vector search, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector for SQL-native filtered retrieval, and Amazon S3 Vectors for cost-optimized scale. You then combine them into a hybrid architecture that orchestrates a single query and merges the results with reciprocal rank fusion. You leave able to answer where your embeddings should live, backed by patterns you built yourself. Bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Amee Shah (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Harshil Shah (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: From system thinking to outcome thinking: The AI-native architect
abstract: The architect role is changing faster than at any point since the cloud itself emerged. AI is reshaping not just what architects build, but how they think, where they spend their time, and what organizations expect. We share observations from leading a global transformation of thousands of AWS Solutions Architects into AI-native practitioners: what shifted in daily practice, what surprised us, and what broke. We explore how outcome-oriented thinking replaces system-oriented thinking, and why the line between building and advising is dissolving. You leave with a practical mental model for how the architecture role delivers value in an AI-native world.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Tarik Makota (Sr Principal SA, AWS)
Andrew Baird (Sr. Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Ryan Law (Senior Principal Engineer, Strategic Initiatives, Grab)

title: Fault-tolerant AI agents: Choosing the right recovery pattern
abstract: When an AI agent crashes at step 20 of 30, you can't just start over. Once state accumulates, a blind retry becomes dangerous. Most teams default to the wrong recovery strategy because they apply stateless retry thinking to stateful workflows. In this session, we compare three approaches: replay-based recovery with idempotent tool execution, checkpoint-and-resume with human-in-the-loop pause/resume, and event-driven compensation across trust boundaries. We'll whiteboard each pattern, map it to real failure scenarios, and build a decision framework based on your agent's state model and fault domain.
speakers: Jeetendra Vaidya (Sr. GenAI/ML Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Sonal Panda (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Architecting for resilience and data residency
abstract: Your data can't leave the jurisdiction, but your workload still has to survive a Region degradation. This chalk talk explores architecture patterns that address both resilience and data residency together. We break the challenge into practical layers: where data lives, how workloads recover, what isolation looks like, and how to maintain business continuity across geographic boundaries. We map each layer to AWS capabilities including Dedicated Local Zones, Outposts, and policy controls, then work through real scenarios together. Bring your architecture challenges and we will whiteboard design patterns and tradeoffs with you.
speakers: Mike Haken (Senior Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Jamie Pasterick (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Andy Orlosky (AWS Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: Patterns for embedding FinOps into cloud architectural decisions
abstract: Every architectural decision carries a cost implication, yet cost is typically discovered in monthly bills rather than design reviews. In this code talk, we demonstrate how to shift FinOps left, optimising before you deploy rather than reacting after. Through two personas, a FinOps engineer and a builder, you will see live how to embed cost governance into infrastructure-as-code, tackle real architectural trade-offs then show how AI coding assistants accelerate this at scale. You will leave with deployable CloudFormation examples and a decision framework for choosing the right cost governance level for your organisation.
speakers: Nataliya Godunok (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS Well-Architected, AWS)
Steph Gooch (Principal Tech Advocate, AWS)

title: Cell-based architecture: Designing blast-radius boundaries
abstract: Cell-based architecture limits the blast radius of failures by partitioning systems into independent, isolated units. But deciding cell boundaries — by customer, geography, or workload — involves trade-offs between operational complexity and fault isolation. This session reveals the decision framework for cell sizing, routing, and cross-cell coordination. You'll learn when cells outperform active-active patterns, how to implement cell-aware deployments, and the true operational cost of cell management. Walk away with a reusable pattern for systems, where failures stay contained, impact reduced, and availability increased.
speakers: Mark Jones (FSI Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Jennifer Tipecska (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Multi-Region hedging: Where it works and where it breaks
abstract: Failover recovers after impairment; hedging survives it. This chalk talk examines where multi-Region hedging holds and where it breaks. We trace hedging across the stack: racing requests through Route 53 ARC and Elastic Load Balancing, containing blast radius with cell-based routing, and confronting the write path, where Aurora Global Database's asynchronous replication surfaces a consistency-versus-continuity trade-off that routing alone cannot resolve. Bring your availability-critical workload; we'll map its hedgeable read and routing paths against those that force an explicit consistency decision.
speakers: Enrique Bastante (Sr. Customer Solutions Manager, AWS Strategic Accounts, AWS)
Nick Dobson (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Resilience patterns for the disconnected edge with Amazon Leo
abstract: Every resilient system eventually has to answer one question: what happens when the network you depend on isn’t there? In this session we discuss Amazon Leo, a low earth orbit satellite connectivity service, as a forcing function to explore patterns for architecting across unreliable, high-latency, and intermittently connected links. We’ll walk through the trade-offs behind routing, data-in-transit security, and where to place compute when bandwidth is scarce and connectivity is a variable. We’ll ground the discussion in hybrid resiliency and edge data collection for AI/ML, but the takeaway is portable to any architecture spanning boundaries you don’t fully control.
speakers: Nick Matthews (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Leo)
Adam Palmer (Principal Networking Architect, Amazon Leo)

title: Deterministic meets probabilistic: Patterns for reliable AI integration
abstract: Production systems demand determinism. AI outputs are probabilistic. The boundary between these two worlds is where this must be resolved. This chalk talk will whiteboard the contracts and integration patterns that hold that boundary: typed interfaces treating model output as untrusted input, propose/commit separation so AI never performs its own side effects, asymmetric verification, bounded generate-verify-repair loops, and compensating actions in place of rollback. We'll work through typical anti-patterns that quietly reach production, where to place the contract in your architecture to avoid these, and the reliability arithmetic that these patterns enable.
speakers: Xin Chen (Sr. Delivery Consultant, AWS)
Bin Liu (Senior Delivery Consultant, Amazon Web Service)

title: Ambient accessibility: Architecting real-time ASL on a Wearable
abstract: What if a DHH person could wear a device and get sign language translation of every conversation around them in under a second? We architect a pipeline that ingests Amazon Bee's ambient audio, transcribes it, transforms English to ASL grammar, generates avatar animations, and streams signed video back. That one-second constraint drives every architectural tradeoff, from whether translation stages run on-device for speed or in the cloud for accuracy, to whether we sign full sentences or start mid-utterance with partial context. We explore the edge-cloud splits and pipeline staging that make sub-second delivery feasible.
speakers: Suresh Poopandi (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Alak Eswaradass (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Serverless at 1M RPS: Lambda, DynamoDB & SQS Scaling Lessons
abstract: We push Lambda, DynamoDB, and SQS to one million requests per second and share what breaks. Learn partition-aware DynamoDB design for extreme write throughput, Lambda concurrency shaping to prevent downstream crush, SQS as a backpressure buffer with adaptive batching, and retry amplification math that turns a blip into a cascade. We present real numbers: cold start budgets at scale, the exact crossover point where serverless cost exceeds containers, and the operational trade-offs at each threshold.
speakers: Jay Colodner (Technical Account Manager II, Amazon Web Services)
Nishtha Yadav (Associate Delivery Consulant, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: When one tenant spikes 100x, your architecture decides who pays
abstract: One tenant spikes 100x. The architecture either isolates the blast radius or turns it into every tenant's outage. Multi-tenant platforms face four decisions at this boundary. Where to place isolation so one workload cannot starve another. How fan-out creates backpressure that propagates upstream. When fair queuing replaces custom throttling code. What qualifies as real-time versus safely queueable. In this chalk talk you decide where your isolation boundaries belong and what trade-offs each placement creates. Bring your own scaling problem. We draw the architecture together.
speakers: Shubhankar Sumar (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Damian Niezgoda (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Your system made a decision. you cannot explain it.
abstract: Your system makes a decision. A human makes a decision. Both write to the same log in the same format. Three months later you need to know which was which. You cannot tell. This is not a logging problem. It is a runtime architecture problem. If decision origin is not captured at the boundary when the decision happens, no system can recover it after. Whether you need this for compliance, debugging, or customer trust, the architectural fix is identical. In this chalk talk you will decide: what to capture at the decision boundary, how much context to store, and when reproducibility justifies the cost.
speakers: Haresh Nandwani (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Richard Ainley (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Stop fixing, start preventing with Well-Architected Agent
abstract: Reactive incident response grows more expensive as environments scale. AWS Well-Architected Agent shifts resilience and security from periodic review to continuous, automated assessment. Its agentic reasoning identifies single points of failure, recovery gaps, and vulnerabilities across 100+ services, ranking findings by workload criticality and business goals. Crucially, each recommendation includes cross-pillar trade-off analysis - showing cost and performance implications — so you improve resilience and security without unintended consequences elsewhere. Walk away able to catch risks before they become incidents.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Saurabh Saxena (Sr Principal, AWS, Amazon)
Ramesh Seshadri (Senior Manager, Product Management, Amazon.com)

title: The coordination decision: when to orchestrate and when to let go
abstract: Distributed workflows need coordination, and most teams pick one approach everywhere: a central orchestrator, or independent services reacting to events. Both fail at scale: orchestration bottlenecks every team's releases, and choreography lets flows stall silently because no component owns the outcome. This session teaches a per-flow method: does any component need to own the flow end-to-end, including completion, failure compensation, and ordering? Using a logistics platform running both patterns on AWS Step Functions and Amazon EventBridge, see the real costs of each, and where orchestration and events hand off.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: John Dougherty (Sr Solution Architect, Amazon)
Aishwarya Subramaniam (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Pitfalls of SaaS: Return of the agent
abstract: Every SaaS architect has hit the classics: noisy neighbors saturating infrastructure, compounding costs eating margins, deployment models chosen too early. Agents amplify all of them — and add surprises. One agent generates more API calls in a minute than a human makes in a week. Shared memory leaks context across tenants in ways no IAM policy catches. Autonomous tool calls cascade across services with no human in the loop. Revisit classic SaaS pitfalls through an agentic lens: familiar problems in new costumes, genuinely new failure modes, and what to change before you find out the hard way.
speakers: Bill Tarr (Principal Partner Solutions Architect, AWS)
Anubhav Sharma (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: SaaS Agents Anywhere: building distributed agentic deployments
abstract: SaaS vendors deploy agents across a spectrum: fully provider-hosted, fully tenant-controlled, and hybrid models in between. Once customers have data residency or cost-visibility requirements, deployment topology determines the operational pattern. In this workshop, build a distributed agentic deployment on AWS spanning your accounts and a tenant's, then exercise the three concerns that surface everywhere on the spectrum: lifecycle management of agents you can't directly see, observability across account boundaries, and reliability when the agent runs somewhere you don't operate. Leave with a working reference deployment you can adapt to your own tenancy model.
speakers: Hasan Tariq (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Markus Doepke (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Unexpected resilience: Lessons from a thousand incidents
abstract: After years of investigating incidents - both within AWS and across customer industries - some resilience lessons stand out. Not the obvious ones, but surprises no runbook could anticipate. We share the strangest, most counterintuitive findings from years of troubleshooting under pressure: failure modes nobody planned for, fixes that made things worse, and patterns that only emerge after enough failures. This isn't a best-practices talk - it's a field guide to building resilience from the unexpected. You'll leave with a sharper eye for hidden risks in your infrastructure - and fresh leads on things you didn't know were there.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Giorgio Bonfiglio (Principal TAM, AWS)
Donald Quindardo (Principal TAM, Amazon Web Services)

title: Inverting the medallion: Serving reads without hitting Gold
abstract: Most teams default to Gold as the serving layer. For regulated systems-of-record like health data stores, ledgers, compliance archives, that's rarely the right choice. They're built for durability and interoperability, not production read traffic. The inverted pattern writes promote up the medallion, reads come from purpose-built Silver projections and Gold holds contractual semantics and never serves directly. In this chalk talk, work through change-data-capture synthesis without source support, write/read path splitting, and a routing gateway developers can't bypass. Bring your most painful regulated read path. Leave knowing when to invert, how to scope projections, and what your gateway must enforce.
speakers: Laks Sundararajan (Principal  Solutions Architect, AWS)
Chaitanya Vejendla (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build Resilient AI Platforms with Oracle AI Database@AWS (sponsored by Oracle)
abstract: AI applications demand continuous access to trusted, business-critical data. In this lightning session, learn how Oracle Maximum Availability Architecture helps protect AI workloads running on Oracle AI Database@AWS. Explore proven patterns for high availability, disaster recovery, data protection, and automated failover across AWS Availability Zones and Regions. See how capabilities such as Oracle Active Data Guard and integrated backup and recovery services help minimize downtime, reduce data loss, and keep AI applications operating through planned maintenance and unexpected disruptions. This presentation is brought to you by Oracle, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Muneer Mirza (Vice President, Multicloud, Oracle Corporation)

title: Route or escalate: Confidence boundaries in multi-domain AI agents
abstract: Building a GenAI system that answers questions across technology domains is straightforward — until the model doesn't know the answer and doesn't say so. For builders designing multi-agent or RAG-based systems, this session presents the confidence-gated routing architecture: classifying every query into high-confidence retrieval, low-confidence escalation to a human specialist, or cross-domain composition. We cover why flat vector retrieval fails multi-domain queries, the trade-offs of graph-based knowledge ontology, and the evaluations framework measuring confidence calibration. Walk away with a routing pattern you can apply any time your AI system must self-report uncertainty rather than hallucinate with authority.
speakers: Roland Barcia (Director: Specialist Technology Team, AWS)
Kandha Sankarapandian (Head of AWS Specialist Prototyping, AWS)

title: Foundational architecture excellence: the operability trade-off
abstract: Elegant architectures that ignore operational reality become expensive liabilities. From hundreds of enterprise engagements, we expose the architectural decisions that silently create operational debt — decomposition without observability boundaries, blast-radius assumptions that fail under correlated load, and abstraction layers hiding the signals operators need. We unpack where good architecture and operable architecture diverge, which trade-offs are worth making early, and what questions your team should be asking before committing to a design. The best architecture is one you can actually run in production.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Saurabh Saxena (Sr Principal, AWS, Amazon)
Farzin Bagheri (Principal Technical Account Manager, AWS)

title: Architecting for five nines with multi-region: Capital One’s journey (sponsored by Capital One)
abstract: Five nines of availability leaves an annual downtime budget of just 5.2 minutes, meaning a single regional failover can consume your entire year. Traditional disaster recovery models simply don't scale to meet this standard. In this session, discover how Capital One evolved its multi-region architectures to sustain regional outages while supporting critical production workloads. We share lessons learned from building and operating active-active topologies, focusing on real-world data consistency models, fault isolation via cell-based architecture, and continuous fault-injection testing. Attendees will walk away with a field-tested matrix for architecting high-availability cloud workloads. This presentation is brought to you by Capital One, an AWS Partner.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Mats Lannér (VP, Software Engineering, Capital One Financial Corporation)
Prem Dhayalan (Senior Distinguished Engineer, Capitalone Bank)

title: Thousands of Databases, $250 a Month: Operating an Agentic Database Estate on AWS (sponsored by CockroachDB)
abstract: What if ~1,000 production-grade databases cost $250/month? Most teams pay more to keep a few clusters idle, each sized for peak load, running at 85–95% unused capacity and provisioned ticket by ticket. That model is breaking. AI agents create databases faster than platform teams can provision, secure or retire them. One engineering group grew from 13 databases to 392 in four months. At 1,000, managing one cluster at a time stops working. This session shifts focus to the estate with 3 architectural changes on AWS: - Separate storage from compute, eliminating upfront capacity. - Run isolated virtual clusters on shared hosts without creating sprawl. - Use agentic operations to observe the estate and recommend actions your team approves. See live demos, a reference architecture and cost model behind the numbers. Bring your hardest questions about running stateful workloads at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by CockroachDB, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater

title: Close the loop: From guardrail blocks into layered defense
abstract: Guardrails block malicious prompts. Every blocked attempt is a signal: proof of what your defenses caught and a clue toward what will be attempted next. Capture that signal instead of discarding it. In this session, you design and deploy a layered enforcement architecture that closes the loop. A stateful detection tier identifies repeated probing across sessions and propagates block decisions to the network edge. You evaluate signals from guardrail violations and apply policies to classify and block the threat. You leave with a deployed pattern applicable to any AI agent workload. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Wei Chen (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Jason Schamp (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Patrick Duffy (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Sanghwa Na (Sr. Specialist SA, Gen AI, AWS)
Jonathan Woods (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: Event storming: Find your service boundaries before production does
abstract: Split a system in the wrong place and you get a distributed monolith: coupled services with network hops instead of function calls. This session tackles the problem most teams get wrong, where to draw the boundary, using Event Storming. Together we map a real domain, trace information flow between actors, and identify natural division points, deciding ownership, data locality, transaction scope, and deployment independence at each boundary. Every decision is evidence based, grounded in observed event flow rather than intuition. Then you go hands on, taking one boundary and deploying it as an independent service on AWS. Leave with a repeatable method for boundary definition plus working code you built yourself. Bring your laptop.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Jim Fernandes (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Ramesh Chidirala (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
John Dougherty (Sr Solution Architect, Amazon)
Vaibhav Sabharwal (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Yongzhe Ren (solutions architect, AWS)

title: Your regulator set your RTO. Not your architecture.
abstract: Organizations with pre-approved failover regions recover in hours. Those without recover in weeks. Same impairment. Same services. One governance decision separates them, and it’s made years before the event. This session presents architectural patterns for multi-Region recovery under sovereignty constraints, drawn from real operational experience with regulated workloads under regional pressure. Three categories: decisions that set your resilience ceiling before any event, dependencies that create circular failure during recovery, and assets nobody backs up until they become the critical path. You leave with the decisions to evaluate before your next DR test.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Hossam Ebrahim (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Paul Armstrong (Lead Architect UKI, Amazon Web Services)

title: Visualizing multi-tenant isolation: Catch your noisy neighbors
abstract: Managing multi-tenant platforms forces trade-offs between cost, complexity, and performance. This session tackles two common challenges: tenant data isolation and the noisy-neighbor problem. Starting from a single-tenant architecture, you consolidate into a shared Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster, building isolation through Cognito-issued JWTs, Lambda-based dynamic policy generation, IAM authentication, and RDS Proxy connection pooling. Then you implement queuing tiers with Amazon SQS to manage load. Visualize real-time request flows, data isolation, and noisy-neighbor effects on your own dynamic architecture simulation and a central 16,000-LED display. Bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Sam Sanders (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Amit Lulla (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Data mesh at scale: The automation layer, proven at Experian
abstract: Federated data ownership is easy to draw and hard to enforce. Is governance enforced in process, or in the platform? Enforce it in the platform, and the hard part becomes the seam between central policy and self-serve provisioning most teams never build. On Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio we architect that seam: one project per data-domain for blast-radius isolation, contracts that block non-compliant publication, policy that cascades but only tightens, and a reconciler turning Git-committed JSON into infrastructure. Experian runs it across dozens of data domains in regulated financial services, cutting domain onboarding from months to self-serve.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Romi Patel (Prototyping Architect, AWS)
Mohammed Ali Syed (Data Engineering Director, Experian)
Rohit Kumar Singh (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Specs, not vibes: Strangling the monolith in the IDE
abstract: Your architecture is full of pets: brittle EC2 instances run by manual runbooks, with no contract between decisions and infrastructure. In this code talk, we abandon slides and prove the Strangler pattern live in the IDE with Kiro and spec-driven development. We decompose a monolith into bounded contexts, generate CDK from the spec, and shift traffic from pets to serverless cattle, confronting the hard parts: where to cut the seam, running old and new together, keeping data consistent. Every architectural decision becomes a machine-verifiable contract you can apply to your own monolith.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Steve Wolfe (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Patrick Duffy (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Load-bearing coupling: Finding the coupling you can't cut
abstract: Teams break up monoliths to move faster, then find the pieces still fail together. Some coupling is doing real structural work: invariants spanning writes, ordering guarantees, timing assumptions baked into callers. Cut it and you get a distributed monolith, the same dependency with new failure modes. In this session, we whiteboard real systems, insert seams, and price what each dependency costs to cross a boundary: consistency, backpressure, retry semantics. Apply a simple test: if a circuit breaker can't open here without breaking correctness, that coupling is load-bearing. Bring your hardest dependency; leave knowing which coupling to cut, which to keep, and why.
speakers: Matt Coles (Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Paul Moran (Principal Technologist, AWS)

title: Twenty years of cloud architecture
abstract: Instant, vast scale and elasticity. Infrastructure as Code. Eventual consistency. Immutable infrastructure. Serverless. Event-driven computing. Internet of Things. Chaos engineering. Zero trust. Pervasive observability. Twenty years of cloud have produced an extraordinary density of patterns — each arriving with conviction and shaping what came next. Some became invisible foundations we build on without thinking. Others evolved in ways nobody predicted. And the evolution continues — now with agentic architectures. What has stood the test of time? What's still evolving? And what can we learn to be ready for the next twenty years?
speakers: Colm MacCarthaigh (Vice President / Distinguished Engineer, AWS)

title: How Southwest Airlines migrated 4,500 agents in just 2.5 weeks
abstract: In just 2.5 weeks from decision to go-live, Southwest migrated 4,500 agents across 17 business units to Amazon Connect Customer without losing a single call. Join this session to hear their key lessons learned from the migration, and how the move unlocked more comprehensive analytics capabilities, giving leadership real-time visibility into previously hidden metrics. Discover what’s next for Southwest, including how they’re implementing agentic AI throughout the customer experience.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Jeff Grant (Senior Technology Consultant, Southwest Airlines)
Ryan Clayborn (Technology - Lead Analyst, Southwest Airlines)
Ayesha Borker (Principal Solution Architect, Amazon)
Ryan Champ (Application Architect, Southwest Airlines)

title: Taking Every Interaction from Mundane to Magic: Agentic CX with Connect Customer
abstract: Every brand is racing to put AI in front of its customers, the biggest opportunity in a generation, but also a risk. In 2026, deflection is dead. Even the customers you help are quietly leaving, because being processed isn't the same as being known. In this session, the VP, Amazon Connect Customer, and SVP, Client Operations Technology, U.S. Bank, show what's possible when serving customers is AI-first by design: your brand shows up before they ask, and every customer feels like your only customer. If you own the customer relationship, this is the one session you can't afford to miss.
speakers: Srinivas Akella (SVP, Software Engineering Director, U.S. Bank)
Cecilia Bolich (Sr. WW Spec SA, Connect, AWS)
Pasquale DeMaio (VP, Amazon Connect, Amazon Web Services)

title: How A Customer Met Surge Hiring in Hours, Not Weeks
abstract: You expanded fast, but your hiring didn't keep up. What started as seasonal growth has become a scramble of manual screening, scheduling delays, and fragile workarounds that can't keep pace with your brand — forcing the impossible choice between speed and quality. Hear how a customer replaced weeks-long hiring with Amazon Connect Talent, putting AI teammates to work running science-backed candidate assessments and AI-led interviews that take candidates from application to same-day offer — evaluated on the substance of their answers. Built on AWS and informed by Amazon's hiring science, Amazon Connect Talent ensures recruiters stay in control of every decision.
speakers: Kate Totaro (Principal PMT, Amazon)
Vikram Modgil (WW GTM Leader, Amazon Connect Talent, Amazon Web Services)

title: From On-Premises to Agentic AI: Bayer's Amazon Connect Transformation Journey (sponsored by Capgemini)
abstract: Capgemini transformed 414 contact center hotlines across more than 68 countries by replacing Cisco UCCE with Amazon Connect and introducing AgentX, an AWS-native agentic AI platform deployed across the Bayer enterprise. Built on Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Connect, Amazon Lex, AWS Lambda, and other AWS services, AgentX delivers real-time agent assistance, automated call summarization, governance controls, predictive analytics, and autonomous workflow execution. Learn how Bayer established a "build once, deploy globally" operating model that enables consistent AI innovation across business units while reducing operational complexity, improving agent productivity, and delivering significant cost savings. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Vivek Sandell (Client Partner, Capgemini America, Inc.)
Andreea Manolache (Home Lead Supply Chain Excellence, Bayer LLC)

title: Shaping the Future of Guest Support at lululemon with an AI-powered experience
abstract: What if you could design Guest Support for the future, not just improve the operation you have today? At lululemon, that question shifted the conversation. Rather than patching together fragmented tools and manual planning processes, the team envisioned the experience they wanted to create for guests and their people, then worked backward to build it. The result was a unified, AI-powered experience launched globally, giving employees more time to build meaningful connections with guests. This session explores how lululemon built a fundamentally different future for Guest Support and the principles leaders can use to do the same at their organization.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Hannah Bloking (Sr. Manager, Solutions Architecture - Applied AI Acceleration, Amazon Web Services)
Shadi El Baba (VP, Guest Support, lululemon athletica canada Inc.)

title: How Flybuys Cut Costs by 24% and Scaled AI Agents Across 10M Members
abstract: 10 million members. Limited visibility into support interactions. High costs. Flybuys needed a new path. In 7 months, they migrated to Amazon Connect Customer, bringing operations in-house, and deploying AI agents that now handle 100% of member interactions. The result of the migration has been a 24% cost reduction while improving customer satisfaction. Join this session to hear how Flybuys took control of their member experience, unlocked deep visibility across every interaction, and are now moving quickly to scale agentic AI across voice and digital channels.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Elias Sayigh (Amazon Connect Solution Architect, AWS)

title: How EchoStar Turned CX and IT Into One Team to Ship AI Experiences
abstract: Most companies treat conversational AI as a technology rollout. EchoStar, the company behind DISH, treated it as a chance to reset how CX and IT work together. Instead of handing specs back and forth, the two teams now build side by side in Amazon Connect Customer, shaping and testing each experience before it goes live. CX owns the customer experience. IT owns data, security, and standards. Changes that took six to eight weeks now ship in about one week - roughly 6× faster. Hear from Echostar's CX and IT leaders on how they transformed their operating model, and leave with a framework to start the same shift.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Sevrin Huff (VP, Echostar)
Tim Baylus (Vice President, Strategic Planning and Shared Services, Dish Network Corporation)
Christina Sansone (VP, CX Transformation, Echostar)
Brian Dawson (AI Executive Strategist, Amazon Connect Customer)

title: Trust, built in seconds: AI-powered banking at scale
abstract: In financial services, trust is earned in seconds: the lost card, the emergency funds, the vulnerable customer who nearly gave up. Those seconds demand that you know who the customer is, understand their need, and resolve it on the spot. Hear how one of the UK's largest banks reimagined customer experience on Amazon Connect Customer, reaching 96% first-point-of-contact resolution across millions of calls monthly. Trace a multi-year journey: real-time AI that helps agents act in seconds, analytics and self-service at scale, and an active-active, multi-region architecture that keeps service running under strict European regulatory and data-residency requirements.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Aly Galal (Head of Sales & GTM - Amazon Connect - EMEA, Amazon Web Services)

title: Citizens Bank: Building AI-Native CX from Vision to Production
abstract: Financial services customers expect fast, personalized service, but compliance, security, and regulatory requirements make automation a high-stakes challenge. Discover how Amazon Connect Customer enables financial institutions to design agentic customer experiences, where AI self-service blends autonomous reasoning with deterministic guardrails for identity verification, fraud checks, and regulatory disclosures. Learn how business teams, not only engineers, build and refine these experiences, automating complex interactions like account servicing, disputes, and payments while maintaining full compliance and governance. See how Citizens Bank lifted containment by 30 points, elevated CSAT, and transformed their contact center without compromising trust.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater

title: Uncover the Opportunity. Build the AI Agent. Scale It Live. (sponsored by NiCE)
abstract: Your CX data already knows where automation will pay off. See Agentic Analytics pinpoint the opportunity, then watch that recommendation become a working AI agent — built, tested, and scaled live. ​ This presentation is brought to you by NiCE, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: George Downey IV (Sr AI Consultant, NiCE Cognigy)

title: Build the Agentic Workplace: What's New on the Slack Developer Platform (sponsored by Salesforce)
abstract: Slack is becoming a multiplayer work operating system, where humans and AI agents build together, not just chat. This session shows AWS developers how to ship on the modern Slack Platform: Code Channels, a new space where agents like Claude Code, Devin, and Cursor collaborate with teams in real time; the Slack Agent Kit for building first-class agents; deep bidirectional MCP support, including the Slackbot MCP Client; Real-Time Search (RTS) for grounding agents in live workspace context; and Block Kit for rich, interactive UI. Leave with a clear path to build your first agentic app on Slack. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Josh Milas (Product Management Director, Slack)

title: From Zero to 20,000 Desktops: Getting Started with Amazon Quick
abstract: Your team is drowning in context-switching: toggling between email, documents, data tools, and chat just to complete a single task. Productivity tools promise to help, but most add complexity instead of removing it. In this fireside chat, hear from customers who faced that exact challenge and deployed an AI work companion across 20,000+ users in under 90 days. Learn what convinced their leadership to invest, how they integrated AI into daily workflows without disrupting existing tools, and what the first 90 days of adoption actually looked like. Walk away with a practical roadmap for bringing Amazon Quick AI assistant to your workforce at scale.
speakers: Jose Kunnackal John (Director of Amazon Quick, Amazon)

title: Getting Started with Amazon Quick: How a Customer Went from Curious to Deployed
abstract: Your team spends hours on work that should take minutes: summarizing meetings, drafting documents, finding answers buried across systems, pulling data from multiple platforms. You know AI should help, but you need to see it work in a real environment before you commit. In this session, see how a customer put Amazon Quick into daily workflows across their organization and watch live as it composes documents, analyzes data, summarizes conversations, and connects to enterprise systems. Hear what problems they were solving, what changed for their teams after deployment, and what surprised them about adoption. Leave with a clear picture of the problems Quick solves and how to evaluate whether it fits your organization.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Leo Ohannesian (Principal Product Manager, Amazon)

title: What's New in Amazon Connect Customer
abstract: Your customers don't experience departments — they experience one journey. But siloed systems, fragmented data, and manual processes between teams create gaps they absolutely feel. This session introduces new Amazon Connect Customer capabilities that close those gaps end to end. Come see how these capabilities work together to deliver the seamless experience your customers expect and the certainty your business demands.

title: Agentic Integration: How AI Agents Replace Static CRM Connectors
abstract: Every enterprise has dozens of integrations connecting their CRM, ticketing, and backend systems to their customer experience platform, and every one of them is static, brittle, and expensive to maintain. In this chalk talk, we explore how Amazon Connect Customer, powered by Model Context Protocol (MCP), shifts integration from point-to-point connectors to intelligent, agentic orchestration. The AI agent reasons across multiple systems in real time, assembling unified customer context that no single system holds alone. We whiteboard the architecture: how MCP connections work, how each new system compounds the intelligence available to every interaction, and how to evaluate which integrations to migrate first. Bring your integration pain (Salesforce, ServiceNow, homegrown systems) and we'll design the agentic alternative on the whiteboard.
speakers: Chintan Gandhi (Senior Solutions Architect Lead - Agentic Integrations, Aamzon Web Services)
Ritesh Choudhary (Sr Solution Architect, AWS)
