title: Best practices for scaling self-managed GPU workstations
abstract: Artists, engineers, and scientists need GPU-powered virtual workstations, but managing VDI at scale means navigating instance selection, capacity, and cost. In this chalk talk, learn how to match EC2 G instances to user personas, from fractional GPU for task workers to full GPU for power users running 3D modeling, compositing, or subsurface visualization. Explore the decision framework covering instance types, DCV streaming, storage, security, and fleet orchestration with Research and Engineering Studio (RES). Whether supporting a VFX render farm's artist desktops, an oil company's subsurface workstations, or an automotive design studio, leave with guidance balancing performance, cost, and simplicity.
speakers: Shreya Manjunath (Senior Product Manager, Not applicable)
Avi Mittal (Sr. WW Spec. Graphics and Viz., Amazon Web Services)

title: Right Compute, right time, right price: A decision framework for HPC and AI at scale
abstract: Large-scale HPC and AI workloads share the same hard problem: getting the right compute, at the right time, at the right price. In this chalk talk, we cover the architecture and provisioning decisions that matter when you move beyond a single instance. Architecture side: cluster design for distributed AI training and tightly coupled HPC simulation, networking trade-offs and where CPUs (x86, Graviton) fit alongside GPUs in production pipelines. Provisioning side: Capacity Blocks for predictable GPU bursts, On-Demand Capacity Reservations for sustained workloads, Spot for fault-tolerant jobs, and Savings Plans for steady-state fleets. We share real customer examples leveraging Amazon EC2 across HPC and AI/ML. Bring your hardest capacity and cost questions.
speakers: Sudhi Bhat (Principal Speacialist Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc)
Avi Kulkarni (Sr. Accelerated Compute Specialist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Graviton5 for data workloads
abstract: Data workloads are bottlenecked by how fast they can access and process information — whether that data lives on local storage, in memory, or behind a lightweight service. New Graviton5 instance families are purpose-built for each tier.

title: Simplifying how you use AWS: automating common patterns on your behalf
abstract: Getting the most out of AWS often means manually setting up the same optimizations, integrations, and best-practice patterns across your applications. What if AWS could handle more of that for you - automatically and securely - so you benefit from AWS capabilities without the setup overhead? In this chalk talk, we explore emerging approaches for running AWS-authored logic in isolated, secure-by-default environments alongside your applications, implementing common patterns on your behalf and simplifying how you consume AWS services. We'll whiteboard how this model works, where it fits in your architecture, and how it changes the effort required to adopt AWS best practices.
speakers: Steve Rice (General Manager, AWS AppConfig & Parameter Store, AWS)

title: Everything you've wanted to know about performance on EC2 instances
abstract: Getting the best compute performance is an art, and knowing low-level details helps a lot. This talk covers everything you've wanted to know: memory topology, accessing hardware counters, hyperthreading side-effects, and how to properly run performance tests and optimize your latency for production.
speakers: Arthur Petitpierre (WW Graviton & Perf Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)
Seth Fox (Head of Solutions Architecture Amazon EC2, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build hybrid quantum-classical solutions for science and engineering on Amazon Braket
abstract: Take the next step into hybrid quantum computing. This expert-level workshop combines Amazon Braket and AWS Parallel Computing Service to build hybrid quantum-classical resources that enable scientific and engineering research in fields like physics and chemistry. You learn how to structure hybrid programs, manage classical resources, and interpret results from real quantum devices. Expect hands-on exercises, detailed guidance, and examples you can use as a foundation for your own projects.
speakers: Tyler Takeshita (Sr. Applied Scientist, AWS)
Sebastian Stern (Principal Specialist Solutions Architect Quantum, AWS)

title: Automating macOS at scale: AMI build, TCC, and provisioning on EC2 Mac
abstract: Automating macOS in the cloud brings challenges Linux and Windows don't. Going from a fresh EC2 Mac instance to a production-ready fleet means clearing non-obvious hurdles: building AMIs with EC2 Image Builder and Packer, pre-approving TCC permissions, bootstrapping Systems Manager, and working with Apple's security model. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through the real friction points teams hit: image pipelines, the TCC dialog problem, remote access, MDM enrollment, and fleet provisioning. Bring your toughest macOS automation questions; most of the session is open Q&A.
speakers: Kyle Krall ( EC2 Mac Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Caitlin Rawlins (Principal Engineer, AWS)

title: Learn how to build a Genomics PCS pipeline on AWS
abstract: Build and run a real genomics variant-calling Slurm pipeline on AWS PCS using a mixed Graviton + GPU fleet. This session will cover PCS queue design, Slurm partition strategy, FSx for Lustre, EFA networking, and result aggregation to Amazon S3. By the end, you’ll create a reproducible, production-grade HPC workflow for life-sciences workloads.
speakers: Shubhendu Dubey (Technical Account Manager, AWS)
Kumar Shubham (TAM (ENT), Amazon Web Services)

title: Hands-on: Harden your AI agents with Nitro Confidential Computing
abstract: Agentic AI systems autonomously orchestrate tools, integrate third-party components, and make decisions, introducing risks from compromised dependencies and agents deviating from intended behavior. Protecting prompts, agent memory, retrieval context, and model weights requires strong isolation and verifiable trust. In this workshop, you will build agentic AI apps, identify threats from untrusted supply chains and uncontrolled autonomy, and mitigate them using AWS Confidential Computing on EC2 with cryptographic attestation, isolated execution, open weight models, and Amazon Bedrock.
speakers: Arvind Raghu (Principal Specialist, AWS)
Sudhir Reddy Maddulapally (SSA Confidential compute, AWS)

title: From zero to HPC: Build production clusters with AWS PCS
abstract: Master AWS Parallel Computing Service at re:Invent. Build fully managed compute environments with zero setup. This hands-on session covers job submission, resource optimization, and intuitive interfaces to accelerate workflows for researchers and engineers. Scale faster without the complexity.
speakers: Timothy Brown (Solution Architect, AWS)
Matthew Vaughn (Principal Product Manager, AWS)

title: Orchestrating Physical AI workloads on AWS: Compute and pipeline patterns
abstract: Physical AI projects — robotics, autonomous systems, digital twins — require complex multi-stage pipelines spanning simulation, training, evaluation, and edge deployment. Each stage demands different compute and orchestration. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architecture patterns combining AWS Batch for parallel simulation, Amazon EKS with Karpenter for heterogeneous GPU/Trainium training, and SageMaker Hyperpod showcasing managed resiliency. We'll compare when to use EKS vs. Batch vs. ParallelCluster, discuss cost optimization with Capacity Blocks and Spot, and solve attendee architectures live on the whiteboard.
speakers: Vincent Wang (GenAI Specialist SA, Amazon)
Carlos Manzanedo Rueda (Startup Specialist SA Tech Lead, AWS)

title: The cloud holodeck: Stream NVIDIA Omniverse, scale headless sim on AWS
abstract: Interactive simulation needs RTX-class GPUs engineers lack; rendering millions of frames needs a fleet nobody wants to babysit. Amazon DCV streams a full NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim workstation from EC2 G instances to any browser, while AWS Batch runs the same scenes headless across GPU fleets for scale. The AWS Visual Asset Management System is the control plane: launching jobs, tracking runs, and versioning outputs. Watch an engineer open a cloud viewport and fan out a thousand-frame jobs live.
speakers: Dan Cotting (Sr. Mgr., WW Specialist SA, Physical AI, AWS)
Kurt Scheuringer (Principal Physical AI Prototyping Architect, AWS)

title: Getting the capacity you need: EC2 Launch APIs and Intelligent Auto Scaling deep dive
abstract: Getting the right compute at the right time is a two-part challenge: launching instances effectively and scaling them intelligently. This deep dive covers both. First, we explore RunInstances—EC2's oldest and most important API—sharing launch best practices, how flexibility helps you get the capacity you need, and how EC2 Fleet incorporates advanced strategies into your calls. Then we go under the hood of EC2 Auto Scaling, and the intelligence that also scales DynamoDB, WorkSpaces, EMR, SageMaker AI, and Aurora. Learn how to use target tracking, predictive scaling, and auto-tuning to automatically and intelligently scale your workloads.
speakers: Justin Kwong (Sr. Software Dev Engineer, Amazon)
Samruddhi Kochkar (Senior Software Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: AI-driven optimizations for HPC configurations on AWS
abstract: Choosing the right HPC configuration often requires extensive benchmarking across instance types, MPI implementations, core counts, and application-specific settings. Learn how AWS uses AI to predict optimal HPC configurations from historical workload data, helping engineers make informed decisions before launching large-scale jobs. We’ll cover the models behind these recommendations and demonstrate how AI reduces trial and error while improving performance, cost efficiency, and time to solution.
speakers: Nicola Venuti (Principal HPC SA, AWS)
Francesco Ruffino (Prin. HPC Specialist SA, AWS)

title: Aperf: An all-in-one tool for performance data collection and analysis
abstract: Aperf is an open-source project created by AWS to accelerate the performance debugging process by enabling experienced users to deep dive into extensive data and less experienced users to identify issues without specialized knowledge. During this session, we'll present its key features and run a demo showing the analysis workflow, from installation, data collection, and then analysis. Finally, we'll open the conversation to collect feedback and feature requests from the audience.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk

Arthur Petitpierre (WW Graviton & Perf Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)

title: Nine Seconds to Zero: Protecting AWS from AI Agent Disasters
abstract: In April 2026, an AI coding agent deleted a company's entire production database in nine seconds, without being asked. The agent was confidently wrong and had the permissions to act on it. In this session, we recreate that incident live using Amazon Bedrock, walk through every failure in the chain, then rebuild the architecture with six hardening layers: Bedrock Guardrails, human approval gates, least-privilege IAM, deletion protection, isolated backups, and real-time monitoring. Walk away with a concrete checklist for designing AI-assisted systems that plan for when the AI is wrong, not just when it performs perfectly.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Jasdeep Singh Bhalla (Senior Software Engineer, GoDaddy)

title: Rebuilding a Platform's Foundation on DynamoDB Streams and Lambda
abstract: Our platform had single points of failure baked into its original design. In this session, I walk through how we closed those gaps across all five AWS Well-Architected pillars: moving event-driven workloads onto DynamoDB Streams and Lambda, cutting costs through smarter data tiering, and building the observability needed to trust the new design under real operational pressure.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Awedis Keofteian (Sr. DevOps Engineer, Washmen)

title: Context Over Code: Making AI-Native Development Work at Scale
abstract: AI coding assistants generate code quickly, but that's not the problem most teams need solved. After rolling out an AI coding companion to 150+ engineers, we learned the real unlock was rethinking how we work, not how fast we type. This session covers our path from AI code companion to AI-Driven Development Lifecycle: building a Context Store with Bedrock Knowledge Bases and MCP to surface decades of institutional knowledge, implementing steering and verification patterns, and managing the organizational change that makes AI-native development stick. You'll leave with a framework for scaling AI beyond individual productivity.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Matt Houghton (Data & AI Architect, CDL)

title: The judgment gap: when Terraform scans clean but fails the audit
abstract: Checkov, trivy, and Prowler check rules someone already wrote. SOC 2 CC6.1 is a sentence open to interpretation. Between them sits the judgment gap, where AI-generated Terraform for S3, CloudFront, API Gateway, and Lambda often lands. We map the gap on the whiteboard together: take real controls from SOC 2 and PCI DSS, set them against what scanner rules verify, and mark what is left over. Then we discuss what closes the remainder: better authoring-side skills, human review, multi-model review, or accepting the risk. Bring a control your team owns; we trace where its enforcement lives, or does not.
speakers: Anton Babenko (CEO, Compliance.tf)

title: Lambda for every scale and workload shape
abstract: Honeycomb spends millions of dollars a year on Lambda. Every cold query runs through a map-reduce backend that used to mean one tier, Lambda Functions, regardless of shape. We outgrew Lambda Functions, not Lambda: Managed Instances now absorbs steady-state baseline traffic at roughly 7.5x lower cost than Functions, MicroVMs takes spikes of load tolerating 1.5 seconds of added latency, and Functions still catches bursty spillover. We'll walk through the observability and benchmarks that drove each cutover, and the routing logic deciding which tier a query lands on before it executes. You'll learn how to scale your serverless workloads multiple orders of magnitude without linear cost.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Liz Fong-Jones (Technical Fellow, honeycomb.io)

title: Hidden trade-offs in distributed architectures
abstract: Asynchronous event-driven architectures enable loosely coupled, scalable, and resilient systems. But the devil is in the details, and hidden complexity emerges when components interact under real-world pressure. Consistency, latency, failure handling, and cost aren't determined by architecture diagrams but by the trade-offs behind the integration patterns and services you choose. Through a real-world case study using AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB, DynamoDB Streams, and AWS Step Functions, you'll investigate unexpected system behavior and uncover the trade-offs behind it. You'll leave with a sharper intuition to see beyond cloud abstractions and make more intentional architectural decisions for resilient systems.
speakers: Anahit Pogosova (Cloud Architecture & Engineering Lead, F-Secure)

title: Why Enterprise RAG Fails: Document AI and  Ontology Patterns on AWS
abstract: Most teams blame embeddings, vector databases, or foundation models when RAG systems underperform. In practice, failures often originate earlier in the pipeline where business meaning is lost during document ingestion. This session explores production Document AI patterns on AWS, including layout-aware extraction, ontology-driven classification, semantic chunking, metadata enrichment, and retrieval optimization. Using financial services examples, we demonstrate how domain ontologies improve extraction accuracy, retrieval relevance, and explainability. Attendees will learn practical architecture patterns, implementation tradeoffs, and a framework for building scalable, trustworthy RAG systems for enterprise workloads.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Bhuvaneswari Subramani (VP, Customer Advocacy & Success, Intuitive.ai)
Ayyanar Jeyakrishnan (Executive Director, WellsFargo)
Vivek Raja P S (Senior AI Solutions Architect, Aivar Innovations)

title: What Building an SRE Agent Taught Us About Agents at Scale
abstract: Anyone can wire up an agent, but operating one safely and cheaply across thousands of sessions is where developer craft begins. Grounded in a production SRE agent we built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK, this session dissects engineering around agentic models: session isolation, context management, and least privilege identity. What broke, and how we fixed it: an agent with too much access, context bloat that wrecked cost, a crash during a tool call that forced durable recovery. You will see where architectures leak, how to evaluate on production traces, and tradeoffs behind resilient agent infrastructure.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Dipin Thomas (Lead Engineer, Xero)
Arshad Zackeriya (Senior Engineer, Xero)
Geethika Guruge (Principal Consultant, Mantel Group)

title: A DevOps Approach to Recover at Scale from Disaster or Ransomware
abstract: Recovering your cloud workload completely after a regional event or ransomware attack is not a checklist; it demands a culture of resilience that turns individual craft into reliable recovery. That culture is built through DevOps. Clear communication, team empowerment, and frequent experimentation and measurement are what separate teams that recover from teams that hope. This session covers the technical requirements for recovering cloud workloads at scale, and the DevOps practices that make those requirements actually work under pressure. You'll leave with practical knowledge to drive full recovery in the face of the worst disasters.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Samantha Eliot (Principal Resilience Architect, Commvault)

title: Your Users Aren't Waiting to Build AI Agents. Are You Ready?
abstract: The spreadsheet wizards and automation tinkerers in your organization are already reaching for low-code and visual builder tools to assemble AI agents on their own. Call it citizen agent building: either governance sprawl, or your fastest path to scale. This interactive chalk talk gives platform, security, and data leaders a reference pattern that puts low-code builders on top and Amazon Bedrock beneath, so the security, data residency, and governance enterprises need come from the foundation rather than from each agent. Amazon Bedrock makes governance possible; your architecture makes it the default.
speakers: Rian Brooks-Kane (Head of Technology & Solutions, Idea 11)
Ian Mckay (Cloud Principal, Kablamo)

title: Your Users Aren't Waiting to Build AI Agents. Are You Ready?

speakers: Rian Brooks-Kane (Head of Technology & Solutions, Idea 11)

title: Giving Your AI Agent a Wallet: The Architecture of Spend Control
abstract: AI agents can now hold a wallet and pay for APIs, data, and even other agents. The demo takes a few hours; making it safe to ship takes much longer. At the whiteboard, using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments, x402 micropayments, and Cedar policy, we design an agent that spends under a hard budget, then break it together. We work through where guardrails belong, why session limits aren't enough, custodial versus non-custodial tradeoffs, and human-in-the-loop without human-in-the-way. Bring your edge cases. You leave with a reference architecture and a checklist for bounded agent autonomy.
speakers: David Victoria (Senior Cloud Architect, Caylent)

speakers: David Victoria (Senior Cloud Architect, Caylent)

title: Agentic commerce in production: multi-agent orchestration on AgentCore
abstract: A single agent that both advises and sells gets fragile fast. This session shows a production multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents, running for real Shopify merchants, where an orchestrator coordinates two specialists: a wellness advisor in a regulated domain and a commerce agent that owns decision and checkout. We walk the decisions that matter: orchestration topology, intent routing and handoffs, shared versus isolated memory across agents, where the action boundary and per-agent guardrails live, and the latency and token cost that coordination multiplies. A demo follows one conversation from advice to checkout. You leave with an orchestration pattern, and the code to implement it directly in your online store.
speakers: Matias Kreder (Engineering Manager, Ryz Labs)
Ricardo Ceci (Founder, VN Studios)

title: Beyond the GPU count: Engineering inference at scale
abstract: You have enough GPUs in your server to cover your software requirements. But is that all you need to consider? In a world where everyone is fighting for GPUs, picking the wrong server type is one of the most expensive mistakes an engineering team makes at scale. This session shares lessons running GPU inference across AWS and bare metal connected privately. You'll see how EKS Hybrid Nodes provides a single scheduling plane, failure modes, and how to use AI to accelerate decisions without replacing engineering judgement. Leave with a cloud and bare metal architectural pattern and a GPU selection framework covering workload fit and server tradeoffs.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater

title: Beyond the Docs: Operating Scoped VPC Endpoints in Real Environments
abstract: Scoped VPC endpoint policies look simple, until production traffic proves otherwise. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through real-world failures we've encountered while deploying account- and org-scoped endpoint policies and trace the identity flows, auth chains, and hidden dependencies behind them. Together, we'll explore a key lesson: endpoint policies evaluate the request that's actually made, not the request you think you're making. Bring your questions and experiences as we whiteboard the assumptions that lead to outages and learn how to spot them before they impact production.
speakers: Kenneth Attard (Enterprise Architect, Betsson)
Meg Ashby (Senior Security Engineer, Abnormal AI)

title: Think Beyond DevOps: SRE, SOC, and Compliance in One AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: As AI speeds up releases, continuous security control assurance and detecting threats in millions of telemetry signals get harder. We transformed AWS DevOps Agent into one agent for SRE, SOC and compliance, effectively addressing AI-era cloud security challenges in production. With AWS Config Conformance Packs for compliance-as-code and security MCP for finding triage, it produces point-in-time compliance and well-architected assessments, and drives alarm-triggered agentic SOC investigations within a controlled agent space, automating responses and keeping human-in-the-loop on high-risk mitigations only. You'll learn the methodology to design an agentic compliance and SOC solution that ports seamlessly into your own environment.
speakers: Richard Fan (Security Engineer, ExpressVPN)
Shaoyi Li (Lead Cloud Engineer, Pax Technology)

title: Ship Reliable AI Agents with Strands Evaluation and AgentCore Evaluations
abstract: Your AI agent works in demos, but can you trust it enough for production? How do you test behavior that can vary on every run, and catch regressions when prompts, models, tools, or workflows change? In this 300-level Code Talk, we'll turn real-world agent failure modes into representative test cases, evaluate both answers and actions, and add risk-based quality gates into CI/CD. Using Strands Evaluation and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, you'll leave this session able to design and implement an evaluation pipeline tailored to your own agents, backed by a public reference implementation you can adapt.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Guille Ojeda (Sr Innovation Architect, Caylent)

room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Guille Ojeda (Sr Innovation Architect, Caylent)

title: KYC in 90 Seconds: Real-Time Onboarding with AgentCore
abstract: Opening a bank account should take seconds, not days. This session shows how AI agents can speed up KYC while keeping the final decision under control, specialized agents that run on Agentcore Harness investigate identity, documents, fraud signals, and screening results, with checks running in parallel. AgentCore Gateway routes tool requests through Cedar policies before tools run, while deterministic rules decide whether a case moves forward or needs human review. The session follows a clean case, an ambiguous case, and a new risk event after onboarding. Attendees leave with a pattern for regulated agentic systems.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Avinash Dalvi (Technical Architect, Quantiphi)
S Logesh (AI Architect, ShellKode)
Poobalan P (Software Engineer 3, Factset)

title: Stop Rolling Back AI Agents: Production Patterns That Work
abstract: The demo shipped. The agent went live. Then someone pulled it back. 74% of organizations that have deployed an AI agent have rolled it back or shut it down, and the rate rises to 81% among those reporting fully mature guardrails. Getting agents into production got easier. Keeping them there without hurting customers did not. We'll walk through the failure patterns behind rollbacks: agents that fail silently, prompts treated as safety boundaries, and monitoring blind to non-deterministic failures. You'll leave with the patterns that prevent them: infrastructure-level guardrails, blast radius containment, and observability built for probabilistic systems.
speakers: Nadia Reyhani (Principal Enterprise Architecture, BHP)
Gunnar Grosch (Developer Advocate, -)
Kristine Armiyants (Head of Technical Advocacy & Marketing, Eleveight AI)

title: Lights, Camera, Fargate—A Reality-TV Startup Hardened for Scale on AWS
abstract: In six weeks on reality TV coding show The Full Stack, we built DataSwarm — a data-observability solution shipped as an open-source CLI with cloud-hosted data analysis and remediation. Great demo, wrong architecture. When real users arrived, the demo cracked. So we pivoted. Long-running agents moved off Lambda onto ephemeral ECS Fargate tasks. API keys swapped for firewalled Amazon Bedrock, feature-branched CI/CD with dev-to-prod promotion, and Next.js behind CloudFront, S3, and Lambda@Edge. We break down each tradeoff from first idea to first customer. Leave knowing how to tell demo-grade architectures from customer-grade ones — and when to make the jump.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Erik Hanchett (Senior Developer Advocate, Amazon Web Services)

title: The Agent Harness You Own on AWS for Regulated Industries
abstract: In regulated industries the model is easy; the governable, auditable, defensible agent is hard. AgentCore ships primitives, but the governance harness you own on top is the real work. We build the rails it does not give you: a fail-closed, blocklist-first permission gate where deny beats a broad allow; a hash-chained audit verifiable off-cloud; and a RACI gate binding every action to a named human. Each maps onto a managed AWS primitive — Identity, Guardrails, Evaluations, Lambda MicroVMs for isolation — naming where the primitive ends and your code begins. You leave with the rails.
speakers: Jacky Chan (CTO, Beever AI Limited)

abstract: In regulated industries the model is easy; the governable, auditable, defensible agent is hard. AgentCore ships primitives, but the governance harness you own on top is the real work. title: Eval-Driven LLM Routing: Cut Costs Without Losing Accuracy
abstract: This session shows how to build an eval-driven LLM routing system: harvest a production eval dataset, define accuracy KPIs using LLM-as-judge, set a non-negotiable accuracy floor as the practitioner's decision, benchmark candidate models, and generate a routing policy optimized for cost within that floor. Result: approximately 80% cost reduction at maintained accuracy. A reference architecture you can start implementing immediately.
speakers: Olivier Leplus (Senior Developer Advocate, AWS)
Luca Bianchi (Chief Technology and Innovation Officer, AWS AI Hero)

title: From Fragmented Infra to Golden Path: An Internal Developer Platform on EKS
abstract: Every team wanted to ship faster, but each was reinventing the same wheels: clusters, pipelines, infrastructure, access. So we built an internal developer platform on Amazon EKS — one golden path that lets product teams go from idea to running service without becoming Kubernetes experts. This is the honest story of that journey. We'll show how we used EKS as the foundation, Crossplane to provision cloud infrastructure through Kubernetes APIs, and Argo CD to drive everything through GitOps. We'll walk through the challenges that nearly derailed us and share what actually moved the needle. You'll leave with a realistic map of the terrain: what worked, what hurt, and what we'd do differently.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Johannes Koch (Principal Engineer Technical Architecture, FICO)

title: Pit Crew AI: Building Multi-Agent Cloud Operations on AWS
abstract: AI can generate code at racing speed, but production workloads still require continuous attention to security, reliability, cost, and operational risks. In this Code Talk, we build a multi-agent architecture on AWS inspired by a Formula 1 pit crew. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, MCP, GitHub, Jira, and Infrastructure as Code, we evolve from a single agent to a team of specialized agents for security, cost optimization, reliability, and observability. Through a live demonstration, you’ll see how agents turn cloud findings into engineering tasks. Attendees will leave with reusable architectures, orchestration patterns, and examples for cloud operations on AWS.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Pablo Inchausti (Senior Cloud Engineer, Caylent)
David Petrocelli (Senior Cloud Architect, Caylent)

title: The agent orchestration spectrum: Agents, Step Functions, or Lambda?
abstract: "Orchestration mode matters more for end user experience than just model choice. In this live-coding session, I build the same GenAI workload three ways: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Step Functions, and AWS Lambda durable functions - and show what each costs in latency, dollars, and debuggability on a production content platform. Leave with a reusable decision framework to match orchestration to your workload."
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Håkon Eriksen Drange (Principal Cloud Architect, Sopra Steria)

title: The agent orchestration spectrum: Agents, Step Functions, or Lambda?
abstract: "Orchestration mode matters more for end user experience than just model choice. In this live-coding session, I build the same GenAI workload three ways: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Step Functions, and AWS Lambda durable functions - and show what each costs in latency, dollars, and debuggability on a production content platform. Leave with a reusable decision framework to match orchestration to your workload."
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Håkon Eriksen Drange (Principal Cloud Architect, Sopra Steria)

title: Observable Agents with Lambda Durable Functions and OpenTelemetry
abstract: When AI agents run as long-lived, multi-invocation workflows on Lambda Durable Functions, standard observability breaks down. A single durable execution spanning five specialists producing independent telemetry, replays pollute logs with duplicates, and no tool can tell you which agents are failing across thousands of concurrent runs. We'll build a multi-agent purchasing coordinator with Lambda durable functions, instrument it with the OpenTelemetry plugin for one coherent trace across all invocations, and CloudWatch insights to answer fleet-wide queries with business context. Attendees leave with fully observable architecture and the investigation pattern from CloudWatch alarm to end-to-end traces and correlated log entries.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Raphael Manke (Senior Product Engineer, Dash0)
Gunnar Grosch (Developer Advocate, -)

title: Answering CX questions 10x faster with Amazon Connect Customer and Amazon Quick
abstract: Amazon Connect Customer generates a deep set of signals from every customer interaction. Sentiment, intent, conversation analytics, resolution outcomes. It's all there and Connect Customer gives you built-in tools to explore it. But we wanted to go further. We wanted anyone in the organization to ask questions about customer interactions in plain language and get answers instantly. So we paired Connect Customer's analytics data lake with Amazon Quick. In this session, we walk through how we did it, including how we handled cross-account Lake Formation access, and show how our broader team now asks questions and reshapes queries on the fly. 10x faster from question to action.
speakers: Kobe Xu (Cloud Architect, Deloitte)

title: Autonomous Remediation with OpenTelemetry and DevOps Agent
abstract: You instrumented everything. You have metrics, logs, and traces. And when production breaks a human still has to piece it together, tab by tab, signal by signal, under pressure. That is not an observability problem, it’s an automation problem. We'll show you an architecture on AWS that closes it. OpenTelemetry captures signals across EKS, ECS, and Lambda. AWS DevOps Agent runs the investigation, finds the root cause, and prepares the fix. By the time a human looks at it, the pull request is ready. Come learn the triggers, investigation loop, and guardrails you need before letting an agent touch production.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Jones Zachariah Noel (AWS Serverless Hero / Senior Developer Relations Engineer, New Relic)
Julia Furst Morgado (Principal DevRel Engineer, Dash0)

title: Sandboxing AI Agents on EKS: Isolation That Scales
abstract: AI agents execute untrusted code — one prompt injection away from data exfiltration. This session covers building graduated isolation for autonomous agents on EKS using the agent-sandbox controller. You'll learn why runtime tiers (runc → gVisor → Firecracker) map to different threat models, how SandboxClaim resources manage ephemeral agent lifecycle, and Cilium FQDN egress filtering that prevents exfiltration without blocking legitimate tool use. We'll whiteboard Karpenter NodePool design for gVisor-capable nodes, discuss cost tradeoffs between isolation levels, and share what breaks when you over-isolate. Leave with a production-ready isolation framework.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Adit Modi (Solution Architect, Lauren)
Ishan Modi (Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Avalara)

title: AI Writes the Code. Who Reviews the Reviewer?
abstract: AI coding assistants now write, refactor, and even review code at scale but who's actually accountable when something breaks in production? This session explores how AI has reshaped the code review process: faster first-pass reviews, AI-generated suggestions, and agentic tools running directly in CI/CD pipelines. We'll examine where AI genuinely improves review quality, where it creates false confidence, and why human judgment remains the deciding factor. You'll leave with a practical framework for combining AI speed with human accountability in your own review process.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Rossana Suarez (Engineer, Naranjax)

title: From Demo to Production: The Craft Behind AI Agents at Scale
abstract: Your agent reasons, calls tools, and demos beautifully. Then production happens. This session is about the craft that lives after the demo: the unglamorous engineering that separates agents that ship from agents that stay in notebooks. Using real AWS accounts and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, I'll walk through deterministic guardrails that make destructive actions impossible (not just discouraged), spend limits an agent can't prompt-inject its way past, evaluation you can trust, and the IAM that silently breaks first. You'll leave with a production-readiness framework for agentic systems—and honest stories about everything that failed on the way there.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Gerardo Arroyo Arce (Senior Principal Software Architect, West Monroe)
Diana Castro Cordero (Cloud Engieneer, Bac)

title: Cocktails to Code Building AI Bartenders with Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Plain-language AI orders fail if models hallucinate items that are out of stock. I built a reliable AI bartender grounded strictly in live inventory data. This session covers how an AI agent on Amazon Bedrock uses Strands Agents, AgentCore, and MCP tools to fetch real-time menus. We will dive into the serverless architecture, see what breaks during live text streaming, and evaluate the cost versus performance tradeoffs of production grounding. You will leave with a reusable pattern and the repository to build reliable, data-driven agents.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Jimmy Dahlqvist (Principal Cloud Architect, Sambla Group)

title: Lambda MicroVMs: The Missing Serverless Primitive for Multi-Tenant Agents
abstract: Lambda Functions are stateless and time out after 15 minutes. Fargate tasks are expensive to keep warm. When building multi-tenant agent platforms, I needed per-tenant isolation without per-tenant cost. Lambda MicroVMs solve this: Firecracker VM-level isolation, 8-hour stateful execution, auto-suspend when idle, instant resume on next request. This session walks through the architecture I built, replacing always-on containers with MicroVMs as per-tenant agent sandboxes. I'll share the tradeoffs, what surprised me, and a deployable pattern you can take home and ship.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Darshit Pandya (Senior Principal Engineer - Platform, Serko)

title: The AgentCore Governance Loop: Policy, Guardrails, Observability
abstract: Building an agent takes an afternoon. Operating it safely across a team takes architecture. In this session learn how to build a multi-agent reference platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and walk the full governance loop including cataloging agents for discovery, enforcing what they can do with Cedar policy at the gateway, filtering what they can say with Guardrails, and tracing behavior through observability. You will learn where the pieces integrate cleanly and where the seams break. You leave with a governance reference architecture you can adapt to any agentic workload, plus the lessons the documentation leaves out.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Harpreet Singh Siddhu (Lead Software Engineer, Penn Mutual Life Insurance)

title: Renaissance Dad: building an agentic learning app for my 9-year-old with Kiro
abstract: Werner Vogels told us to become Renaissance Developers — curious polymaths who blend disciplines and own what they build. I took it literally: as a dad, I used Kiro and agentic AI to build a learning app that helps my 9-year-old practice math and school lessons. In this session, I'll share the full architecture: an OCR agent that imports exercises from photos of school notebooks, an adaptive agent that personalizes difficulty, and a coaching agent that guides instead of correcting. We'll deep-dive into multi-agent orchestration patterns, vision model integration, spec-driven development with Kiro, and the guardrails required when your end user is a child. Attendees will leave with reusable agentic patterns applicable far beyond education.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Sylvain Bruas (AWS Ambassador, TEAMWORK)

title: Craft, Don’t Vibe, Your MVP
abstract: Many people today use LLMs only for code generation. The best teams embrace AI across all stages of the SDLC. The decisions made before building the first version of your product directly affect its viability and success. Rather than relying on vibe coding to make these decisions implicitly, agents can be used to evaluate architectural options, compare trade-offs and challenge assumptions before a single line of code is created. This session explores how high-performing teams are investing time capturing standards, patterns and expertise, making them available for agents to apply consistently. Learn from practical real world examples how AI is being used to accelerate the delivery of production-ready systems, rather than those that carry technical debt from day one.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Matt Lewis (AWS EMEA CTO, IBM)

title: Now serverless has servers. What now?
abstract: I spent years advocating for serverless, but as a CTO, I could not always see a viable path to bring it into certain business scenarios. In this talk, I share what has changed with the new AWS capabilities, why this can change the game for larger companies, and, along the way, I explore the concepts and how these services work in more depth to help us think about architecture with more clarity.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Evandro Pires da Silva (Cofundador, evandropires.com.br)

title: Designing for Operability: Catching Performance Gaps Before Scale
abstract: A training workload had plenty of GPU capacity, yet utilization remained low and training time kept increasing. The GPUs were healthy. The real bottleneck was upstream: the data pipeline could not feed them fast enough, leaving expensive accelerators waiting for work. This talk walks through how we traced that utilization gap, found where throughput was being lost, and identified the signals that could have exposed the problem earlier. Through this production experience, we’ll look at what it means to design for operability before scale, when performance, utilization, and cost problems are still easier to fix.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Jofia Jose Prakash (Principal Architect, Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI))

title: Architecting Enterprise Agents on Bedrock
abstract: Enterprise agents on Amazon Bedrock are complex distributed systems, combining models, tools, memory, and orchestration into something that has to behave predictably in production. In this session, I walk through practical architecture patterns for building enterprise-grade agents: multi-agent coordination, tool routing, session management, and hybrid workflows using AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda. Drawing from real production systems, I cover the trade-offs that matter most when moving agents from prototype to production, where reliability and scale actually get tested. Walk away with concrete patterns you can bring back to your own agent architecture.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Namrata Shah (Managing Director, Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association - (TIAA-CREF))
Ellliott Cordo (Founder/Builder, Data Futures Inc.)

title: Beyond Prompts: Crafting Production GenAI from Scratch
abstract: Building reliable GenAI applications requires deliberate systems engineering, not just prompt engineering. After collaborating with AWS Professional Services on an enterprise client, I learned how to build production-grade web apps the official AWS way. Bypassing basic buzzwords, we map a compound serverless conversational assistant engineered from scratch using AWS CDK, CloudFront, Cognito, API Gateway, and ⁠Amazon Bedrock. Examine how to handle real-world token streaming failures, manage state in DynamoDB, and implement strict Infrastructure as Code. Leave with complete source code and a concrete approach to balancing model performance against infrastructure cost in highly concurrent production environments.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Steven Leung (Senior Software Engineer, Versent)

title: AI Didn't Wait for Security: Now What?
abstract: AI didn't wait for your security review. Developers already ship code with agentic AI, coding assistants, and MCP servers without governance; blocking them lowers efficiency and leaves you falling behind. This builder-focused session dissects the architecture of a governed AI platform. You'll learn how to build a centralized MCP broker with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and Runtime, and how agent requests gain identity and permissions. You'll build and distribute a curated agentic skills catalog and reusable agentic blueprints. Finally, you'll see how AI SDLC frameworks bring consistency and higher-quality artifacts, with DevOps and security agents woven into key stages.
speakers: Stav Ochakovski (DevOps Engineer | AWS Hero, Eon)
Ran Isenberg (Senior Principal Architect, Palo Alto Networks)

title: Practical PKI for On-Prem Devices with IAM Roles Anywhere
abstract: Secure authentication of your humans and machines is a challenge every organization faces, especially if your proof of identity is not already in AWS. In this session, we'll talk you through multiple ways to set up or use PKI - such as Belgium's eID or a hardware key - to securely access AWS with phishing resistant authentication built using IAM Roles Anywhere. This will include live demos and code samples. By the end of the session we will stop worrying about plain text credential storage because we can use trusted hardware instead.
speakers: Ben Bridts (Principal AWS Technologist, Cloudar)

title: One-Way Doors: Launching a Regulated Financial Exchange on AWS in 2026
abstract: AWS turns 20 this year. Starting fresh in 2026 means navigating hundreds of services with no clear map for which decisions are one-way doors. I'll share how we built a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse from the AWS Organizations up. The full security stack (ControlTower, Config, GuardDuty, Security Hub, and IAM) built in the right order from day one. We almost walked through the wrong door. A pre-launch architecture review with our engineers and AWS solution architects caught it in time. Here's how to have that conversation before it's too late.
speakers: Margaret Valtierra (Technical Program Manager, Optex)

title: Scaling Multi-Cluster EKS Without Burning Your Infrastructure Budget
abstract: Managing hundreds of Amazon EKS clusters breaks standard multi-tenant architectures under the weight of shared control planes, noisy neighbors, and runaway cross-AZ data transfer costs. This interactive chalk talk skips the slides to whiteboard the painful realities of multi-cluster fleet topology at scale. We will dissect the architectural trade-offs between monolithic clusters and localized micro-clusters, mapping out exact blast-radius constraints. Bring your worst infrastructure bottlenecks; we will openly debate cluster life-cycle automation, shared VPC patterns, and cost-allocation frameworks, leaving you with a battle-tested blueprint to optimize fleet operations on Monday morning.
speakers: Sagar Utekar (Site Reliability Engineer, CrowdStrike)

title: Move your app to AWS Elastic Beanstalk and forget the ops
abstract: Running a production application should not mean owning the infrastructure under it. This lightning talk shows how AWS Elastic Beanstalk assumes ongoing operational responsibility for your applications — deployment, scaling, patching, monitoring, and upgrades — whether you bring source code, a container image, or an existing workload. In a few minutes, you will see how to identify which workloads are ready to move and what the path looks like, so your teams ship applications while AWS runs the operations underneath. You own the application. AWS owns the operational responsibility.

title: Optimizing Kubernetes in the Age of AI (sponsored by Zesty)
abstract: Agentic development dramatically reduces the cost of writing code, but it hasn’t removed the cost of operating it. Infrastructure teams are now responsible for the cost, performance, and reliability of workloads they didn’t build. In this session, we'll explore how these shifts are changing Kubernetes optimization. We'll discuss why CPU, Memory, and GPU resources are often miscalibrated, why native tools like HPA and Karpenter don't solve resource inefficiencies, and how platform teams can maintain cost accountability without slowing developer velocity. You'll leave with practical strategies to continuously optimize resources, improve utilization, and keep Kubernetes infrastructure cost-efficient as AI adoption scales. This presentation is brought to you by Zesty, an AWS Partner.

title: Don't build agents, build environments instead (sponsored by Modal)
abstract: The hard part of background agents is the background, not the agent. We'll talk about the common design that software factories have converged to and why building environments for agents is still hard. This presentation is brought to you by Modal, an AWS Partner.

title: Amazon ECS Gateway: Managed ingress for containerized applications
abstract: Amazon ECS Gateway is a new account-level resource that simplifies ingress for containerized applications by provisioning and managing networking infrastructure in your account. In this lightning talk, learn how platform teams define organizational networking standards once on a gateway and associate it with one or more clusters, creating a centralized way to govern how traffic reaches ECS services. Service teams simply opt in and inherit those standards with no networking expertise required. We cover host-based routing with Application Load Balancers, how up to 25 services can share an ALB to optimize cost, and how ECS provisions, scales, and removes ALBs as services connect and disconnect. We close with gateway routes, ALB metrics, and service action logs that give you full visibility into every operation ECS performs on your behalf.

title: Running compute-efficient workloads on Amazon EKS Auto Mode
abstract: Amazon EKS Auto Mode, powered by open source Karpenter, simplifies infrastructure management while optimizing compute resources. Karpenter provisions Amazon EC2 Instances based on the requirements of your workload. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll gain practical experience in advanced workload scheduling, continually compute optimization with Karpenter consolidation, explore AWS Graviton and AWS spare capacity through Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Whether you’re new to EKS Auto Mode, or an experienced operator you’ll learn best practices for running efficient workloads on Amazon EKS while simplifying Kubernetes cluster management.
speakers: Erez Zarum (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Dmitry Nutels (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Layered security for Amazon EKS: Patterns that scale
abstract: Kubernetes gives you powerful primitives for running workloads at scale, but its default configuration prioritizes flexibility over security. In this chalk talk, we work through a layered defense strategy for Amazon EKS: hardening the control plane, implementing least-privilege RBAC and pod security standards, securing the software supply chain, enforcing network segmentation, and building runtime threat detection. We'll discuss real-world patterns customers use to move from reactive security posture to proactive guardrails — covering both EKS Auto Mode and self-managed configurations. You'll leave with actionable strategies you can apply immediately.

In this builder's session, deploy an agentic AI application on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate and take advantage of what containers give you, including hardware-level task isolation, unlimited runtime for long-running agent conversations, VPC networking for secure tool access, and Service Connect for multi-agent communication. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.
speakers: Suguna Devarla (Software Dev Manager, Amazon)
Ashok Srirama (Principal Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)
Raj Bagwe (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS)
Shamanth Devagari (Delivery Consultant/Containers Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Sathya Balakrishnan (Sr. Manager, Solutions Architecture, Amazon Web Services)

title: Building resilient deployment pipelines with Amazon ECS
abstract: Every application has a different risk profile when you ship a new version. A payments API needs different safeguards than a marketing page. In this workshop, learn how to match Amazon ECS deployment strategies to your workload requirements. Configure blue/green deployments for services requiring instant failback, canary deployments for APIs where you validate with real traffic before full cutover, and linear deployments for gradual migrations that build confidence at each step. Integrate pause hooks for manual approvals and external validation, and set alarm-based triggers that automatically revert bad releases before customers notice. Bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Mike Rizzo (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Islam Mahgoub (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Amazon EKS incident response and remediation with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: When an incident hits, engineers lose time pivoting between kubectl, metrics, logs, and traces to find root cause. In this builder session, you'll drive the AWS DevOps Agent through a production-realistic incident end to end: detect the anomaly from observability signals, correlate metrics, logs, and traces to a root cause, and execute automated remediation with a human-in-the-loop gate. You'll wire the observability inputs the agent consumes, review its diagnosis journal, and validate recovery. Leave with a repeatable detect-diagnose-remediate-verify pattern and a permission-scoped remediation playbook you can adapt to your own clusters.
speakers: Balachandra Hebbagilu Nagaraj (Sr. Cloud Support Eng. (CONT), Amazon Web Services (AWS))
Frank Fan (Principal Container Solution Architect, AWS)
Swarna Kunnath (Senior Cloud Application Architect - AppMod, AWS)
Shyam Sunder Kulkarni (Sr. Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Luis Arcega (Sr Partner Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Building and securing AI agents on Amazon EKS
abstract: AI agents now generate and run their own code at runtime, turning secure agent execution into a platform engineering problem. Containers alone were not built to run untrusted, autonomous code safely at scale. In this hands-on workshop, you will build an agent on Amazon EKS using the Strands Agent SDK, MCP, and Amazon Bedrock, then progressively harden and operate it: run it with stronger workload isolation, apply controls over what it can access, establish scoped identity for secure communication, and manage its lifecycle in production. You will leave able to architect, deploy, secure, and operate production-ready agentic workloads on Kubernetes.
speakers: Aaresh Sharma (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect - Containers, Amazon Web Services)
Sai Charan Teja Gopaluni (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build a production multi-tier application on Amazon ECS
abstract: Real applications have frontends, APIs, workers, and databases that all need to communicate reliably. In this workshop, build a complete multi-tier containerized architecture on Amazon ECS from scratch. Configure service-to-service networking with Service Connect, implement per-tier autoscaling policies, deploy updates with automated rollback, and observe your application using CloudWatch Container Insights. Walk away with a working architecture you can use as a reference for your own workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Simone Tallevi-Diotallevi (Sr. Partner Solutions Architect, AWS)
Guillaume Delacour (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Deploy accelerated workloads with Amazon ECS Managed Instances
abstract: Amazon ECS Managed Instances let you run workloads on specialized EC2 hardware without managing the infrastructure underneath. In this workshop, deploy accelerated workloads across ML accelerators on fully managed compute. Dive deep into ECS capacity providers, learn how to optimize costs and horizontally scale accelerated workloads. Finally, we’ll monitor accelerators through CloudWatch Container Insights. Walk away with a working configuration you can adapt for your own accelerated workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: pradip kumar Pandey (Delivery Consultant, Amazon web services)
Sai Kumar Samala (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect, GenAI & Agentic Platform, Amazon Web Services)

title: From your first Amazon EKS cluster to a self-serve developer platform
abstract: The best Kubernetes platforms are invisible to the people who use them. Developers provision, deploy, and scale through self-service interfaces without needing Kubernetes expertise, while platform teams reclaim the cycles once spent on cluster operations and lifecycle management. That is the standard now that Amazon EKS is engineered to deliver. Come hear how EKS sees developer experience evolving: Auto Mode removing undifferentiated operational load through managed compute, scaling, and add-ons; EKS Capabilities exposing AWS services as governed, self-serve building blocks; and AI agents taking on operational workflows (upgrades, diagnostics, remediation) that platform teams have owned for years.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Jesse Butler (Amazon EKS, PMT, AWS)
Nirmal Mehta (World Wide Tech Leader Containers, Amazon Web Services)

title: Running AI agents you can trust on Amazon EKS
abstract: AI agents are rapidly moving from prototype to production, and running them at scale presents new challenges. Untrusted, AI-generated code executes in your environment. Many agents share the same infrastructure. Workloads spin up, act, and tear down constantly. Join this session to learn how to run agents securely on Amazon EKS with VM-level isolation, wire up the primitives agents need for tools, memory, and orchestration, and manage fleets of short-lived, bursty workloads. You'll also see how the same EKS platform you run your critical workloads on extends into the agentic era and where we're headed next.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Carlos Santana (Sr. WW Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: What's new and what's next for Amazon ECS
abstract: Amazon ECS keeps getting simpler to run and more capable at scale, and this session provides a product and engineering leadership view of where it is headed next. See how recent investments make ECS faster to deploy applications on, more cost-efficient, and ready for a new class of AI and agentic workloads. We'll discuss the range of compute options, from Fargate to Amazon ECS Managed Instances and how they provide customers choice and flexibility. You will leave this session knowing how to apply the newest ECS capabilities to your workloads today, and what to plan for as the roadmap unfolds.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Rayman Aeron (Director, Elastic Container Service, Amazon Web Service)
Alexandr Moroz (Product Manager, AWS)

title: Accelerate AI workloads with GPUs on Amazon ECS Managed Instances
abstract: Running GPU workloads in containers means choosing the right accelerator, right-sizing instances, and scaling without over-provisioning. Amazon ECS Managed Instances handles infrastructure lifecycle while giving you access to the latest GPUs and accelerators. In this session, explore how to launch GPU capacity with managed provisioning, scale based on real GPU metrics rather than CPU proxies, and automatically recover from hardware failures. Hear how a customer built and scaled their production AI infrastructure on Amazon ECS Managed Instances to serve GPU-backed workloads while optimizing cost and operational agility.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Abhishek Nautiyal (Principal Product Manager Technical-External Services, Amazon Web Services)
Raphael Beamonte (Director of Engineering, Ramp)
Olly Pomeroy (Specialist Solution Architect, Containers, Amazon Web Services)

title: Secure agents at scale on Amazon ECS with VM-level isolation
abstract: If you run agents, multi-tenant services, or regulated workloads on shared infrastructure, the isolation boundary is an important security consideration. This session shows how to design that boundary using VM-level isolation on Amazon ECS. You will leave knowing how to isolate tenants and untrusted agent workloads from one another, apply least-privilege execution toward compliance obligations, and run it all efficiently at scale. Whether you build agentic AI platforms or sensitive multi-tenant applications, you will walk away with a practical blueprint for strong isolation on ECS.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Ashok Srirama (Principal Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)
Nick Peters (Software Development Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: Accelerate application development with Amazon ECS Express Mode
abstract: What if deploying a containerized application on Amazon ECS required just your code and a few configuration choices? Amazon ECS Express Mode makes that possible by handling observability, networking, and security out of the box. In this session, learn how Express Mode accelerates development for individual developers and platform teams without sacrificing control. Discover practical techniques to optimize your workflows, enhance reliability, and reduce operational overhead. Leave with actionable strategies to increase development velocity using the latest Amazon ECS innovations.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Mike Rizzo (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Jay Russo (Software Development Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Mike Brandin (Software Engineer, Meta)

title: Building resilient Amazon ECS applications: a multi-layer approach
abstract: In this interactive chalk talk, we explore how to build resilient Amazon ECS architectures by examining failure modes across multiple layers of the stack. We walk through specific scenarios such as deployment failures, Availability Zone impairments, and dependency cascades that cycle tasks faster than you can debug them. We discuss architectural patterns, ECS capabilities for resilience, and common mistakes to avoid that turn minor issues into incidents. You'll leave with a concrete mental model for hardening your ECS services and a checklist you can apply to your own workloads.
speakers: Nitheesha Myneni (Senior Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Sai Kumar Samala (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect, GenAI & Agentic Platform, Amazon Web Services)

title: AI-accelerated migration from self-managed Kubernetes to EKS Auto Mode
abstract: Most teams start with one or two Amazon EKS clusters and grow into a fleet. AWS manages the control plane, but on standard EKS your team still owns version upgrades, add-ons, node lifecycle, and operational efforts. This session shows how to move that undifferentiated work to Amazon EKS Auto Mode, and how AI accelerates the migration itself. See how agentic tooling inventories your EKS clusters, translates node and add-on configuration, and flags what must change before you cut over. Learn patterns for enabling EKS Auto Mode with minimal disruption, then scaling the migration across your fleet in a fraction of the time manual work takes.
speakers: Aritra Nag (Specialist Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Ioannis Moustakis (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Strategies for agentic-ready architectures on Amazon EKS
abstract: As AI agents become first-class workloads, the platforms that host them must evolve. This session explores how Amazon EKS enables agentic-ready architectures — combining multi-tenancy isolation, dynamic scaling, and fine-grained security boundaries to safely run autonomous agent workflows at scale. We'll examine how platform engineering patterns born from SaaS modernization (control plane/application plane separation, tenant-aware networking, and cost allocation) translate directly to orchestrating multi-agent systems. Attendees will learn practical patterns to provision, isolate, and observe agentic workloads on Kubernetes while maintaining operational control and cost efficiency.
speakers: Omri Shiv (Senior Open Source ML Engineer, AWS)
ENG HWA TAN (Principal Solutions Architect (Containers), Amazon Web Services Singapore Pte Ltd)

title: Observability-driven scaling: Teaching EKS clusters to right-size themselves
abstract: Scaling container workloads reactively by waiting for CPU to spike or pods to crash leaves money on the table and risks user-facing latency. This chalk talk explores observability-driven scaling: using CloudWatch Container Insights, KEDA, and custom metrics pipelines to make Amazon EKS clusters anticipate demand before it arrives. We walk through real architectures where teams replaced reactive HPA with predictive scaling informed by business metrics, reduced over-provisioning by 40%, and cut P99 latency during traffic ramps. Bring your scaling headaches and we'll whiteboard solutions together.
speakers: Tiago Reichert (Principal Specialist SA, AppMod, AWS)
HC Lo (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Network observability on Amazon EKS: From coverage gaps to insights
abstract: As container workloads grow more distributed and interconnected, the network between them becomes the hardest thing to see. Traffic sprawls across pods, nodes, and AZs, quietly driving up cost through inter-AZ transfer and NAT processing, and when latency spikes, it is hard to tell which flows are responsible. This chalk talk explores how to close that gap with Container Network Observability, Network Flow Monitor, and OpenTelemetry-based Container Insights on Amazon EKS. See how to trace traffic across pods, nodes, and AZs. Learn how to attribute network cost and latency to the workloads driving them, and turn those signals into action.
speakers: Ikenna Izugbokwe (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Lukonde Mwila (Senior Product Manager, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: Architect production MCP servers on Amazon ECS
abstract: Your MCP server works perfectly on a single Amazon ECS task. Then agents multiply, sessions collide, and scaling breaks everything. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the infrastructure patterns that make MCP servers production-ready on Amazon ECS. We'll cover horizontal scaling with externalized session state, request routing, fine-grained authentication, and autoscaling based on agent request patterns. We'll discuss multi-service topologies where different tool categories run as independent ECS services behind a shared ingress layer. Bring your current MCP architecture, and we'll design the production upgrade together.
speakers: Piyush Mattoo (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Abhishek Nanda (Senior Modernization Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)

title: Reduce incident response time on Amazon ECS with AI observability
abstract: You get paged. Your ECS service is returning errors. You open six tabs, task logs, ALB metrics, deployment history, CloudWatch alarms, container health and start piecing together a timeline by hand. In this chalk talk, explore how AI-powered observability changes that workflow. See how CloudWatch Investigations ingests your existing telemetry, correlates signals across services and infrastructure, and produces root cause analysis in minutes instead of hours. Discuss how to structure logs and metrics so automated investigation actually works, and how Managed Daemons keep your collectors consistent without redeploying applications. Bring your incident response questions for an open discussion.
speakers: Sushanth Mangalore (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Bhupendra Washishtha (Senior Product Manager-Technial, External Services, AWS)

title: Decouple and scale Amazon ECS workloads with event-driven patterns
abstract: Not every container workload needs to run all the time. Some should wake up when an event arrives, process it, and stop. Amazon ECS makes this straightforward, but choosing the right trigger pattern matters. In this chalk talk, discuss how to connect events to containers using Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SQS, and AWS Step Functions. Walk through four common patterns: single-event task launch, queue-based consumer scaling, fan-out processing, and multi-step workflow orchestration. Explore how to handle failures gracefully with dead-letter queues and retry policies, and how Amazon ECS provides serverless compute for event-triggered deployments.
speakers: Masatoshi Hayashi (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, Containers, Amazon Web Services Japan G.K.)
Matthew Meckes (Principal Containers Specialist, Amazon Web Services)

title: The golden path for agentic workloads: safe by default on Amazon EKS
abstract: Every team is shipping agentic apps, and they are landing on your platform faster than you can review them. As the platform team, you own the blast radius: untrusted code, over-broad permissions, and unbounded egress you never signed off on. This code talk walks through the controls that let you say yes safely. See how to enforce VM-level isolation for workloads running untrusted or AI-generated code. Learn how to scope identity and network egress so an agent reaches only what it should. Discover how to codify these as policy so every new agent inherits the guardrails by default.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Dima Breydo (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Tsahi Duek (Principal Solutions Architect, aws)

title: Fleet-wide AIOps for Amazon EKS with the AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: Operating one EKS cluster is manageable. Operating a fleet of them is where the hard problems live: failures that surface far from their cause, VPC CNI IP exhaustion, Karpenter churn, and upgrades that stall across clusters. This chalk talk shows how AIOps and the AWS DevOps Agent bring order to operations at fleet scale. See how the DevOps Agent correlates signals across clusters to find root cause instead of chasing symptoms. Learn how it turns noisy telemetry into a diagnosis and a recommended fix. Discover the guardrails that let agents act on your fleet safely, with the blast radius bounded.
speakers: Sai Vennam (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Lucas Soriano Alves Duarte (Pr. Specialist SA Agentic Transformation, AWS)

title: Troubleshooting and recovering failed Amazon ECS deployments
abstract: Your Amazon ECS deployment just failed: new tasks will not launch, traffic is not shifting, and your team needs to ship an update now. In this code talk, we live-troubleshoot real failures step by step, showing how to diagnose the root cause, recover the service, and build guardrails that prevent repeat failures. We then go further, using the AWS DevOps Agent and ECS remote MCP tools to diagnose issues faster by correlating signals and surfacing likely causes. You will leave with a repeatable troubleshooting playbook for ECS deployments, both manual and AI-assisted.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Mikhail Shapirov (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS Partner Org, Amazon Web Services, Inc.)
Vikram Venkataraman (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc)

title: 5 Amazon ECS features that prevent common production incidents
abstract: Five configuration mistakes cause the majority of Amazon ECS production incidents. All five are fixable in under a minute. AZ spread off means one zone failure takes your service down. Short health check grace periods kill containers that are still starting. Disabled circuit breakers let bad deploys roll forward across every task. Default dependency timeouts turn one slow call into a cascading outage. Placement constraints pack tasks onto too few hosts. In this lightning talk, see the incident each feature prevents, the specific attribute to verify, and the fix. Leave with a production-readiness checklist your team can use before every release.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: David Ugarte (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: How Hertz Made Karpenter Smarter with autonomous AI-Driven Optimization (sponsored by Cast AI)
abstract: Hertz used Cast AI agents to make Karpenter much smarter: the agents autonomously analyze every workload, rightsize it, then continuously instruct Karpenter how to rearrange nodes to cut waste. Hertz's platform engineering team deployed this across their multi-cluster EKS fleet entirely through Terraform. Sonal will show the real numbers: where the extra savings hid, how infrastructure-as-code took onboarding from pre-dev to production, and what it takes to automate cost optimization at fleet scale without babysitting it. This presentation is brought to you by Cast AI, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Sonal kumar sinha (Principal Architect, Sonal Kumar Sinha)

title: Multi-tenant compute modernization with Amazon EMR on EKS
abstract: What does it take to run millions of diverse jobs a day across many tenants without costs spiraling or one bad workload taking down the fleet? In this chalk talk, we explore how organizations modernize a multi-tenant compute layer on EMR on EKS to serve batch analytics, streaming, ML, and agentic AI from one platform. We whiteboard the choices that make it possible: custom bin packing to mix heterogeneous tenant workloads efficiently, EKS provisioned control planes to sustain high job throughput per cluster, and Graviton to drive down cost per job. Bring your scaling challenges and we'll design solutions together.
speakers: Ifetayo Stewart (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Akshara Shah (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Multi-tenant SaaS and agentic apps on Amazon EKS
abstract: Amazon EKS has become the runtime of choice for ISVs building agentic SaaS, offering the control, workload isolation, and networking flexibility that managed runtimes cannot. The challenge is multi-tenancy: how do you run agent workloads for hundreds of tenants on shared infrastructure without blast radius, cost leakage, or isolation drift? In this workshop, build a multi-tenant agent deployment on EKS with tenant isolation across namespaces and network policies, IRSA-backed credentials per agent workload, and per-tenant observability via OpenTelemetry. Each lab ends with an isolation proof. Leave with a reference architecture you can apply directly to your cluster.
speakers: Kunal Ghosh (Sr SA, Strategic Accounts, Amazon Web Services)
Abraham Arellano (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Eliminate wasted compute capacity with Amazon ECS
abstract: Running containers on Amazon EC2 often means paying for capacity you never use, from idle instances to fleets that drift out of shape as workloads change. This chalk talk shows how Amazon ECS Managed Instances tackles that waste through consolidation and infrastructure optimization, automatically right sizing instances to real demand and repacking workloads off underutilized capacity. Work through practical scenarios on the whiteboard to see how these decisions play out and how instance selection and capacity provider design shape your monthly bill. Bring the cost and utilization challenges from your own clusters, because this session is driven by group discussion.

title: Enhanced container image access & distribution with Amazon ECR
abstract: Amazon ECR is trusted by millions to store and serve container images, but the way teams discover, trust, and consume container software is evolving fast. In this session, the ECR product team shares where container distribution on AWS is heading: making it easier to find the software you need, trust what you run, acquire it simply, and pull it privately and securely inside your own environment. Through practical examples, we'll explore new capabilities that help publishers reach customers at scale and help organizations govern and consume containers with confidence. Whether you publish container software or run it in production, you'll leave with a clear picture of how ECR is becoming the center of the container software supply chain.

title: Intelligent, right-sized compute on Amazon EKS
abstract: Running Kubernetes at scale is a constant trade-off between performance, availability, and cost. This session covers the year's advances in Amazon EKS compute: faster node provisioning and consolidation, finer control over how and when your data plane changes, and new capabilities that match capacity to what workloads actually use rather than what they request. Whether you run Karpenter directly or fully managed EKS Auto Mode, you will see how to cut waste, raise utilization, and get more predictable efficiency for demanding CPU, GPU, and AI/ML workloads. Expect practical patterns and live demos you can apply to your own clusters.

title: Defense-in-Depth for Containers on Amazon EKS: A Layering Story
abstract: On a default Amazon EKS cluster, a single pod is a compromise away from the whole cluster - shared node credentials, flat networking, implicit trust, open egress. In this code-first session we start there, then trace how EKS security grew layer by layer as the threat model matured. We rebuild an over-privileged workload live, adding one control at a time: scoped pod identity, admin and DNS network policies, and private certificate trust with zero-downtime CA rotation. We finish by running a lateral-movement attempt against the hardened workload and watching it fail at multiple layers — the whole point of defense-in-depth.

title: Accelerate platform engineering on Amazon EKS
abstract: Platform teams struggle to balance developer velocity with operational efficiency. Self-service platforms promise faster delivery, but require orchestrating multiple tools, managing infrastructure complexity, and maintaining governance. In this workshop, you'll build an Internal Developer Platform using Amazon EKS Capabilities, which provides fully managed Argo CD for continuous deployment, ACK for AWS resource management, and kro for Kubernetes resource orchestration. You'll deploy polyglot applications, implement progressive delivery strategies, and automate infrastructure management while leveraging AI to boost productivity. Leave with practical experience in platform engineering patterns to ship faster without sacrificing control. You must bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Sebastien Allamand (Sr. Specialist Solution Architect, AWS)
Shani Adadi Kazaz (Serverless & Containers Specialist, Amazon)
