title: Amazon EKS: Infrastructure as code, GitOps, or CI/CD
abstract: Explore diverse architectures for deploying workloads including agents on Amazon EKS. Learn about secure software supply chain automation options including CI/CD pipelines, IaC (using Terraform & CDK), and GitOps patterns with Argo CD. Discover how Amazon EKS Capabilities, a suite of fully-managed platform features for deployments and resource orchestration eliminate operational overhead for building on Kubernetes. You will understand how these approaches complement each other from developer, architect, and operator perspectives. Get insights on selecting the right deployment strategy based on team structure and skill sets, and learn how to effectively combine DevOps and GitOps patterns to match your needs.
speakers: Alessandro Germer (Senior SDE, AWS)
Sebastien Allamand (Sr. Specialist Solution Architect, AWS)

title: Amazon EKS: Infrastructure as code, GitOps, or CI/CD
abstract: Explore diverse architectures for deploying workloads including agents on Amazon EKS. Learn about secure software supply chain automation options including CI/CD pipelines, IaC (using Terraform & CDK), and GitOps patterns with Argo CD. Discover how Amazon EKS Capabilities, a suite of fully-managed platform features for deployments and resource orchestration eliminate operational overhead for building on Kubernetes. You will understand how these approaches complement each other from developer, architect, and operator perspectives. Get insights on selecting the right deployment strategy based on team structure and skill sets, and learn how to effectively combine DevOps and GitOps patterns to match your needs.
speakers: Alessandro Germer (Senior SDE, AWS)
Sebastien Allamand (Sr. Specialist Solution Architect, AWS)

title: Cloud-native Java on Amazon EKS
abstract: Learn how to build cloud-native Java applications based on best practices, and discover ways you can optimize application performance for fast startup and efficient resource usage in containerized environments. In this builders’ session, gain hands-on experience as you learn how to reduce memory overhead, lower cold start latency, and achieve sub-second startup times when building Java applications on Amazon EKS. You will also learn how to use Amazon Bedrock to analyze profiling and thread dump data to uncover performance patterns and generate optimization insights.
speakers: Andrei Shakirin (Senior Sloution Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Dumitru Pascu (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Yuriy Bezsonov (Senior Partner Solutions Architect, AWS)
Sascha Moellering (Principal Specialist SA for AI-DLC, Amazon Web Services EMEA Sarl)
Laura Schlosser (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Optimize analytics workloads on Amazon EKS for performance and cost
abstract: The analytics landscape is undergoing a shift as global data volumes grow at unprecedented rates. This rapid growth, combined with rising demand for real-time analytics, is driving organizations to modernize and optimize their data processing pipelines and analytics workloads. EKS’s cost-performance and scalability make it the best place to run these workloads. In this workshop, you will learn hands-on how to optimize EKS for Spark & Kafka workloads using different Karpenter configurations, Spot and Graviton instances, and NVMe volumes. You will also explore observability best practices and granular cost visualization per job. You must bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Sundar Shanmugam (Sr. Cloud Infrastructure Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Ramesh Mathikumar (Principal Consultant, Amazon Web Services)

title: Inside Amazon EKS: the resilient foundation for critical workloads
abstract: Real-time financial systems, large-scale AI, and mission-critical platforms run on Kubernetes, and they demand a robust engineering foundation. This session goes under the hood of what makes Amazon EKS the backbone for the most demanding workloads. See how cellular isolation contains blast radius and EKS Provisioned Control Planes eliminate downtime during peak operational periods, backed by an industry-leading SLA as clusters scale into large fleets. Learn how EKS Auto Mode integrates with Application Recovery Controller zonal shift to protect the control plane and running pods during an impaired Availability Zone, keeping critical applications available with no extra configuration.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: George John (Principal Product Manager, Amazon)
Sri Saran Balaji Vellore Rajakumar (Principal Engineer, Amazon)
Shane Corbett (Container Specialist, AWS)

title: ML, automotive, and robotics simulations at scale on AWS Batch
abstract: Simulation and ML workloads share a hard problem: they must burst to enormous scale, run to completion reliably, and do it without a standing fleet draining budget between runs. This session shows how AWS Batch orchestrates large-scale simulation and training pipelines end to end. See how AWS Batch schedules and scales compute on demand, so jobs run when needed and nothing sits idle otherwise. Learn how simulation outputs flow through a shared data lake into GPU-accelerated training, closing the loop between data and models. Discover the orchestration and scheduling patterns that keep a real customer's high-throughput pipeline efficient.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Peter Dachnowicz (Principal Technical Account Manager, Amazon)
Nikita Buldakov (Sr. Product Manager Technical - External Service, AWS)
Jason Rupard (Principal Engineer, AWS)

title: Deep dive into networking architectures for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes
abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore hybrid networking design patterns for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes. We’ll cover different IPAM and routing strategies for hybrid pod networks, including Cilium BGP control-plane integration with your on-premises infrastructures. We’ll also explore various load balancing and Kubernetes services networking options for your hybrid nodes. Additionally, we’ll deep dive into the new Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway, demonstrating how it simplifies pod-to-pod communication, webhook connectivity, and AWS service integration across cloud and on-premises environments - without requiring changes to your existing network infrastructure.
speakers: YoungJoon Jeong (Sr. Container Specialist SA, AWS)
Sheng Chen (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect - Infra Modernization, Amazon Web Services)

title: Deep dive into networking architectures for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes
abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore hybrid networking design patterns for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes. We’ll cover different IPAM and routing strategies for hybrid pod networks, including Cilium BGP control-plane integration with your on-premises infrastructures. We’ll also explore various load balancing and Kubernetes services networking options for your hybrid nodes. Additionally, we’ll deep dive into the new Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway, demonstrating how it simplifies pod-to-pod communication, webhook connectivity, and AWS service integration across cloud and on-premises environments - without requiring changes to your existing network infrastructure.
speakers: YoungJoon Jeong (Sr. Container Specialist SA, AWS)
Sheng Chen (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect - Infra Modernization, Amazon Web Services)

title: Scale, optimize and deploy inference with Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode
abstract: Accelerated workloads make node provisioning challenging. Picking the wrong instance, scheduling constraint, or disruption policy impacts GPU utilization and drives up costs. This deep dive covers how Amazon EKS provisions and scales accelerated compute for real inference workloads, whether you run managed Auto Mode or self-managed Karpenter. See how both select across GPU and accelerator families and honor topology-aware scheduling. Learn the NodePool and disruption settings that keep utilization high without hurting latency-sensitive serving. Discover how Dynamic Resource Allocation and GPU sharing squeeze more inference out of every device, plus accelerator-aware node repair that keeps long-running jobs healthy.
speakers: Erez Zarum (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Sheetal Joshi (Principal SA, AWS)

title: Breaking down batch inference with Ray Data on Amazon EKS
abstract: Batch inference is more than running a model over a large dataset. In this interactive chalk talk, we build an end-to-end batch inference architecture on Amazon EKS one component at a time. We examine when to use Spark with Ray Serve and when Ray Data can unify preprocessing and inference. Along the way, we address data sharding, storage and data movement, GPU scheduling, autoscaling, batch sizing, checkpointing, retries, observability, security, isolation, and cost. Attendees will leave with a practical decision framework and a production architecture for operating reliable, scalable batch inference with Ray Data and the KubeRay Operator.
speakers: Andy Palmer (Director, Technology, AWS)
Vara Bonthu (Principal Open Source Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)

title: Scale financial risk simulations with AWS Batch and Amazon ECS
abstract: Financial institutions run millions of simulations overnight to price options, stress-test portfolios, and satisfy regulators. Scaling those workloads means balancing queue depth against compute cost. AWS Batch on Amazon ECS eliminates that tradeoff — containers scale elastically, Spot instances cut compute cost, and job orchestration handles retries and memory tuning without custom scripts. In this chalk talk, walk through a production architecture where a quantitative hedge fund runs its entire research compute on AWS Batch. Then open the whiteboard and discuss how to apply these patterns to your own pricing engines, VaR calculations, or scenario analysis workloads.
speakers: Boris Litvin (SA, Amazon)
Matthieu Bonville (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Customize and serve models at scale on Amazon EKS
abstract: Serving and customizing models in production often involves running expensive GPUs at high utilization, maintaining low latency as traffic spikes, and scaling to demand without over-provisioning. Increasingly teams are doing it on Amazon EKS. This session covers how to efficiently run GPU workloads, select the right accelerator for each workload, and apply optimization techniques that increase utilization and lower costs. Explore model customization through fine-tuning and RAG, and serving and autoscaling patterns that keep inference fast and efficient. See how hybrid workloads span cloud and on-premises GPUs with EKS Hybrid Nodes and where AWS is investing next.
speakers: Sajjan Gundapuneedi (Senior Software Development Manager, Amazon)
Christina Andonov (Principal SA, AWS)
Salva Jung (CIO, LG Uplus)

title: Move Fast With AI Agents Without Betting the Business (sponsored by MontyCloud)
abstract: You are under pressure to put AI agents to work fast, without betting the business. Everyone is racing to build agents, but no one is governing them. MontyCloud is an AI-native, autonomous CloudOps platform built on one conviction. As agents become easy to create, value moves to trusted execution. Walk away with a blueprint for turning insights into governed workflows, and governed workflows into trusted outcomes. See a live demo where any agent, model, or tool acts only with the right context, identity, policy, approvals, and cost controls. Learn why the unit of value is the governed workflow. This presentation is brought to you by MontyCloud, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Eric Morrissey (Director of Sales Engineering, MontyCloud)

title: Enterprise-Grade Outcomes. Within Reach for Growing Businesses. (sponsored by Accenture)
abstract: Discover how Accenture Edge for AWS helps growing organizations (under $3B in annual revenue) achieve the same transformative outcomes as larger enterprises through pre-built, outcome-driven solutions designed for speed, simplicity, and value. We are taking enterprise-grade talent and tools and making them accessible and approachable. Translation: Big outcomes at lower costs thanks to pre-configured solutions. Hear real examples of customers that accelerated cloud adoption, reduced costs, strengthened security, and modernized faster with Accenture and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Dusshyant Roy (Managing Director, Accenture)
Chris Wegmann (AABG Accenture CTO, Accenture)

title: Accelerating cost optimization on AWS
abstract: Finding and implementing cost optimization recommendations sustainably require constant monitoring and action. Join this session to learn how you can accelerate your optimization outcomes while maintaining flexibility in how savings are distributed across your organization. See how you can also measure, share and continuously improve your results.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Mary Nachimov (Sr. Technical Product Manager, AWS)
Jimmy Yang (Principal Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Autonomous operations: reducing MTTR at scale, feat. BMG Bank
abstract: Operations teams face a growing volume of production incidents, but investigating root cause manually is slow and doesn't scale. At Banco BMG, one of Brazil's most established financial institutions with more than 9 million customers, roughly 350 operational events occurred daily, each investigation taking hours. In this lightning talk, see how AWS DevOps Agent began investigating these events autonomously, reducing root cause identification from hours to minutes. Learn to integrate the agent with your observability tools, correlate telemetry, logs, and code, and turn every investigation into compounding efficiency that lowers MTTR.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Everton Queiroz (IT Executive, Banco Bmg)
Matheus Arrais (WW Tech Lead, CloudOps, AWS)

title: How 2 Billion Records Became One Data Product at Verisk (sponsored by Senzing)
abstract: Every insurance data product, underwriting or claims, hinges on one question: is this the same person or organization across systems? Verisk answers it once, at scale, treating the answer as a data product. This session unpacks how Verisk used AI-powered entity resolution on AWS to turn fragmented, siloed, acquisition-inherited data into one reusable identity asset, a proprietary entity ID appended across policies, claims, and enrichment data, not another MDM project. A five-person team built this across 2 billion records and 400 million identities with sub-second response. That data commands premium value, and identity became infrastructure, not a cleanup project. This presentation is brought to you by Senzing, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Gurpinder Dhillon (Head of Data & AI, Senzing Inc)
Gurshish Dang (Head Enterprise Data Mgmt, Verisk Analytics)

title: From Workloads to Agents: Rethinking Cloud Resilience (sponsored by Cohesity)
abstract: Under the shared responsibility model, you own the security and recoverability of your entire cloud estate - and that estate now includes AI agents. In this session, HUB International will share their experiences.​ Agents are becoming core infrastructure, executing actions across interconnected systems at machine speed. Yet most organizations can't recover agent memory, credentials, or configurations any better than they could recover a corrupted server a decade ago. Join us to see how Cohesity's resilience platform extends AWS-native protections to agents and infrastructure alike, so risk doesn't outrun your ability to recover. This presentation is brought to you by Cohesity, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Theresa Miller (Senior Director, Technical Marketing, Cohesity)
Monsef Elalamy (Senior Director, Cloud & Infrastructure, HUB International)

title: Give Your Best Engineers Back to the Roadmap, Not the Pager (sponsored by NeuBird)
abstract: Forty percent of engineering time goes to firefighting instead of the roadmap you funded. The problem isn’t a lack of dashboards or headcount, it’s that these engineers are forced to act as the glue across these fragmented tools. Between incidents, an autonomous Production Ops Agent keeps working. It deepens its model of your environment, right sizes observability spend, and turns every incident into a captured fix nobody has to relearn. This session shows how NeuBird AI has helped teams recover 200 plus engineering hours a month and cut incident costs 60 percent or more, not by hiring more people or buying more dashboards, but by giving one agent the job of running production so your senior engineers can go back to building it. This presentation is brought to you by NeuBird, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Ara Zarifian (Forward Deployed Engineer, NeuBird)

title: From AI-Assisted Engineering to Autonomous Operations (sponsored by Dynatrace)
abstract: As enterprise AI matures, the opportunity extends far beyond software development. Join United Airlines, AWS, and Dynatrace to discover how insights powered by AI, full stack cloud observability, and runtime intelligence are helping engineering and operations teams improve reliability, accelerate delivery, and reduce operational complexity. Learn how leading organizations are using real-time data to automate investigations, predict issues before customer impact, and move toward autonomous operations. The session will cover real-world adoption lessons, AI governance considerations, and practical steps to balance automation with accountability while unlocking greater value from AI across the software lifecycle at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Dynatrace, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Jon Griffiths (Field CTO, Dynatrace)
Margarita Rubio (MD - Crew and Catering Technology, United Airlines)

title: Manage cloud costs and AI spend with AWS Cost Management
abstract: Join this breakout to learn how AI is helping teams manage cloud costs more effectively, and why managing the cost of AI itself is becoming just as important. We cover AWS FinOps enhancements across both dimensions. On the "AI for FinOps" side, learn how your team can operate more efficiently through automation and agentic workflows. On the "FinOps for AI" side, see how you can access and manage your AI spend with granular cost data and governance. Walk away with a repeatable governance model as you scale AI with confidence.
speakers: Matt Berk (Principal TAM, AWS)
Bowen Wang (Principal Product Manager Outbound, Amazon Web Services)
Jordi Espasa Clofent (FinOps Director, Aviv Group GmbH)

title: Fewer Incidents, Faster Fixes: Expert-led Cloud Operations on AWS
abstract: Automation can close tickets, but it takes human expertise to understand your business, anticipate what's coming, and make the judgment calls that keep your cloud resilient at scale. See how AWS combines deep human expertise with AI-powered capabilities to go beyond automated remediation. AWS cloud experts, armed with intelligent tooling and deep environmental context, proactively identify risks, guide architectural decisions, and help your team navigate complex challenges automation alone can't solve. Through real-world examples, see how this expert-led approach reduces incidents, accelerates resolution, and frees engineers to focus on innovation.

title: Stop fighting fires: operations that prevent incidents
abstract: The best incident is the one that never happens, yet most teams stay stuck firefighting. Learn to collect the right operational signals beyond just observability and use AI to spot problems before they page anyone. We'll cover auto-healing and remediation with traditional techniques and AI agents that catch misconfiguration before production. You'll discover how early-warning systems spot issues before customers do, and how agentic investigation turns past incidents into ranked recommendations that prevent future ones. Walk away with actionable steps to start building proactive operations.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Isaiah Salinas (Sr. WW Specialist SA, CloudOps, AWS)
Ania Develter (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Best practices for agentic-driven operations
abstract: AI agents are moving from assistants to operators, but how do they actually work within your operational workflows? Understand the architecture of agents that detect anomalies, diagnose root cause across distributed systems, and execute remediation like rollbacks, scaling, and traffic shifts. Learn how agents reason over telemetry, sequence actions, and determine when to escalate. Explore best practices for shaping agent behavior through guardrails, approval gates, and feedback loops as core design elements. Leave with a framework for evaluating where agents should act autonomously versus where human judgment remains essential.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Dave Schnorr (Assoc. Dir Observability Engineering, Best Buy)
Bill Fine (Senior Product Manager, Amazon)
Metanat Hooshsadat (Principal Software Engineer, AWS)

title: Improving operations with agentic AI
abstract: Your operational telemetry is growing faster than your team. Learn how agentic AI can work across your observability stack, correlating metrics, logs, and traces to detect issues, identify root cause, and initiate remediation without waiting for a human to connect the dots. Explore patterns for agents that triage alerts, reduce noise, surface actionable insights, and execute operational runbooks. See how to integrate agents into your monitoring and incident response workflows, from signal detection through resolution. Leave with practical approaches to reduce mean time to recovery, eliminate repetitive toil, and give your team time to focus on reliability improvements that matter.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Elliot Markowitz (Vice President, Verisk Analytics)
Greg Eppel (Principal WW Specialist, Generative AI, Amazon Web Services)
Igor Sedukhin (Director, AWS)

title: Observability and operations in the AI era
abstract: Generative AI broke the assumptions traditional monitoring was built on, and teams struggle to keep non-deterministic systems predictable, explainable, and affordable. This session opens on that challenge, then shows how the newest observability capabilities give you visibility into model quality, cost, and agent behavior across your AI stack, using traces, spans, and confidence scoring, illustrated with real customer patterns.
speakers: Andres Silva (AWS) (Principal Specialist Solutions Artchitect, Amazon)
Pratul Chakre (Head of GTM, CloudOps, Amazon Web Services)

title: Turn security logs into actionable intelligence
abstract: Security teams drown in logs but struggle to investigate fast. In this hands-on session, turn raw security telemetry from CloudTrail, S3 access logs, and VPC flow logs into actionable intelligence with Amazon CloudWatch. We'll centralize logs in the CloudWatch Unified Data Store, then query across sources to investigate real scenarios: after-hours data access, credential misuse, and exfiltration patterns. You'll build a security dashboard that surfaces who did what, from where, and when. Walk away with reusable queries and dashboards you can deploy in your own accounts, moving from reactive log search to proactive security visibility.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Rafael Pereyra (Principal Security Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Erik Weber (Sr. WW Specialist SA, Cloud Operations, AWS)
Thomas Sceifers (Senior Technical Account Manager, AWS)

title: Cut through Kubernetes signal overload with unified observability
abstract: Kubernetes at scale buries teams in high-cardinality signals that traditional pipelines truncate or split across separate backends, so the answer you need is never in one place. In this hands-on builders session, you send OpenTelemetry metrics and logs from an EKS cluster into Amazon CloudWatch, deploy Container Insights, and decide which signals actually matter. You use automatic resource enrichment to build your own dashboards and alerts, deciding what to alert on and why rather than running pre-made scripts. You leave knowing how to cut through high-cardinality noise and set up alerts that drive action.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

title: Keep your open source observability, move to managed scale
abstract: Teams standardized on Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch should not have to abandon their tools to get scale and lower operational overhead. In this hands-on builders session, you will learn about instrumentation and collection powered by OpenTelemetry, and explore that telemetry into managed open source services: ship metrics to PromQL in Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces in Amazon OpenSearch Service, and correlate all signals in Amazon Managed Grafana. Own your telemetry pipelines end-to-end with open standards and AWS managed services.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

title: Turn raw telemetry into answers with OpenTelemetry
abstract: Raw telemetry arrives noisy, unlabeled, and hard to query, so teams waste time cleaning data before they can act. In this hands-on builders session, you set up OpenTelemetry for metrics, logs, and traces from a live sample application, then use Amazon CloudWatch pipeline processors to enrich and normalize the data in flight. You build the enrichment rules, explore results with natural language query, and leave with a reusable pattern for turning raw signals into analysis-ready telemetry.

title: I didn't know my AI agent was doing that!
abstract: AI agents are non-deterministic - they can burn tokens, stall, or drift into wrong behaviour with no warning, and teams often have no visibility until something breaks. In this hands-on builders session, you will use Amazon CloudWatch to observe live agents from both the console and your IDE: trace what an agent actually did, spot failures, and surface anomalous behaviour. Working with real agents - a production agent and a custom chatbot - you build the detection and alerting yourself and leave able to apply it to the agents you run in production.

abstract: Security teams cannot manually hunt through every log for the one event that matters, and threats move faster than analysts can query. In this hands-on builders session, you will build automated detection and response on your security telemetry: metric filters and anomaly detectors that flag suspicious activity, findings routed to alarms that page the right people, and automated remediation that acts before an analyst logs in. After tuning detections to cut false positives, walk away with a pipeline that watches your logs so your team does not have to.

abstract: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how spend maps to business outcomes. In this builders' session, you'll get hands on with the latest cost management capabilities for Amazon Bedrock. You'll tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control Gen AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. You'll then query new product metadata in CUR2 and visualize cost-per-million-token trends in CUDOS. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

title: Embed FinOps into your CI/CD pipelines
abstract: Cost overruns from infrastructure changes often go undetected until after deployment, making shift-left cost governance a critical capability for platform and DevOps engineers. This builders' session guides attendees through constructing a working cost estimation gate integrated directly into a CI/CD pipeline. Using AWS CodePipeline, the AWS Pricing Calculator, and CloudFormation change sets, attendees build a pipeline stage that evaluates infrastructure cost impact at pull request time and enforces configurable spend thresholds before deployment proceeds. Bring a laptop to complete hands-on exercises with expert guidance in a small-group setting.

Using AWS CodePipeline, the AWS Pricing Calculator, and CloudFormation change sets, attendees build a pipeline stage that evaluates infrastructure cost impact at pull request time and enforces configurable spend thresholds before deployment proceeds. Bring a laptop to complete hands-on exercises with expert guidance in a small-group setting.

title: From pod to multi-region: Resilient workloads on Amazon EKS
abstract: Building resilient workloads on Amazon EKS requires thinking in layers, from pod-level reliability to multi-region failover. In this chalk talk, explore each layer: Pod Disruption Budgets and Topology Spread Constraints, Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode for fast node recovery, EFS vs EBS for stateful workloads, AWS Backup for cross-region protection, and Route 53 with ARC for region switching. Debate active-active vs active-passive tradeoffs and validate RTO/RPO targets with Resilience Hub.
speakers: Ioannis Lioupras (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Jean-Francois Landreau (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Orchestrate failover and failback for effective Disaster Recovery
abstract: Failing over one app is easy — orchestrating failover and fail back across interdependent apps is where DR plans break. Real recovery requires dependency-aware orchestration across your entire stack. In this code talk, we live-code full-stack Region failover using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) Region switch: building sequenced workflows so databases switch before app tiers, validating steps with health checks, rehearsing with practice runs, and safely reversing the sequence for fail back. Leave ready to replace your paper DR plan with coded, repeatable recovery and measured RTO to prove it.
speakers: Ashish Panwar (Senior Technical Account Manager, Amazon)
Jason Brown (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Observe AI agents beyond your perimeter
abstract: Your developers are burning tokens on AI coding agents with zero visibility. Claude Code and OpenAI Codex run on laptops, outside your perimeter, with no telemetry reaching your observability backend. In this session, we fix that. Using native OpenTelemetry export and Amazon CloudWatch's OTLP endpoint with a single bearer token, with no collectors, no sidecars, no credential wiring, we ship metrics (token usage, cost, productivity), logs (tool decisions, errors), and traces (agent reasoning chains) directly from developer machines. Then we build a live dashboard with per-team cost attribution and anomaly alerting, all queryable with PromQL. Walk out ready to deploy in minutes.

title: Orchestrate multi-layer disaster recovery for critical workloads
abstract: Your AZ recovery plan and your Region failover plan were probably built by different teams, tested at different times, and have never run together. The result: untested failover paths that turn outages into incidents. Explore how to build a unified recovery framework with Amazon Application Recovery Controller. From zonal autoshift for rapid single-AZ mitigation, to Region switch for cross-Region failover, learn how ARC unifies both layers into a single orchestrated approach. Then discover how to run automated resilience tests that continuously validate your recovery posture before a real event forces the question.
speakers: Darshan Patel (Sr. Technical Account Manager, AWS)

title: Where's the slowdown? Build observability from frontend to databases
abstract: When an application slows down, the cause can hide anywhere from the frontend to the database, and siloed tools make teams guess. In this workshop, you will build full-stack observability across application, infrastructure, and database layers, bringing RDS and Aurora signals and database logs into one store and correlating them with audit activity. You decide what to trace and build the dashboards that connect a symptom to its root cause. Leave with skills to trace any slowdown across layers in a single pane.

abstract: An AI agent can answer every request successfully and still make the wrong decision. In this builders’ session, you will build an end-to-end audit loop on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using Amazon CloudWatch for traces, AgentCore Evaluations to apply an LLM-as-a-judge against business rules, and AWS DevOps Agent to investigate alarms. Then watch a customer service agent refund a customer without required human approval, while traces show zero errors. Reconstruct the decision, and see the loop automatically surface what error monitoring misses.

Discover how the next-generation AWS Resilience Hub handles the tedious work like mapping dependencies, assessing posture, and preconfiguring resilience tests, leaving your teams to focus on closing the gap between the system you think you operate and the one you actually do.

title: Building a Cost Governance framework for AI that scales
abstract: AI spend starts with model tokens but often misses costs from agent runtimes, memory, data, and supporting services. In this chalk talk, we'll map an AI workload from architecture to bill, then apply a practical framework to measure, attribute, optimize, and govern its cost and value. Using AWS FinOps Agent as an example, we'll examine how its architecture creates costs across Amazon Bedrock and supporting services, and how to govern those costs. Bring your AI cost challenge and leave with a model that helps FinOps and engineering teams assign ownership, find waste, and set effective controls.

title: Simplify multicloud: manage and monitor VMs in one place
abstract: As your compute spreads across multiple clouds and on-premises, every environment ends up with its own agents, tooling, and consoles. Patching, access, and monitoring happen a different way in each one, and no single view shows what is running or how it behaves. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to bring every instance under one operational model with AWS Systems Manager, no matter where it runs, and then get metrics and logs from all of them into Amazon CloudWatch. We work through the tradeoffs and patterns that hold at scale. Leave able to run and observe your whole fleet as one.
speakers: Jose Ponce Martinez (Sr. Technical Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Nereida Woo (WW Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

abstract: Most teams turn on AI-driven operations before thinking about how they will scale. We discuss areas your strategy should consider that will allow you to scale to additional capabilities more quickly and where Frontier Agents could help. Leave with a foundational framework and a maturity discussion for your team.

Rovan Omar (Principal Technologist, AWS)

title: Modernize confidently with production intelligence
abstract: Static code analysis tells you what to modernize. It doesn't tell you what breaks when you do. Runtime dependencies, real traffic patterns, and operational risk stay invisible until cutover, when surprises are most expensive. AWS DevOps Agent adds the missing ingredient: production intelligence fed directly into your AWS Transform modernization plan. The result is assessments grounded in reality and migrations that stay safe through execution. In this chalk talk, we discuss how to incorporate production intelligence from DevOps Agent into an automated migration pipeline by Transform Custom. Bring your modernization challenges to discuss.
speakers: Venugopalan Vasudevan (Pr. Specialist SA, AWS)
Harvinder Nagpal (WW Specialist, Amazon)

title: Tag once, find anything: scale resource tracking across accounts
abstract: Inconsistent tags make it hard to see what runs where. In this code talk, we build automation that keeps tagging clean at scale: a tagging schema that defines the keys and values that matter, an AWS Config rule that flags non-compliant resources, and an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that remediates them automatically or with approval. We also query untagged resources across thousands of resources and multi accounts. Leave with working code you can adapt for cost allocation, access scoping, and AI-assisted root-cause analysis.
speakers: Mohamed Othman (Sr. Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Nisha Notani (Snr Technical Account Manager, AWS)

title: Recover and prove your full stack without disrupting production
abstract: Meeting your recovery time and point objectives is non-negotiable. For your critical workloads, that means orchestrated, tier-aware recovery within minutes, with a plan you've actually tested. Most teams haven't, because testing often means disrupting production. So, the plan stays on the shelf and RTOs stay theoretical. In this session, see AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery replicate servers into low-cost staging and recover the full stack in the right order, in minutes, then rehearse the same failover without production noticing. Learn how to run non-disruptive recovery drills against your own environment and prove your RTOs before an incident does it for you.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Pritam Bhalerao (Sr. Product Manager, Amazon Web Services Inc.)

title: Evolve your observability for the agentic era
abstract: Your agent passed every test last week. Today the same prompt returns a different, pricier answer, and nobody can say why. Agents drift as models and prompts change beneath them, and a green dashboard won't catch it. This session covers what evaluations ("evals") are: automated checks that score an agent's output for quality, accuracy, and cost. You'll learn how an eval-driven loop catches that drift on live traffic, traces it to the change that caused it, compares models and prompts, and attributes spend down to the agent and user, so regressions get blocked before they reach production. Then see how Amazon CloudWatch Omni does this across AWS and other clouds, covering your agents and applications in one place.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Nikhil Dewan (Head of Product Management, Amazon)
Matheus Arrais (WW Tech Lead, CloudOps, AWS)

title: Elevate your observability with OpenTelemetry on AWS
abstract: Getting full visibility across your stack shouldn't mean stitching together disconnected tools and proprietary formats. When you standardize on OpenTelemetry with AWS, you get rich, unified telemetry from metrics, logs, and traces across your containers, Kubernetes clusters, AI workloads, and everything in between. Collect deep telemetry using OTLP ingestion, PromQL querying, and automatic enrichment with Amazon CloudWatch's native OpenTelemetry. No fragmented data. No vendor lock-in. Just one telemetry foundation that gives you the context you need to understand what's happening across your entire environment. Learn how to achieve richer data, unified observability, and a production-ready architecture that scales with you.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Michael Wishart (WW BD, Observability, Amazon Web Services)
Steve McCurry (Principal Product Manager, AWS)

title: Wrong, Not Broken, & Why your Observability should know the difference
abstract: Agentic applications need different access patterns and tooling than traditional apps. Teams often stitch together several tools and act as the human orchestrator just to answer a basic question: is my agent doing what the business needs? That gets harder when the agent runs on one cloud and calls models or APIs on another. In this session, we show how CloudWatch Omni brings AI agents and applications across clouds into one view, accelerating root cause whether its due to performance, availability or response quality.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Imaya Kumar Jagannathan (Principal Customer Success Specialist, Observability, AWS)
Nikhil Kapoor (Principal Product Manager - Technical, AWS)

title: High latency! Is it the code, the container, or the host?
abstract: Your app is slow, but is it the code, the container, or the underlying host? When your stack spans clouds, hybrid, and on-prem, correlating application performance to infrastructure health means jumping between tools and guessing at root cause. Join this session as we walk through how to map application signals such as traces, errors, and latency directly to the infrastructure, regardless of where it runs. You'll see how to pinpoint whether the problem is your app or the compute it sits on, without stitching dashboards together manually.
speakers: Oliver Smyth (Principal SDE, Amazon)
Rodrigue Koffi (Sr. Specialist SA, Observability, AWS)

title: Logging strategy for agentic investigations
abstract: Most logging strategies get built one team at a time. Each team picks its own destination and format, so an AI agent investigating an incident has to search across accounts and reason over a dozen schemas. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard a CloudWatch logging design that centralizes logs and enriches them on ingest with service context, so your agents start every investigation with what they need. We'll debate what to transform at ingest versus keep raw, and which logs earn hot storage. Bring the log setup you run today and we'll redraw it with you.
speakers: Siddharth Bhate (Principal Product Manager - Technical, Amazon Web Services)
Brad Gilomen (Sr. Manager Observability, AWS)

title: Best practices for building an observability strategy in the age of AI
abstract: Most observability strategies were built for a pre-AI world and are no longer enough. Your data foundation remains critical, but the way you use that data is changing fast. In this chalk talk, we explore what stays the same, what must evolve, and what's new as AI reshapes observability. We'll cover the shift from static dashboards to dynamic experiences, from reactive alarms to AI-driven insights, and the new questions you need to answer, like how well your agents are performing. Join us as we share what AWS is learning as we embrace AI-led observability.
speakers: Helen Ashton (Sr. Customer Success Specialist (Observability), AWS)
Adam Rubinsky (Senior Product Manager - Technical, AWS)

In this chalk talk, we explore what stays the same, what must evolve, and what's new as AI reshapes observability. We'll cover the shift from static dashboards to dynamic experiences, from reactive alarms to AI-driven insights, and the new questions you need to answer, like how well your agents are performing. Join us as we share what AWS is learning as we embrace AI-led observability.
speakers: Helen Ashton (Sr. Customer Success Specialist (Observability), AWS)
Adam Rubinsky (Senior Product Manager - Technical, AWS)

title: Learnings from resilience testing in AWS
abstract: In this talk, we'll describe some of the resilience testing we've been doing in AWS. We'll talk a bit about the Game Day Region, why it exists, and how we use it. We'll talk about the types of test we run, the philosophy behind them, and some takeaways that you, our customers, can also apply.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Gavin McCullagh (Senior Principal Engineer, Amazon)

title: Optimize container observability to reduce cost
abstract: At scale, container environments generate metrics and logs that increase both cost and noise for engineering teams. This session explores architectural strategies for managing observability data across containerized workloads using OpenTelemetry. Learn how to control metric cardinality, design sampling policies that preserve critical signals, and evaluate managed backend tradeoffs. You'll leave with a framework for building cost-aware container observability.
speakers: Vikram Venkataraman (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc)
Carlo Bergonzini (Software Development Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Optimize container observability to reduce cost
abstract: At scale, container environments generate metrics and logs that increase both cost and noise for engineering teams. This session explores architectural strategies for managing observability data across containerized workloads using OpenTelemetry. Learn how to control metric cardinality, design sampling policies that preserve critical signals, and evaluate managed backend tradeoffs. You'll leave with a framework for building cost-aware container observability.
speakers: Vikram Venkataraman (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc)
Carlo Bergonzini (Software Development Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Instrument a service with OpenTelemetry
abstract: In this live demo, we take an uninstrumented service from zero observability to correlated metrics, logs, and traces in minutes using Open Telemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Walk through the shortest path to production-grade instrumentation: SDK configuration, collector setup, signal routing, and surfacing the first actionable insight.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Phani Kumar Lingamallu (Pr. Partner Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Agentic AI Needs Agentic Infrastructure: Autonomy on Amazon EKS (sponsored by ScaleOps)
abstract: Enterprises now ship software that reasons and acts on its own. The infrastructure underneath still waits for a human to edit YAML. This session makes the case that autonomous workloads demand autonomous infrastructure, and shows what it looks like on Amazon EKS today: agents held to fractional GPU allocations that track real consumption, pod requests that stay honest as behavior drifts, and Karpenter consolidating nodes fed by accurate signals. You'll hear how enterprises run this in production with ScaleOps, and where autonomous resource management goes next. Leave with a blueprint for infrastructure that manages itself. This presentation is brought to you by ScaleOps, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Gilad Elyashar (CPO, ScaleOps)

title: Trusting an Autonomous Agent With Your Production Environment (sponsored by NeuBird)
abstract: The biggest barrier to autonomous operations isn't capability, it's trust.Handing an incident to an autonomous agent raises a fair question. How do you know it is not guessing from raw log lines. This session shows how NeuBird AI reasons over your live environment and shows the causal chain behind every root cause, not a coincidence in the metrics. We’ll examine the guardrails that make production deployment safe: VPC-native execution, zero external data retention, complete auditable reasoning paths, and human-gated action approvals. Learn how to safely transition from human-driven triage to trusted, autonomous production operations on your own terms. This presentation is brought to you by NeuBird, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Andrew Lee (Technical Marketing Engineer, NeuBird)

title: Drive AI at full speed: The enterprise blueprint (sponsored by HashiCorp)
abstract: AI gave teams a faster car. It did not fix the roads. As teams create more applications, infrastructure and complexity, the challenge shifts from moving faster to operating smarter. Enterprises need context to understand what is happening, agency to act across the tools they already use, and control to keep speed from becoming chaos. In this session, see how Terraform and Vault together with Kubernetes, Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore and IBM Concert to standardize delivery, secure access and connect application context to action across hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by HashiCorp, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Kyle Ruddy (Senior Director, Product Marketing, HashiCorp, an IBM company)
Cole Morrison (Head of Brand Story & Principal Evangelist, HashiCorp)

title: Monitor and optimize costs for Amazon Bedrock
abstract: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how that spend maps to business outcomes. In this lightning talk, see how to tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Adam Richter (Senior Optimization Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Build a per-tenant observability stack for Agentic SaaS
abstract: Multi-tenant ISVs need per-tenant observability that traditional dashboards can't deliver — aggregated metrics hide the tenant causing the problem, and shared traces don't tell you whose agent misbehaved. In this session, build a per-tenant observability stack for agents. You'll instrument agent invocations with tenant-aware traces and session replay, build tenant-scoped dashboards that surface noisy neighbors and latency outliers, and configure alerting that fires on per-tenant thresholds rather than aggregate signals. By the end, you'll have an observability setup that scales with your tenant count without a separate data pipeline — and patterns to extend it as your agent architecture grows.
speakers: Rocket . (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Matt Tichenor (Senior Product Manager, AWS)
Venkatavaradhan Viswanathan (Sr.Partner Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Yoginder Sethi (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))
Ulli Hinze (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: 5 Questions Terraform, OpenTofu, and CloudFormation Can't Answer (sponsored by Spacelift, Inc.)
abstract: Every infrastructure change is one run: code, an engine, a plan, an apply. That run is still a wall of unstructured log text, and the questions about your estate go unanswered. Five to ask of your IaC: Did Terraform, OpenTofu, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, or Ansible run it, and does it matter? Where does the time go, and can OpenTelemetry tracing show you? What happens outside the engine: providers, state, policy-as-code, drift, queue time? What about unmanaged resources, the half of your AWS account no run ever touched? Who gets self-service, and can an AI agent be trusted with an apply? This presentation is brought to you by Spacelift, Inc., an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Jonah Kowall (SVP Product and Design, Spacelift)

title: How Infor Uses AWS Agentic AI to Transform Cloud Operations at Scale
abstract: Infor (a Koch Industries company) runs one of the largest enterprise footprints on AWS. As that footprint grew, manual release gates, incident investigations, and periodic security assessments couldn't keep pace. Hear how Infor is adopting AWS agentic AI to reshape operations: DevOps Agent for incident triage and release readiness, Continuum for continuous security validation, and the Well-Architected Agentic AI Lens for production guardrails. Leave with a blueprint for agentic AI at scale.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Durga Dash (VP Cloud Operations, Infor (US), LLC)
Saurabh Saxena (Sr Principal, AWS, Amazon)

title: Autonomous SRE: AWS DevOps Agent in Financial Services
abstract: In this session, learn how a large financial institution deploys AWS DevOps Agent as an autonomous SRE teammate to reduce incident investigation time from hours to minutes and free engineering teams from reactive firefighting. Explore the architecture spanning CloudWatch, Splunk, GitHub, and Slack integrations, and see how the agent correlates telemetry across data sources to identify root causes and generate mitigation plans. Walk away with practical patterns for deploying agentic operations in regulated, compliance-sensitive environments.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Prem Dhayalan (Senior Distinguished Engineer, Capitalone Bank)
Saurabh Saxena (Sr Principal, AWS, Amazon)

title: Take Action on Operational Issues with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: There's a big difference between an agent that gives you a remediation plan and one that can carry it out. In this session, see how AWS DevOps Agent goes beyond investigation to take action on operational issues across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments. Learn how directed actions and defense-in-depth controls govern what the agent can do, with layered opt-in, per-action approval, and built-in guardrails that keep operations safe
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: Diagnose Complex Workloads with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: Follow an investigation of a complex workload using AWS DevOps Agent. Trace an application-level symptom through multiple layers of your environment across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments. See how DevOps Agent analyzes telemetry, correlates signals across layers, identifies likely root causes, and delivers targeted remediation. Learn practical techniques for investigating workloads and reducing the manual effort of diagnosing problems across distributed environments.

title: Resolve Incidents and Validate Releases with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: Follow an issue from detection to resolution. In this builder's session, see how AWS DevOps Agent investigates incidents across AWS, multicloud, and on-premises environments, analyzing telemetry and correlating signals to pinpoint root causes and deliver targeted remediation. Then use the AWS DevOps Agent release management agent to review the code changes for production readiness before they reach your customers. Every review is informed by production intelligence that AWS DevOps Agent continuously builds from your environment.

title: Catch bad agent behavior before your users do
abstract: AI agents are non-deterministic. The same prompt can call the wrong tool, pick up bad context, or quietly degrade and you won't know until users feel it. Amazon CloudWatch Omni gives agents a first-class observability home built on open standards. Instrument an agent and trace every LLM call, tool invocation, and reasoning step. Run built-in evaluators to score response quality, then compare configurations against golden datasets. Correlate agent behavior with the services it depends on and investigate in natural language. Leave able to evaluate, debug, and operate agents with confidence.
speakers: Manish Dhawaria (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Observe AI agents and workloads end to end
abstract: Get hands-on with Amazon CloudWatch Omni, the next evolution of CloudWatch that monitors your AI stack end to end, from the agent all the way down to the self-hosted inference workload serving it, converging application and agent observability into one AI-powered solution. Instrument an agent, trace its execution, and run evaluations against golden datasets. When something degrades, explore auto-discovered topology and golden metrics to pinpoint where latency or errors creep in. Navigate from alarm to the responsible inference workload, and let Omni's AI-powered investigation trace the root cause.

title: Observe your applications and agents in one place
abstract: Traditional monitoring tools weren't built for the complexity of modern agentic and distributed applications. Teams juggle siloed dashboards, fragmented logs, and disconnected signals with no unified way to troubleshoot across agents, applications, and infrastructure. Amazon CloudWatch Omni is an AI-powered observability experience organized around your teams and the applications they run, combining OpenTelemetry interoperability with CloudWatch scale. See how you can troubleshoot applications faster and manage agents with confidence using automatic service discovery, dependency mapping, built-in evaluations, and natural-language investigation — all from the Omni UI, your IDE, or your favorite tools.

title: Build full-stack observability for agents and apps
abstract: When your applications include AI agents that reason, plan, and act autonomously, observability has to evolve too. Disconnected tools and siloed signals slow teams down right when speed matters most. In this chalk talk, we walk through real scenarios and trace an agent's chain of thought across services, correlating agent failures with infrastructure, and using natural-language investigation to cut resolution time. We diagram how service discovery, dependency mapping, evaluations, and IDE-native telemetry come together so you can ship agents with confidence.

title: Monetizing your applications with AWS
abstract: In this session, learn how to transform your finished application into a revenue-generating SaaS product. Learn about analyzing your cloud infrastructure, choose pricing models, and instrumenting code for usage metering. You'll see how to manage the complete billing lifecycle, from subscription management and invoicing to tax calculation and payment processing. Walk away with a clear path to accelerate your time-to-market and start charging customers.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: Find the waste hiding in your accelerator fleetÂ
abstract: GPU and AI accelerators are the most expensive resources your teams run â€” and the hardest to observe when shared across teams. Most platform owners can't tell which workload is using which device, whether it's working or idle, or what a stalled run is costing per hour. When something degrades, teams find out after a crash or a surprise bill.Â This lightning talk explores how to spot what's sitting idle, pinpoint a failing device without sacrificing the healthy ones around it, and prioritize fixes by how much spend you can recover.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater

title: Troubleshoot Workloads End to End with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: Application issues can originate anywhere across the stack, from compute and container environments to networking, data, and AI services. In this session, see how AWS DevOps Agent investigates issues end to end across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments, analyzing telemetry and correlating signals across layers to pinpoint root causes and deliver targeted remediation. Learn how teams troubleshooting complex workloads can resolve issues faster and spend less time moving between tools and data sources.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater

title: Investigate Incidents Across Teams with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: Production incidents typically involve multiple teams, but tooling and investigations are often siloed. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS DevOps Agent meets teams where incident response already happens. See how engineers can interact with the agent directly from tools like Slack, consolidating investigation activity, findings, and recommended actions alongside team communication. Bring your multi-team incident patterns and discuss approaches to faster, more connected incident response across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments.

title: Build better, review faster: AI-Powered Well-Architected reviews
abstract: Periodic reviews can't keep pace with infrastructure that changes daily. In this hands-on workshop, stand up the AWS Well-Architected Agent for continuous, goal-driven reviews across a multi-account environment. Configure agent profiles, cross-account role chaining, and business goals that prioritize across Cost Optimization, Security, Resilience, and Performance pillars. See how the agent enriches Trusted Advisor, Compute Optimizer, and Resilience Hub signals with cross-pillar trade-off analysis. Run pre-deployment reviews against CloudFormation, CDK, and Terraform, then remediate through AI-generated SOPs. Wire recommendations into CI/CD via the Well-Architected API. For architects, platform engineers, and operations leads who want always-on architectural governance in their delivery lifecycle.

title: Allocate shared AWS infrastructure costs to your business units
abstract: Shared Amazon S3 buckets, Amazon EKS clusters, and network resources improve efficiency but can obscure which applications and business units drive spend. In this session, learn how to attribute shared costs based on actual usage. Follow a practical example using AWS Split Cost Allocation Data for S3 and EKS and Flexible Cost Allocation for networking. Then use AWS Cost Categories and Data Exports to combine each business unit’s share of storage, compute, and networking spend into a unified view. Walk away with a repeatable approach to showback and chargeback across your shared AWS environment.
speakers: Erik Nestorovic (Sr. Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Take control of how AWS credits are allocated across your accounts
abstract: In this lightning talk, learn how to split any credit into precise amounts and transfer them to the accounts that need them. We walk through real-world workflows in the Console and API, show how split credits work seamlessly with sharing and pausing for full lifecycle control, and demonstrate how to replace monthly chargeback spreadsheets with a 5-minute workflow. Walk away with a playbook for giving every team a predictable credit budget as your organization scales.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater

title: End-to-end resilience for your cloud workloads
abstract: In this session, learn how to continuously assess and validate the operational resilience of your end-to-end business services using AWS Resilience Hub. See how GenAI agents automatically discover and map your application dependencies to give you a holistic picture of your resilience posture. Get actionable recommendations to close gaps, generate regulatory compliance artifacts to meet your compliance needs, and put it all to the test with end-to-end resilience testing to prove it.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater

title: Recovering AWS Graviton workloads with orchestrated Disaster Recovery
abstract: You moved to AWS Graviton for better price-performance, but is your disaster recovery keeping pace? A recovery that lands on the wrong architecture, or brings tiers up out of order, turns a routine failover into an outage. In this chalk talk, whiteboard with disaster recovery experts how AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) now protects Graviton-based (arm64) Linux servers and recovers them onto Graviton instances, keeping the architecture intact end to end with nothing extra to configure. Then design a recovery plan that brings your application back tier by tier, in the right order, with wait times and critical-server gates. Bring your toughest arm64 and recovery-order questions, and leave with a DR design you can drill on Monday.

title: Building eval-driven observability for AI agents
abstract: Multi-agent systems fail in ways your dashboards cannot show: one agent hands off bad context, another retries, and the API still returns 200. In this live coding session, start with a multi-agent app on LangGraph, Strands, and CrewAI, and instrument it with OpenTelemetry and OpenInference. Trace it from the first prototype run, evaluate agents on demand with LLM-as-judge evaluators, A/B test prompt and model variants before promoting to production, pull production traces into a versioned dataset, reproduce the failure locally, and ship the fix. All from your IDE, without switching tools.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Sudhir Kumar (Sr Sofware Dev Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Raviteja Sunkavalli (Sr. WorldWide Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Scaling operations with MCP, ACP, and A2A
abstract: Operational complexity doesn't scale linearly but your approach to managing it can. In this chalk talk, we'll use AWS DevOps Agent to explore three protocols shaping how operations teams work at scale: MCP (connecting to operational data and actions), ACP (delegating tasks to purpose-built agents), and A2A (coordinating across autonomous agents). We'll discuss how protocol choice affects decision-making, when to extend capabilities vs. delegate, and how to design architectures that grow with your operational footprint. Leave with a clear mental model for when to reach for each protocol and how they fit together.
speakers: Babu Samayapuram Suthanthira Raju (Global Solutions Architect, AWS Singapore Pte. Ltd)
Jyothi Madanlal (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

Jyothi Madanlal (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Optimize AI apps on Amazon Bedrock for cost, latency, and control
abstract: As AI workloads scale, engineers face complex trade-offs between cost, latency, and response quality. This code talk explores advanced optimisation techniques for production AI applications on Amazon Bedrock: prompt engineering, model selection, caching, and context window management. Through live coding, attendees examine the reasoning behind each design decision, observe cost impact via AWS Billing and Cost Management, and learn to instrument apps to detect performance regressions. Understanding the tokenomics of your AI stack is essential to operating efficiently at scale.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Andy Brown (Sr Manager, FinOps, AWS)
Steph Gooch (Principal Tech Advocate, AWS)

title: Go headless: managed harness to custom DevOps orchestration
abstract: Your AI agents need production-grade orchestration, but should you own the loop or let AWS handle it? We build one on-call responder three ways: an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness for a managed loop with built-in memory and tool routing, AgentCore Runtime for full control, and AWS DevOps Agent as a batteries-included DevOps harness. Then we build the shape most teams land in: your own orchestrator, DevOps Agent composed in headless over remote MCP and A2A. Bring your challenges and leave with patterns for building composable, robust pipelines that automate complex DevOps workflows end-to-end.
speakers: Priyatam Mudivarti (Sr Specialist Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Simon Guo (Principal Software Engineer, Amazon)

title: When agents run code: sandboxes for reliable DevOps
abstract: LLMs hallucinate. Code doesn't. When your AI agent investigates a production incident, some answers demand computation, not just reasoning. In this code talk, we crack open the sandbox in AWS DevOps Agent: an ephemeral, investigation-scoped Linux environment where the agent writes and runs code inside a Lambda MicroVM with read-only AWS access and zero lateral blast radius. We'll discuss how networking allowlists, pre-installed packages, and executable skills give you deterministic, auditable results for log parsing, metric correlation, and multi-source analysis. Bring your problems and we'll whiteboard the isolation boundaries live.
speakers: Simon Moore (Software Development Manager, AWS)
Chetan Suri (Sr. Specialist TAM, Cloud Operations, AWS)

title: Rethink release management for the agentic coding era
abstract: GitOps was designed for human-speed change. Agentic coding tools now generate pull requests faster than any team can review and safely release. Your release process is the new bottleneck. In this code talk, we'll live-code a GitOps release workflow where AWS DevOps Agent acts as an intelligent release manager, validating the results through a release pipeline at every promotion gate. Instead of manual approvals, DevOps Agent uses production intelligence (runtime dependencies, service health, deployment risk) to make real-time go/no-go decisions. Learn how to wire DevOps Agent into your GitOps reconciliation loop so releases match the velocity of agentic code generation without sacrificing safety.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Arun KM (Principal Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Carl Caum (Senior Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

speakers: Arun KM (Principal Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Carl Caum (Senior Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build-time context for faster agentic incident response
abstract: AI agents can fix production issues, but only with the right context. In this talk, an AI agent builds a feature and, in the same pull request, creates the context it needs on call: instrumentation, alarms, dashboards, and skills, all as code. Then you break the live app. Watch an agent use those skills with Amazon CloudWatch Omni and AWS DevOps Agent to triage, find the root cause, and ship the fix. Leave with patterns that give agents the context to operate what they build.
speakers: Jared Nance (Principal Software Engineer, AWS)
Arun Chandapillai (Sr. GenAI SA, AWS)

title: Correlate database query latency to user impact
abstract: Diagnosing performance degradation across distributed applications requires more than isolated database or application metrics. It demands correlated, end-to-end telemetry. This code talk demonstrates a scenario that unifies database performance signals with application-layer telemetry using OpenTelemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Learn how to implement trace-to-query correlation, design log aggregation patterns for accelerated root cause analysis, and build metric relationships that surface bottlenecks across the full stack. You'll be able to connect a slow database query to its downstream user impact.
speakers: Phani Kumar Lingamallu (Pr. Partner Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Alex Livingstone (Principal Specialist Solutions Architect, Cloud Operations, AWS)

title: Pinpoint latency in microservices with distributed tracing
abstract: Diagnosing latency across a high-scale Amazon EKS environment is complex when pods scale dynamically and trace context fails to propagate across service boundaries. In this code talk, we instrument containerized microservices with OpenTelemetry, propagate context across service hops, and correlate spans, metrics, and logs in Amazon CloudWatch. Live coding shows how a single slow request reveals the exact container and code path responsible for degradation, using targeted span attributes and exemplars to make Kubernetes-scale traces navigable. You'll also see the trade-offs behind sampling strategies and collector deployment topologies that affect overhead, fidelity, and cost at production scale.
speakers: Kevin Lewin (Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Carlos Henriquez Quintana (Principal Software Dev Engineer, AWS)

title: Build a fully managed open source observability stack on AWS
abstract: You want open standards without the operational burden of self-managing backends. In this code talk, we live-code a complete open source observability architecture: instrument a service with OpenTelemetry (auto and manual), configure the OTel Collector pipeline, and route metrics to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces to Amazon OpenSearch Service. Walk through each integration decision from SDK selection to collector topology, and leave with a working, production-ready stack built entirely on open source standards with zero infrastructure to manage.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Anirudha Jadhav (Sr. Software engineering manager, AWS Opensearch)
Lucas Vieira (Sr Customer Success Observability Specialist, AWS)

title: Close the gap between code and production
abstract: Why is it so hard to connect a production alert to the code change that caused it? Metrics and traces reveal something is wrong but stop short of the function responsible. Developers guess which deployment introduced the regression, manually correlating dashboards with recent commits. Meanwhile, AI coding agents that could help write fixes are blind to runtime behavior. In this code talk, we'll explore how to close the gap between observability signals and the code your team owns, what new signals make that connection possible, how developers and AI agents can consume them, and what changes when observability reaches the code level.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk

title: Multicloud in the Real World: Financial Services, Healthcare, and Manufacturing (sponsored by Oracle)
abstract: Oracle AI Database@AWS gives organizations a new way to bring mission-critical Oracle data closer to their applications, analytics, and AI services in AWS. This session shares a clear overview of the multicloud value proposition, including application proximity, operational simplicity, enterprise performance, security, and access to AWS services. Three Oracle industry leaders will explore what that value looks like in practice. Hear how financial institutions can strengthen fraud detection, risk management, and customer experiences; how healthcare organizations can generate trusted clinical and operational insights; and how manufacturers can improve forecasting, supply chain decisions, asset performance, and operational efficiency. Leave with a practical understanding of Oracle AI Database@AWS and concrete examples of how multicloud can support industry-specific AI and business outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Oracle, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Edwin Upson (Senior Vice President, Oracle)

title: Escaping IIoT Pilot Purgatory: Why Your Database Breaks at Scale (sponsored by Tiger Data)
abstract: Seventy-four percent of industrial IoT projects stall somewhere between pilot and production. The hard part is that the pilot worked. That is exactly what makes the failure so difficult to diagnose. Pilots succeed because a few hundred sensors over a few weeks fits comfortably in almost any database. Production does not. Storage costs compound faster than the budget that approved them, ingest hits a cliff with no warning, and the real-time dashboard that sold the project turns into a loading screen. See where industrial systems and typical AWS pipelines reach their limits and how to scale beyond them. We’ll explore a proven architecture using AWS IoT Core, Amazon Kinesis, AWS Lambda, and a single Postgres database to support more than one million connected devices reporting every second. This presentation is brought to you by Tiger Data, an AWS Partner.

title: Powering Interactive Agents with Live Context (sponsored by Materialize)
abstract: How do you keep an agent's understanding of the world fresh enough for it to act on? Interactive agents need current context about the customers, orders, inventory, accounts, and other entities they reason about. But assembling that context from constantly changing operational systems is complex, forcing teams to choose between stale data, expensive recomputation, or complex pipelines. This talk will show how to build continuously updated context in SQL that is trustworthy enough for agents to rely upon. You'll learn how to transform operational data into agent-ready representations, keep attributes and relationships up to date as the underlying data changes, and propagate those changes to search indexes and embeddings when needed. Attend if you're deploying AI agents to production and want to give them fresher, more complete context and tighten their read-act-react loop. This presentation is brought to you by Materialize, an AWS Partner.
topics: amazon managed streaming for apache kafka (amazon msk)

title: Single Agent to Global Scale: One Postgres, Any Workload, Run by Agents (sponsored by YugabyteDB)
abstract: An agent needs a Postgres database for perhaps twenty minutes. A payments platform needs one that never goes down across three regions. Most teams cover that range with different products, several vendors, and scores of on-call operators. Yugabyte delivers it as a single stack on AWS. YugabyteDB is distributed PostgreSQL built for global scale and resilience that also scales down to fractional instances. YugabyteDB AMP puts agents in charge of the fleet, handling provisioning, migration, and on-demand tuning. Meko gives agent teams the shared context they run on. See what it takes to run every Postgres workload on one foundation. This presentation is brought to you by YugabyteDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Autonomous DBOps: Agentic AI for maintaining databases
abstract: Maintaining performance for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS often requires manual effort, such as tuning queries, managing indexes, and handling alerts. In this builders' session, learn how to leverage agentic AI solutions implementing LLM-powered autonomous agents to monitor, diagnose, and optimize relational databases in real time. We will demonstrate how AI agents can analyze slow query logs, recommend or apply tuning actions, and trigger intelligent alerts using Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Cloudwatch, AWS Lambda, and Amazon Systems Manager. abstract: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native managed relational database that lets you create, manage, and scale your database resources with ease. abstract: Explore high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) design patterns for SQL Server and Oracle databases on Amazon RDS. In this session, learn about the features offered by Amazon RDS for business continuity, including Multi-AZ deployments, read replicas, and cross-region replication. Discover the customizations that Amazon RDS enables for HA and DR while also allowing you to bring your own license (BYOL) for SQL Server. Also learn how globally resilient solutions architected with Amazon RDS minimize downtime and meet stringent business continuity requirements for mission-critical workloads.

abstract: Blue/green deployments for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS simplify the process of upgrading and performing maintenance on your databases. abstract: Developers love building on powerful, serverless Amazon DynamoDB, and as their production tables grow in size and traffic, they want to discover what mechanisms and optimizations can be applied to reduce costs. Cost optimization can be done both in the design phase and during operations. In this session, learn how to model and measure costs, explore Database Savings Plans to reduce spend on predictable workloads, and discover cost optimization tools that can help you along the way.

title: Build stateful agentic AI workflows with Aurora, MCP, and AgentCore
abstract: How do you take an AI agent from a local prototype to a governed application that recovers from failure? In this session, follow a reference application through five phases: querying business data with SQL, connecting agents to Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, adding hybrid retrieval, deploying to production, and enabling durable workflows. See how Aurora PostgreSQL unifies relational data, pgvector embeddings, full-text search, and workflow state. Explore Strands Agents on Bedrock AgentCore, verify identity and enforce row-level security for data access, and govern tool calls with AgentCore Policy. Code walkthroughs show recovery from saved steps, idempotency to prevent duplicate actions, and audit records that make outcomes traceable.
