title: Build a digital asset tokenization issuance solution
abstract: The emergence of digital assets and stablecoins requires bridging traditional message-based finance protocols such as SWIFT and ISO 20022 to programmable settlement rails while preserving institutional security, auditability, and governance. In this session, learn how to build a production-ready end-to-end hybrid settlement architecture on AWS that ingests financial messages, normalizes them into canonical settlement instructions, and executes tokenized asset transfers on-chain. Explore hardware-backed signing with AWS KMS, on-chain signer governance, and three settlement patterns: issuance, redemption, and transfer, with full audit trails, idempotent transaction handling, and EIP-712 typed signing. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Architect Oracle Database@AWS for resiliency and scale
abstract: Dedicated Exadata infrastructure inside AWS data centers gives Oracle workloads full feature compatibility alongside cloud native flexibility, but architecting for resiliency at scale demands deliberate design choices. In this session, explore architecture patterns for primary and disaster recovery deployments on Oracle Database@AWS, including strategies for multi-terabyte migration and managing petabyte-scale Oracle estates. Join a live whiteboarding discussion where AWS experts cover ODB@AWS deployment options, DR configurations, and operational design choices. Architect with validated best practices drawn from real customer deployments.

title: Optimizing prediction market and trading infrastructure
abstract: Centralized exchanges, decentralized exchanges, and prediction markets share a critical challenge: managing the tension between resiliency and latency. AWS customers have solved this at scale on low-latency platforms trading digital assets 24/7. In this session, AWS specialists dive deep into architecture patterns and real-world examples addressing each challenge. Learn best practices for designing resilient, low-latency trading infrastructure using the latest AWS capabilities built for these markets.

Josh Levinson (Principal Product Manager, Technical, External Services, EC2 Core Product Management, Amazon Web Services)

title: Scaling ElastiCache globally: 500+ clusters & 1.3 trillion ops/day
abstract: Managing ride-hailing demand across 1,100+ cities and 8+ million daily transactions in real time requires scalable, resilient, sub-millisecond in-memory data operations. In this session, learn how inDrive evolved from a monolithic on-premises Redis OSS cluster to over 500 distributed Amazon ElastiCache clusters spanning 8 AWS Regions, executing 1.3 trillion operations daily. Discover how inDrive eliminated bottlenecks in single-CPU utilization, network saturation, and hotspot shards, and how a zero-downtime migration to the Valkey engine on ElastiCache improved performance and reduced costs. Learn a production-tested blueprint for scaling data-intensive systems across multiple AWS Regions.

abstract: Expedia Group manages thousands of database instances across hundreds of AWS accounts. When incidents strike at this scale, every second counts. In this session, learn how a customer-driven vision for agentic AI evolved into a joint design partnership for autonomous database operations on Amazon Aurora. Discover how agents diagnose incidents across fleet-scale telemetry and deliver actionable recommendations to engineers. This joint initiative demonstrates how AI agents reduce incident response time and serves as a blueprint for teams seeking to automate database operations at scale. Learn how AWS is building the underlying capabilities to make autonomous operations real.

abstract: In this session, gain the skills needed to deploy end-to-end agentic AI applications using your most valuable data. This session focuses on data management using processes like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and provides concepts that apply to other methods of customizing agentic AI applications. Discover best practice architectures using AWS database services like Amazon Aurora, DynamoDB, and Neptune, along with analytical, data processing and streaming experiences found in SageMaker. Learn data lake, governance, and data quality concepts and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Bedrock Knowledge Bases, and other features tie solution components together.

title: 10x Faster Vector Indexes: GPU Acceleration in Amazon OpenSearch with NVIDIA cuVS (sponsored by NVIDIA)
abstract: At billion-vector scale, vector index construction can become a performance and cost bottleneck for retrieval, RAG, and AI workloads. Amazon OpenSearch Service Vector Acceleration uses NVIDIA cuVS to accelerate index construction, delivering up to 10x faster builds at a quarter of the indexing cost while preserving the OpenSearch experience. This 300-level session goes under the hood of the architecture: how eligible builds are offloaded to managed GPU workers, how cuVS and CAGRA accelerate graph construction through the Faiss backend, and how the graph is converted into an HNSW index for CPU-based search. We will examine how segment size, quantization, and ingestion patterns affect GPU utilization, build speed, and efficiency. Attendees will leave with guidance for identifying good-fit workloads, optimizing ingestion, and modeling performance and cost benefits for their own deployments. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Vamshi Vijay Nakkirtha (Sr. Software Engineering Manager, AWS)
Navneet Verma (Principal Software Engineer, AWS)

title: Building the data architecture that survives agentic analytics (sponsored by Edelbyte)
abstract: Human queries are bounded, repeatable, and predictable, so techniques like caching, sampling, and precomputation keep them fast and affordable. AI agents are none of those. One prompt becomes dozens of novel, complex queries at machine speed, so caching an agent's curiosity is nearly impossible. At a leading automotive R&D group, 1,400 engineers and their agents query 200 petabytes of vehicle telemetry, with 600 terabytes ingested daily, to engineer higher-quality, more reliable vehicles and reach production faster. This session shows the AWS architecture behind it and how it delivers real-time analytics with full retention at the scale agents have made standard. This presentation is brought to you by Edelbyte, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater

title: SQL Server to Amazon RDS: lessons from Xero's 900 database migration
abstract: What does it take to migrate the databases behind 5 million small businesses without anyone noticing? Xero, the global cloud accounting platform, moved 900 SQL Server databases to Amazon RDS for SQL Server with near-zero downtime. In this session, Xero shares how the team orchestrated cutovers, approached schema migration, and used managed patching, automated backups, and capacity planning in Amazon RDS to return engineering time to product development. The session covers the migration planning and decision points most relevant to engineering teams running large SQL Server fleets on aging self-managed infrastructure.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater

abstract: Amazon Aurora is a serverless relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and DSQL. Aurora provides managed high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) capabilities in and across AWS Regions. In this session, explore the Aurora HA and DR capabilities and discover design patterns that enable the development of resilient applications. Learn how to establish in-Region and cross-Region HA and DR using Aurora features including Multi-AZ deployments and Aurora Global Database, and how Aurora DSQL multi-Region clusters provides the highest level of availability and application resilience.

title: Essentials for migrating from Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
abstract: Migrating from Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition can be a transformative journey, offering significant cost savings and performance benefits. However, this transition requires careful planning and execution. In this session, discover the essential things you need to know to ensure a smooth and successful migration from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL and the optimal architectures to enable such a migration. Learn best practices and pitfalls to avoid from seasoned experts who have helped many customers walk this path.

abstract: In this live coding session, we'll show you how to work with Amazon Aurora DSQL from a developer's perspective. We'll develop a sample application to highlight some of the ways developing for Aurora DSQL is different than PostgreSQL. We'll cover authentication and connection management, optimistic concurrency transaction patterns, primary key selection, analyzing query performance, and best practices.

title: AI agents for PostgreSQL replication and partitioning
abstract: Recent PostgreSQL releases introduced transformative capabilities for logical replication and partitioning, including filtering, parallel apply, sequence replication, and improved planning for partition-heavy workloads. These features are powerful, but tuning them for a specific environment remains complex. In this session, learn to build agents for these core PostgreSQL concepts on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: one that analyzes workloads to recommend optimal logical replication configuration, and a partitioning agent that evaluates query patterns and table bloat to guide table partitioning strategy.

abstract: GraphRAG combines knowledge graphs with RAG to produce explainable responses grounded in semantic relationships between concepts, entities, and underlying content. Agentic GraphRAG takes this further, allowing agents to autonomously decide which GraphRAG tools to use to achieve information goals. In this session, build an agentic GraphRAG application using the open source AWS GraphRAG Toolkit. abstract: Amazon DynamoDB supports native vector search, enabling semantic queries, agentic recommendations, and image-based matching without additional infrastructure. In this session, explore how to design a single-table data model for a recipe database, bulk-load thousands of items with embeddings, and build three vector-powered features: semantic search, a smart recommendation agent, and image-based meal matching. Learn how to configure vector indexes, composite keys, and global secondary indexes on a fully serverless stack, and leave with reusable patterns to add vector search to your own DynamoDB workloads. abstract: Unintended agent actions and incorrect outputs are difficult to investigate without a structured provenance layer. In this session, learn how to design an agent observability system using Amazon DynamoDB to capture the operational audit log and Amazon Neptune to model causal dependencies between retrieved facts and agent decisions. Explore the data model, instrumentation patterns, and graph query techniques that answer what data an agent retrieved, what it concluded, and how those conclusions shaped the final output, making every agent decision traceable and explainable. abstract: Failures happen. Regions degrade, Availability Zones go offline, and networks partition. In this session, learn how to architect Amazon DynamoDB applications that maintain availability and data integrity across a spectrum of failure modes, from single-AZ impairments to full-Region disruptions. Explore the DynamoDB primitives that underpin resilience, including global tables, multi-Region strong consistency, backup and restore, snapshots, and streaming, and how to compose them into patterns that meet strict RTO and RPO objectives. Using scenarios drawn from recent large-scale events, examine trade-offs between consistency, latency, and availability, and discover operational best practices for detecting, responding to, and recovering from failures.

title: Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
abstract: What if your agent's most convincing answer rests on the wrong evidence? Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Aurora PostgreSQL across more than 500,000 product listings in three connected hands-on labs. Debug SQL combining full-text search, pg_trgm fuzzy matching, and pgvector semantic search under shared filters. Repair reciprocal rank fusion, inspect Amazon Bedrock reranking, and compare retrieval settings against judged queries. Then build a Strands agent, connect its retrieval tools through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, and deploy it to AgentCore Runtime. Trace its searches to cited specifications and reviews, and test what happens when requirements change. Leave with reusable retrieval SQL and working agent code.

In this session, learn how some basic data structure decisions led to these characteristics. And how those same decisions provide immutable, point-in-time restore. abstract: With an innovative architecture that decouples compute from storage and advanced features like Aurora Global Database and low-latency read replicas, Aurora reimagines what it means to be a relational database. In this session, dive deep into the newest Aurora features. Explore how Aurora supports agentic AI through vector search and MCP servers for agent access. abstract: Master advanced techniques for evolving Amazon DynamoDB data models without application interruption. Starting from a performance investigation, review recommendations and apply remediation through human-in-the-loop approval gates backed by scoped IAM permissions and API guardrails. abstract: AI agents are autonomous, stateful, and capable of invoking external tools. In a multi-tenant SaaS system, every one of those capabilities is a potential data isolation failure. In this workshop, build a complete multi-tenant agentic AI solution enforcing tenant isolation across Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with row-level security, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon S3 Vectors. Implement tenant-scoped vector stores for RAG, agent memory backed by multiple database engines, MCP-based tool authorization gated by subscription tier, and usage metering. Leave with a working reference architecture that prevents cross-tenant data leakage. Bring a laptop to participate.

abstract: Turn Aurora PostgreSQL runbooks into agent skills and test whether they improve an agent's advice. Work through three incidents on a live cluster: RDS Proxy session pinning that starves checkout connections, a payout job whose open transaction blocks checkouts, and stalled order delivery alongside a long-running transaction that holds back vacuum cleanup. Complete and refine skills that cover pre-flight checks, execution, validation and rollback. Freeze a grading rubric, then compare the same agent, hosted on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, without and with your skill. Write Python recovery checks that reject incomplete fixes, perform the repairs yourself, and verify customer recovery using independent database and business records.

title: Build a knowledge graph-based agent guardrail with Amazon Neptune
abstract: AI agents assert relationships such as compatible products, cleared counterparties, or approved suppliers, derived from LLM reasoning rather than verified data. When these assertions are wrong, downstream business decisions fail. In this session, explore how to implement Amazon Neptune as a post-generation verification layer. Before the agent responds, a graph traversal confirms or contradicts the assertion against a live knowledge graph. Learn how to build the verification tool, the override pattern when Neptune contradicts the model, and the graph data model for storing authoritative relationship data that constrains agent behavior. Bring your laptop to participate.

abstract: Semantic caching uses vector similarity search to retrieve cached LLM responses for semantically equivalent queries, reducing inference latency and cost in agentic AI architectures. In this session, dive deep into implementing semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, covering embedding generation, similarity scoring, and relevance threshold tuning. Explore advanced production patterns including per-user cache namespacing for personalized responses, tenant isolation strategies to prevent cross-tenant data leakage, and techniques for validating that cached responses remain contextually appropriate for incoming queries at scale. abstract: Modern algorithmic trading platforms deploy fleets of specialized AI agents, including market analysts, risk assessors, order executors, and compliance monitors, that must coordinate in real time without conflict. In this session, follow along as a trading platform's multi-agent workflows are coded live using Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey. Valkey Streams organize agent task queues, pub/sub channels broadcast market signals to agent swarms with low latency, and vector similarity search gives agents memory of prior market scenarios. Discover how atomic Lua scripts prevent duplicate orders and enable exactly-once workflow transitions.

title: Build agentic payment investigators on Aurora PostgreSQL & AgentCore
abstract: Payment dispute resolution and ledger reconciliation require agents that reason over transactional history, retrieve precedent with precision, and write through idempotent workflows. In this session, learn how to build two production-grade payment agents on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: a dispute investigator that classifies cardholder disputes and drafts representment narratives, and a reconciliation agent that resolves breaks between internal ledgers and bank statements. Both share one investigator pattern: an agent reasoning over structured records, retrieving precedent with pgvector, and writing through an idempotent ledger. Go deep on SERIALIZABLE state machines, hybrid retrieval that knows when a trigram index beats an embedding, confidence-scored human-in-the-loop routing, and trace-to-row observability with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

title: Red teaming Aurora and gen AI: offense, defense, response
abstract: Databases and generative AI workloads are high-value targets that demand continuous adversarial testing. In this session, learn how AWS red team engineers use AI to discover innovative ways to strengthen Amazon Aurora and other cloud-native database services against modern threats. Explore how red team findings shape architectural decisions that contain blast radius by design, and how AI-augmented detection and response mechanisms close the loop at machine speed. Learn a practical framework for red teaming cloud environments and AI systems, designing for assumed breach, and building response capabilities that match the velocity of modern threats.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater

Will Sovran (Senior Security Engineer, AWS)

title: DynamoDB: the database designed for trillion-scale vector search
abstract: As vector search becomes a standard component of AI applications, scaling to billions or even trillions of vectors while maintaining single-digit millisecond latency and high recall remains a significant challenge. In this session, deep dive into the decisions made when building vector indexes for DynamoDB, including how vector indexes shard alongside table data, the scatter-gather query mechanism that keeps latencies tight, and the filtering that avoids recall degradation at scale. Learn how the partition key in DynamoDB maps naturally to multi-tenant workloads, enabling per-tenant index isolation without operational overhead. Discover the trade-offs between recall, latency, and cost in production for real-time vector search.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Rashmi Krishnaiah Setty (Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Abhinav Duggal (Principal Engineer, Amazon)

title: Adopt evolving Amazon DynamoDB resiliency design patterns
abstract: In this session, discover recently developed resilience mechanisms for DynamoDB workloads and how existing, advanced resilience patterns have been evolving. Learn how to use the global tables architecture with specific metrics and thresholds that drive effective failover decisions, as well as DR patterns that achieve low RTO and RPO without global tables overhead. Through whiteboard discussion, explore a variety of resilient DynamoDB workload solutions for specific use cases, including incremental export for undoing bad writes, which is faster and less disruptive than a full PITR table restore, approaches to protect against ransomware and data destruction, and cross-account table migration strategies.
speakers: John Terhune (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Jason Hunter (Principal SA, Amazon)

title: Context engineering for agents: memory, SQL, knowledge graphs & skills
abstract: An agent's context window is a finite attention budget, and database-backed agents must keep that context current, selective, and traceable. In this session, architect solutions to trace a task as it builds context using Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, Amazon Neptune, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Examine how agents cache hot state, retrieve operational rows, apply SQL filters, maintain vector and full-text indexes, refresh stale records, traverse knowledge-graph relationships, load skills, and discover MCP tools. Explore freshness policies, invalidation, provenance ledgers, access boundaries, and compaction patterns for production-grade agentic applications.
speakers: David Gardner (AWS Solution Architect Database Specialist, AWS)
Don Simpson (Principal Technologist, AWS)

title: Migrate workloads to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
abstract: Running self-managed document databases at scale introduces significant operational burden, version lock-in, and rising infrastructure costs. Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) addresses these challenges with a fully managed, highly available service. In this session, examine compatibility features that simplify migration from existing document database environments, and work through architecture decisions affecting performance, cost, and reliability. Discover how enhancements in version 8.0 deliver up to 5x compression and 7x query performance improvement. Discuss common migration blockers, schema transformation approaches, and newest compatibility additions that reduce friction during cutover. Learn a framework for planning and executing document database migrations on AWS.
speakers: Jim Mlodgenski (Senior Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Douglas Bonser (Sr. Specialist Solution Architect, AWS)

title: Deploy and manage blockchain nodes on AWS
abstract: Self-managing blockchain nodes at scale requires expertise in infrastructure sizing, storage optimization, chain synchronization, snapshot management, and patching, amid rapidly evolving protocols. In this session, explore a reference architecture for deploying self-managed nodes on AWS using Amazon EC2 and AWS Blockchain Node Runners, an open source initiative. The session includes a whiteboard walkthrough of a sample solution, diving deep into each component, addressing key challenges, and exploring AI-driven node deployment with Kiro and how to leverage AWS DevOps Agent for management.
speakers: Yinal Ozkan (Sr. Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Everton Fraga (Sr. Web3 Specialist SA, AWS)

title: Global transactions in Amazon Aurora DSQL
abstract: Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database built for global scale. In this session, Marc Brooker, AWS VP and Distinguished Engineer, dives into the exact algorithms Aurora DSQL uses to achieve faster-than-light consistent reads, strong isolation, durability, and atomicity across regions. The session covers the specific tradeoffs each algorithm makes and what those tradeoffs mean in practice.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Marc Brooker (VP and Distinguished Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build an agentic context layer with ontologies on Amazon Neptune
abstract: Most knowledge graphs answer questions but never close the loop with operational systems. In this session, explore how to build an ontology-driven context layer that transforms a knowledge graph into an active control plane for AI agents. The session covers RDF ontology design, SHACL constraint validation, synchronization patterns, agent integration, and write-back mechanisms that propagate decisions to systems of record. Hear how Lockheed Martin applied these patterns in production, enabling agents to reason across supply chain, manufacturing, and engineering domains. Leave with a concrete architectural blueprint and lessons learned from building context layers that act while increasing your trust.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Jeff Bascle (Research Director, AI Enablement, Lockheed Martin Corporation)
Taylor Riggan (Principal Graph Architect, Amazon Neptune, Amazon Web Services)

title: Amazon DynamoDB: How to build a foundational service
abstract: Whether to take a dependency or reimplement something are important decisions in any system architecture, affecting performance, durability, and availability. Amazon DynamoDB serves millions of customers while also underpinning many AWS services, a dual role that forces rigorous decisions about dependencies, failure isolation, and multi-Region architecture. In this session, the DynamoDB engineering team walks through how those constraints shape architectural choices, including when DynamoDB uses DynamoDB to implement itself. The session presents a structured framework for dependency analysis, covering multi-zone and multi-Region tradeoffs, applicable to any system you build and operate, to help identify design risks before they become failures.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Craig Howard (Sr. Principal Engineer, Amazon)
Amrith Kumar (Senior Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: Design a governed ontology in Neptune that any agent can query
abstract: Your agents can answer questions. Can they explain why, and would two agents give the same answer? Most enterprise AI stalls in pilot because business meaning lives in scattered prompts, pipelines, and code. In this session, learn how to use Amazon Neptune to turn entities, relationships, policies, and rules into a governed ontology and knowledge graph that any agent framework can query. See how AI-assisted authoring cuts modeling from months to hours, where one rule update propagates across every agent and each answer carries an inspectable reasoning trace. The graph stays in your account.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Brad Bebee (Director, Amazon ElastiCache, Neptune, and Timestream, AWS)
Meet Bhagdev (Head of Product, ElastiCache, Neptune, and MemoryDB, Amazon Web Services)

title: Amazon Aurora architecture patterns for open table format analytics
abstract: Modern analytics architectures increasingly rely on open table formats like Apache Iceberg but combining operational and analytical data remains complex. This session explores emerging patterns for bridging Amazon Aurora with open table format analytics. Learn architectural patterns for bidirectional data flow between databases and data lakes. Topics include design patterns for analytical workloads, performance optimization and reverse ETL, and deep dives into maintaining transactional consistency when streaming database changes to Amazon S3 Tables, delivery guarantees, and type mapping.
speakers: Tim Stoakes (Sr. Principal Technologist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Netflix on Aurora PostgreSQL: Operating 40TB+ after fleet migration
abstract: In this session, learn why Netflix moved workloads from a self-managed, distributed PostgreSQL-compatible database on EC2 to Aurora, and how they operate 40TB+ today. Aurora shared storage eliminated cross-node coordination overhead, delivering up to 75% lower latency. Explore the operational model developed by the platform team, featuring NVMe tiered cache for multi-TB datasets using optimized reads instances, cluster cache management for resilience following failover, query plan management for plan stability, and how PostgreSQL statistics and CloudWatch Database Insights power on-call triage and cost optimization.
speakers: Grant McAlister (Senior Principal Engineer, AWS)
Sabrina Zhao (Software Engineer, Netflix)

title: Built by Agents: Rethinking Reliability for AI-Native Companies (sponsored by Traversal)
abstract: AI is changing how quickly software can be built, shipped, and scaled. For AI-native companies, that can mean more services and complexity earlier in their growth. Many traditional reliability practices were designed for a different pace, when teams had more time to document, instrument, and build operational knowledge as they scaled. This conversation brings together leaders from a fast-growing legal AI company and one of the world’s largest digital banks, alongside leaders from Traversal, the AI SRE that diagnoses, fixes, and prevents incidents across enterprise environments. They’ll discuss how AI is changing development and operations, new failure modes in AI-native systems, how lean teams approach reliability as they scale, and the role of AI SREs in a broader shift toward AI understanding, managing, and improving production systems. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater

title: AWS infrastructure as code: A year in review
abstract: Your infrastructure code deserves the same developer experience as your application code. This session recaps what's new for AWS CloudFormation and the AWS CDK: early change-set validation, the CloudFormation Language Server for your IDE, Stack Refactoring without downtime, drift-aware change sets, CDK Mixins for composable abstractions, cross-account output references, and the CDK Toolkit Library. See how these capabilities shorten your dev-test cycle and strengthen deployment safety.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Mark Rambow (Sr. Manager, Software Development, Amazon Web Services)
Aakash Deshpande (Product Manager, AWS)

title: Beyond the pilot: How customers scaled Kiro and proved the value
abstract: Adopting a coding agent is as much an organizational challenge as a technical one. In this panel, engineering leaders from companies that deployed Kiro at scale share what worked: rollout strategies that drove adoption, training approaches that met developers where they were, governance guardrails that satisfied security teams, and the metrics they use to measure productivity impact. Bring your questions—this is an open conversation about the patterns, pitfalls, and payoffs of making AI-assisted development the default across an engineering organization.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Diana Kennedy (Chief Information Officer, Retail and Enterprise Architecture, NatWest Group)
Michael Erdman (Managing Director, Technology - Digital Platforms, Southwest Airlines Co.)
Rory Richardson (AWS) (Director, AWS)
Kym Weiland (Sr. Vice President Delivery Services, FINRA - Financial Industry Regulatory Authority)

title: 10x or bust: How Amazon's Frontier teams ship with Kiro
abstract: Amazon teams using Kiro and AI-native workflows are shipping features in hours that used to take weeks. But the gains didn't come from better prompts. They came from better practices, from rethinking how developers and teams work instead of just adding shiny tools on top of existing SDLC processes. This session dissects three real experiments: a pathfinder initiative, a structured sprint, and in-situ pilots across 50+ teams. You'll learn the five practices that compound into 4.5x–10x gains, the mistakes that kill momentum, and how to run your own pilot starting Monday.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: McLaren Stanley (Sr. Principal Engineer, Amazon)
Eva Knight (Worldwide GTM Specialist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Learn new AI development skills with Kiro
abstract: Discover Kiro, the IDE for structured agentic development. In this builder’s session, explore how to use Kiro as your intelligent partner - helping to understand complex codebases, crystalize detailed requirements, and deliver quality solutions at unprecedented speed. You will iterate with Kiro to finalize your detailed design, before using Kiro to orchestrate AI agents and implement a fully working solution – all while maintaining complete control throughout the development process. You must bring a laptop to participate in this session.

title: How AI-Powered DevSecOps Fueled Intuitive Machines' Race to the Moon (sponsored by GitLab)
abstract: In 2019, Intuitive Machines won a NASA contract to land a spacecraft near the Moon's south pole — with five years to build every system from scratch and a team of just 50 developers. Join James Blakeslee, Vice President of Engineering at Intuitive Machines, as he shares how the team used AI-powered DevSecOps to ship mission-critical software fast enough to become the first U.S. venture in 50 years — and the first commercial company ever — to land intact on the Moon. You'll learn how they're now using GitLab Duo Agent Platform and Amazon Bedrock to accelerate development toward their next lunar lander. This presentation is brought to you by GitLab, an AWS Partner.
speakers: James Blakeslee (Vice President of Engineering, Intuitive Machines)
Cherry Han (Field CTO, GitLab)

title: When Telemetry Steers the Robot: Observability for Physical AI (sponsored by groundcover)
abstract: Path Robotics is pushing physical AI beyond the lab into tough industrial environments. Its Obsidian AI model autonomously welds production parts, while Rove brings that intelligence into shipyards on a Boston Dynamics quadruped. When AI moves into the physical world, observability becomes mission-critical. Built on AWS, Path needs visibility into AI applications, robot motion, and welding arcs, where traditional observability tools fall short. In this session, Path Robotics and groundcover share how they replaced legacy SaaS observability with a BYOC architecture spanning commercial and sovereign environments. groundcover’s eBPF sensor delivers instant visibility into agentic applications and field robotics, providing critical production context. This presentation is brought to you by groundcover, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Noam Levy (Field CTO, groundcover)

title: Shipping AI Code with Confidence Using Bluebox by Dynatrace and AWS Kiro (sponsored by Dynatrace)
abstract: See how Western Governors University uses Bluebox by Dynatrace and AWS Kiro to deliver AI-generated code with greater confidence. By combining live production intelligence with AI-assisted development, teams can provide agents with real runtime context, detect issues quickly, and create evidence-backed GitHub Issues for rapid remediation. Learn how Bluebox supports the software lifecycle before, during, and after deployment, helping teams validate fixes, reduce risk, and accelerate software delivery. This presentation is brought to you by Dynatrace, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Angel Marchena (Director, Technical Operations, Western Governors University)
Jason Ostroski (Field CTO, Dynatrace LLC)

title: After the Agents Write the Code: A Field Report From 100 Million Code Reviews (sponsored by CodeRabbit)
abstract: What does it take to move from human-centered software development to fully agentic development, so you can ship dramatically faster without sacrificing quality or security? More than 2 million times a week, CodeRabbit reviews a change before it merges, whoever or whatever wrote it. From where we sit, we see teams solving agentic coding, but not yet agentic shipping. Now that code is cheap to write, four things have become bottlenecks: review, understanding, prioritization, and security. CodeRabbit hit all four and cleared them, which is how it ships 10x more software without adding engineering headcount. David Loker, VP of Applied AI, shares the four practices that helped, how roles and workflows changed, and why a team has to build trust to ship fast. This presentation is brought to you by CodeRabbit, an AWS Partner.
speakers: David Loker (VP of AI, CodeRabbit Inc.)

title: Building an Open and Real-time Fraud and Decisioning Engine with Mastercard and Redis (sponsored by Redis)
abstract: Ever get a text that your Mastercard was used in a transaction you didn't make? That's because every card swipe has to be evaluated before it's cleared to keep fraud from slipping through. Join Sivakumar Palanasami, Mastercard's EVP of Data Platforms, to learn how his team's real-time fraud decisioning model built with Redis on AWS and for a sneak peek of what they're doing next. This presentation is brought to you by Redis, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Siva Palanisamy (Executive Vice President, Data Platforms, Mastercard Incorporated)

title: Claude Keeps Building: How Coding Agents Change Software Development (sponsored by Anthropic)
abstract: Coding agents make sustained, autonomous progress on real software. The question is what happens to the rest of the software development lifecycle. Claude Code runs for hours unattended, works beyond the terminal, and takes on more of the work around the code. We'll show where it stands and how engineering changes when the whole lifecycle becomes automatable: what engineers do, how review and testing evolve, where quality comes from when code is cheap. Live demos on AWS and numbers from our engineering, where Claude writes most of our code. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

title: The Best Engineer in the Room Doesn’t Write Code (sponsored by Anaconda)
abstract: AI generates code faster than teams can review and ship it. The bottleneck has moved, and so has the work of the highest leverage engineers. Engineers build coding factories: repeatable systems that combine user intent, persistent context, agent execution, automated checks, and human judgment. Drawing on AWS’s AI-Driven Development Life Cycle, we’ll see how Kilo by Anaconda meets developers where they work and how Amazon Bedrock brings model choice into the factory, tracing one build failure through verification and escalation. Attendees leave with a framework for agent workflows that deliver, and a clearer view of where engineering judgment matters. This presentation is brought to you by Anaconda, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Emilie Schario (VP, Engineering, Anaconda (FKA Continuum Analytics))

title: Rebuild CI for AI coding agents with content based caching (sponsored by RWX)
abstract: Continuous integration was designed around human pace. A developer pushes a branch, a webhook fires, and a ten minute wait feels acceptable. AI coding agents break that assumption, and validation becomes the longest part of the cycle. Explore how RWX rebuilt the layer underneath continuous integration for agent driven work, including content based caching that skips work already proven unchanged, graph based task execution, a container runtime built for reuse, and a command line interface agents call directly rather than waiting on Git. Learn which parts of a pipeline are structurally slow and which are simply misconfigured. This presentation is brought to you by RWX, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Dan Manges (Cofounder, RWX)

title: Inside the Governed Agentic Software Factory at Enterprise Scale (sponsored by CloudBees)
abstract: Code is now abundant. AI agents now write, test and deploy code autonomously; the bottleneck has shifted from generating code to governing what reaches production. Loreli Cadapan, VP of Product at CloudBees, takes you inside the governed agentic software factories that the world’s most regulated engineering organizations are building, where every change, human or agent, is visible, auditable and accountable. The work starts after the code changes: encode existing rules as enforceable policy across your toolchain, keep humans in the loop where it matters, and ship software you can stand behind. Because you write code for a reason, and we make sure that reason becomes true. This presentation is brought to you by CloudBees, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater

title: Change. Wait. Debug. Let AI drive the infrastructure loop. (sponsored by HashiCorp)
abstract: Make a change. Deploy it. Wait. Dig through the logs. Try again. For years, that loop has cost infrastructure engineers countless hours—time that could be spent shipping what comes next. In this session, discover how to take engineers out of the routine operational loop without giving up oversight. Define the outcome, let AI work through the iterations, and step back in only when a real decision needs you. See the pattern in action with Terraform, Vault, Kubernetes, Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and more. This presentation is brought to you by HashiCorp, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Kyle Ruddy (Senior Director, Product Marketing, HashiCorp, an IBM company)
Cole Morrison (Head of Brand Story & Principal Evangelist, HashiCorp)

title: Build Once, Deploy Anywhere: Agentic AI from Data Center to Edge with Qualcomm & AWS (sponsored by Qualcomm)
abstract: AI is moving beyond the cloud, requiring developers to deploy intelligent workloads across data centers, edge infrastructure, vehicles, industrial systems, PCs, and mobile devices. The challenge is scaling AI efficiently across diverse hardware environments. In this session, learn how Qualcomm and AWS enable developers to build agentic AI applications across the compute continuum, from cloud training to real-time edge and on-device inference. Discover how open frameworks, portable AI runtimes, and streamlined workflows accelerate development and deployment. Through examples spanning automotive, IoT, industrial edge, mobile, datacenter, and cloud use cases, explore how a unified developer experience reduces complexity, increases flexibility, and helps deliver scalable AI applications anywhere. This presentation is brought to you by Qualcomm, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater

title: The Agentic SDLC (sponsored by Postman)
abstract: Autonomous agents are no longer assisting the software development lifecycle. They are rewriting it. When agents write, review, test, and ship code at machine speed, the SDLC stops being a sequence of human handoffs and becomes a control problem. This session covers the failure modes that only appear at scale: review queues that no human can absorb, test suites that validate the wrong invariants, provenance gaps that make incidents unexplainable, and CI/CD pipelines built for tens of commits a day now absorbing thousands. It closes with the specific architectural decisions engineering leaders should be making now, drawn from our own experience running agents in production. This presentation is brought to you by Postman, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: Controlling the AI Software Factory (sponsored by LaunchDarkly)
abstract: AI isn't just making software faster; it's changing how software is produced. Engineering teams now run agents that write code, review PRs, validate releases, and deploy around the clock. The promise is real, but so is a new problem: how do you stay in control of systems that never stop evolving? Edith Harbaugh, CEO of LaunchDarkly, argues the defining challenge of the AI era isn't generating code, it's controlling autonomous systems in production, where agents drift and the old detect-fix-redeploy playbook breaks down. She'll share what LaunchDarkly learned building its own AI software factory, and how engineers stay in charge. This presentation is brought to you by LaunchDarkly, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: Inside Real AI Software Factories: Lessons From the Teams Building Them (sponsored by LaunchDarkly)
abstract: Everyone's talking about AI software factories. Far fewer have actually built one. In this panel, engineering leaders, partners, and teams putting agents into production go past the hype to the real work: where agents accelerate delivery, where they break, and what it takes to keep humans in control as autonomy scales. Expect specifics, not theory—what worked, what didn't, and what they'd do differently. Whether you're experimenting with coding agents or scaling toward autonomous delivery, you'll leave with practical patterns for building a factory that's genuinely fast and safe. Join us for an honest conversation about engineering at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by LaunchDarkly, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Jonathan Nolen
Timothy Cook (Director of Product, LaunchDarkly)

title: Who Checks the Agents? Quality and Governance for the Agentic SDLC (sponsored by Qodo)
abstract: Agents now plan work, write code, generate tests and open PRs—sometimes without human review before production. Yet most teams rely on a trust model built for a slower SDLC: one reviewer, one merge gate and one chance to catch what went wrong. That model fails when agents operate at every stage and final review can’t reveal what happened upstream. This session treats trust as a property of the pipeline, not a final checkpoint. We’ll explore why the system generating code shouldn’t also verify it, how to turn tribal standards into enforceable, auditable controls, and where independent review belongs between spec and deploy. Key takeaways: Why end-stage review fails in an agent-driven SDLC. How to enforce and trace standards across teams, repos and AI tools. How to decide what can merge automatically, what needs human review and how to document that decision for auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Qodo, an AWS Partner.

title: Brownfield development across large codebases with AI agents
abstract: Most production code has no spec. It was written by teams that moved on, and its docs went stale long ago. When you inherit a service, prepare a migration, or chase an incident, you spend days reconstructing what the system does, and your AI agent rediscovers the same behavior in every new chat. We'll first sketch how to generate a structured model of an existing system from its code: its invariants, dependencies, and hidden assumptions. Then it's your turn. Bring your questions and your hardest brownfield problems, and we'll work through them together at the whiteboard.

title: Best practices for helping agents understand code you didn't write
abstract: Most production code has no spec. It was written by teams that moved on, and its docs went stale long ago. Before a refactor, migration, or incident fix, developers spend days on code archaeology, and AI agents have to rediscover the same behavior in every new chat with little prior context. Learn how to turn an existing codebase into a structured, persistent model of what the system does: its properties, invariants, component interactions, and hidden assumptions. See how that model helps you onboard faster, baseline behavior before a refactor, and give your AI agent context that's reusable across sessions.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater

title: Best practices for working with shared coding agents on your team
abstract: Software development happens through teamwork, but agent work is often trapped in individual sessions. The developer who starts the work becomes the coordinator who needs to relay feedback, reconstruct decisions, or keep agents moving. Working with agents as a team has many paper cuts, but there are best practices you can implement. Follow an issue from investigation through implementation, testing, and review, with requests, decisions, and approvals attributed along the way as work progresses. Learn how team-scoped knowledge, reusable practices, and clear permission boundaries let agents take on ongoing responsibilities while people keep control of what ships.

title: Build a team shared agent workflow from issue to tested PR
abstract: How do you let agents carry development work across teammates without handing over control? In this code talk, build an issue-to-review workflow that you can share with your team. Follow the code and configuration for setting up guardrails, permissions, shared workflows, logging, and best practices, so teammates can steer the implementation or review who requested or approved each action alongside the evidence the agent produced. Bring questions and follow along as we explain why each boundary exists and how to adapt the pattern to your toolchain and approval process.

title: Bring your tech debt: build a custom transformation that fixes it
abstract: Every codebase has that annoying pattern: the deprecated internal library, the logging convention nobody follows, the framework migration that keeps getting deferred. In this small-group builder session, you'll tackle yours. Bring a real modernization problem from your own code and build a custom transformation in AWS Transform custom that solves it—defining the transformation in natural language, running it against a repository, and refining it until it holds up. No fixed curriculum and no slides: this is open-ended, hands-on time. Stuck for an idea? We'll have a few ready-made problems on hand. You must bring your laptop to participate.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Gokul Sarangaraju (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Suresh Natarajan (Sr. TAM, AWS)
Dinesh Balaaji Prabakaran (Sr Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Bring your tech debt: build a custom transformation that fixes it
abstract: Every codebase has that annoying pattern: the deprecated internal library, the logging convention nobody follows, the framework migration that keeps getting deferred. In this small-group builder session, you'll tackle yours. Bring a real modernization problem from your own code and build a custom transformation in AWS Transform custom that solves it—defining the transformation in natural language, running it against a repository, and refining it until it holds up. No fixed curriculum and no slides: this is open-ended, hands-on time. Stuck for an idea? We'll have a few ready-made problems on hand. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Too many tools: Building software in the age of agents
abstract: AI now touches every stage of software delivery: coding assistants, autonomous agents, modernization tools, security scanners, operations, and the list grows every week. Which do you actually use, and when? This open discussion helps you make sense of the SDLC tooling landscape. Bring your scenario and we'll talk through it together: when to hand work to an autonomous agent versus a deterministic tool, how to chain AI across design, code, review, and operations without creating new bottlenecks, and how to avoid adopting every shiny agent at once. Leave with a plan for building software with AI, not just a tool list.

abstract: Releasing software shouldn't mean holding your breath. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS CodePipeline, CodeBuild, and AppConfig help you automate safe, hands-off deployments to Amazon EC2, ECS, and Lambda across accounts and Regions. Learn to apply canary and linear traffic-shifting strategies, wire CloudWatch alarms for automatic rollback, and use stage-level conditions to gate promotions on integration tests. title: Beyond code generation: accelerating the entire SDLC on AWS
abstract: Teams pour AI into code generation and wonder why they're not shipping faster. In reality, accelerating one stage just moves the bottleneck downstream. This session follows a single task across its entire lifecycle and shows where AI compounds. We'll design and build with Kiro, pay down tech debt with AWS Transform, catch vulnerabilities early with AWS Continuum (formerly known as AWS Security Agent), ship through safe CI/CD pipelines, and resolve production issues with AWS DevOps Agent—then feed what we learn back into the next task. Come see our vision for an SDLC where every stage moves at the same speed.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Tony Patino (Enterprise Architect, Transamerica)
Adnan Bilwani (Principal Specialist, GenAI - Next Gen Development Experience, Amazon Web Services)
Ryan Bachman (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: Ship faster with AWS CloudFormation
abstract: AWS CloudFormation lets you manage infrastructure as code with increasing confidence and speed, whether you're deploying directly or through AI agents. In this chalk talk, we dive into the capabilities that shorten your dev-test cycle and keep deployments safe: deploy in seconds with Express mode, catch errors before deployment with pre-deployment validation, author templates faster using the CloudFormation Language Server in your IDE, connect AI agents to CloudFormation with the Agent Skill and MCP Server, reorganize stacks without disruption using Stack Refactoring, and prevent accidental overwrites with drift-aware change sets. Bring your templates and your toughest questions, we'll workshop solutions live.

title: Your runtime Is being deprecated. Your weekend isn't.
abstract: Your inbox fills with runtime deprecation notices—hundreds of Lambda functions on Node.js 20, Python 3.10, and whatever's next. Handling them one by one drains capacity you'd rather spend on features. This hands-on workshop flips the script: instead of chasing individual apps, you'll modernize a fleet. Using AWS Transform custom, you'll run AWS-provided transformations to upgrade Lambda runtimes at scale, then stand up continuous modernization to scan repositories against a baseline, prioritize what's drifting, and open pull requests automatically. Turn a wall of end-of-support alerts into a queue of ready-to-merge PRs. You must bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Renuka Krishnan (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Alpna Daniels (GTM Leader, GenAI, Amazon)

title: Agentic development with AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
abstract: AI coding agents can write application logic, but can they provision your infrastructure too? In this chalk talk, explore AWS Cloud Development Kit's (AWS CDK) latest capabilities—Mixins, the CDK Toolkit Library, and programmatic synth/deploy APIs—make CDK a first-class target for agentic workflows. See how agents reason about constructs, compose infrastructure from natural-language intent, and validate results before deployment. We'll discuss patterns that work, guardrails that keep agents safe, and where human judgment still matters. Bring your questions—this is an interactive session for anyone curious about the intersection of AI agents and infrastructure as code.

Learn maintenance and operations tips including cross-account output references and programmatic deployments with the CDK Toolkit Library. Get an introduction to building your own constructs. Explore testing tools—cfn-lint, CloudFormation Guard, and early change-set validation—to catch errors before deployment. Learn language features like Stack Refactoring and drift-aware change sets that help you evolve templates safely over time. You must bring your laptop to participate.

abstract: Learn how to create applications that use real-time data to keep users engaged. In this workshop, build a multiplayer application with live updates and group chat functionality using AWS Amplify Gen 2. Define your backend—data model, auth rules, and real-time subscriptions—in TypeScript and deploy to a cloud sandbox in seconds. Connect your frontend to a serverless backend powered by AWS AppSync WebSockets. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Beyond the IDE: autonomous development with Kiro web and mobile
abstract: Kiro web and mobile bring agentic development to your browser—every session in an isolated cloud sandbox, no local setup, accessible anywhere you have an internet connection. In this hands-on workshop, you'll work with Kiro two ways. First, iterate interactively: connect a repo, explore the codebase, and shape changes in real time. Then go hands-off: assign a task from a tracked issue, let Kiro plan and implement autonomously, and review the pull request it opens. Sessions run in the cloud and keep going after you close your laptop—check in and review diffs from your phone with the Kiro iOS app. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: What's new in full-stack AWS app development
abstract: Web developers are under pressure to deliver differentiating experiences to more users, faster than ever. Building secure, reliable, scalable applications at 10x speed takes solutions that let developers start easily, ship quickly, and iterate without friction. In this breakout, we'll share how AWS is evolving to meet the needs of modern full-stack developers from defining backends in code and connecting real-time data, to deploying and scaling globally with minimal overhead. Join us to see what's new and where full-stack development on AWS is headed.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Nikhil Dabhade (Principal Product Manager - Technical, Amazon Web Services)
Praneeta Prakash (Sr. Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: From Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering At Scale
abstract: Most developers use AI coding assistants as interactive tools and see modest gains. A small cohort works differently: they treat agents as autonomous workers they direct and validate, and the results are a step function in productivity improvements, not an increment. In this session, we break down what these power users do differently, share success stories, where experts still find friction, and the bottlenecks coming next. We'll share demos so you leave with concrete, repeatable practices for getting orders-of-magnitude more out of Kiro agents.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Pooja Giri (Software Development Manager, AWS)
Doug Clauson (Principal Product Manager - Kiro, AWS)
Ricardo Britto (Head of AI & Telco Innovation, Ericsson)

title: How Kiro learns: an AI coding agent that improves with every session
abstract: Learn how Kiro turns working sessions into durable knowledge and how to design, debug, and evaluate an agent’s memory lifecycle. See how Kiro extracts learnings from explicit instructions and task outcomes, such as successful build commands or rejected pull requests. Explore how it consolidates new knowledge with existing memories, resolves contradictions and expiring facts, and retrieves only relevant context for tasks. You’ll also learn how provenance keeps memories auditable and correctable, how memory stays consistent across IDE, CLI, and web, how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory scopes knowledge globally or by repository, and how retrieval quality is measured by task outcomes.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: David Killmon (Principal Software Engineer, AWS)
Trevor Mack (Distinguished Engineer, Rapid7)
Navyata Bawa (Head of Developer Education, AWS)

title: Tech debt anonymous: bring your worst code to this chalk talk
abstract: We all have it: the monolith nobody wants to touch, and the pile of small apps and Lambda functions racking up end-of-life notices. This chalk talk is your support group. Bring your real modernization headaches and we'll discuss how AWS Transform tackles the whole spectrum. On one side, Transform custom handles the big, complex jobs: decomposing Java and .NET monoliths, translating languages, upgrading frameworks at scale. On the other, continuous modernization autonomously scans thousands of repositories, prioritizes what's drifting, and opens remediation pull requests on a schedule. Bring questions about your own portfolio and leave with a plan of attack.
speakers: Venugopalan Vasudevan (Pr. Specialist SA, AWS)
Avi Nidumbur (WW Leader of Solutions Architecture, Dev Experiences and Agents, Amazon)

title: Learn faster: Experimentation in an AI world
abstract: AI makes it possible to generate and test far more product variations than a team could create by hand. But running more experiments only helps if you can release each variation safely, measure the right signals, and separate meaningful results from noise. In this code-focused session, you’ll learn how to use AI and feature flags to control experiment variants, target audiences, adjust exposure, and shut down underperforming tests without redeploying. We’ll also examine how Amazon has recently used AI in experiments on Amazon.com to create variations and extract better signals from the results.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Steve Rice (General Manager, AWS AppConfig & Parameter Store, AWS)
Ben Shumpert (Sr SDE, AWS)

title: Build a backend before your coffee gets cold with AWS Blocks
abstract: What if you could stand up a full application backend—database, auth, real-time messaging, file storage, even an AI agent—in TypeScript, running locally, with no AWS account required? AWS Blocks is an open-source framework where each "Block" bundles your app code, a local dev implementation, and production AWS infrastructure. Compose the Blocks you need, run one command to develop locally, then deploy the same code to AWS unchanged. Built for a world where AI agents write the code, Blocks ships steering files that guide agents to correct architecture from the start. In this lightning talk, see how fast full-stack can be.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Salih Güler (Senior Developer Advocate, AWS)

title: How startups ship faster with Kiro
abstract: Startups live and die by velocity. Small teams, big ambitions, and no time to waste. In this session, hear how fast-moving startups are using Kiro to punch above their weight: turning ideas into working software with spec-driven and agentic development, keeping a lean team focused on product instead of boilerplate, and shipping features that would normally demand far more engineers. We'll describe real patterns startups use to move from concept to production quickly, and share practical takeaways any team can apply. Whether you're a founder, an early engineer, or scaling quickly, learn how agentic development helps small teams build big.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Helen Hasbun (Sr Product Marketing Manager, Amazon)
Rene Brandel (Cofounder & CEO, Casco)

title: Outrun technical debt in the age of autonomous development
abstract: The legacy estate has not gone away. Aging applications with undocumented business logic, outdated frameworks, and platforms nobody wants to touch remain a priority. Agentic tools have increased development velocity, but speed does not eliminate technical debt — it changes its shape. This compounding debt erodes productivity, weakens security posture, and inflates operational cost. Learn how AWS Transform custom and continuous modernization help organizations assess and remediate technical debt at scale — from framework migrations like Angular to React to language translations like C to Rust.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Ali Maaz (Head of WW GTM, Kiro, Amazon)
Ritik Khatwani (Senior Worldwide Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Alessandro Lori (CTO, Verizon Connect)

title: Simple Governance: How Kiro Makes Enterprise Policies Human-Friendly
abstract: Kiro agents execute code, invoke models, and interact with external services on behalf of developers. Enterprise administrators desire to constrain what agents can do without slowing developers down. We built a centralized governance system backed by Dogwood/Cedar that compiles admin-authored policies into governance documents enforced across every client (IDE, CLI, Web,Mobile) and server-side services. The system separates governance from configuration, uses deny-wins semantics with fail-closed enforcement, and scopes rules by hierarchies. Learn how we use Kiro itself to author and analyze governance policies to make enterprise controls human-friendly and manageable.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Nima Kaviani (Principal Product Manager, AWS)
Vipin Mohan (Principal Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Under the hood of Kiro Crew: orchestration, memory, and safe autonomy
abstract: Handing real work to a crew of agents raises real questions: How does it coordinate parallel subagents without losing the thread? How does memory save across sessions so agents don't start cold? How do you give agents access to your code and CI while staying safe? In this chalk talk, we'll dig into how Kiro Crew works: observable multi-agent orchestration over Agent Client Protocol, self-evolving memory and skills you can inspect and edit, scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs, and defense-in-depth security with sandboxing, denied-by-default commands, and signed audit logs. Bring your architecture and security questions and we'll whiteboard through them.
speakers: kirankumar chandrashekar (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Ryan Yanchuleff (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Full stack development on AWS: bring your questions
abstract: Building modern web and mobile front ends means juggling a lot of moving parts, and everyone's stack looks a little different. This chalk talk is an open Q&A, so bring your real questions and challenges. We'll talk through how AWS Amplify helps you define backends in code and ship full-stack apps fast, how AWS AppSync powers real-time and offline data with managed GraphQL and WebSocket APIs, and how AWS Device Farm lets you test across real browsers and mobile devices before your users do. Whether you're starting a greenfield app or scaling an existing one, come ready to steer the conversation.
speakers: Avinash Karthik Chalamalasetty (Software Development Manager, Amazon)
Andrés Aguilar (Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: The AWS CLI in an Agentic World: Less Tokens, More Done
abstract: AI coding agents are increasingly orchestrating cloud infrastructure, but they can be expensive and slow when every action requires chaining low-level API calls. The AWS CLI offers a different path: composable, structured commands that collapse multi-step workflows into single invocations. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Agent Toolkit gives AI agents first-class access to AWS through the CLI, why purpose-built commands are inherently cheaper for agents to execute, and what "developer experience for machines" means for CLI design going forward.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Alex Shovlin (Software Engineer, AWS)
Liam Greenamyre (Principal Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build a SaaS control plane with Kiro specs and Strands multi-tenant constructs
abstract: A SaaS control plane - tenant onboarding, billing, configuration management, agent provisioning is the most repeatable software every software vendor builds from scratch. In this builder's session, use Kiro specs to define the control plane requirements and let Kiro implement the scaffolding, then wire multi-tenant agent capabilities using Strands' open-source constructs. You'll build a working onboarding flow, a tenant configuration store, and a simple agent provisioning endpoint - all from a spec, not from scratch. Leave with a reusable starting point for your own control plane and a pattern for using Kiro and Strands together to accelerate platform development.

abstract: As you delegate more complex development work to AI agents, manual coordination can limit how much you can take on. Learn how to automate multi-agent orchestration to reduce supervision while maintaining your quality standards. This session explores patterns for dividing work among focused agents and building reusable processes that include verification. Through examples from the Kiro team and HERE Technologies, see how these principles apply in Kiro workflows and learn the trade-offs in context management, execution time, and cost.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: mac Merritt (Sr. SDE, Amazon)
Romain Dura (Principal Engineer, AWS)

title: Best practices for making coding agent orchestration more deterministic
abstract: As agents work on longer, more complex tasks, the context window fills up and the agent can lose track of its plan and execution steps. The manual setup required to get multi-agent orchestration to reliably complete these kinds of tasks can be complex and brittle. In this chalk talk, we will walk through best practices, tools, and patterns that power users have perfected to set up and scale multi-agent workloads. Bring questions, challenges, or edge cases you ran into and we'll walk you through how to approach them to improve reliability.
speakers: Arundeep Nagaraj (Sr Manager, Customer Success, Kiro, Amazon Web Services)
Romain Dura (Principal Engineer, AWS)

title: Build on top of large codebases without breaking your code
abstract: Your AI agent writes code fast, but when you unleash it on a large codebase, context can fill up quickly and the agent can make questionable implementation choices. Learn how Kiro uses neurosymbolic techniques to understand what you want to build, removing ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. Then, learn simple practices you can use to keep your agent implementation surgical, and detect drift before it spreads all over your codebase.
speakers: Anil Maktala (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Making Kiro Crew work for your team
abstract: Kiro Crew is the persistent, open source development workspace that remembers your context, learns how you work, and coordinates across your unique tools and workflows, so you come back to progress instead of another workflow to restart. In this session, you'll learn how to make Kiro Crew work for your team: wire in the tools your team already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape shared memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold and maintain team standards and best practices.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater

title: Building 10x Organizations - Using Modern Productivity Metrics (sponsored by Atlassian)
abstract: 10x developers may be a myth, but 10x organizations are very real, as proven by the influential study performed in the 1980s, ‘The Coding War Games.’ In this keynote-style session, teams will take a detailed, granular look at the barriers to productivity developers face today and modern approaches for removing them. You’ll learn about the history of productivity theory, and how previous practices have influenced our current understanding. DevOps and Platform Engineering philosophy is clearly converging on developer experience. But which of these approaches works? DORA? SPACE? DevEx? What should we invest in and create urgency behind today so we don’t have the same discussion again in a decade? This presentation is brought to you by Atlassian, an AWS Partner.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Justin Reock (CTO, DX // Atlassian)

title: From code to production in seconds — building web apps that last
abstract: Getting a web application live is fast. Keeping it running, reliable, and affordable as you grow is the hard part. In this chalk talk, we dig into the developer journey from first deploy to production scale: zero-config deployment, full-stack provisioning with open-source building blocks, and how to scale without starting over. Bring your questions about framework support, backend integration, and pricing.

title: Ship web apps that just work
abstract: Your agent can ship a web application in seconds. What happens after that is the hard part. In this session, learn how you and your agents get everything you need in one place, integrated and ready in seconds. We walk through how to go from code to production without configuring infrastructure, how the Agent Toolkit keeps deployments reliable, and how to scale without starting over.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater

title: Continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) on AWS
abstract: Whether you're shipping a monolith or hundreds of microservices, every change needs to reach production safely and quickly. In this session, learn how to build a CI/CD pipeline with AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild using infrastructure as code. The pipeline will utilize AI agents running on Amazon Bedrock to review every change—pull requests and direct commits alike—for security flaws, code quality, architecture, and accessibility. The agents report what they find, while you write rules to determine whether ship...or stop. AWS CodeDeploy will orchestrate canary deployments that roll back automatically when an issue is detected by an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Emil Lerch (Principal Specialist, AWS)
Leo Zhadanovsky (Enterprise Technologist, Education/SLG/Elections, WWPS, Amazon Web Services)

title: What AI agents need from an application backend
abstract: AI agents build applications differently than people do. They work from code, call APIs, run in parallel, and keep working after you close your laptop. In this session, learn what a backend has to provide for an agent to carry an application from first prompt to production: schema and configuration as code the agent can read and change, serverless infrastructure with nothing to size or provision, data APIs and authentication that work on the first call, isolated environments for every experiment the agent runs, logs the agent can query when something breaks, and approval steps that keep destructive changes in your hands.

title: Trusted intent: How Kiro proves your specs before writing any code
abstract: Your AI agent writes code fast, but is it building what you actually meant? Kiro's requirements analysis goes far beyond asking an LLM to generate a spec. It combines auto-formalization, SMT solvers, and neuro-symbolic techniques to mathematically detect ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. In this session, learn how we turned decades of formal methods into a developer experience that feels like answering simple yes/no questions while catching the bugs that cost the most to fix.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Nadia Labai (Senior Applied Scientist, AWS)
Brian Beach (Tech Lead, Developer Experience, AWS)

title: Make the agent code while you sleep
abstract: Anyone can prompt an agent. The hard part is getting it to work the way you want—for hours, unattended, without going off the rails. This advanced workshop digs into orchestration. You'll build a custom agent, then set a goal so strong the agent can't redefine it or declare victory early. You'll decompose work across subagents, use directives like /goal to keep execution on track, and design guardrails that let an agent run long and autonomously while landing where you intended. We'll use Kiro, but these patterns transfer to any agentic system. You must bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Keerthi Sreenivas Konjety (Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Govindhi Venkatachalapathy (Sr.Specialist Solution Architect, AWS)

title: Build your own crew: hands-on with Kiro Crew
abstract: Kiro Crew is an open-source, multi-agent workspace you can bend to your own workflows. In this hands-on workshop, you'll put it to work. Hand your crew a real task and watching it plan, spawn parallel subagents, and gate each action for your approval. Then personalize: wire in the tools you already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold. Finally, assemble a purpose-built App to run a workflow end-to-end, from intake through review. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Apply Amazon's frontier team playbook to your organization
abstract: AI coding agents sped up code generation, but not how fast it reaches customers. Teams seeing 4.5x to 10x gains aren't just adopting tools. They've redesigned how they work. In this chalk talk, learn what these "frontier teams" do differently: investing in agent context and steering files, making intent explicit before code is written, feeding agents well-scoped work instead of babysitting them, shifting testing left so agents self-correct before they reach the pipeline. We'll unpack real examples from teams across Amazon and talk through how to run your own pilot. Bring your questions about making AI work in your organization.

Alok Dhamanaskar (Engineering, Kiro, AWS)

title: Mastering agentic development: skills, custom agents, and steering
abstract: The best results from agentic AI don't come from clever one-off prompts, but from shaping how agents work. In this session, go beyond prompting to learn techniques that apply to any agentic coding tool. Craft reusable skills that encode your team's know-how, build custom agents tuned to specific jobs, and use steering files to carry your conventions and architecture across sessions. We'll cover how to set goals the agent will actually follow, when to let it run autonomously, and how to tell a skill that's useful versus noise. We'll demo live in Kiro, but the principles transfer wherever you work.

title: AWS AI League: Build agents with AgentCore (Agentic Football Cup)
abstract: Coordinating agents is where multi agent systems break. They duplicate work, drop handoffs, and burn tokens. In this workshop, build and deploy five autonomous agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Kiro and the Strands Agents SDK, then field them five versus five in live Agentic Football matches. Write the tools your agents call, orchestrate multi turn reasoning across a maze like arena, and solve coordination problems that decide the match. Tune prompts, roles, and tactics between rounds and watch your score climb a live leaderboard. Leave with working code, production ready multi agent patterns, and a shot at the Finale.

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Designing Agentic AI Applications
abstract: Ever stared at multiple disconnected systems held together by manual handoffs and thought, "there has to be a better way"? Agentic AI is that better way. In this hands-on Rodeo session, you team up to design an end-to-end agentic solution for a real-world scenario: multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop decision points, and MCP integration. Swap ideas with other teams, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns for turning manual chaos into autonomous workflows.
