abstract: Everyone wants AI. Nobody wants to be the team that shipped it without security and governance. In this Rodeo, you'll join a team and face three demanding stakeholders: a security hawk, a data visibility champion, and a platform lead, racing to get Agentic AI live. Your team's mission: build a governance architecture that keeps all three happy. Together, you'll whiteboard, debate, and build against the clock, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns. Best architecture rides away with the win.

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Building an AI-Ready Data Foundation
abstract: Your data estate wasn't designed for AI agents. Nobody's was. But somewhere between your RDBMS, NoSQL clusters, and that untouchable data lake, an agentic-ready architecture waits to be built. In this Rodeo session, your team draws a challenge: a legacy warehouse needing a semantic layer, a sprawling lake needing an ontology, or a metadata mess that lets agents in without letting governance out. Your job: build a data layer that makes agents productive, keeps compliance calm, and gives analysts self-service. You'll whiteboard ontologies, debate metadata, and wire up multi-agent access against the clock. Best architecture rides away with the win.
speakers: Anurag Singh (Leader Solutions Architecture, AWS)
Jigna Gandhi (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Transforming Customer Experience with AI
abstract: "Your call is important to us." Nobody believes that anymore, and neither do your customers. Contact centers are being rebuilt around AI, and getting the architecture right is what separates the experiences people love from the ones they dread. In this Rodeo session, you'll join a team and design the transformation yourself: voice AI that understands people, routing that knows why they're calling, and handoffs to humans that don't start with "can you repeat your issue?" You'll whiteboard, swap ideas with teammates, and build against the clock, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns. Saddle up! The design that finally makes "your call is important to us" true rides off with the win.
speakers: Troy Dieter (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Jacob Scheatzle (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Disha Jayswal (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: AWS wherever you need it: From the cloud to the edge
abstract: While most workloads can run in the cloud, some remain on-premises or at the edge due to low latency, local data processing, or data residency needs. AWS Local Zones, AWS Outposts, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS AI Factories extend AWS services, APIs, and tools to metro areas, on-premises data centers, and the far edge. Explore how these infrastructure offerings power a broad range of hybrid cloud and edge computing use cases such as financial trading, manufacturing, and AI. Learn how AWS helps you run regulated workloads with edge requirements, power generative AI with edge data, and migrate workloads with on-premises dependencies, featuring AT&T's migration and modernization at scale.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Ian Cottingham (Director, Software Development, Amazon Web Services)
Rama Raghavan (AVP Cloud Architecture, AT&T Inc.)
Spencer Dillard (Director, Software Dev, EC2, Amazon Web Services)

title: Optimizing SAP RISE for Cost and Scale with Intel (sponsored by Intel)
abstract: Discover how Intel's custom SAP-certified Intel® Xeon® 6 processor, exclusively available on AWS, transforms and accelerates your SAP RISE journey. Engineered to deliver the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel cloud processors, this powerful solution unlocks up to 50% higher SAPS performance. Whether migrating, consolidating, or scaling SAP workloads, Intel Xeon 6 on AWS empowers organizations to optimize costs, enhance efficiency, and maximize their SAP RISE investment — driving faster, smarter, and more cost-effective outcomes for modern enterprise demands. This presentation is brought to you by Intel, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Emanuele Baldassarre (Managing Director, Accenture)
Caitlin Anderson (Corporate VP Sales and Management Group, Intel Corporation)

title: Building Beyond the Hardware: Transforming IBM i/AIX Workloads with AWS (sponsored by Lightedge)
abstract: IBM Power organizations support mission-critical workloads across industries. Now, there are more infrastructure options than ever before, providing hybrid transformation opportunities and challenges. This session explores how to develop a hybrid strategy that balances performance, resiliency, security, and business objectives. Hear how enterprises are exploring a phased modernization strategy that rehosts IBM workloads in a hybrid cloud environment, connects to AWS, and evolves their infrastructure. Learn how they establish secure, low-latency AWS connectivity and integrate IBM business logic with cloud-native services. This session provides proven frameworks, architectural insights, and modernization strategies to reduce risk, accelerate transformation, and maximize infrastructure value. This presentation is brought to you by Lightedge, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Aileen Curtin (Director, Cloud Center of Excellence, Lightedge)
josh patterson (Solutions Architect, Lightedge)

title: From Dashboards to Agents: Building an Agentic NOC (sponsored by Selector AI)
abstract: For decades, NOCs have been built around dashboards, alerts, and humans manually stitching together signals from dozens of disconnected tools. That model is breaking under the complexity of modern hybrid networks and sprawling multi-cloud estates. Simply bolting AI onto existing monitoring tools isn't enough to fix it. This talk reimagines the NOC around purpose-built agents built for cloud-scale operations, each progressing through a five-stage maturity model (Observe, Monitor, Triage, Optimize, and Act), that governs how much autonomy each agent earns over time. Attendees will leave with a concrete mental model for evolving their own cloud operations stack from tools that observe to agents that act. This presentation is brought to you by Selector AI, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Michael Bonnett Jr (Senior Systems Engineer, Selector)

title: Stop paying for idle GPUs on Amazon EKS (sponsored by Apptio)
abstract: AI workloads can consume millions of dollars in infrastructure before anyone notices whether they're being used efficiently. GPUs sit idle, clusters become overprovisioned, and engineering teams struggle to balance performance with rapidly growing costs. In this session, learn how engineering teams running Amazon EKS can identify wasted GPU capacity, understand the true cost of AI workloads, and automate optimization without sacrificing application performance. We'll share practical techniques to improve utilization, reduce waste, and optimize AI infrastructure at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Apptio, an AWS Partner.
topics: red hat openshift service on aws (rosa)
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Andrew Midgley (Principal Product Marketing Manager, IBM)
Joe Dahlquist (VP Product Marketing, IBM)

title: From Intent to Interconnection: Building Multicloud Networks in Minutes (sponsored by Equinix)
abstract: Modern enterprises span clouds, AI providers, private infrastructure, partners, and sovereign environments, yet networking is still built one connection at a time. Equinix Fabric One introduces a new approach: declare the business outcome you need and let the platform automatically compose the secure, resilient, any-to-any network required to deliver it. In this live demo, see how Fabric One transforms multicloud networking into an intent-driven experience. Watch a simple declaration trigger automated routing, cloud peering, encryption, resiliency, and failover across multiple providers and destinations. See how Equinix enables organizations to move from “choose, design, configure, operate” to “declare, compose, deliver.” This presentation is brought to you by Equinix, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Ben Thomas (Sr. Principal Networking, Technical Marketing, Equinix)

title: How Max Mara built multicloud FinOps with open source
abstract: Max Mara runs hundreds of applications across AWS, GCP, Alicloud, and on-prem serving 20+ million monthly visits, but had no unified view of cost or correlation to business outcomes. In this session, hear how they implemented open-source Cloud Intelligence Dashboards with FOCUS (FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification) to consolidate all sources into a single framework. Learn how unit economics — "Cost per Order" across 11 brands — drove 21% monthly cost optimization with minimal engineering effort. Walk away with an open-source based playbook for multicloud FinOps that delivers measurable results at enterprise scale.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Alessandro Bellini (FinOps Manager & Cloud Architect, Max Mara Fashion Group)
Yuriy Prykhodko (Principal Technologist | Head of Cloud Intelligence Dashboards, AWS)

title: Choosing the right hybrid deployment for your AI workloads
abstract: Organizations are running AI workloads for model training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning and inference, across an expanding set of environments, including AWS Regions, AWS Local Zones, AWS Outposts, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS AI Factories. The right deployment option depends on latency, data sovereignty, compute density, and scale. See how customers deploy accelerated AI across the hybrid spectrum: NVIDIA GPU-based and AWS Trainium-powered instances in Local Zones, purpose-built AWS AI Factories for large-scale training and model serving, and edge deployments for real-time inference. Hear how customers navigate these decisions, including Databricks tapping GPU capacity on AWS Local Zones and T-Mobile running latency-sensitive distributed inference, and learn which environment fits each AI workload without compromising performance and compliance.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Shivam Saggar (Sr. Product Manager (Tech), Amazon Web Services)
Shelby Seward (DMTS, Sr. Director, T-Mobile)
Chris McEvilly (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Real-world migrations: Lessons learned migrating to AWS Outposts
abstract: Organizations with data residency and digital sovereignty requirements face a critical question: how do you move workloads from on-premises infrastructure to AWS Outposts without disrupting compliance posture or operations? This Level 300 session distills lessons from migrating customers to Outposts across industries, organization sizes, and migration strategies, featuring SERPRO, Brazil's federal data processing company, and AT&T, migrating telecom workloads at scale. The session walks through the processes that delivered results, the quantifiable outcomes measured, and the critical mistakes to avoid. Learn how to select the right migration approach and navigate common blockers. The session also covers transitioning from first-generation to second-generation Outposts hardware.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Frankie Negro (Senior Hybrid Edge Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Marcelo Andrade (Cloud Engineer, SERPRO)
Scott Rose (Senior Manager Solution Architecture - Telco, AWS)

title: Workload Identity Federation in multicloud environments
abstract: Eliminating long-lived credentials across clouds is essential for secure multicloud operations. This session presents three proven identity federation patterns: leveraging native OIDC providers from Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure to assume AWS IAM roles with short-lived tokens, federating Kubernetes service accounts across cloud boundaries, and using SPIFFE/SPIRE for cryptographic workload identity across Kubernetes clusters. We walk through architecture decisions, trust policy design, and security best practices for each approach - covering GCP Workload Identity, Microsoft Entra ID federation, and cross-cluster OIDC. Attendees leave with actionable blueprints for credential-free multicloud access.
speakers: Preetam Rebello (Sr. Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Simran Singh (Canada, FSI Sr. SA, AWS Canada)

title: Governing autonomous AI agents across cloud boundaries
abstract: When autonomous agents coordinate across cloud boundaries, who enforces the rules — and how do you revoke access instantly when one goes rogue? In this chalk talk, we whiteboard governed multi-agent coordination: Cedar as a portable policy engine across AWS, Azure, and GCP, A2A protocol for cross-cloud agent communication, and a kill switch for instant revocation. The audience picks the scenario — flight delays, trade failures, or healthcare cancellations — and we draw how policy, identity, and coordination work at each boundary crossing.
speakers: Prema iyer (Sr. Technical Account Manager, AWS)
Arko Dutta (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Scaling interactive generative AI at Netflix with AWS Local Zones
abstract: Generative AI VFX and Animation teams at Netflix require the latest GPU hardware for creative workflows, including real-time rendering, VFX editorial, and color correction. These workloads demand low-latency access to high-performance compute close to creative teams. AWS Local Zones make this possible by placing Amazon EC2 G7e instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs in the Los Angeles metro. Netflix's Studio GenAI Infrastructure, including GenAI Sessions and Universal Compute Service, uses Local Zones to serve just-in-time combinations of software and hardware in secure, isolated sandbox environments. Tools like ComfyUI and AI Toolkit with complex dependencies run on task-oriented, elastic GPU assignments, so Netflix scales creative AI workloads efficiently without managing physical infrastructure.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Justin Rosen (Engineering Manager, Netflix, Inc.)
Daniel Heckenberg (Staff Software Engineer, Netflix)
Mathew George (Senior Product Manager - Techincal, External Services, Amazon Web Services)

title: VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts with AWS Transform
abstract: Many organizations struggle to migrate VMware workloads due to complex dependencies, network translation challenges, and the need to support both cloud and on-premises targets. In this workshop, you use AWS Transform MGN, an agentic AI service, to execute an end-to-end VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts. You work through AI-driven discovery, dependency mapping, intelligent wave planning, automated network conversion, and orchestrated execution. See how Trianz's Concierto platform also integrates with AWS Transform to streamline migration to AWS Outposts with automated orchestration and operational governance.
speakers: Aditya Lolla (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Gokul Chandra Purnachandra Reddy (Principle Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: How Adobe unified multicloud observability with open source
abstract: Adobe operates production services across AWS and Azure, but 20+ monitoring tools and per-cloud dashboards turned every cross-cloud incident into a translation problem before debugging could begin. In this session, hear how Adobe standardized on OpenTelemetry and consolidated to four open-source technologies (Cortex, Grafana Tempo, FluentBit, and Grafana) with AWS as the operational hub processing 1M+ trace samples per second. The result was a single pane of glass for every engineer regardless of where workloads run, and multi-million dollar savings through telemetry compression. Walk away with a proven, vendor-independent playbook for multicloud observability built on open source and open standards.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Vikram Mehto (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Chris Featherstone (Sr Engineering Manager, Adobe)

title: Gemini gets closer to traders with AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
abstract: Gemini, a NASDAQ-listed crypto exchange, serves traders with diverse latency needs. For the most latency-sensitive workloads, AWS Outposts at Gemini's NY5 facility runs adjacent to the matching engine with sub-millisecond connectivity via cross-connects. For cloud-native traders, AWS Local Zones in NYC deliver sub-2ms latency to the matching engine through Amazon VPC peering: bringing compute into New York Local Zone cuts round-trip latency by roughly 80%, with provisioning in minutes rather than months. For customers prioritizing simplicity, the AWS Region offers a fully managed API that also serves agentic trading systems via Model Context Protocol (MCP). Hear how Gemini's tiered model turns compute placement into a competitive lever for your location-sensitive workloads.
speakers: Ina Rademacher (Sr ESM, AWS)
Joshua Smith (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Architecting AWS Outposts networking for enterprise and ultra-low-latency workloads
abstract: This session covers networking on second-generation AWS Outposts, spanning scalable multi-site topologies and ultra-low-latency bare-metal deployments. Learn how the second-generation dedicated network rack, local gateway routing domains, and intra-VPC and inter-VPC communication form the foundation for segmentation and local connectivity. See how the design extends to multi-site interconnections spanning Outposts and AWS Local Zones, extended VPC designs, and resilient architectures grounded in AWS Well-Architected principles. Explore how bare-metal instances with high-throughput accelerated networking and rack topology support co-located workloads where every microsecond matters.
speakers: Harsha Sanku (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Leonardo Solano (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: How RBC built a regulated multicloud platform
abstract: Enterprises running regulated workloads across multiple clouds face a compounding challenge: every platform decision — databases, message buses, orchestration — deepens lock-in and complicates compliance. The Royal Bank of Canada chose a different path. Over seven years, RBC built a multicloud Kubernetes platform spanning AWS, Azure, and on-premises, purpose-built for financial services under multi-jurisdictional oversight. RBC shares how they eliminated vendor lock-in by migrating to open-source databases and messaging, established a "golden path" that lets teams deploy to any cloud without rearchitecting, and extended that foundation into agentic AI operations for automated root-cause analysis and remediation. Walk away with a practical playbook for building a compliant, portable multicloud platform that strengthens your security posture at every layer.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Vinh Tran (RBC Fellow, RBC)
Chris Brandon (WW FSI Enterprise Technologist Lead, Amazon Web Services)
Ernani Cecon (Vice President, Hybrid Cloud, Royal Bank of Canada)

title: How Emirates built Multicloud Agents with open-source Agentic AI Gateway
abstract: Enterprises running AI agents across multiple clouds face fragmented model access, inconsistent pricing, and vendor lock-in. Open-source Gateways provide a unified interface to orchestrate Models across Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Google Vertex AI based on use-case requirements and token economics. This session demonstrates how Emirates built a multi-cloud agent architecture using an open-source Agentic AI Gateway as the routing layer and Bedrock as the primary backbone. Learn patterns for cost-based routing, fallback strategies, model selection by capability, and unified observability across model and cloud providers.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Shivagami Gugan (Chief Technologist Worldwide, Amazon Web Services)
Mahmoud Abid (Head of AI and immersive Platforms, Emirates Group)
Rishi Singla (Sr Solutions Architect, amazon web services)

title: Architecting for digital sovereignty with AWS Hybrid Cloud solutions
abstract: This session uses real-world case studies to understand how AWS hybrid cloud architectures such as AWS Local Zones, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS Outposts help customers meet their digital sovereignty needs. It examines data residency boundaries, network separation, operational controls, and security guardrail options available in hybrid cloud solutions. It then shows how to configure governance controls, including Service Control Policies (SCPs), to help customers comply with regulatory requirements. Finally, it covers how to detect and prevent unauthorized data flows between hybrid infrastructure and the parent Region.
speakers: Sherry Lin (Principal Product Manager, Amazon)
Lakshmi VP (Solutions Architect - WWPS, AWS)

title: Applying the Well-Architected Framework to AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
abstract: AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones bring cloud closer to your end users and workloads but introduce architectural decisions that do not exist in a purely cloud-native model. Designing for resilience when infrastructure sits in your facility, and balancing security and cost across hybrid topologies, calls for rethinking each pillar. In this chalk talk, the session walks through the AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar by pillar, exploring how each applies and where it bends at the edge. Bring your toughest design questions. The session draws out real-world patterns, discusses trade-offs, and builds a practical mental model for well-architected hybrid solutions.
speakers: Adam Duffield (Senior Technical Account Manager, AWS)
Manthan Raval (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: From prototype to production agents across clouds
abstract: Most agent prototypes share the same shape. One loop, a long lived key on every tool, memory in a side table, the rules in the prompt, and a trace that ends at the model call. It works in a demo. Production readiness and portability across clouds come down to the same four decisions, identity, tool access, state, and governance. In this chalk talk we draw that prototype and rebuild it live into a production agent, one decision at a time, with the room voting at every fork, including how to split the agent, where rules live, how identity federates across providers, where memory has its home, and how one governance layer sees every hop. Then we add a new cloud provider to the drawing and show how little changes.
speakers: Clark Richey (Principal Technologist, Amazon)
Shankar Ramachandran (Principal Technologist, AWS)

title: How LSEG Built a Multicloud Internal Developer Platform with Kubernetes and AI
abstract: At London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), deploying enterprise workloads traditionally took weeks or months of onboarding, governance, networking, and operational setup. In this session, we’ll share how a small AI-augmented engineering team built RouteOne: LSEG’s fully managed multicloud application platform, enabling developers to deploy compliant workloads across multiple cloud providers in minutes by committing their code and a single YAML definition. We’ll explore the Kubernetes-based control plane, enterprise guardrails, and AI-native developer experience powered by APIs, MCP and agent skills. We’ll also share lessons learned from using AI-assisted engineering practices to rapidly deliver a lean, enterprise-grade platform in a regulated environment.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Richard Chester (Principal Solution Architect, AWS)
Dean Bryen (Head of Cloud Platform Engineering, LSEG PLC)

title: How Itaú built cell-based resilience for critical workloads across clouds
abstract: Mission-critical workloads require extreme resilience without the latency penalty of multi-region architectures, especially when strong consistency and real-time external integrations are required. In this session, discover how cell-based and shard-based architectures reduce blast radius and contain failures across cloud providers while keeping latency within strict thresholds. Explore traffic management patterns between cloud providers, data replication strategies including synchronous and asynchronous approaches, and consistency models. Learn how architectural adapters enable workload portability and provider independence. Gain practical patterns for cross-cell replication and automated failover, with examples from Itaú Unibanco's production environment.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Bruno Emer (Principal Technologist, Amazon Web Services)
Jorge Rua (Distinguished Engineer, Itaú Unibanco)
Guilherme Greco (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Migrate and modernize workloads with AWS Outposts
abstract: Organizations running on-premises workloads on legacy virtualization platforms are looking to migrate applications to AWS and modernize them to be more resilient and operationally consistent with their cloud workloads. AWS Outposts supports customers on this journey and is now available in second-generation single- and multi-rack offerings that deliver new instance types and Amazon EBS storage, up to 40% better price-performance, and enhanced networking features for monitoring and security. This session covers migration and modernization strategies for organizations looking to move to a cloud operating model on-premises, as well as strategies for first-generation Outposts customers to upgrade to the latest generation.
speakers: Brianna Rosentrater (Senior Hybrid Edge Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Vaibhav Phadnis (WW GTM Lead - AWS Outposts, Amazon)

title: Right workload on the right cloud - multicloud workload placement
abstract: You operate a multicloud organization, and every new workload raises the same challenge: which cloud should this workload run on? Too often the answer comes down to habit, existing vendor relationships, or whoever argues loudest, and workloads end up somewhere that adds complexity, risk, or complicates compliance. In this session you will learn how to approach multicloud workload placement so that the decisions you make are explainable, repeatable and auditable.
industry: Financial Services; Healthcare & Life Sciences; Travel & Hospitality

title: Multicloud Operating Models for ISVs
abstract: ISVs adopting multiple clouds face the same trade-offs. This breakout distills cloud-agnostic operating-model patterns from production multi-cloud estates -- workload placement, abstraction layers, resiliency, and FinOps (optimization, tokenization), and unified observability -- illustrated by SAP running at 25,000+ accounts across AWS, Azure, and GCP. SAP's team walks through what stayed cloud-specific, what they unified, and what they had to invent. Leave with operating-model patterns you can apply across clouds.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Joachim Aumann (Senior Solution Architect, AWS)
Dave Smith (Lead Architect, SAP Global Cloud Operations)
Olga Calvo (Customer Solutions Manager, AWS)

title: How Workday built multicloud data interoperability foundation for Agentic AI
abstract: As enterprises scale agentic AI, the hardest problem is often giving agents secure, governed access to data spread across multiple clouds. Physically copying the data between clouds introduces cost, latency, and governance risk. In this session, you will learn how Workday leverages Apache Iceberg catalog federation to build bidirectional, zero-copy integration that enables cross-cloud data access without duplicating or moving data. You will see how this open standard based approach lets AI agents reason over trusted enterprise data in place, with governance and business context preserved.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Mehreen Ali (Principal Software Development Engineer, Workday)
Shankar Ramachandran (Principal Technologist, AWS)
Avijit Goswami (Principal Applied AI Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: How Marriott built AI-powered travel search with agents on AWS and model on GCP
abstract: Marriott's guest-facing AI travel search, Ask Bonvoy, runs across two clouds by design: Gemini Flash on GCP handles conversational reasoning, while AWS powers the agentic backbone — EKS for orchestration, Aurora PostgreSQL with pgVector for RAG retrieval, and Bedrock Guardrails for real-time safety. This split lets Marriott pick the best model for the job without re-platforming, and scale across 9,000+ properties. In this lightning talk, learn how Marriott's engineering team wired a multi-cloud agentic architecture with model portability built in — and walk away with cloud-agnostic patterns for inference routing, agentic orchestration, and safety guardrails across clouds.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Bharat Lakhiyani (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: How 3M does multicloud incident management with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: Incident response in multicloud environments is challenging because of fragmented observability and depth-of-skills gaps in your teams across cloud providers. In this session, learn how 3M used AWS DevOps Agent to investigate failures at scale across 250+ AWS accounts and a connected Azure estate of comparable scale. You will see a quick demo of how DevOps Agent investigates cross-cloud failures, reducing the required human effort from hours to minutes. Walk away with lessons learnt and a deeper understanding of how DevOps Agent helps you in multicloud environments.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Vijay Sitaram (Principal TAM, AWS)
Chinnayya Ganachar (Senior Architect, 3M)

title: GPU orchestration using NVIDIA Run:ai across the edge
abstract: AWS and NVIDIA have collaborated for over a decade to deliver GPU-accelerated solutions across the cloud and edge, yet Kubernetes still treats GPUs as opaque, unshareable integers. In this Level 400 code talk, learn how to deploy NVIDIA Run:ai on Amazon EKS and execute a complete model lifecycle on shared GPU infrastructure. Using Terraform, provision EKS clusters on Amazon EC2 instances with NVIDIA L4 GPUs, install the Run:ai control plane and cluster agents, and configure project-scoped GPU quotas with priority-based sharing. Then see how Run:ai orchestrates a QLoRA fine-tuning job on Qwen3-14B and serves the resulting adapter with vLLM so you can compare base model responses against your fine-tuned model in real time.
speakers: Alex Iankoulski (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Siva Devabakthini (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc)
Robert Belson (Senior Developer Advocate, Amazon Web Services)

title: Implementing agentic AI solutions on-premises and at the edge
abstract: Learn how to extend Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to hybrid and edge services to build distributed agentic apps using Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication with on-premises data. Get hands-on with hybrid agentic AI using Amazon Bedrock and Strands Agents while exploring AWS hybrid and edge solutions for data residency compliance.
speakers: Fernando Galves (Senior Applied AI Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Kyle Palasti (Edge Specialist Solutions Architect, National Security, Amazon Web Services)

speakers: Fernando Galves (Senior Applied AI Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge
abstract: As organizations use agentic AI to automate complex infrastructure operations, many have data residency, low latency, and security requirements that depend on running AI closer to their data. This workshop explores how customers deploy self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge to meet these requirements while enabling autonomous operations. Learn how to architect, provision, configure, and optimize AI agents that run locally, and how to extend the same architecture to AWS hybrid and edge infrastructure such as AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts.
speakers: Fernando Galves (Senior Applied AI Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Chris McEvilly (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge
abstract: As organizations use agentic AI to automate complex infrastructure operations, many have data residency, low latency, and security requirements that depend on running AI closer to their data. This workshop explores how customers deploy self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge to meet these requirements while enabling autonomous operations. Learn how to architect, provision, configure, and optimize AI agents that run locally, and how to extend the same architecture to AWS hybrid and edge infrastructure such as AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts.
speakers: Fernando Galves (Senior Applied AI Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Extend Amazon EKS clusters for on-premises and edge use cases
abstract: This chalk talk covers strategies for modernizing distributed applications with Amazon EKS across AWS Regions, AWS Local Zones, and AWS Outposts. It demonstrates how EKS delivers a consistent experience across these deployment options, minimizing latency and enabling data residency. The session explores deploying a real-world application to an EKS cluster across distributed environments while maintaining a unified control plane. It covers use cases and design patterns for architecting resilient and scalable applications, following AWS Well-Architected Framework principles for consistency and security.
speakers: Eric Vasquez (AWS Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Jared Thompson (Sr. Systems Development Engineer, AWS)

title: How Amazon Robotics runs AWS Outposts across hundreds of fulfillment centers
abstract: Amazon Robotics operates AWS Outposts across hundreds of fulfillment centers, each supporting multiple teams with distinct workload requirements. In this code talk, learn how the team architects isolation on shared Outposts infrastructure, manages resource quotas across competing workloads, and implements high-availability strategies that keep robotic systems running through hardware and network failures. The session walks through the team onboarding model, failover patterns between Outposts and the parent AWS Region, and monitoring strategies that detect degradation before it impacts fulfillment operations.
speakers: Ian Cottingham (Director, Software Development, Amazon Web Services)
Gabe Gagliano (Senior Principal Technologist, Amazon)

title: What FanDuel learned running containers on hundreds of AWS Outposts
abstract: Running containerized workloads across dozens of AWS Local Zones and hundreds of AWS Outposts demands operational patterns that hold up at fleet scale. In this session, learn how FanDuel operates Amazon EKS across a huge hybrid edge fleet with a focus on high availability, patching, observability, service disruption handling, and autoscaling. The session digs into how workloads respond gracefully to service link and hardware disruptions, and how autoscaling behaves when compute is fixed and on-rack. Discover the operational model that keeps a large edge fleet healthy without growing the platform team at the same rate.
speakers: savallur Vallurupalli (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Ramsey McGrath (Staff Engineer, Fanduel)
Josh Coen (Sr Mgr, Solution Architecture Hybrid Edge, AWS)

title: Rivian's journey to Multi-Availability Zone factory resilience on AWS Outposts
abstract: Discover why Rivian chose AWS Outposts to support mission-critical manufacturing applications that produce vehicles at its Normal, Illinois, plant. Explore how Rivian architected highly redundant infrastructure across multiple Outposts racks, using fast Amazon EC2 provisioning and scaling to meet production line demands. This session covers Multi-Availability Zone deployment for high availability, Amazon RDS read replicas across racks for database resilience, and AWS Unified Operations for proactive observability across its hybrid environment. Learn how Rivian plans to scale this model into its 9-million-square-foot mega factory in Georgia.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Peter Dachnowicz (Principal Technical Account Manager, Amazon)
Adam Shake (Senior Manager Factory Site Reliability Engineering, Rivian Automotive, LLC)

title: Deployment strategies for highly available edge applications
abstract: Organizations need to be able to deploy critical applications that are highly available and fault-tolerant at the edge. These workloads are often some of the most demanding in terms of durability and availability requirements. Deploying workloads on AWS hybrid cloud and edge computing services like AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts requires planning for networking, compute, storage, and other failure modes. In this chalk talk, dig into each of these services, review use cases, and examine reference architectures. Learn design considerations and deployment patterns for high availability and disaster recovery.
speakers: George Oakes (Sr. Hybrid Solutions Architect, AWS)

speakers: George Oakes (Sr. Hybrid Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: SaaS Agents Anywhere
abstract: Customers make deliberate choices about where their workloads run. For SaaS vendors delivering agentic products, that means the runtime has to meet the workload where it is, not the other way around. This chalk talk teaches the everywhere agent pattern for SaaS: keep the control plane on AWS, run the agent runtime and data-plane execution wherever the customer's data lives. Learn three decisions: which destinations to support and when (multi-cloud, on-prem, or both), how to run agent runtimes outside AWS without rewriting your control plane (packaging, model backend selection, dependency portability), and how to manage identity, observability, and lifecycle across environments you don't own. Leave with the decision framework for shipping SaaS agents anywhere the customer's data lives.
speakers: Anthony McClure (Partner Solutions Architect, AWS)
Erik Anderson (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Accelerating with NVIDIA Omniverse: VW’s Battery Manufacturing Digital Twin (sponsored by NVIDIA)
abstract: Deloitte helped Volkswagen Group Components design and deploy a cloud-native, AI-ready digital twin on AWS, powered by NVIDIA Omniverse and the OpenUSD standard, for the GS7 battery production environment. By consolidating fragmented factory data — CAD models, robot programs, camera configurations, and defect imagery — into a photorealistic, simulation-ready scene on AWS, the team enabled virtual commissioning, synthetic inspection data generation, and earlier production validation. The result is a reusable, scalable platform built on AWS infrastructure and NVIDIA's industrial metaverse stack that reduces physical trial effort, accelerates line ramp-up, and creates a foundation for AI-driven quality inspection at scale. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Joerg Clobes (Head of Digitally Enabled OpEx, Volkswagen AG)
Martin Jaster (Digital Transformation & Governance, Volkswagen Group Components)

title: Dark Factory or Human in Every Loop: Building the Agentic SDLC in Between (sponsored by Port IO)
abstract: Your developers ship faster than ever. Your organization doesn't. The bottleneck moved from writing the code to everything that happens after it. Agents can help, but only with a trustworthy picture of your org and real permission to act in it. That's an agentic SDLC. Nobody ships you one, because yours is shaped like your organization. So we'll build one live for a company that doesn't exist: a t-shirt printer whose three factories disagree on what a medium is. Then we take the humans out and see how dark the factory gets. An agent built it in two hours. This presentation is brought to you by Port IO, an AWS Partner.

title: Building the Construction Cloud: How Procore AI &Amazon Bedrock Power the Built World (sponsored by Procore)
abstract: Construction generates massive volumes of structured and unstructured data, such as drawings, RFIs, and safety reports, that most AI infrastructure isn't built to handle. In this session, we'll break down how Amazon Bedrock's model access, guardrails, and enterprise controls power Procore AI, and why that combination is what makes construction-specific AI viable at enterprise scale. You'll leave with a clear picture of the architecture, and why we think this is the first real blueprint for AI in the built environment. This presentation is brought to you by Procore, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Thiago da Costa (SVP, AI & Data, Procore Technologies, Inc.)

title: Amazon Leo: Connectivity Beyond the Reach of Existing Networks (sponsored by Amazon Leo)
abstract: Amazon Leo is building a constellation of over 3,200 low Earth orbit satellites to deliver fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities worldwide. In this session, learn how Leo's advanced satellite technology, purpose-built customer antennas, and deep integration with AWS will extend reliable connectivity to enterprises, governments, and individuals — wherever they are. Walk away with a clear understanding of Leo's architecture, use cases, and how it complements existing network infrastructure to close the global digital divide. This presentation is brought to you by Amazon Leo, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Nick Matthews (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Leo)

title: The co-build playbook: Turn AWS partner programs into deployable industrial solutions (sponsored by Belden)
abstract: Manufacturers know their machines generate valuable data — yet most digital initiatives stall before they scale, trapped between legacy OT protocols and cloud analytics that were never designed for the plant floor. This session shows how a connected partner ecosystem closes that gap. Learn how Belden acquires, conditions, and secures data at the physical layer, and how Edge2Web Factory Insights turns that data into high-powered analytics and AI-enriched insights based on AWS IoT SiteWise. Discover the reference architecture behind a joint deployment, from edge protocol connectivity to AI-driven insight. See how co-development with AWS compressed the path from whiteboard to production. And explore how to apply this pattern to your own operations. This presentation is brought to you by Belden, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: From discoverable to buyable: Commerce stacks for agent-driven shoppers (sponsored by Stripe)
abstract: Join Stripe on how AI is changing how shoppers find and buy products—and what it means for your commerce stack. With 20% of holiday ecommerce traffic projected from AI agents, this session is designed for retail leaders moving from "exploring" to "ready." Converting this traffic requires a different approach to catalog readiness, checkout, fraud, and fulfillment. Attendees will leave with clear priorities to act on today and carry into 2027. This presentation is brought to you by Stripe, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Danny Smith (Agentic Commerce Solutions Lead, Stripe, Inc.)

title: Build an intelligent contact center with Zendesk and AWS (sponsored by Zendesk)
abstract: Contact center teams need to resolve issues consistently across channels while giving agents the information and tools to act. In this session, discover how Zendesk and AWS work together to create a native contact center experience within Zendesk that connects customer interactions, workflows, and systems in one connected environment. Learn how AI can enhance voice support by handling routine needs, guiding conversations, and helping customers reach resolution faster. See how human handoffs preserve the customer’s history, needs, and progress, giving agents the context they need to step in seamlessly, personalize the experience, and move each interaction toward resolution. This presentation is brought to you by Zendesk, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Nuri Gocay (Director of Platform Architecture, Zendesk, Inc.)

title: Reimagining Patient Engagement with AI and Cloud (sponsored by Incedo Inc.)
abstract: Life sciences organizations are exploring how AI and cloud can transform engagement across the patient journey. This executive discussion will examine how connected data, generative AI and intelligent automation can enable more personalized, timely and responsive patient experiences. The conversation will explore opportunities to reduce friction, improve engagement, drive adherence, and deliver more connected omnichannel experiences aligned with business priorities. It will also address the challenges of data fragmentation, governance, trust and adoption. Attendees will gain practical executive perspectives on moving beyond AI experimentation to scalable, responsible solutions that deliver meaningful value for patients and life sciences organizations. This presentation is brought to you by Incedo Inc., an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Nitin Seth (CEO & Co-Founder, Incedo Inc - SI Partner)

title: How Telecom leaders are putting AI to work
abstract: Leading Telecom operators are putting AI to work on the industry's toughest problems. Carriers are using AI to build revenue, improve network efficiency, deliver next-generation customer experiences, and modernize legacy systems. Yet fragmented data, legacy systems, and complexity create headwinds. This session explores the trends reshaping the industry and the challenges operators face. Through real-world examples and technical details, you will hear about the latest solutions and how leading carriers are building on AWS to scale their early experiments into production results.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Ishwar Parulkar (Chief Technologist, AWS Industries, AWS)

title: Modernizing Care for the Underserved: Montefiore's Cloud Journey
abstract: Montefiore Einstein is one of New York's leading academic health systems, serving 1.3 million Bronx residents across 11 hospitals and 300+ ambulatory locations. To best care for patients, most of whom rely on Medicare or Medicaid, Montefiore needed to modernize its enterprise technology. Montefiore selected AWS as its strategic cloud provider to build a secure, scalable, and resilient foundation that strengthens security and optimizes costs. This session explores how the transformation—including an Epic migration—enables AI-powered clinical decision support, improves the reliability of critical medical records, and expands patient access through Amazon One Medical. Learn the strategies, lessons, and cloud-first approach driving better outcomes for the patients and communities Montefiore serves.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Matt Dinger (Global Lead - Epic, AWS)
Deepesh Chandra (Chief Digital and Information Officer, Montefiore Health System)

title: Computing‑Power‑Cooling Synergy: Building the Future of Global Data Infrastructure (sponsored by Kehua Tech)
abstract: The rapid growth of AI workloads is driving new demands for large-scale data center infrastructure, with challenges in power supply, high-density cooling, and system integration. In this session, we will share real-world deployment practices and introduce end-to-end infrastructure solutions, including highly reliable UPS power systems, liquid cooling technologies, and turnkey integrated solutions. We will explore how computing, power, and cooling synergy can optimize data center efficiency, improve deployment agility, and accelerate the development of AI-ready infrastructure. This presentation is brought to you by Kehua Tech, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Lane Peng (Head of North American Office, Kehua Data Co., Ltd.)

title: Molecule to Market: Bayer & Capgemini Accelerate Drug Discovery with NVIDIA BioNeMo (sponsored by NVIDIA)
abstract: Bayer's CropKey strategy relies on target-based and profile-driven discovery to develop the next generation of crop protection solutions. A key challenge is enabling broad access to advanced AI models for protein structure prediction, target exploration, molecular docking, and molecular design, which are often complex and costly to operate. This session highlights how Bayer and Capgemini built a scalable, cloud-native platform on AWS that provides researchers with easy access to state-of-the-art biomolecular AI capabilities by leveraging NVIDIA BioNeMo NIMs. By operationalizing foundation models in a secure and cost-efficient environment, the platform helps close critical knowledge gaps in early discovery and accelerates the application of AI across the crop protection R&D pipeline. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Lukas Kuckelkorn (AWS Strategist – Northern & Central Europe, Capgemini)
Dr. Janosch Achenbach (Digital Transformation Lead - Data Science, Bayer AG - Crop Science)

title: Winning the War on Fraud with Network-Powered Intelligence (sponsored by Vonage, Part of Ericsson)
abstract: Fraud is winning. SIM swaps have surged over 1,000%; synthetic identity cases are up 60% year-over-year, legacy OTP defenses are structurally broken — and fraudsters know it. Every industry feels it. Banks, healthcare providers, retailers, rideshare and delivery platforms, all fighting the same battle, all demanding the same answer: security that doesn't sacrifice the customer experience. As the first and only communications and Network API provider to achieve the AWS Financial Services Industry Competency, Vonage is changing the equation. Discover how enterprises are moving to a model where identity is verified silently at the network layer, before fraud happens. Built on AWS, powered by direct carrier intelligence. This presentation is brought to you by Vonage, Part of Ericsson, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Oscar Rodriguez (Sr. Dir. Global Partner Solutions - API BU, Vonage)
Ramesh Krishnan (Head, HyperScaler Partnerships, Vonage)

title: Proof of What You Know: Building Trust in an AI Skills Economy (sponsored by Pearson)
abstract: As AI reshapes hiring and learning, proving what you know is becoming just as important as proving who you are. Pearson's digital wallet vision connects verified credentials, skills, and identity into a trusted, portable record that learners can use across certification, education, and employment journeys, helping employers and institutions move beyond self-reported claims to verified evidence of capability. This presentation is brought to you by Pearson, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Juan Garcia (Director, Strategic Partnerships, Pearson)

title: A Day Without Handoffs: Telecom Operations With Amazon Quick
abstract: See how telecom employees use Amazon Quick to handle billing disputes, automatically address network issues, and manage service requests from a single workspace. Pulled from real-world use cases at telecom companies around the world, these demos pull context from OSS/BSS, run complex workflows, and close the loop without handing off to another team!
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater

title: Deploying Governed AI Agents in Clinical AI
abstract: Millions of patients wait too long for imaging each year as demand outpaces capacity, and the shortage is projected to worsen significantly by 2030. Radiology Partners is tackling this with MosaicOS, a full imaging lifecycle system powered by agentic AI that spans order placement through billing. In this lightning talk, learn how MosaicOS uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to orchestrate multiple AI models across the radiology workflow while maintaining governance and observability required in regulated clinical environments. See how agentic orchestration moves radiology from tool-level automation to coordinated, clinician-directed intelligence at scale.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Dan Eakin (Sales Leader, AWS)
Bret Borota (Director, Healthcare, Amazon)

title: Beyond AIOps: Operating safely in the age of agent sprawl
abstract: As organisations move from a small number of AI assistants to a distributed ecosystem of agents that can discover tools, make decisions, and act, operational excellence must evolve. Drawing on HMRC’s work to develop a governed platform model for agentic systems, this session explores a practical maturity model spanning inventory, ownership, identity, delegated authority, observability, blast-radius controls, evaluation, and human accountability. Learn how existing platform engineering, SRE, security and service-management practices can be extended across cloud and SaaS ecosystems without creating a separate governance regime for every agent or vendor. Designed for platform leaders, SREs and architects preparing to scale agents safely in complex, regulated environments.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Ash Thankey (Managing Director and General Manager, UK, Germany and Intl Organizations, Public Sector, Amazon Web Services)
Paul Moran (Principal Technologist, AWS)
Tarran Benson-West (Distinguished Engineer - AI & Engineering Platforms, HMRC)
Samuel Walls (Chief Architect, HM Revenue & Customs)

title: AI-Ready Data Foundation: Improve AI Accuracy in Healthcare and Life Sciences
abstract: Most healthcare and life sciences organizations are experimenting with AI, but far fewer are able to move out of pilots and into production at enterprise scale. More often than not the blocker is not the model, it is the data foundation beneath it, especially for healthcare and life sciences customers who operate with fragmented and heavily regulated data. This session shows how an AI-ready data foundation becomes the strategic control point that governs meaning across the enterprise and makes AI accurate, trustworthy, and reusable on real data. We present a framework for building a unified data stack on AWS, from governed open storage through the semantic and agentic layers, and how to build it incrementally while keeping control, context, and accountability.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater

title: Evaluating AI agents for production in financial services
abstract: Financial institutions building AI agents face a core challenge: how do you prove an agent is reliable enough for production when regulators demand explainability and consistency? How do you reliably detect when a production agent's behavior drifts? In this chalk talk, we explore patterns for rigorous agent evaluation in regulated environments. We discuss defining ground truth, measuring agent quality with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, and automating re-evaluation as prompts, tools, and parameters evolve. Leave with practical blueprints for constructing datasets, choosing metrics, and building continuous agent evaluation workflows for production.
speakers: Jorge Castans Garcia (Senior Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Jannis Kambach (Customer Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build multi-agent warranty and repair intelligence for automotive
abstract: Warranty and repair workflows span claim history, technical service bulletins, supplier quality records, and regulatory thresholds — a high-cost, fragmented data challenge for automotive OEMs. In this builders session, construct a multi-agent warranty and repair intelligence system using Strands SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Build a triage agent that classifies incoming cases, a research agent that queries Bedrock Knowledge Bases across TSBs and repair records, and a resolution agent that synthesizes findings into a structured decision with cited evidence routed for technician approval via human-in-the-loop controls.
speakers: Amit Kumar (EV and AI Tech Lead, AWS)
Venkat Devarajan (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Ajit Kumar KP (Sr. Specialist SA - GenAI/ML, AutoMfg, Amazon Web Services)
Vijai Thoppae (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS)
Gopi Krishnamurthy (Sr. AI/ML Solutions architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: How Netflix auto-selects the right storage for every ML training workload
abstract: ML training workloads demand fast data access, but choosing the right storage for a given workload is complex. At Netflix, we solved this by building an intent-driven storage layer that takes workload characteristics and automatically selects, provisions, and mounts the optimal storage for that workload. Our users write code once; the backend adapts transparently. In this session, we share the architecture behind our selection framework, how we built a high-throughput S3 disk cache, and how you can apply the same pattern using generally available AWS storage services to reduce cost and eliminate storage guesswork.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Jake Luszcz (Staff Software Engineer, Netflix)
Shweta Keshavanarayana (Sr. Customer Solutions Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build a unified student insight platform on AWS Quick
abstract: Advisors triaging at-risk students, deans auditing course difficulty, executives tracking retention: every university role needs student-success insights, but the tools they rely on today are disconnected, static, and slow to surface risk before it becomes attrition. In this builders’ session, learn how to use AWS Quick to understand your institutional data and deliver explainable, persona-aware insights through one architecture. See how advisors can identify at risk students with cited data, trigger early intervention when a student’s risk score changes, and generate executive ready reports that connect student outcomes to optimized resource allocation and institutional strategy.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Jumana Nagaria (Prototype Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Akash Doshi (AI Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Mohamed Salah (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS)
Mohammed Reda (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Abdilmajide Ali (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Mastering LLM tokenomics: From token costs to business outcomes
abstract: Financial institutions are scaling generative AI and agentic workloads to production and need strategies to keep costs aligned with business value. With enterprise workloads requiring retrieval, orchestration, validation, and governance layers, understanding token economics becomes critical to sustainable growth. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through design patterns for controlling token consumption while maintaining quality, including prompt compression, semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache, tiered model routing with Amazon Bedrock, and cost attribution using Amazon CloudWatch. We'll whiteboard the hidden cost drivers in agentic AI systems and share design patterns that financial institutions use to control token consumption while maintaining quality.
speakers: Anurag Singh (Leader Solutions Architecture, AWS)
John Cherian (Architect, AWS)

title: Automate dispute resolution with Amazon Connect and Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Dispute resolution calls require agents to navigate multiple systems simultaneously, frustrating customers and driving up costs. In this session, integrate Amazon Connect with Amazon Bedrock to build an AI-assisted dispute workflow. Amazon Connect flows retrieve transaction context from Amazon DynamoDB while an Amazon Bedrock agent drafts resolution options ranked by policy compliance. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway manages tool calling with Cedar-based access policies and centralized observability across each interaction. Real-time transcription surfaces relevant account history and post-call summarization auto-populates the CRM. Implement PII redaction in call recordings, configure retention policies, and test escalation paths when AI cannot resolve a dispute.
speakers: Kayla Jing (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Kalindi Parekh (Solutions Architect 1, Amazon Web Services)
Ajay Desai (Sr Technical Account Manager, AWS)
Arnab Chakraborty (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Advancing the Mission with AI and HPC Supercomputing Pods on AWS
abstract: Cloud supercomputing has become a technology imperative for American competitiveness. In this session, discover how AWS's up to $50B investment in U.S. Federal Supercomputing on AWS promotes rapid innovation for national security, defense, weather, and research. Learn how our new AI and HPC Supercomputing Pod on AWS delivers a fundamentally new supercomputing model, and how AI and HPC are converging to elevate mission outcomes. Ideal for mission owners, architects, and tech leaders.

abstract: AI agents that can autonomously transact open new possibilities in financial services—from purchasing market data to paying for risk scores in real time. In this builders' session, you'll configure an AI agent using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments with the open source x402 protocol. You'll set up payment managers, connect to data providers, define budget controls with IAM policies, and monitor transactions with Amazon CloudWatch. Leave with a working agent that autonomously transacts, reasons about costs, and delivers results end to end.

title: Build stablecoin infrastructure from key management to agentic payments
abstract: Stablecoins are redefining payments and settlement infrastructure in financial services. In this session, build a production-ready stablecoin infrastructure on AWS spanning secure key management with AWS Key Management Service and and AWS Nitro Enclaves, multi-signature governance workflows, token minting/burning/swapping operations, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments for autonomous agent-to-agent transactions. Get hands-on experience building wallet infrastructure and executing USDC stablecoin operations end-to-end. Walk away with a working architecture that bridges traditional key management with the emerging agentic commerce paradigm.

title: Event-driven AI agents for security triage with AWS Continuum
abstract: Security teams need to detect, correlate, and respond to threats faster than manual processes allow. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS Continuum orchestrates event-driven AI agents that triage, investigate, and escalate security incidents in real time. We walk through how alerts from Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub flow through Amazon EventBridge, triggering AWS Lambda functions that invoke agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, with human-in-the-loop controls for high-severity events. Discover best practices for reducing alert fatigue, accelerating MTTR, and scaling security operations for financial services and other regulated industries where every response must be explainable and audit ready.
speakers: Nikita Jaggi (Senior Manager, Solutions Architecture, AWS)
Lavanya Bandari (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Ashish Kumar (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Modernizing Legacy Telecommunications OSS/BSS Systems
abstract: Legacy modernization is one of the most complex challenges facing Telecommunications companies today. In this Chalk Talk, we will explore strategies to accelerate VMware and mainframe migrations using Agentic AI. Using a real-world scenario, we will walk through how AWS Transform and Amazon Bedrock are used to meet the technical and business requirements of these projects and explore trade-offs in migration design and infrastructure choices. Come ready to discuss your own migration challenges!
speakers: Visu Sontam (Principal SA, Telco, AWS)
Antonello Arpino (Head Of OSS/BSS and Enterprise IT modernization, amazon web services)

abstract: When live or streaming video breaks, every second costs revenue and audience trust. This session shows how to build coordinated AI agents using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands SDK that ingest observability data from AWS Media Services and partners, reason across signal domains, and accelerate root cause identification. Walk away with an architecture for agentic operations that turns reactive troubleshooting into proactive resolution.

title: Automate disaster recovery with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
abstract: Financial institutions face stringent regulatory requirements for operational resilience, demanding reliable disaster recovery with tight RTO/RPO targets across complex application portfolios. Yet failover procedures often remain manual and prone to error under pressure. In this chalk talk, we explore how to design a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that orchestrates end-to-end disaster recovery automation for regulated workloads. We’ll walk through how a coordination agent delegates to specialized sub-agents for readiness verification, infrastructure operations, Terraform code generation, Git operations, and deployment validation—each with human-in-the-loop approval gates.
speakers: Chiara Marzano (Customer Engineer, AWS)
Arnav Khare (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Right tool, right layer: Combining ML models and autonomous agents
abstract: Financial institutions deploy dozens of models and manual workflows that struggle to work together at scale. Machine learning excels at fast, explainable decisions while agentic AI orchestrates multi-step workflows with reasoning and adaptability. Real value is knowing when to use each and combining them into one system. In this chalk talk, we present a decision framework and demonstrate an architecture where machine learning models score and detect while agents reason, act, and close the loop while delivering the auditability regulators require. We walk through a Know Your Customer (KYC) example, then open the floor. Bring your use case.
speakers: Kinnera Vajjala (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Chetan Sharma (Banking & Wealth Industry Development, AWS)

title: Telecom NOC operations: Automating incident response with AI agents
abstract: Modern telecom networks span thousands of distributed components, forcing network operations teams to interpret high volumes of alarms, separate root causes from downstream symptoms, and coordinate remediation across systems under time pressure. In this workshop, you will build AI agents that read, reason about, and execute Standard Operating Procedures for network deployment and remediation. First, deploy a 5G standalone core on Amazon EKS using an agent built with the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock. Next, operate a closed-loop remediation agent, inject real failures, and observe how it detects, correlates, and resolves problems.
speakers: Cheng Liu (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Daniel Lupescu (Software Development Engineer, AWS)

title: Physical AI in Telecom: A Framework for Workload Placement
abstract: Some physical AI workloads need sub-millisecond performance at edge cell sites, others are better suited to a full AWS Region, and many fall in between on AWS Local Zones or AWS Outposts. In this chalk talk, we provide a framework for matching each workload to the right option. We trace the physical AI development lifecycle, examining how data sovereignty, latency, data gravity, and token economics interact to shape placement decisions at each phase. Based on real-world use cases, we discuss the options so you leave with a placement framework you can apply immediately.
speakers: Young Jung (Sr. Manager of Telco Network SA, Amazon Web Services)
Angelo Sampietro (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Service)
Umer Chaudhary (Sr. Mgr Network Solutions, AWS)

title: Telecom Contact Centers: Design Patterns for integrated AI Agents
abstract: IVR frustrates telecom customers, and the context from the automated interaction is gone when a human finally receives the call. Come to this chalk talk ready to work on what replaces it. After a short framing of the design space, the group takes on three questions. How should a customer-facing AI agent on Amazon Connect be built, and where do its boundaries sit? How does full conversation context survive the handoff? Should OSS and BSS integration use MCP, prebuilt Amazon Connect integrations, or both? Bring your toughest scenarios. In this working session, we will reason through the trade-offs live.
speakers: Shalima Bhalla (Global Head of Customer Experience Solutions-Telco, AWS)
Robin Harwani (Head of Telecom Industry Solutions, Amazon)

title: Telecom Contact Centers: Design Patterns for integrated AI Agents
abstract: Telecom customers demand fast, accurate service, yet IVR systems frustrate them, and when calls reach a human agent, context from the automated interaction is lost. Based on real-world implementations, this chalk talk explores alternatives to IVR using AI powered agents. We will walk through architectural options for customer facing agents built on Amazon Connect, how to pass conversation context to human agents when they step in, and options for integrating with OSS/BSS services using MCP and prebuilt integrations in Amazon Connect. We will examine the trade-offs that come with each design choice, so bring your questions!
speakers: Shalima Bhalla (Global Head of Customer Experience Solutions-Telco, AWS)
Robin Harwani (Head of Telecom Industry Solutions, Amazon)

title: Build self-healing agents from diagnosis to disaster recovery
abstract: Most AI agents stop at the root cause report, leaving engineers to act under pressure. In this workshop, build three cooperating agents on a pre-provisioned workload using Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon Application Recovery Controller. A live app throws 4XX errors and a troubleshooting agent runs root cause analysis. Then build a remediation agent to apply the fix. When 5XX errors signal an Availability Zone impairment, you'll extend the remediation agent to consult a resilience agent before acting. Leave with a working reference implementation you can adapt to your financial services or enterprise environment.
speakers: George Agiasoglou (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Hisyam Jukifli (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: How Blue Origin built a centralized enterprise knowledge graph on AWS
abstract: Building enterprise AI applications shouldn't require every team to reinvent the wheel — standing up data pipelines, managing security, and keeping knowledge bases current. Blue Origin faced this at scale: dozens of teams, hundreds of data sources, and growing demand for AI apps that could reason across all of it. The answer was RAGNet — a centralized enterprise knowledge graph platform built on Amazon Neptune and Amazon Bedrock that aggregates structured and unstructured data into a secure, always-current graph any developer or AI agent can query in plain natural language.
speakers: Clark Stevens (Director, Enterprise Data Management & AI, Blue Origin)
Prabu Mohan (Principal Data Architect, Blueorigin)
Jay Naves (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Build a multi-agent system for hyper-personalized customer journeys
abstract: Delivering personalized experiences across complex customer journeys requires agents that understand intent, maintain context, and coordinate across systems. In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI personal banker using a home buying scenario as the example. Your agents extract intent from natural conversation, build dynamic customer profiles, and orchestrate workflows across internal banking systems and external ecosystem APIs. Implement multi-agent patterns for shared memory, readiness signals, and coordinated decisioning using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents Framework, and MCP. Walk away with reusable orchestration patterns you can apply to any personalized customer experience.
speakers: Islam Elhamaky (Senior FSI SA, AWS)
Sachin Kulkarni (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Patterns for mitigating AI-powered security threats in financial services
abstract: AI-driven vulnerability identification creates elevated risks for financial services organizations as attackers find and exploit software and configuration flaws at machine speed. Patching alone is no longer sufficient. In this chalk talk, we explore mitigation patterns that help financial institutions reduce exposure and strengthen their defensive posture. Walk through how Amazon Inspector, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, AWS Continuum, Kiro, and network isolation work together to detect, contain, and respond to AI-accelerated threats. Attendees will gain mitigation strategies and actionable next steps they can take back to their security teams.
speakers: Russell Lewis (Principal Financial Services Compliance Specialist, AWS)
Parth Pandit (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: How WBD Became the First Media Company to Go Agentic Across AdTech
abstract: Buying and selling media has historically been manual, constrained by legacy systems and fragmented tools. Warner Bros. Discovery is changing that. As the first media company to integrate agentic AI workflows into every system across the media lifecycle, WBD is leapfrogging the competition by embedding autonomous agents at every step: planning, forecasting, optimization, and measurement. This converged platform makes linear TV as addressable and measurable as digital. Learn how WBD and AWS are replacing decades of manual process with self-improving agents that drive precision, yield, and entirely new monetization models at scale.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Dr. Nage Sethu (SVP Technology Converged Advertising & Linear Systems, Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc.)
Ken Kanagaraj (Principal Architect, AWS)

title: Content at the Speed of Live: AI-Powered Media Ops at Live Nation
abstract: Live Nation's subsidiaries generate petabytes of live event content across siloed storage. When an artist creates a viral moment, teams need it in fans' hands in minutes not days. In this session, learn how Live Nation built a platform that unifies fragmented media silos so teams can search, create, and publish in near-real time. Built using the guidance for a Media Lake on AWS, along with Amazon Bedrock, the platform uses AI-driven moment detection to surface key content automatically. We cover architecture, lessons from festival-scale deployment, and impact on fan experience.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Anubhav Mehrotra (VP, Head of Product, Data & Fan Engagement, Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.)
Mateo Thompson (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Robert Raver (Principal Solutions Architect, Media & Entertainment, AWS)

title: How Prime Video Built an AI-assisted Creative Suite on AWS
abstract: Premium animated series traditionally take 3.5 years to produce. Prime Video AI Studios built the AI-Assisted Creative Suite on AWS to compress production to under 12 months, with plans to extend support to live-action shorts, second-unit VFX, and feature films. The suite is powered by AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK that select models, build creative workflows, construct prompts, and evaluate outputs. Learn how Prime Video trains and serves their first-party diffusion model fleet on Amazon SageMaker and EKS, running on Amazon EC2 P6 GPU clusters for production-grade throughput and latency.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Rachel Kelley (Principal Tech BD, GME, Amazon Web Services)
Kartik Garg (Head of AI Studios Product/Tech, Prime Video & Amazon MGM Studios)

title: Real-time AI video enrichment with AWS Elemental Inference
abstract: Retrofitting videos to add subtitles, vertical formats, social cuts, and searchable metadata often means new encoders, manual editors, and multiple integrations. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS Elemental Inference can help extend reach, enhance engagement, and improve monetization by layering subtitling, vertical framing, key-moment clipping, and contextual metadata onto live and on-demand video without rebuilding your stack. Learn about the benefits of a single managed service that will improve latency, quality, and lower costs for video workflows.
speakers: Vipul Patel (Architect, Comcast)
Phil Harrison (Senior Product Manager, AWS Elemental)
Kiran Patel (Senior Product Manager - Technical, AWS)

title: KNFSD File Cache: Extending Your NFS Storage into the Cloud
abstract: Need to cache and serve NFS data from on-premises filers, across Availability Zones and Regions, or from other cloud providers with full read and write-back support? In this chalk talk, dive into KNFSD File Cache, an open-source, kernel-based NFS caching proxy on Amazon EC2 that transparently extends existing NFS storage into AWS. A single Terraform module stands up a production-ready, autoscaling cluster with high throughput and at low cost. Discuss hybrid and burst-compute patterns across M&E, HPC, Financial Services, and Life Sciences industries—eliminating latency without migration, client changes, or vendor lock-in.
speakers: Andy Hayes (Snr Solutions Architect, AWS)
DJ Rahming (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
