title: How Mercedes-Benz accelerates engineering and production with AI
abstract: Mercedes-Benz is using agentic AI on AWS to transform how vehicles are brought to life, from engineering to production. Hear how Mercedes-Benz is using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to accelerate engineering for 14,000 engineers—building specialized AI agents that reason over millions of interconnected artifacts, compressing specification generation by 90%, from 35 weeks to 3.5. On the factory floor, discover how Mercedes used AWS to build a fully cloud-native manufacturing execution system orchestrating 1M+ vehicles annually, with AI-powered quality intelligence providing rapid root-cause analysis and digital twins helping optimize throughput. Walk away with real-world lessons for deploying industrial AI at scale.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Jan-Peter Krämer (Solution Manager, Mercedes-Benz Group AG)
Daniel Schleicher (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Scaling Multi-Account IAM at Netflix: Access, Visibility and Credentials
abstract: Managing IAM across a large, fast-growing AWS footprint quickly outgrows manual review — every permission change creates friction for engineers and queue time for operators. We'll cover a control-plane approach that ties together high-level IAM abstractions, automated workflows, and business context to drive the majority of AWS access needs. Developers describe intent against concrete resources instead of hand-writing JSON; Access Analyzer–backed probes auto-approve routine changes; administrators get a single pane of glass over SCPs, identity and resource policies, CloudTrail/S3 errors, and AWS Config history. Credential delivery flows through the same plane, enabling context-aware scoping for human and agentic callers alike.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Jay Dhulia (Security Software Engineer, Netflix)
Prateek Sharma (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: How GE Vernova scaled self-service AI Agents to 75,000+ workers on AWS
abstract: GE Vernova set out to put AI directly into the hands of every employee; from the C-suite to field engineers through its Amp 2.0 platform. In this session, learn how GE Vernova integrated Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and AgentCore to deliver self-service agentic capabilities enabling employees across all roles to interact with enterprise data, automate workflows, and surface insights via natural language. Learn and discover how the team designed agents serving diverse personas, the governance and guardrails for enterprise-wide deployment, and how AgentCore's managed infrastructure enabled rapid scaling without custom orchestration. Walk away with a blueprint for democratizing AI across a global industrial workforce.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Abhishek Naik (Sr Manager Solution Architecture, Amazon Web Services)
Tony Miles (Senior Principal AI Engineer, GE Vernova)

title: Decision patterns for AI Agents with Amazon Connect Customer
abstract: Contact center AI agents require critical architecture decisions around tool integration, voice prompt engineering, and quality evaluation at regulatory scale. In this chalk talk, we walk through the decision framework for choosing first-party tools versus AWS Lambda versus MCP integrations based on latency, complexity, and compliance requirements. Explore deterministic state-machine patterns for voice prompt engineering with Amazon Connect Customer AI Agents. We discuss automated evaluation pipelines using Amazon Connect Customer Conversational Analytics and generative AI to score 100% of interactions. Debate trade-offs and leave with a decision model you can apply to your own contact center environment.
speakers: Mansoor Khan (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Ganesh Prabhu Jayachandran (Sr Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services, Inc.)

title: Enterprise-Ready: How NetEase Governs AI at Scale
abstract: Learn how NetEase, one of the world's largest gaming companies, is building enterprise AI governance as AI adoption scales across the organization. Discover how Amazon Bedrock enables multi-model routing, cost controls, and team-level budget management to optimize AI usage. See how NetEase enforces governance with company-wide AI policies, Bedrock Guardrails for content safety, and Bedrock AgentCore for orchestrating agentic AI workflows with centralized governance and observability. Learn why a platform-first approach to cost, access, and safety is critical for enabling AI innovation at enterprise scale.
speakers: Dan He (效能研发部技术总监, NetEase, Inc.)
Zhuobin Huang (Sr. Solutions Architect Manager, AWS)

title: An Epic Tale: Hyperscale Storage & Compute for the Fortnite Ecosystem
abstract: The metaverse will not be built by one studio. It will be built by thousands of teams shipping petabytes of content, running millions of build and render jobs across regions every day. The engineers behind Lore, Epic's distributed version control system for massive binary repositories, and Overmind, a multi-region ephemeral compute orchestrator, reveal the AWS architecture that makes it possible: self-managed scheduling on EC2, S3/DynamoDB/Keyspaces/Aurora for the data plane, EKS-hosted control planes running durable workflows, and MSK for replayable event streams. Leave with a concrete reference architecture and lessons on tenant isolation, regional sovereignty, and global platform scale.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Paul Sharpe (Technical Director, Cloud, Epic Games, Inc.)
Mattias Jansson (Technical Director, Epic Games, Inc.)
Dan Backhaus (Senior Technical Account Manager, AWS)

title: Inside T-Mobile's Kinetic Edge: Real-Time Physical AI at Scale
abstract: In a Physical AI world, tokens traveling across a telecom network must trigger real-world actions with sub-millisecond latency. Learn how T-Mobile built its Kinetic Edge Platform using AWS Outposts, Amazon SageMaker, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, delivering deterministic performance, ultra-low latency, and precise synchronization on a network serving 130M+ customers. We'll cover how to assess Physical AI network requirements and map them to AWS infrastructure options. You'll leave knowing how to build AI into the network edge and where it creates the most value.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Matthew Feider (Sr. Manager, Business Development — Physical & Edge AI, T-Mobile)
Waqar Afzal (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Behind the Scenes: Building the Telecom Concierge
abstract: Whether you caught the demo on the expo floor, or you are enhancing your customer service systems with AI, this chalk talk dives into the architectural decisions powering a hyper-personalized customer experience. Explore the intelligent routing and retrieval trade-offs, and understand the business model implications when operators can shrink their physical footprint without degrading experience. Leave with a reference framework for designing context-aware systems at scale, a decision matrix for your retail strategy, and clarity on the ROI drivers so you can architect similar solutions in your network.
speakers: Rahul Shira (Sr. Industry Technical Product Marketing Manager - Telecom, AWS)
Aymen Saidi (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: How Bristol Myers Squibb Scales AI from Experiments to Enterprise with AWS
abstract: Bristol Myers Squibb is scaling AI from targeted experiments to enterprise transformation through its AI Accelerator program. In this session, hear how BMS pairs business-led innovation with AWS to move AI use cases from idea into production. See how this approach is applied across Product Development and Supply, where AI helps improve decision velocity, strengthen supply resilience, optimize operations, and speed the delivery of medicines to patients. Learn how BMS and AWS built the foundation, operating model, and reusable capabilities to scale AI responsibly, turning isolated wins into a repeatable enterprise capability that other organizations can follow.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Brian Loyal (Principal AI/ML Solutions Architect - Healthcare and Life Sciences, Amazon Web Services)
Ethan Sena (Vice President, AI, Cloud & Productivity, Bristol Myers Squibb)

title: How Novartis is Reimaging an AI-Native Drug Development with AWS
abstract: Developing a new medicine takes 10 to 15 years and $2.6 billion, and timelines are getting longer. Novartis decided not to optimize the old model but to replace it, building an AI-native ecosystem spanning information, decision, and physical AI across the drug development lifecycle. In this session, hear how AI now writes over 80% of their RWE protocols in production, then go deep on intelligent decision systems that optimize clinical trial planning, and formulation optimisations that improve the medicines Novartis creates. Learn how Novartis and AWS are compressing the path from AI prototype to production, turning ambition into patient impact.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Sander Timmer (Head of Data Science and AI, Novartis)
Daniel Pitman (Principal Proserve Cloud Architect, AWS)

title: Physical AI for MedTech: From Intelligent Devices to Business Impact
abstract: Physical AI — AI that senses, reasons, and acts in the physical world — is reshaping medical devices. From surgical robots to connected infusion pumps, imaging to wearables, every next-gen device needs training, simulation, edge deployment, and fleet management at scale. In this chalk talk, we’ll architect the full Physical AI stack on AWS for medical devices — SageMaker for model training, IoT Greengrass for edge inference, regulated OTA at fleet scale, and NVIDIA solutions integrated into the AWS backbone. We’ll whiteboard the hard tradeoffs — edge vs. cloud, regulatory constraints, and scaling from prototype to 100K devices. Leave with a reference architecture and a clear path to pilot
speakers: Shaun Qualheim (Sr. Manager, Solutions Architecture, Amazon Web Services)
Juli Hysenbelli (Global Lead Connected Care - AWS Healthcare & Lifescience, Amazon Web Services)

title: Deploy a HIPAA-Eligible AI Agent with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
abstract: Your clinical team wants an AI agent that summarizes patient notes—but one leaked SSN means a $1.5M HIPAA penalty. In this session, we build a working Amazon Bedrock Agent with HIPAA controls baked in. Guardrails automatically redact low-risk identifiers and block critical PHI, routing flagged content through Amazon EventBridge to an SQS review queue. AWS CloudTrail captures the full audit trail, and IAM restricts the agent to BAA-covered services only. You leave with a deployable CDK stack ready for production.
speakers: Adam Birnbaum (Senior Assurance Consultant, AWS)
Shreya Singh (Assurance Consultant, Amazon Web Services)

title: How Bayer Designed 50K Proteins on Amazon Bio Discovery
abstract: This chalk talk explores how to architect agentic AI workflows for generative protein design at enterprise scale. Using Bayer's oncology nanobody campaign as the reference implementation, we walk through the technical and scientific decisions behind a pipeline that generated 50,000 candidates and 3,000 prioritized candidates in weeks using Amazon Bio Discovery. Topics include: model orchestration patterns for generative and predictive models, designing scoring functions that encode biological mechanism (not just binding affinity), iterative feedback loops between computation and wet-lab validation, and scaling considerations for enterprise drug discovery programs. Attendees will leave this session with a reusable architectural blueprint for building agentic biomolecule design workflows on AWS.
speakers: Christoph Berns (ML Scientist, Bayer AG)
Milton Yu (Principal Product Manager, AWS)

title: From Millions of Gamers to AI at Scale: Roblox's Hybrid AWS Architecture Unleashed
abstract: "Auto-scaling was only the beginning. At Roblox, scaling means continuously adapting to changing capacity, hardware availability, GPU constraints, and unpredictable global demand. Join Roblox to learn how they combine AWS with on-premises infrastructure to dynamically place workloads across regions, architectures, and AI providers. Using EC2 Capacity Health Visualizer, hybrid scheduling, multi-region load balancing, self-hosted AI inference alongside Amazon Bedrock, and heterogeneous compute (x86, Graviton, Inferentia, Trainium, GPUs), you will learn how Roblox keeps gaming and AI services responsive under record-breaking load."
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Vandana Tewani (Sr. Customer Solutions Manager, AWS)
Ivan Marcin (Senior Technical Director, Roblox Corporation)

title: Mastercard: Training a large transaction model on billions of transactions
abstract: Large language models transformed text. Large transaction models (LTMs) aim to do the same for payment and commerce data. Instead of brittle, hand-crafted feature pipelines feeding hundreds of specialized models, LTMs are transformer-based foundation models pre-trained directly on billions of anonymized transactions, learning rich representations of transactions, merchant behavior, consumer activity, and financial risk. This session introduces Mastercard's LTM program, the architectural choices behind it, and the unique challenges of tokenizing and training on tabular and sequential financial data at massive scale. We show how foundation models power diverse production use cases, from fraud detection to personalization to reaching underserved cardholders.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Steve Flinter (Distinguished Engineer, Mastercard)
Gurinder Singh (Principal Solutions architect, Amazon web services)
Josh Allbright (SVP Data Science, Mastercard)

title: Accelerate your agentic AI mission from prototype to ATO in weeks
abstract: Agencies, the industrial base, and technology partners want agentic AI in production, but few have navigated the path across classification levels. In this chalk talk, learn real-world patterns for taking Bedrock agents and foundation models from prototype to authorized production across commercial and AWS Government Regions (FedRAMP, DoD CSP SRG IL2/4/5, classified) on one portable security baseline, without a rebuild; what is authorized at each level; the tradeoffs at each level; and ATO strategies that turn guardrails, observability, and evaluations into control evidence your assessor can use. Guardrails and audit-trail demos. Ideal for architects and security leads.
speakers: David Schatzman (AWS GovCloud (US) Business Development Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Shawn Asfeld (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Build, simulate, and validate physical AI-driven robotic systems
abstract: Commissioning industrial robots typically takes weeks of physical testing. Digital twins with real-time physics simulation and multi-agent AI optimization can compress that timeline from weeks to hours. In this builders session, construct a digital twin of a multi-robot manufacturing cell using virtual PLCs and controllers, real fieldbus connectivity, real-time physics simulation in NVIDIA Omniverse, and Amazon EC2 as the compute backbone. Leave with an AI-optimized robotic program validated against real-world conditions before ever touching real hardware. Generated in 60 minutes using open standards and open toolchains, the result is a reusable blueprint that scales across cells, lines, and sites.

title: Agentic AI for manufacturing: Build a cross-domain digital thread
abstract: Manufacturing data lives in silos — from engineering systems through production lines. In this workshop, build an agentic digital thread: a knowledge-graph-powered AI system that unifies OT and IT data across the product lifecycle and answers cross-domain questions in real time. Using Amazon Neptune, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and AWS IoT SiteWise, deploy agents that autonomously traverse connections from product design through production operations — linking engineering changes to equipment assets to quality events — without point-to-point integrations. Leave with a deployable reference architecture adaptable to any manufacturing environment.

title: Build a Video Semantic Layer for Media Agent and Agent Harness on AWS
abstract: This workshop tackles a question most media organizations have yet to ask: your video pipeline extracts rich metadata for human search and discovery, but is it actually optimized for agents? In this hands-on session, you will build the semantic infrastructure that bridges that gap: multimodal embeddings tuned for machine recall, hybrid search that combines vector similarity with keyword precision, and an entity graph that maps content relationships into structures agents can reason over. By the end of this workshop, you will have a media agent harness that queries, enriches, and continuously improves their video understanding, making video content not just searchable by people but optimized at scale for agents.
speakers: James Wu (Principal AI/ML Specialist SA, AWS)
Amit Kalawat (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Build the Patient Record Your Healthcare AI Agents Actually Need
abstract: The average US patient has records scattered across 40+ systems. Medication lists conflict, allergies are duplicated, and clinical notes contradict structured data. Every AI agent you connect downstream inherits that mess. In this builder session, you use AWS HealthLake to resolve patient identities across fragmented sources, normalize clinical concepts to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm, and produce a unified, queryable FHIR record. Then you use a unified SDK to wire Amazon Connect Health agents to your clean data layer, simulate a patient encounter, and generate a structured clinical note that writes back to HealthLake. You leave with a deployable data foundation that accelerates Connect Health agent integration today and supports any custom agent you choose to connect tomorrow.
speakers: Chris Haddad (Health AI/ML Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Umair Khalid (Sr. Product Architect - Healthcare AI, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build the Patient Record Your Healthcare AI Agents Actually Need
abstract: The average US patient has records scattered across 40+ systems. Medication lists conflict, allergies are duplicated, and clinical notes contradict structured data. Every AI agent you connect downstream inherits that mess. In this builder session, you use AWS HealthLake to resolve patient identities across fragmented sources, normalize clinical concepts to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm, and produce a unified, queryable FHIR record. Then you use a unified SDK to wire Amazon Connect Health agents to your clean data layer, simulate a patient encounter, and generate a structured clinical note that writes back to HealthLake. You leave with a deployable data foundation that accelerates Connect Health agent integration today and supports any custom agent you choose to connect tomorrow.

abstract: The restaurant industry is transforming as AI agents move from pilots to production. Leading QSR and casual dining brands are deploying a "virtual general manager," multiple specialized agents orchestrated together to optimize drive-thru ordering, kitchen workflows, labor scheduling, and guest experience in real time. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a multi-agent architecture using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK, with Amazon Nova Sonic powering voice ordering at sub-2-second latency. abstract: In this hands-on workshop, build Agentic Real-Time Framework (ARTF)-compliant agents that operate inside the bidstream, using the Agents for Advertising framework on Amazon Bedrock. You'll construct an agent container that accepts bid requests and returns pricing decisions to the ARTF specification, then orchestrate a multi-agent pipeline that simulates adversarial auction scenarios and scores your bidding strategy against the outcomes. title: Build a brand knowledge graph for retail and CPG AI
abstract: Retail and CPG brands invest years building product expertise, from visual styling rules to ingredient pairing and formulation knowledge, that generic AI simply cannot replicate. In this builder session, you'll construct a Graph RAG solution that encodes brand-specific curatorial knowledge into an Amazon Neptune Analytics knowledge graph with multimodal vector embeddings. Using a CPG product catalog, you'll build graph schemas capturing formulation relationships, brand hierarchies, and cross-category pairing rules. Then see how vector similarity search combined with graph traversal enriches retrieval context before grounding Amazon Bedrock LLM responses. Leave with a working deployed architecture adaptable across retail and CPG.

abstract: More than half of web traffic now comes from AI bots that consume content built for humans while returning little value to publishers. First, you'll build a pipeline that converts images, video, and audio into concise, agent-friendly markdown summaries including interpreting what's shown, said, and meant, while preserving the originals for human readers. abstract: Education institutions field thousands of student inquiries each semester across enrollment, financial aid, and academic support. In this chalk talk, we architect agentic AI-powered student services using Amazon Connect Customer. You’ll configure a knowledge base with university content and connect it to Connect Customer for real-time AI-generated recommendations during live calls, then deploy a self-service experience that resolves common inquiries over voice and chat. title: Replacing eligibility rules engines with Neurosymbolic AI in HHS
abstract: State HHS agencies spend hundreds of millions maintaining eligibility rules engines built on Drools or proprietary tooling. These systems are brittle, expensive, and impossible to audit. We built a different path: Ingesting policy, using Large Language Models, and building a formal logic representation, followed by using neurosymbolic techniques to produce a verified rule set, enabling deterministic eligibility decisions with full audit trails. No hallucinations. Provable correctness. We walk through the architecture, show a working prototype processing SNAP and Medicaid policy, discuss pricing at scale, and share early results from state engagements.

title: AtoZ AI Co-Scientist: Multi-Agent Systems That Do Research With You
abstract: Can an AI system move beyond answering questions to actually conducting research alongside you? We built one. AtoZ AI Co-Scientist is a multi-agent orchestration platform where specialized agents collaborate through a unified interface to discover literature, synthesize knowledge via graph-routed retrieval, generate hypotheses, implement baselines from papers, and run experiments autonomously. title: Attesting to Secrets in Zero Knowledge
abstract: It is possible to prove factual statements about systems to observers without revealing any details about those systems beyond the stated claims. This is surprising, but not as surprising as the fact that it is borderline practical using Zero Knowledge Proofs. This talk will give an overview of the mathematical foundations of Zero Knowledge Proofs and introduce both interactive and non-interactive proof schemes. It will then dive into the details of some of the current general purpose Zero Knowledge proof systems (e.g., zk-SNARK and zk-STARK) and show how to use Zero Knowledge libraries to attest to (or prove) properties of software systems without sharing the implementations of those systems.
speakers: Tristan Ravitch (Principal Applied Scientist, AWS)

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Evaluating AI Safety with Formal Guarantees
abstract: As AI systems become increasingly capable and autonomous, safety evaluation is emerging as a critical challenge. While current evaluations largely rely on benchmark performance and empirical red-teaming, these approaches provide limited guarantees about real-world risk. This talk will explore an emerging direction in AI safety: evaluating model behavior with formal statistical guarantees. We will discuss how ideas from reliability engineering, robustness certification, and risk assessment can be applied to quantify catastrophic failure probabilities, the assumptions behind such guarantees, and their implications for deploying and governing frontier AI systems. This topic is highly relevant to the future of trustworthy and accountable AI.
speakers: Weitong Ruan (Senior Applied Science Manager, Amazon)
Qian Hu (Applied Scientist, Amazon)

title: Building fast with automated reasoning at Amazon S3 scale
abstract: S3 has a long history of using automated reasoning, but a core challenge has been applying these techniques to large systems while maintaining development velocity. Over time, we've learned to balance cutting-edge science with engineering velocity to accelerate development. We'll share diverse techniques for validating critical storage components, from black-box model-based validation using formal API specifications, to white-box verification with specialized concurrency checkers for ensuring transaction serializability and crash consistency. You'll learn how S3 engineers and scientists are advancing systems verification with new tools and ideas that you can apply to your own systems.
speakers: Rajeev Joshi (Principal Applied Scientist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Charting the AI Search Frontier: From Retrieval to Reasoning
abstract: Large language models have shifted expectations about search: from retrieving documents to answering questions directly; from single-type data to multi-modal data; from one-shot lookup to multi-step reasoning. This is the new frontier of search empowered by AI. What should you know about the AI Search frontier? How can you make AI search provide the highest accuracy on your data, while keeping latency and costs in check? Join us to chart the course — and leave with a practical map.
speakers: Nina Mishra (Scientist, AWS)
Amin Saberi (, AWS)

title: Deterministic control for probabilistic agents: proving safety holds
abstract: AI agents are probabilistic: vulnerable to prompt injection, hallucination, and unexpected tool composition. The controls around them must be deterministic. This session explores how to define provable safety envelopes for autonomous agents, drawing from the authorization and formal verification research behind AgentCore policy. We examine how automated reasoning guarantees policy correctness, how neuro-symbolic approaches combine LLM flexibility with mathematical verification for policy authoring, and how agents' action spaces can be reduced before execution. Attendees will also get a first look at new research extending these guarantees to emerging agentic authorization challenges.
speakers: John Tristan (Senior Principal Scientist, Amazon)

title: Encoding Authorization in Logic from Puzzles to Production
abstract: Automated theorem provers can reason symbolically about a system's behavior and prove properties like "no user can ever escalate their own privileges" across all possible inputs. Of course, this requires modeling your problem in first-order logic, which demands careful thinking to precisely capture all behaviors of your system. In this session, learn how to encode your problem in first-order logic: starting with a logic puzzle to build intuition, then a toy authorization language, and finally what it takes for a full production system like Cedar, a fine-grained authorization language built with high assurance. We discuss challenges including ensuring correctness and completeness of the encoding.
speakers: Liana Hadarean (Principal Applied Scientist, Amazon Web Services)

title: How neurosymbolic AI formalizes natural language into verifiable logic
abstract: Organizations want to automate enforcement of critical rules—financial, legal, regulatory—yet those rules live in ambiguous natural-language documents. Bridging this gap is error-prone and expensive. In this session, we show how neurosymbolic AI enables subject-matter experts to formalize natural-language rules into mathematical logic—capturing the original intent in an unambiguous, executable, and verifiable form. We cover the mathematical foundations and demonstrate through practical examples how formalized rules can serve as agent guardrails, compliance checks, and trusted knowledge sources. Attendees will leave with a deep understanding of how neurosymbolic techniques can help them formalize and operationalize their own domain rules.
speakers: Aman Goel (Senior Applied Scientist, AWS)
Dimitra Giannakopoulou (Sr. Principal Applied Scientist, AWS)

title: How to think about NUMA: Optimizing AI inference on EC2
abstract: Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) topology shapes how every byte of model weight reaches a compute core, and misalignment silently costs throughput. This session explains why NUMA matters for memory locality when running models on EC2, and what changes across Graviton-, Intel-, and AMD-based instances. CPU inference requires deliberate alignment of threads to data, especially as SIMD and AMX instructions amplify memory bandwidth demands per core. Even on GPU instances, host-side NUMA affects preprocessing and KV cache offload. Understand your hardware topology and leverage it to get the most from your inference workloads.
speakers: Tyler Jones (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect - Compute, AWS)
Kinnar Sen (Principal SSA, Compute, AWS)

title: Inside Amazon S3: How a one-page design reached planetary scale
abstract: When Amazon S3 launched in 2006, its design requirements fit one page: scalable, reliable, fast, inexpensive, simple, with no single points of failure. The system was built to treat component failure as normal and use scale as an advantage. Today those founding principles describe an architecture serving hundreds of millions of requests per second across tens of millions of drives, maintaining eleven nines of durability while shipping features without downtime. Hear S3 principal engineers trace the decisions from single host to strong consistency at global scale, how formal methods verify correctness, and how the team balances innovation with operational safety.
speakers: James Bornholt (Senior Principal Engineer, AWS)
George Porter (Sr. Principal Engineer, Amazon AWS)

speakers: James Bornholt (Senior Principal Engineer, AWS)
George Porter (Sr. Principal Engineer, Amazon AWS)

title: Inside NKI: How AWS designed a kernel language for peak AI performance
abstract: What does a kernel language need to unlock peak performance on Trainium, AWS purpose-built AI chips for better price performance? The AWS Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) is a Python-embedded DSL that goes beyond framework-level abstractions, giving developers direct access to Trainium's three-level memory hierarchy and four compute engines. Explore the design choices that enable hardware-level optimization, dissect production kernels powering FlashAttention variants, MoE routing, and on-device collectives, and debate where tile-based languages converge or diverge across accelerator architectures. Discover how NKI extends to support MXFP8 and disaggregated inference. You will leave able to write your own custom, hardware-optimized kernels.
speakers: Liran Alon (Senior Principal Engineer, Amazon)

title: Knowledge Representations for Autonomous Software Lifecycle Management
abstract: What formal properties must a software representation satisfy for agents to manage entire application lifecycles autonomously — reasoning at the specification level, not the code level? This session examines the open scientific questions behind agentic code understanding: encoding both structural topology and business semantics into a unified knowledge graph, extracting and grounding business rules when institutional context has been lost, enabling agent reasoning over large heterogeneous graphs without coherence degradation, and establishing deterministic validation signals that replace human judgment with formal guarantees. Drawing from graph theory, knowledge representation, specification mining, and formal verification research, we explore what makes these problems hard, where current approaches break at scale, and what architectural principles make full-lifecycle autonomy tractable. Attendees will leave with a rigorous understanding of the representation and reasoning foundations required for agents that don’t just generate code but understand, validate, evolve, and replace software as knowledge.
speakers: Alexis Henry (Sr Software Development Manager, Amazon)
Ankur Shanbhag (Software Development Manager, AWS)

speakers: Alexis Henry (Sr Software Development Manager, Amazon)
Ankur Shanbhag (Software Development Manager, AWS)

title: Lifecycle of a pod: trust boundaries in VM-isolated containers
abstract: Trace a pod from kubelet's RunPodSandbox call to process execution inside a VM isolated sandbox, then dissect the hard problems at each boundary crossing: how do you enforce policy on what runtime actions are allowed? How do you transport container images into an isolated environment the parent cannot read? Where does attestation fit, and how can you truly trust what is running inside? We examine how the trust model shifts between untrusted host and untrusted guest, explore the tradeoffs between CRI compatibility and security invariants, and discuss how EKS is approaching VM-level workload isolation
speakers: Fletcher Woodruff (Senior Software Development Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Todd Neal (Principal Software Engineer, Amazon)

title: Measuring emergent risks in frontier models
abstract: As frontier models scale in capability, so does their potential for deceptive and manipulative behavior—risks that static, single-turn evaluations fail to capture. We present our multi-layered approach to measuring emergent deception under Amazon's Frontier Model Safety Framework (FMSF), combining automated benchmarks, expert red-teaming, and uplift studies. We will dive deep into two innovations: D-REX, a benchmark detecting discrepancies between benign outputs and malicious internal chain-of-thought reasoning; and LH-Deception, a multi-agent simulation revealing emergent "chains of deception" across extended task sequences. Together, these tools address critical gaps in frontier safety evaluation and inform deployment governance.
speakers: Rahul Gupta (Sr. Manager, Amazon)

title: Modeling Human Preference: Pairwise Battles to Agentic Systems
abstract: Every time we rank an LLM, we're building a model of human preference — yet for most queries there's no ground truth, only a person's sense of which answer is better, shifting with expertise, culture, and expectations. This session examines how we model preference across two regimes: pairwise battles, arena-style voting ranked through Bradley-Terry, and agentic systems, where preference spans long-horizon, multi-step, tool-using tasks. Reward models and LLM-as-judge are themselves learned preference models; from our experience at Amazon, we examine when to trust them and how to separate progress from preference-overfitting. Attendees will learn what modeling preference at scale demands.
speakers: Pradeep Natarajan (Sr. Principal Scientist, Amazon)
Swastik Roy (Sr. Applied Scientist, Amazon)

title: Nitro Isolation Engine: Formally verifying confidentiality
abstract: What does it mean, *precisely*, for the data of a virtual machine to be confidential? Answering this question will take us on a journey into low-level systems and high-level mathematics as we unpack this question in the context of the AWS Nitro System, the underlying virtualization platform that powers Amazon EC2. You will discover the low-level hardware and software that isolate virtual machines, our precise mathematical definition of confidentiality, and the methods we use to establish this crucial property for the AWS Nitro Isolation Engine. No background in virtualization systems or formal verification is expected.
speakers: Nathan Chong (Principal Applied Scientist, AWS)
Dominic Mulligan (Senior Applied Science Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Prefill, decode, schedule: LLM inference without bubbles
abstract: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto distinct GPU pools, but creates new problems. Head-of-line blocking on prefill, stragglers on decode, and pipeline bubbles when phases switch. This session goes deep on how to solve them. We cover temporally-disaggregated pipeline parallelism to eliminate phase-switching bubbles, adaptive scheduling across heterogeneous instances, tensor vs. pipeline parallelism tradeoffs for latency and throughput, constrained decoding with context-sensitive grammars for structured output without sacrificing token throughput, and KV-cache parallelism for multi-million context serving.
speakers: Anthony Liguori (VP/Distinguished Engineer, Amazon.com)

title: Quantum Error Correction - Progress, Hardware, and What's Next
abstract: Quantum computers have the potential to solve some of today's most challenging computational problems — but they suffer from significantly higher error rates than their classical counterparts. In this talk, we introduce quantum error correction (QEC) and compare the hardware requirements of leading QEC methods against the commercial roadmaps of quantum hardware companies. To ground the discussion, we begin with a brief revisit of classical error correction before walking through recent breakthroughs in quantum error correction. Attendees will leave with an informed perspective on where QEC stands today and the challenges that will define the field's progress in the coming years.
speakers: Tyler Takeshita (Sr. Applied Scientist, AWS)
Mao Lin (Applied Scientist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Self-verifiable watermarks: defending AI provenance against forgery
abstract: As organizations deploy generative AI at scale, watermarking has become the critical trust layer for establishing content provenance, meeting emerging regulatory requirements, and protecting brand integrity. But what if an adversary could stamp a fake watermark onto any image and frame your service? We show a diffusion-based forgery attack bypasses current defenses with just 1,000 samples. To close this gap, we introduce a self-verifiable message mechanism—SeedBind and ContentBind—that transforms verification into a structural consistency check, reducing forged bit accuracy to near-random without modifying the underlying watermarking pipeline. Discover how to harden AI provenance at scale.
speakers: Weitong Ruan (Senior Applied Science Manager, Amazon)
Fan Yang (Senior Applied Scientist, Amazon.com Inc)

title: Teaching Telemetry to Think: From Raw Signals to Root Cause
abstract: An AI agent investigating an incident starts cold: no sense of normal, no topology, no causal history. It rebuilds context from raw documents every time. What if the telemetry understood itself first? We'll examine an intelligence layer for agentic observability, where streaming detectors and a live service graph distill billions of signals into incident observations, then fine-tuned reasoning models, built on open-weight LLMs, correlate them into ranked root causes. Whiteboard with us on the hard parts: what to teach a model versus retrieve at inference, how domain fine-tuning beats frontier scale, and where reasoning models still fail.
speakers: Shiva Kasiviswanathan (Principal Applied Scientist, AWS)
Krishna Balasubramanian (Amazon Scholar, Amazon)

title: The Evaluator Is the Algorithm: Evolving SOTA for $15
abstract: We discovered a phase transition in LLM-guided code evolution: when the evaluation function provides smooth gradient signal, SOTA emerges automatically regardless of model choice; when it doesn't, no compute compensates. This "evaluator-dominance principle" emerged from stress-testing evolutionary search across 403 problems in 27 domains on Amazon Bedrock — 20× the scale of Google's original AlphaEvolve — achieving 96% SOTA-matching at $15/problem median cost. We'll present the Bedrock-native architecture (MAP-Elites, staged evaluation cascade, Opus/Haiku phase routing), a production vehicle routing deployment saving 1.28% on 100,000-customer routes at $530 total spend, and the evaluator design methodology that determines success or failure.
speakers: Rohit Malshe (Director Research Science, Amazon.com)

title: The Mathematics of Backlogs: Why Your Queue Will Never Drain
abstract: Your consumers are healthy, your pods are green - yet your backlog isn't shrinking. Why? Because systems provisioned for steady-state have zero recovery capacity. In this chalk talk, we'll derive the formulas that govern backlog formation and drain, explore the non-linear utilization cliff where small traffic spikes become catastrophic, and work through the real-world complications: retry amplification, stale-message degradation, and multi-stage cascades. Bring your architectures - we'll whiteboard whether they can actually recover from failure, or just survive it.
speakers: Rajesh Kumar Pandey (Principal Engineer, Amazon)
Tejas Ghadge (Senior Software Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Verifying Post-Quantum Cryptography at Speed
abstract: Traditionally, cryptographic engineering involves a performance/assurance trade-off: clean code is easy to audit and maintain, yet slow; handwritten assembly is fast, yet hard to validate. Discover how automated reasoning helps to overcome this tension, following the example of mlkem-native and mldsa-native, two open-source post-quantum cryptography libraries co-maintained by AWS and deployed in AWS-LC, Amazon's cryptography library. In these libraries, constraint solving enables automated superoptimization at the assembly level, while formal verification vets the result. Contrary to the popular belief that assurance costs speed, it is automated reasoning that enables deep optimization, verification and rapid deployment of cryptographic code at cloud scale.
speakers: Hanno Becker (Principal Applied Scientist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Virtualization Architecture Behind AgentCore's Runtime Security Model
abstract: Journey into the sophisticated virtualization architecture that powers AgentCore's runtime security model. This session examines the intricate mechanics of session isolation at the virtualization layer, exploring advanced techniques in compute and memory virtualization, virtual machine snapshot optimization, and virtual memory deduplication. Drawing from operating systems research and systems security principles, we'll demonstrate how these components work together to create robust security boundaries for agent workloads. Attendees will gain deep technical insights into the mathematical and systems-level concepts that position AWS at the forefront of secure agent runtime architectures, showcasing our industry-leading approach to securing code execution in agent environments.
speakers: Marc Brooker (VP and Distinguished Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: What Can Neurosymbolic AI Prove About Agent Behavior?
abstract: AI agents that write and execute code autonomously create a fundamental trust problem: how do you guarantee behavioral boundaries without constraining the flexibility that makes agents useful? This chalk talk examines how neurosymbolic AI is making provable guarantees practical at scale: autoformalization translating natural-language constraints into temporal logic, satisfiability solvers whose exponential improvement keeps pace with exponentially harder verification problems, and LLMs guiding proof search in theorem provers like Lean, creating a virtuous cycle where better proofs yield stronger provers. We'll stratify what can be proved today, what requires LLM-discovered inductive invariants, and where undecidability still draws a hard line.
speakers: Nadia Labai (Senior Applied Scientist, AWS)

title: World models for indoor robots: what breaks and why
abstract: World models promise to give robots predictive understanding of their environment, yet applying them to indoor robotics exposes fundamental gaps in how transformers reason about geometry. In this session, we present findings from building a trajectory-conditioned lidar world model for Diligent Robotics' hospital fleet on AWS. We examine why standard loss metrics fail for generative spatial predictions, why rotation breaks factored attention even with explicit conditioning, and the minimal set of inductive biases needed to restore geometric coherence. Attendees leave with a diagnostic framework for spatial reasoning failures in transformer-based world models.
speakers: Sarik Ghazarian (Applied Scientist, Amazon)
Parmida Atighehchian (Senior Applied Scientist, Amazon (AWS))

title: State of the art Fairness and Admission Control
abstract: Preventing long outages, meta-stable events, thundering herds, Denial of Service Attacks, resource or concurrency starvation, or noisy neighbor issues all depend on fairness and admission control. We’ll do a deep, interactive dive into practical techniques that prevent or mitigate real-world issues. We’ll get into details of back-pressure, PID control loops, shuffle sharding, floodgates, and other novel techniques that we’ve developed at AWS, and we’ll cover common mistakes that we see in the industry.
speakers: Colm MacCarthaigh (Vice President / Distinguished Engineer, AWS)

title: Beyond RSA: Post-quantum data encryption using ML-KEM in AWS KMS
abstract: RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography secure nearly every application today, and both are vulnerable to future cryptographically relevant quantum computers. Data captured now can be decrypted later, so applications needing long-term confidentiality should adopt post-quantum encryption well before those computers arrive. AWS KMS now offers ML-KEM, the NIST-standardized replacement for RSA and ECDH key establishment and ultimately encryption under asymmetric keys. It protects the private keys in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSMs. In this session, learn about ML-KEM and how to use it as a building block for quantum-safe encryption using Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE).
speakers: Vipul Gupta (Principal Engineer (AWS KMS), AWS)

title: EC2 at 20: Rebuilding the control plane while it is running
abstract: Amazon EC2 launched in 2006 as four services backed by a single MySQL database. Twenty years later, it is one of the largest distributed systems ever built — and most of that original architecture had to be replaced while serving production traffic, with no maintenance window and no change to the API contract customers depend on. In this session, EC2 engineers dive deep on two of the hardest migrations: making the control plane Availability Zone independent so a single-AZ event cannot escalate into a regional one, and moving EC2 metadata off MySQL. We walk through the failure modes that forced each decision, how correctness was verified before every cutover, how we proved a single-AZ failure stays in a single AZ, and the things we got wrong along the way. You will leave with migration and isolation patterns you can apply to your own systems at any scale.
speakers: Don McGarry (Senior Principal Engineer, AWS)

title: Visual reasoning will be bigger than language reasoning
abstract: Today’s vision-language models can describe images fluently, yet still struggle with the spatial and perceptual reasoning required for robotics. This talk argues that visual reasoning—reasoning through points, sketches, trajectories, depth maps, and other grounded representations—will become more important than language reasoning for physical agents. It traces progress from benchmarks exposing fundamental perception failures to methods that teach models to reason directly in visual space. These ideas culminate in robotics foundation models that convert visual plans into robot actions. The resulting systems are interpretable, steerable, deployable zero-shot on affordable hardware, and competitive with proprietary models trained on substantially more data. We showcase how these ideas are advancing the goal of accessible, general-purpose robotics to the broader research community.
speakers: Ranjay Krishna (Assistant Professor, University of Washington)

title: How AI is Changing Everything (Computer Systems, Education, Driving, and More)
abstract: Reflecting on my roles as Head of Computer Science at MIT, Director of the MIT Education Exch(AI)nge, and Chief Scientist at Cambridge Mobile Telematics, I will discuss how the rise of generative AI is reshaping software, computer science itself, higher education, and the ways data- and AI-driven companies create value from data. In computer science, we are seeing explosive growth both in the range of problems AI can solve and in the new systems and tools required to make AI effective, efficient, and reliable. In higher education, we are rethinking fundamental questions about what students need to learn, as well as how we teach and assess our students. At CMT, we are applying new AI architectures to better understand mobility data, particularly road and driver risk. I will use concrete examples and results to explore the common theme of how to achieve the greatest impact from AI.
speakers: Samuel Madden (Professor, MIT)

title: The Cogs of a Well-oiled Software Factory
abstract: The "Software Factory" is a new buzzword for a fully autonomous agent driven software development process. Many organizations are trying to set up such a factory, but this is easier said than done. In this talk, from my experience setting up such factories for ourselves and other businesses, I will explain some of the elements of a software factory (issue triage, spec generation, implementation, review, and testing), and some of the pain points that we have experienced at each step. I will also cover how to evaluate the effectiveness of each of these steps and how to build a self-improvement pipeline so the factory gets better and better with feedback from its human supervisors.
speakers: Graham Neubig (Co-founder, CMU / OpenHands)

title: Data Environments for Agents
abstract: AI agents increasingly query databases, modify files, and operate applications. Their effectiveness depends on the environments in which they act: what information they can discover, which alternatives they can explore, and what happens when they make mistakes. This session examines how data environments can help agents accomplish more while bounding the consequences of failure. Drawing on research from Columbia’s Data, Agents, and Processes Lab, we explore branching and recovery across databases and live execution state, data flow controls that enforce policies and guide agent behavior, and evaluations that reveal bottlenecks in finding and using information. Participants will leave with a framework for reasoning about the responsibilities of models, execution systems, and human interfaces when building agentic applications.
speakers: Eugene Wu (Associate Professor, DAPLab, Columbia University)

title: Recursive Self-Improvement on the Job
abstract: This talk will discuss RSI (recursive self-improvement) agents that proactively and continuously learn on the job. Agents onboard a new knowledge job just like human employees. Through RSI, we show that agents can outperform human testers on the same job across accuracy, efficiency, and cost. The talk will end with a discussion on the future of human-AI collaboration.
speakers: Yu Su (CEO, NeoCognition)

title: No torque sensors, no problem: learning safe physical interaction for humanoids
abstract: How do you make a humanoid robot safe to operate alongside people, without the torque sensors? Fauna Robotics Sprout is a humanoid robot that uses a position-command interface, yet it must regulate the forces it exchanges with the world. We show how Sprout learns compliant behavior that approximates classic impedance control, through mechanisms that control force at the joints and in task space. We describe how these controllers are trained and how they enable safer, whole-body interaction.
speakers: Josh Merel (, Fauna Robotics)

title: Building the machine that builds the machine
abstract: At AWS, we're constantly looking for ways to automate parts of the building process with agents. An upcoming launch takes this to the extreme, releasing an application that was built entirely by autonomous agents without a human ever touching the code base. The agents built a first version over a weekend. But turning that into a robust application was a much longer journey than we expected. In this talk, we pull back the curtain on this upcoming launch and talk about the machine that builds the machine.
speakers: Matt Goldberg (Senior Principal Engineer, AWS)
Lennart Schneider (Applied Scientist, AWS)

title: Beyond Next-Token Prediction: World Models for Human Health
abstract: Next-token prediction has been effective for language, but is it the right learning objective for achieving clinical intelligence from longitudinal human health data? In this talk, we show that treating health records as flat token sequences limit the advancement of foundation models in healthcare. We then introduce a Health State–Action World Model that abstracts longitudinal records into learned representations of patient health states and clinical actions, and models how these states evolve under different interventions. This abstraction enables pretraining models to predict future health events, diagnoses, treatments, and responses to treatment. Across large-scale datasets, we show that moving from token-level prediction to state–action modeling enables clinical intelligence that cannot be achieved through token prediction alone, while generalizing strongly to unseen patients.
speakers: Chenyan Xiong (CEO & Co-Founder, Xlue Inc.)

title: Japan Wrap-up Session
abstract: This session will be delivered in Japanese and provides a comprehensive recap of the major announcements and strategic updates from the keynote sessions throughout the event. Experienced speakers will summarize the most impactful innovations and key messages from AWS leadership. Designed for a broad audience, from developers and engineers to business decision-makers, this session will help you identify and prioritize the announcements most relevant to your organization. It will also help you prepare to share what you learned at re:Invent with your teams when you return to the office
speakers: Yasuhiro Kose (Director, Head of Japan Technology, Amazon Web Services Japan G. K.)
Taro Hirose (Manager, Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Japan G.K)
Kempei Igarashi (Sr. SA Manager, Retail & CPG, AWS Japan, Amazon Web Services)
Issei Kawasaki (Manager, Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Japan G.K.)

title: Developer Keynote
abstract: Building software has never moved faster, and it has never asked more of developers. In this keynote, AWS Engineers and Heroes from the community tackle what's still hard: going from idea to a live app in minutes, building agents that actually work, and trusting code you didn't write yourself. Expect live demos, hard-won lessons from the AWS team that built a new service with an AI software factory, and an honest look at how the developer's job is changing. Come see how AWS is making it easier to build anything you can imagine, then go build it.
speakers: Clare Liguori (Senior Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Marc Brooker (VP and Distinguished Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Eric Johnson (Principal Developer Advocate, Amazon)

title: CEO Keynote
abstract: Join AWS CEO Matt Garman for the re:Invent 2026 CEO Keynote as he shares the latest innovations powering the agentic era. From AI infrastructure and inference to data, agent platforms, and the software agents AWS is building, see how AWS gives you the depth, breadth, and integration to build what's next with new announcements and stories from customers already doing it.
speakers: Barbara Karuth-Zelle (COO, Allianz SE)
Matt Garman (CEO, Amazon Web Services)

title: Data & AI Keynote
abstract: The future is already here...it's just not evenly distributed in production. Most teams have agents that shine in a demo and stall before they do real work. The ones who get to production changed three things: how agents reach their data, how they measure what agents are worth, and the limits they set. Join Swami Sivasubramanian and Andy Warfield to learn how to make these same shifts in your organization.
speakers: Andy Warfield (Vice President and Distinguished Engineer, AWS, Amazon Web Services)
Swami Sivasubramanian (Vice President, AWS Agentic AI & Emerging Technologies, AWS)
Francessca Vasquez (VP, Frontier AI Engineering & Services, AWS)

title: Partner Keynote
abstract: AWS Partners, this one's for you. You're powering today's biggest transformations, and AWS is building alongside you to make co-selling and going to market simpler. This is your biggest moment of re:Invent, where you'll leave knowing where to invest and how to win in the agentic era. Join Dr. Ruba Borno and guests including AWS CEO Matt Garman for a game plan built on agent-run migrations with your data plugged in, your expertise embedded in customer tools, and more profitable business models, plus a Marketplace and Partner Central demo on reaching more buyers faster. Don't miss it.
speakers: Ruba Borno (VP, AWS Specialists & Partners, AWS)
Bob Cagnazzi (CEO, Presidio Global Public Sector)
Matt Yanchyshyn (VP, AWS Marketplace & Partner Services, AWS)
Matt Garman (CEO, Amazon Web Services)

title: Technical Innovations Keynote
abstract: Agents don't follow a script. They change plans mid-task, reach for tools they didn't know they'd need, and create demand you can't predict. For two decades, the hardest workloads builders brought to AWS have pushed us to rethink everything from Graviton and Trainium to the shape of the data center network, to the way storage scales, and how we prove systems behave as intended. Join AWS's top engineers and scientists for an under-the-hood look at the technology that came out of that pressure, the kind of story you won't hear anywhere else. See how AWS infrastructure adapts as your work changes, freeing you to stop engineering around constraints and build anything you can imagine.

Understand why reengineering now matters: organizations that preserve legacy workflows risk slowing AI adoption while others redesign operations for an AI first world. Discover how Camunda ProcessOS works with Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to discover, re-engineer, and improve end-to-end processes. See how Camunda’s agentic orchestration combines deterministic controls with dynamic AI agents, human approval, observability, and auditability. Learn how to assess your environment, build team capability, and match the right migration pathway to each workload. title: Strategies for optimizing your migration: Lessons from ExxonMobil
abstract: Migrating to the cloud and running efficiently once you're there are two different disciplines. In this session, hear ExxonMobil's firsthand journey from a large-scale lift-and-shift migration to a disciplined, data-driven optimization practice, and the role the AWS Optimization and Licensing Assessment (OLA) played both before the move and after, for ongoing optimization. Parker Caputo (ExxonMobil) shares how his team used real utilization data to right-size 1300+ EC2 instances and realize over $2M in annualized savings without sacrificing performance. We'll then explore the tools and programs that make optimization an informed decision at any stage, and close on the layer most native tools can't see on their own: Microsoft licensing. Learn why licensing can represent 30–50% of Windows and SQL Server workload TCO, and how to optimize it as part of your cloud cost strategy.

To make that data estate conversational, they built an external-facing AI product powered by 30+ Databricks Genie Agents, each scoped to a specific energy domain, then composed into cross-commodity endpoints via MCP servers. The system handles 300K+ queries per month, with customers asking complex analytical questions in natural language and getting governed, auditable answers backed by Unity Catalog. abstract: What if modernization started beyond the code? SoftServe is reimagining application modernization by working backwards from business needs and desired outcomes to determine what should change and why. In this session, see how SoftServe Agentic Application Modernization combines this outcome-driven approach with CAST Software, AWS Transform, Kiro, AI-DLC and specialized AI agents to accelerate discovery, assessment, transformation, and validation. Learn how SoftServe provides the AI foundation to orchestrate and govern these agents, turning modernization into an intelligent, repeatable journey that enables AI for organizations, connects business intent with technology decisions and execution on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by SoftServe, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Ruslan Kusov (Cloud COE Director, SoftServe)

title: Adding agentic AI to your legacy app without a rewrite
abstract: Full legacy application rewrites take years. Agentic AI lets you deliver value now. In this code talk, we build an AI agent that wraps an existing legacy application without changing the core system. You'll see how the agent understands user intent, calls existing application functions, and helps users complete business tasks through a modern conversational experience. Ask questions as we go from legacy to AI-assisted workflow in real time. You'll leave ready to put agentic AI in front of your legacy application today.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Franz Stefan (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Robert Hanuschke (Senior Specialist SA Modernization, Amazon Web Services)

title: Watch AWS Transform convert SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL live
abstract: Modernizing SQL Server and its dependent .NET applications to Aurora PostgreSQL typically requires months of manual effort across schema conversion, stored procedure rewriting, and application code changes. In this code talk, see how AWS Transform uses agentic AI to automate this journey end-to-end. Through a live walkthrough, we'll showcase complex schema transformations, T-SQL to PL/pgSQL stored procedure conversions, Entity Framework provider updates, and wave-based orchestration of multi-database estates with human-in-the-loop validation checkpoints. Ask questions throughout. Leave with patterns for modernizing SQL Server at scale.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Prasad Rao (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Alexander Dragunov (Senior Partner Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Building for Always-On: Resilient Trading to Agentic AI on Modern Data Foundation (sponsored by Cognizant)
abstract: Learn how LPL Financial built an always-on trading platform on AWS that supports 32,000+ financial advisors with resilient, multi-region architecture for mission-critical, latency-sensitive workloads. Discover how a unified data foundation across trading, brokerage, and custodial systems creates a trusted layer for innovation, and learn the realities of deploying agentic AI in a regulated broker-dealer environment. Gain practical insights into architecture patterns, governance, real-time data access, key tradeoffs, and lessons learned that can help accelerate your own modernization and AI initiatives. This presentation is brought to you by Cognizant, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Abhishek Sharma (EVP, Head of Wealth Tech, Lpl Financial Holdings Inc.)

title: Building Cross-Enterprise AI Agents with MCP and A2A on AWS
abstract: Enterprises run hundreds of applications from ERP, CRM, supply chain, and beyond and yet orchestrating intelligent actions across these systems remains a challenge. In this chalk talk, learn how to architect and manage cross-enterprise agentic orchestration using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We explore how Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication enable AI agents to seamlessly interact across application boundaries through a single, unified chat interface. Walk away with practical architecture patterns for connecting SAP and adjacent enterprise systems like SalesForce, ServicesNow etc into a cohesive, AI-powered automation layer
speakers: Arne Knoeller (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: How Bayer modernized R&D analytics into an agentic decision engine
abstract: Bayer's R&D analytics relied on manual pipelines, fragmented tooling, and engineering-heavy workflows that bottlenecked scientists. In this session, hear how Bayer modernized that stack into an agentic decision engine on AWS, cutting token costs by roughly 600% and saving scientists 70% of their engineering time. We'll trace the modernization journey from legacy analytics architecture through the migration to cloud-native services and show how that foundation enabled autonomous multi-agent workflows that now orchestrate R&D decisions at enterprise scale. Leave with a framework for modernizing analytics into agentic AI capabilities.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Subbu Dandamudi (Sr Dir Machine Learning Ops &  Data Science, Bayer)
Saurabh Saxena (Sr Principal, AWS, Amazon)

title: Govern and optimize AI agents for desktop work on WorkSpaces
abstract: Your most valuable business processes often run inside desktop applications and mainframes that expose no APIs for AI agents to call. In this session, learn how to use Amazon WorkSpaces to give agents a governed desktop where they operate these applications directly, just as an employee would. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into scoping what agents are permitted to do, auditing agent actions, and configuring agent identity. We'll walk through strategies for agent optimization: how to choose the right agent tools, select the right model for your workflow, and build reusable agent skills. Applied together, these techniques cut task time, lower cost, and increase the accuracy of your agent workflows.
speakers: Ed Mahlum (Principal Product Manager, AWS)
Andrew Morgan (Principal Developer Advocate, AWS)

title: From migration to continuous modernization: reduce tech debt at scale
abstract: Learn how agentic AI is transforming enterprise modernization from one-off projects into an always-on practice. In this session, we explore how organizations are accelerating cloud migration, modernizing mainframe, Windows, and custom applications, and continuously reducing tech debt across their entire portfolio, evolving their pipelines from CI/CD to CI/CD/CM (continuous modernization). See how teams are compressing modernization timelines from years to months while keeping codebases current and AI-ready. Hear from product leader Neha Goswami on the latest innovations and what's ahead.
speakers: Everett Dolgner (AWS Transform, AWS)
Neha Goswami (Director, Developer Experience, Agentic AI Leadership, Neha)

title: Your playbook for modernizing 988K lines of .NET in 2 days
abstract: Transaction Network Services (TNS) needed to modernize their Altitude payments platform that included 274 projects, 988K lines of code, and 20 years of legacy .NET Framework to .NET 10. Their estimate: six months. The result: two days, 26 modules migrated, and 34 security vulnerabilities resolved. In this session, you'll learn what made it possible - from upgrading shared libraries first, running deterministic tools before AI, using human-verified tests, to keeping engineers on the keyboard after the tools stop running. Walk away with a practical, repeatable playbook for accelerating large-scale .NET modernization.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Mustaali Dehnuwala (VP PAY Development & Engineering, Transaction Network Services, Inc.)
Anitha Deenadayalan (Principal Solutions Architect, Developer Transformation, Amazon Web Services)

title: Meet Your AI Teammate for WorkSpaces Administration
abstract: Whether you run WorkSpaces today or are evaluating cloud desktops for the first time, operational overhead follows every virtual desktop deployment: ongoing monitoring, systemic issues that surface as tickets, and end-user requests that consume administrator time. Most teams operate reactively, triaging problems after they surface and manually guiding users through resolution. This session explores how Amazon WorkSpaces Advisor is using AI to reduce resolution time for both IT administrators and end users. We'll walk through the operational challenges we're hearing from customers, share our approach to solving them, and demonstrate early results from production environments. Bring your deployment architecture questions.

title: Provision Desktops for Builders Faster with WorkSpaces
abstract: Builders lose days configuring environments. IT teams struggle to govern the growing sprawl of AI tools and extensions across their organization. In this session, we explore these challenges and share how Amazon WorkSpaces is approaching the builder desktop experience. We'll discuss what enterprises need to provision environments faster, maintain governance across multiple surfaces, and keep pace as AI-assisted development becomes the norm. Bring your questions.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

title: Scaling legacy app modernization with autonomous agents
abstract: Legacy application modernization is a coordination and code generation problem. A large application must be understood, verified, and integrated without losing fidelity. AWS Transform for mainframe reads legacy code and extracts its business rules into traceable specifications that describe what the application does. Learn how AWS Transform overcomes this modernization challenge, and discover the latest capabilities for scaling modernization that compress delivery from days to hours.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater

title: Faster tech debt remediation without the setup overhead
abstract: In this Code Talk, learn how continuous modernization enables faster tech debt analysis and remediation by starting directly from your cloud accounts. Instead of manually connecting code repositories upfront, you can begin identifying tech debt immediately using lifecycle-event signals from your cloud environment. The platform then provides an easy path to resolution with automatic generation of pull requests. We will walk through the account-first workflow and how it gets you from discovery to remediation faster with less setup.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk

title: Build and test HA/DR architectures for Microsoft workloads on AWS
abstract: Can your Windows Server applications and SQL Server databases survive a system outage? In this builders' session, you'll find out by building and testing HA/DR architectures against simulated failures. Get hands-on experience with Elastic Disaster Recovery and Systems Manager to construct resilient infrastructure and recovery automation. Measure RTO and RPO in real time as you purposely break production workloads. Explore additional topics like RDS, S3, Elastic Beanstalk, and AWS Managed AD. You'll leave with a validated resiliency blueprint and the confidence to protect your most critical Microsoft workloads.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Builders' Session
speakers: Kevin Sookhan (Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Chase Lindeman (Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Luciano Bernardes (Specialist Sr. SA - IMM, AWS)
Sagal Farah (Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Sivasekar Elumalai (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Decompose a monolith database into microservices with agentic AI
abstract: Enterprise architects face a critical challenge: breaking monolithic database-centric applications into microservices while managing risk and cost. Where do you draw domain boundaries? How do you extract 20 years of business logic from stored procedures into the application layer? This chalk talk reveals the two-layer decomposition strategy—combining database structure and runtime execution patterns—to identify service boundaries. Leveraging AWS Transform and Kiro, collapse months of manual analysis, design and development into hours of executable code. Through live whiteboarding, learn the data-driven framework enabling business logic extraction, independent deployment, licensing cost reduction, and faster modernization.
speakers: Angus Tong (Senior Solutions Architect, Migration, Amazon Web Services)
Saurabh Sharma (Sr. Modernization Solutions Architect, Amazon AWS)

title: Four labs to shrink your Windows and SQL Server licensing bill
abstract: Lift-and-shift gets you to the cloud, but it doesn't solve the licensing costs that follow. In this builders' session, you'll work through four labs to reduce your Windows and SQL Server spend on Amazon EC2: (1) enable Compute Optimizer for continuous fleet right-sizing; (2) use Optimize CPU to align cores with compute requirements; (3) classify SQL Server HA clusters to remove passive-node licensing fees; and (4) downgrade SQL Server Enterprise to Standard edition. Leave with a production-ready cost optimization blueprint.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Builders' Session
speakers: Thiago Mantovani (Sales Specialist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Modernize Windows to Linux and SQL to PostgreSQL with agentic AI
abstract: Moving workloads from Windows to Linux and SQL Server to PostgreSQL has always been a complex, multi-step project. Agentic AI changes the game by orchestrating the entire journey for you. In this expert-level workshop, you'll start with on-premises Windows Server workloads in a simulated data center and migrate to Amazon EC2 covering agent installation, continuous replication, and cutover. Then you'll modernize by upgrading SQL Server to PostgreSQL and migrating PHP to Amazon EKS, applying replatforming patterns in practice. You'll leave with end-to-end experience executing OS and database modernization, accelerated by agentic AI. Laptop required.
speakers: Aidan Keane (Principal Specialist SA, AWS)
Gianpaolo (GP) Albanese (Infrastructure Migration Modernization Specialist SA, AWS)

title: Turn your cloud migration into a security transformation
abstract: Forward-looking organizations aren't just migrating to AWS — they're using migration to transform their entire security posture. In this workshop, your workloads have just landed on AWS and you'll immediately secure them using sandbox accounts. You'll use Amazon GuardDuty to detect runtime-level threats and malware, Amazon Inspector to prioritize software vulnerabilities, and AWS Security Hub to correlate findings into actionable exposures. You'll finish by building an automated remediation pipeline that isolates compromised resources without human intervention. Leave with a repeatable Day 1 security playbook for any migrated workload. Laptop required.
speakers: Rochak Karki (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Shivam Patel (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc.)

title: Automate your landing zone and network migration with AWS Transform
abstract: Designing landing zones and translating on-premises networks into cloud-native architectures is complex and time-consuming. AWS Transform automates both. In this workshop, you'll see the landing zone agent analyze your requirements and deploy AWS Control Tower, organizational units, service control policies, and workload accounts as infrastructure as code. Then the network agent translates VMware networking components or firewall configurations into VPCs, subnets, security groups, and transit gateways with hub-and-spoke or isolated topologies, ready for deployment in CDK or Terraform modules. Laptop required.
speakers: Suhail Fouzan (Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Todd Gruet (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Break free from Oracle licensing and modernize to Aurora PostgreSQL
abstract: Oracle modernization promises freedom from licensing, lock-in, and operational overhead, yet projects stall on PL/SQL packages, schema quirks, and application logic that resists automated translation. In this workshop, you'll migrate a live Oracle workload to open-source Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL end-to-end and tackle the hardest schema conversion challenges that derail real-world projects. You'll work through PL/SQL translation, dependency resolution, and validation using AWS agentic AI.
speakers: Harpreet Virk (Sr. Solutions Arch - IMM-GFS, AWS)
Tejpreet Reen (Database Specialist Sr. SA, AWS)

title: Best Practices for .NET modernization with AWS Transform
abstract: As organizations look to reduce tech debt for their .NET applications, builders are looking to accelerate modernization with AI tools. In this hands-on session, we'll explore best practices for modernizing .NET Framework applications with AWS Transform. You'll learn how to work alongside the agent to reach a desired outcome. Together, we will apply plan customizations, steering documents, checkpoints, and iteration. Come ready to share your use cases and leave with practical steps to efficient, cost-effective modernization. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Builders' Session

title: Secure and modernize code simultaneously with agentic AI
abstract: Most modernization teams bolt security on as an afterthought, creating costly late-stage vulnerabilities. In this code talk, you'll follow along as we build a custom agent using Strands Agents SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that takes a security-first approach. We wire up AWS Transform agents for tech debt analysis via MCP integrations, connect AWS Continuum for deep code-level vulnerability scanning, and orchestrate everything through Kiro. The result: an agent that synthesizes a security-hardened modernization plan and autonomously executes it. See AI agents collaborate in real time to transform and secure code simultaneously, eliminating handoffs between teams.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Sreekumar Nair (Sr Spec SA Migration+Modernize, Amazon Web Services Singapore Private Limited)
Anand Bilgaiyan (Senior Specialist Partner solution Architect Enterprise Transformation, AWS)

title: Move your multi-tenant agents to serverless AgentCore
abstract: Running multi-tenant agents on Kubernetes gives you flexibility, but it introduces certain operational overhead like cluster management, scaling decisions, and identity plumbing. In this workshop, you'll migrate agents to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's serverless infrastructure without giving up isolation or control. Starting from a working agentic SaaS application on Amazon EKS, you'll progressively refactor each component onto AgentCore: implement tenant isolation, configure shared MCP tools with per-tenant scoping, and instrument tenant-aware memory and observability. You'll validate tenant separation at every step and leave with hands-on experience moving multi-tenant agent infrastructure to a managed architecture. Laptop required.
speakers: Hoseong Seo (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
