title: Design your AWS Transform pipeline for parallel modernization at scale
abstract: How do you modernize thousands of applications concurrently to meet aggressive migration timelines? In this chalk talk, we'll work through architectural patterns for scaling AWS Transform with CI/CD integration: parallel processing with serverless compute, programmatic orchestration via APIs, container strategies, observability at scale, and campaign coordination across teams. Bring your use case and whiteboard it with us. Whether you need pipeline integration, secure private repo processing, or a self-service modernization platform, we'll design your architecture together.
speakers: Deepak Dixit (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Anitha Deenadayalan (Principal Solutions Architect, Developer Transformation, Amazon Web Services)

title: Large-scale VMware exit: engineering a 10,000+ server migration wave engine
abstract: Organizations facing VMware licensing pressure need more than a migration plan. They need a structured exit strategy spanning assessment, mobilization, migration, and modernization. In this session, we discuss how AWS Transform drives business outcomes at each phase: portfolio assessment that quantifies TCO reduction, wave planning that protects application uptime, automated cutover orchestration that eliminates risk, and post-migration modernization that captures cloud-native savings. Drawing from real-world examples, we explore how teams compressed 18-month timelines into ten or lower using AWS Transform and agentic capabilities for migrating compute, database and storage resources, then open the discussion to address your specific use cases.
speakers: Siavash Irani (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Shiva Vaidyanathan (Principal Cloud Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Free your .NET app from Windows licensing with AI-powered portability
abstract: This workshop walks you through modernizing a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to cross-platform .NET 10. You will learn how to transform a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to .NET 10 Blazor using AWS Transform Interactive Mode. Throughout the session, you will interact with the AI agent in real-time asking questions, reviewing assessment and transformation plans, and examining transformation results, including code diffs and build verification. Finally, use Kiro to identify and fix post-transformation runtime issues, such as layout problems, and containerize and deploy the transformed application to Amazon ECS Fargate using the Kiro IDE.
speakers: Khurram Khawaja (Principal PMT-ES, AWS)
Mangesh Budkule (Sr. Specialist Solution Architect, Amazon)

title: Modernize your full .NET and SQL Server stack with AWS Transform
abstract: Modernizing Microsoft workloads means tackling .NET and SQL Server together, not as separate projects. In this workshop, you'll use AWS Transform to compress this effort into a single sprint and reduce operating costs by up to 70% by moving off costly licenses. Working from a legacy app, you'll port .NET Framework code to modern, cross-platform .NET, migrate SQL Server to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, then containerize and deploy to Amazon ECS or EKS. You'll leave with a proven approach to transform your full stack into a scalable, cloud-native architecture. Come ready with your personal GitHub account. Laptop required.
speakers: Jose Guay (Sr. Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services (AWS))
Tekena Orugbani (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect., Amazon Web Services)

title: AIOps for SAP on AWS: Proactive Log Intelligence with Amazon Bedrock Agents
abstract: SAP operations teams spend hours sifting through thousands of log lines to diagnose outages, often only after business impact has occurred. In this workshop, learn how to implement AI-powered operations for SAP workloads on AWS, whether customer-managed or RISE with SAP. Ingest SAP system logs into Amazon CloudWatch using the CloudWatch Agent and SAP ECS LogServ, then deploy an AI agent that will enable proactive analysis and reactive root-cause investigation. Leave with a deployable architecture, real customer examples, and guidance to get started in days with your own agent.
speakers: Adam Hill (WW Tech Leader - SAP, Amazon Web Services)
John Gray (SAP Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: Accelerate legacy Java modernization with custom AI-powered transformations
abstract: Legacy applications on outdated frameworks and deprecated runtimes represent a growing modernization challenge. In this workshop, use AWS Transform custom to build and execute transformations that accelerate Java modernization at scale. You'll define transformation rules using natural language and code examples, execute multi-step upgrades (Java 8 to 21, Spring Boot 2 to 3, Jakarta EE), refine quality through the agentic AI feedback loop, validate with built-in testing, and run campaigns across multiple repositories. You'll leave with reusable transformation definitions you can apply to your own Java codebases. Laptop required.
speakers: Rachel Yen (Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Ritik Khatwani (Senior Worldwide Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Planning for migrations, and operating databases on AWS with Redgate (sponsored by Red Gate)
abstract: Moving a database from on-premises to the cloud is easy to get wrong: undersized instances, surprise costs, unplanned downtime. Join Kellyn and John as we look at Redgate Monitor's new database migration planning feature, designed to help you size, plan, and cost a move with real data instead of guesswork. We will also explore how Redgate Monitor is evolving to support the next generation of database operations, supporting teams who are using AI assistants and Agents who need access to observability data quickly, giving operational staff faster answers and smarter recommendations when managing complex database systems. This presentation is brought to you by Red Gate, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Kellyn Gorman (Engineer and Advocate, Redgate)
John Martin (Technology Partner and Alliances Manager, Redgate Software)

title: What's new in eero networking
abstract: Join us to learn about the latest innovations in eero networking. This session covers new capabilities in AI-powered network analytics, simplified connectivity, centralized security, and multi-WAN resilience - all built cloud-native and designed to scale.

title: Your network, your rules: Global routing policies with AWS Cloud WAN
abstract: As global networks scale, they demand deterministic traffic paths, not best-effort routing. In this workshop, gain granular control over traffic flows between Regions, VPCs, and on-premises locations using AWS Cloud WAN routing policies across a multi-Region network. Through hands-on labs, configure route filtering to control reachability, summarize prefixes to reduce routing table complexity, and influence preferred paths with BGP attributes. Leave with practical skills to design scalable, policy-driven connectivity architectures. Bring your laptop.
speakers: Shubham Singh (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect - Networking, Amazon Web Services)
Mandar Alankar (Senior Networking SA, Amazon Web Services Inc.)

title: Resolve it all: Build hybrid DNS architectures on AWS
abstract: Your enterprise runs workloads across multiple Amazon VPCs while maintaining connectivity to on-premises data centers, and DNS is the glue holding it all together. In this workshop, build a realistic hybrid DNS architecture using the latest Amazon Route 53 capabilities. Participants will learn how to centralize DNS configurations with Route 53 Profiles, replace conditional forwarding rules with native delegation using Resolver Delegation Endpoints, detect and block DNS-based threats with DNS Firewall, and enable secure authenticated resolution for distributed clients with Route 53 Global Resolver. Bring your laptop and resolve hybrid DNS once and for all.
speakers: Kunj Thacker (Senior Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Mevlit Mustafa (Senior Networking Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Centralize AWS PrivateLink endpoints at scale with Amazon VPC Lattice
abstract: Organizations scaling across multiple AWS accounts need AWS PrivateLink endpoints in every VPC, driving up costs and fragmenting access controls. In this session, construct a centralized endpoint architecture in a shared services VPC and expose endpoints to consumers through Amazon VPC Lattice. Configure resource gateways to front endpoints and custom domain names to simplify DNS management, which eliminates Amazon Route 53 Profiles or manual records. Learn how to layer in fine-grained access controls that scale with your environment. Walk away with a deployable pattern for endpoint consolidation at scale.

title: Cut through the options: Choosing the right AWS connectivity solution
abstract: AWS offers a growing range of connectivity services, including AWS Direct Connect, AWS Interconnect (multicloud and last mile), AWS Transit Gateway, and AWS Cloud WAN. But when should you use one over another? In this chalk talk, evaluate your connectivity options and avoid over-engineering your network design. Walk through real-world scenarios and a structured decision framework to understand which service aligns with your requirements. Attendees gain clear guidance and discover practical decision tools for selecting the right service for your scenario. Come prepared with your questions.
speakers: Jordan Rojas Garcia (Sr. Networking Specialist SA, AWS)
Daniel Neri (Sr. WW SSA, Networking, Amazon Web Services)

Attendees gain clear guidance and discover practical decision tools for selecting the right service for your scenario. Come prepared with your questions.

Daniel Neri (Sr. WW SSA, Networking, Amazon Web Services)

abstract: You're collecting Amazon VPC Flow Logs and Amazon CloudWatch metrics, but still can't answer "why can't this instance reach the internet?" In this chalk talk, explore practical approaches to network observability on AWS, no deep expertise required. Cover the key logs and metrics that actually matter, how to read them, and how to set up simple dashboards and alerts that tell you something is wrong before your users do. Bring your monitoring questions, and we'll discuss real scenarios to help you build observability that works for your team.

abstract: Great health checks tell you exactly how your application is really performing, not just that a port is open. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard meaningful health check patterns across ELB, Amazon Global Accelerator, and Amazon Route 53 that covers how to validate database readiness, confirm replica currency, and verify end-to-end request success. We'll explore thresholds, timing configurations, and graceful failover strategies. Bring your architectures, including diagrams, napkin sketches, or draw live on the whiteboard, and we'll design your health strategy together. Leave with actionable patterns that reflect true application liveness.

Satish Katpally (Principal Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

abstract: You started with a single Amazon VPC, and it worked. But as your organization grows, so does your network complexity. In this chalk talk, we'll work through the decision points of scaling from one VPC to many. When should you split workloads? How do you connect VPCs - peering, hub-and-spoke, or mesh? How do you segment traffic, centralize inspection and egress, plan IP addressing at scale, and integrate hybrid connectivity? title: Private AI agent egress: VPC Lattice meets AgentCore Gateway
abstract: Your AI agents need to call private MCP servers, internal REST APIs, and OAuth providers, but those backends must never touch the public internet. In this lightning talk, we demo how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway uses managed Amazon VPC Lattice endpoints to route agent traffic privately into your VPC. We'll configure a private MCP server target, show traffic staying on the AWS backbone, and cover key patterns including intermediate domain routing, private certificate workarounds with ALB, and cross-account connectivity. Walk away with a repeatable pattern for secure, zero-public-internet agentic workloads.

title: Build What’s Next with an AI-Ready Programmable Network (sponsored by Lumen)
abstract: As AI, cloud, and data-intensive applications reshape business, infrastructure must become as dynamic as the workloads it supports. In this session, Lumen explores how programmable networking helps organizations simplify connectivity, improve performance, and securely scale across cloud, edge, and enterprise environments. Learn how real-time network orchestration gives teams greater agility and control while accelerating AI and modernization initiatives. Through examples, including Lumen’s collaboration with AWS to streamline enterprise connectivity, discover how a programmable network creates the resilient digital foundation needed to build what’s next. This presentation is brought to you by Lumen, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Marc Andre Oriani (VP, Enterprise Segment, Lumen Technology)

title: See the routes change: Live BGP with AWS Direct Connect
abstract: AWS Direct Connect can feel like a mystery beneath the surface, and many customers never get hands-on access. In this show and tell, we change that. Starting from a live connection and on-premises router, watch a Direct Connect maintenance unfold in real-time from both sides of the BGP session. See how AWS signals maintenance ahead of time through AS path prepending, graceful shutdown, and how traffic shifts to the backup path before any route is withdrawn. Whether you run 1G or hundreds of 100G ports, leave with the policy and checklist to get through your next maintenance without a page.
speakers: Harold Lotz (Senior Network Development Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Josh Dean (Sr Product Manager-Tech, Direct Connect, Amazon)

abstract: Amazon VPC is a foundational service on AWS, giving you control over your virtual networking environment. title: Enforce encryption in transit using Amazon VPC Encryption Controls
abstract: Regulated workloads demand encryption in transit, but verifying coverage across VPCs, instances, and endpoints is manual and error-prone. In this session, audit and enforce encryption in transit for Amazon VPC traffic using VPC Encryption Controls. Learn how to enable Monitor Mode to assess current encryption posture, migrate to Nitro instances, activate AWS Transit Gateway encryption for cross-VPC traffic, and switch to Enforce Mode. Analyze encryption status across Amazon EC2, NLB, AWS Transit Gateway, and Amazon S3 endpoint flows with Amazon VPC Flow Logs. Leave with hands-on experience enforcing encryption for HIPAA, PCI DSS, and FedRAMP compliance.

Ankush Goyal (Sr. Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Your IPs, your rules: Dynamic edge routing without NAT for AWS BYOIP
abstract: Some workloads need the public IP the world sees to live directly on the Amazon EC2 instances, with no translation in the path. Email gateways rotating sender IPs, VPN concentrators assigning a dedicated address per client, or security appliances terminating traffic on the exact advertised address need the instance to own those public IPs. In this live-coding talk, we build that model end-to-end on AWS: writing CloudFormation for BYOIP pools and Bring Your Own ASN, coding NAT-free ingress routing so traffic arrives untranslated, and configuring BGP peering with Amazon VPC Route Server for high availability.
speakers: Ammar Latif (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Srinivas Kurla (Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: Bridging clouds: Building global multicloud and hybrid networks on AWS
abstract: It's no secret, enterprises today run workloads across multiple clouds and on-premises data centers, but stitching together global connectivity without complexity remains a challenge. In this workshop, easily extend AWS connectivity to other clouds and on-premises environments using AWS Interconnect, AWS Direct Connect, and AWS Cloud WAN. Build a global multicloud network, then apply Amazon VPC Lattice to enforce security and handle overlapping IP address spaces without complex NAT configurations. Leave equipped to architect and deploy hybrid network architectures using modern application networking patterns. Bring your laptop.
speakers: Mike Jager (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Mike Bentzen (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Building an interconnectivity fabric across AWS accounts and orgs
abstract: Deploying workloads across AWS accounts - whether across an organization, between business units, or alongside acquired entities - creates connectivity complexity that traditional networking options don’t cleanly solve. You face IP coordination headaches, overly broad network surface exposure, and heavy per-resource infrastructure just to share a service privately. In this session, build a private interconnectivity fabric: a federated architecture where multiple organizations share services privately and bidirectionally with independent governance. Combine Amazon VPC Lattice, resource gateways, AWS PrivateLink, and AWS Resource Access Manager into a cross-organization platform covering bidirectional topologies and federated governance.

title: Your WAN, reimagined: SD-WAN on the AWS global backbone
abstract: Your enterprise WAN was built for a world where applications lived in data centers. That world is gone, but you're still paying for MPLS circuits and waiting weeks for new sites. What if you could replace that backbone entirely? AWS offers the largest global infrastructure footprint of any provider: resilient, agile, low-latency, and encrypted. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how to connect your SD-WAN to AWS Cloud WAN, maintain segmentation from branch to VPC, and pay only for what you use—no long-term contracts. Bring your WAN architecture and we'll show you what it looks like without the middlemen.
speakers: Anandprasanna Gaitonde (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Mehdi Dahane (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect – Networking, Amazon Web Services)

abstract: As ISVs scale their SaaS platforms, network architecture becomes a critical decision: balancing tenant isolation, compliance, and operational efficiency. In this chalk talk, examine proven connectivity patterns using AWS PrivateLink, AWS Transit Gateway, and Amazon VPC Lattice for multi-tenant environments. Explore how to enforce strong tenant boundaries at the network layer, handle cross-account connectivity at scale, and reduce operational complexity as your business grows. Whether building a new multi-tenant platform or evolving an existing one, leave with architecture blueprints ready for production.
speakers: Tom Adamski (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Rizwan Mushtaq (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: Scaling website delivery with Amazon CloudFront: one configuration, many sites
abstract: Most enterprises don’t run just one website, they run many: a corporate site, regional or sub-brand sites, plus internal portals for each. Managing TLS certificates, WAF rules, and cache behavior separately for every one creates configuration drift, inconsistent security posture, and operational overhead that scales with your site count. In this workshop, you’ll use Amazon CloudFront to define a single reusable baseline configuration and apply it consistently across many websites - whether they represent different brands, business units, or access levels - while still allowing targeted overrides where a site genuinely needs to differ (stricter WAF on internal portals, a custom origin for a sub-brand). You’ll leave with a working reference architecture and a decision framework for what belongs in the baseline vs. the override.
speakers: Derek Ziehl (Sr Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Evan Lecklider (Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Harith Gaddamanugu (Sr.Solutions Architect- Edge Services, AWS)
David MacDonald (Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: Origin management for multi-region resilient applications with Amazon CloudFront
abstract: In this session, you'll learn comprehensive origin management with Amazon CloudFront to build secure, resilient content delivery systems. We'll cover automatic failover mechanisms with CloudFront and Route 53, configure granular origin routing with CloudFront Functions, and secure origins using S3 with Origin Access Control (OAC) and VPC private origins for enhanced security. We'll explore integrating on-premises infrastructure through AWS Direct Connect for hybrid architectures, and deploy Origin Shield to further optimize cache performance and reduce origin load.
speakers: Carlos Salazar (US, Specialist Sr. SA, Amazon Web Services)
Jonathan Woods (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: Architecting anti-piracy defenses for video streaming with Amazon CloudFront
abstract: Modern streaming demands instant revocation, concurrent stream limits, device-bound sessions, and per-user policy decisions at the edge. In this chalk talk, whiteboard the full decision space with us. We'll map the trade-offs between signed URLs, signed cookies, and emerging token approaches like Content Access Tokens (CAT) built on CBOR Web Tokens, then diagram the architecture patterns behind them: embedding custom claims and evaluating them in CloudFront Functions, using CloudFront KeyValueStore for real-time revocation without key rotation, and chaining tokens across HLS/DASH segments. Bring your hardest content protection scenarios, such as credential sharing, restreaming, geo abuse. We'll work through them together at the board, leaving you with a framework for matching protection mechanisms to your security and business requirements.
speakers: Matt Carter (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Christer Christer (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Practical applications of edge compute in Amazon CloudFront
abstract: Edge compute is a practical way to build faster, smarter applications. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll dive into how Amazon CloudFront empowers developers to run custom logic at the edge using CloudFront Functions, Lambda@Edge, and the Key Value Store. We'll explore real-world use cases, architectural patterns, and recent feature launches that unlock powerful personalization, performance optimization, and cost efficiency. Come ready to whiteboard, ask questions, and discover how to push intelligence closer to your users.

title: Exploit a software vulnerability, then stop it: From code to containment
abstract: Step into the role of a DevSecOps engineer tasked with hardening your organization's web applications after a security audit. In this hands-on workshop, a simulated lab walks you through real threat scenarios, and you respond using layered AWS security services. Start with AWS Security Agent to catch vulnerabilities pre-deployment, then use Kiro's agentic capabilities to auto-remediate issues without leaving your IDE. Scan EC2 instances and SBOMs for supply-chain risk, apply virtual patches via AWS WAF, and fully remediate with AWS Systems Manager. Finally, contain an active GuardDuty-detected incident by blocking C2 communication with Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall and AWS Network Firewall, proving that layered defenses hold even against unpatched vulnerabilities.
speakers: Vishal Lakhotia (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS)
Paul Kelsey (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Securing Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with AWS WAF and a self-healing security agent
abstract: As enterprises move generative AI agents from prototype to production, securing the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes a first-class requirement, not an afterthought. In this hands-on workshop, you'll attach AWS WAF natively to a Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with no ALB, no VPC Interface Endpoint, and no Lambda proxy required, enabling managed rule groups, rate-based rules, and IP-based access controls that protect every tool behind the Gateway with a single configuration. We will launch simulated attacks and watch AWS WAF block them in real time. Finally, you'll build an agent that pulls signals from AWS WAF, and autonomously remediates threats and generating a plain-English incident summary.
speakers: Piotrek Witkowski (Specialist SA, Edge Services, Amazon Web Services)
Alex Moening (Sr Soulutions Archatect, AWS)

title: Surviving the drop: Build a flash-sale control plane with CloudFront
abstract: Product drops, ticket on-sales, and viral promotions can spike traffic 50x in seconds. Origin infrastructure is the wrong place to absorb it. In this workshop, build a complete launch-day control plane using Amazon CloudFront Functions and CloudFront KeyValueStore. Implement a launch gate with VIP early access, a percentage-based throttle that dials traffic to your purchase origin in real time, sticky A/B testing for product pages, and a global kill switch - all controlled by KeyValueStore updates that propagate worldwide in seconds, with zero deployments and zero origin changes. Along the way, use edge location metadata for geo-staggered launches and trace every gate decision with CloudFront Functions access logging. Leave with patterns you can apply to any high-demand launch event. Attendees must bring a laptop.
speakers: Sanchith Kandaka (Specialist SA, AWS)
Fenil Patel (Solutions Architect, Edge Services, Amazon)
David MacDonald (Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: What's new in Amazon Route 53: DNS innovations for 2026
abstract: Explore the latest innovations in Amazon Route 53, AWS's fully managed DNS service. This session covers 2026 launches including Route 53 Global Resolver for secure anycast DNS resolution from anywhere without VPNs, DNS Views sharing across accounts, and expanded DNS Firewall threat protection through partnerships. In this session, we also cover Profiles enhancements for simplified multi-VPC DNS management with granular IAM controls, and expanded domain registration support. Learn how these capabilities help you secure DNS resolution, simplify hybrid and multi-account architectures, and strengthen your DNS security posture at scale.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Bhargav Talluri (Senior Manager, Product Management Technical, Amazon Web Services)
Hardik Rathod (Sr Product Manager Technical, Amazon Web Services)

title: Resilient by design: Last Mile and Multicloud Interconnect
abstract: Connecting a data center, a branch office, or another cloud to AWS has meant weeks of partner coordination, cross-connects, BGP configuration, and redundancy you design. AWS Interconnect - last mile and AWS Interconnect - multicloud move that work into the AWS Console and API, with resilient design built in. We start with the AWS Direct Connect building blocks and whiteboard what changes. You stop ordering cross-connects, configuring BGP, and designing redundancy. You still choose where it connects: a virtual private gateway, AWS Transit Gateway, or AWS Cloud WAN. Bring your hybrid and multicloud challenges.
speakers: Steve Bruggeman (Principal Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Donald Quindardo (Principal TAM, Amazon Web Services)

title: Resilient by design: Simplifying last-mile connectivity with AWS
abstract: Establishing resilient private connectivity from data centers and branch offices to AWS has traditionally required weeks of partner coordination, physical cross-connects, and manual resilience configurations. Yet true resilience demands more than provisioning a second connection. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how AWS Direct Connect and AWS Interconnect each address location diversity, device diversity, BGP routing policy, and failover validation. Compare dedicated links with full routing control to fully managed connections with built-in redundancy, explore integration with AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN, and evaluate maximum versus high resiliency models. Bring your hybrid connectivity challenges.
speakers: Steve Bruggeman (Principal Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Donald Quindardo (Principal TAM, Amazon Web Services)

title: Deep dive into Elastic Load Balancing for modern workloads
abstract: Architect high-performance, resilient network infrastructure using Network Load Balancer and Gateway Load Balancer. This deep dive covers advanced load balancing, multi-protocol support, and security appliance integration at scale. In this session, we explore NLB source IP preservation, GWLB transparent inspection architecture, and deployment patterns. Topics include performance optimization, troubleshooting methodologies, QUIC support, and resilience capabilities including Zonal Shift and Zonal Autoshift. Whether you're running financial trading platforms, gaming backends, or large-scale SaaS, learn practical blueprints for designing architectures that deliver high availability and predictable performance while maintaining inline security inspection and compliance.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Felipe da Silva (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Milind Kulkarni (Principal Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Connectivity strategies across AWS Partitions
abstract: Organizations increasingly operate across AWS commercial, GovCloud, Sovereign Cloud, and China Regions to satisfy regulatory, data residency, and national security requirements. But connecting them introduces networking challenges that go well beyond standard multi-Region design. In this session, learn cross-partition connectivity patterns using AWS Site-to-Site VPN, AWS Direct Connect, and application-layer proxies alongside DNS resolution strategies, compliance boundary enforcement, and operational trade-offs. We walk through architectural blueprints for securely linking partitions while preserving the isolation guarantees they exist to enforce, and share lessons learned from customers navigating ITAR, GDPR, and national sovereignty mandates at scale.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Kunal Sharma (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Rohit Aswani (Principal Solutions Architect - Networking Specialist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Elastic Fabric Adapter powering the largest AI workloads on AWS
abstract: AWS built Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to bring high-performance networking to the cloud - powered by the Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) protocol designed for elastic, reliable, cloud-scale performance. This session explores EFA's origins in high-performance computing (HPC) and its evolution into the backbone of today's largest AI training and inference architectures. Discover how early architecture decisions now unlock novel use cases across pretraining, reinforcement learning, and disaggregated inference with hundreds of thousands of accelerators. We dive into recent innovations including library integrations, protocol optimizations, and performance gains.
speakers: John Pangle (Principal Product Manager - Tech, Amazon)
Erez Zarum (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Scaling and securing MCP Servers with AWS Load Balancing and WAF
abstract: MCP servers are becoming essential infrastructure in enterprise AI environments, and running them in production demands both scalability and security. Join this chalk talk to explore patterns for scaling and securing your MCP servers using AWS native services. We'll cover how to configure Application Load Balancer for MCP traffic characteristics, implement health checks and routing policies, and scale horizontally across availability zones. We'll also cover how to enforce security controls with AWS WAF, including request filtering, rate limiting, and tool-level access policies. Whether you're running a handful of MCP servers or deploying at enterprise scale, you'll leave with actionable architectures for production-ready deployments.
speakers: Max Hausner (Networking Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Eitav Arditti (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Scaling and securing MCP Servers with AWS Load Balancing and WAF
abstract: MCP servers are becoming essential infrastructure in enterprise AI environments, and running them in production demands both scalability and security. Join this chalk talk to explore patterns for scaling and securing your MCP servers using AWS native services. We'll cover how to configure Application Load Balancer for MCP traffic characteristics, implement health checks and routing policies, and scale horizontally across availability zones. We'll also cover how to enforce security controls with AWS WAF, including request filtering, rate limiting, and tool-level access policies. Whether you're running a handful of MCP servers or deploying at enterprise scale, you'll leave with actionable architectures for production-ready deployments.
speakers: Max Hausner (Networking Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Eitav Arditti (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Ready before the surge - smart ELB capacity reservations
abstract: Your Load Balancer scales automatically for most traffic, and now you can prepare it for predictable spikes before they arrive. Product launches, flash sales, live events, and Monday-morning market opens deserve a load balancer that's ready instantly. Load Balancer Capacity Unit (LCU) Reservation pre-provisions a capacity floor so your infrastructure is never caught cold. In this session, we introduce new capacity management capabilities across ALB, NLB, and GLB that turn reservation planning into a data-driven workflow. Learn how to analyze historical patterns, set the right capacity floor, and release reservations with confidence.
speakers: Ikenna Izugbokwe (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Hema Halagatti (Senior Product Manager, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: From shopping agents to shoppers: Amazon CloudFront patterns for peak retail
abstract: Peak retail traffic is no longer just more shoppers. AI shopping agents, scrapers, and personalized experiences now collide on the same edge. In this session, learn advanced Amazon CloudFront patterns to handle all three. See how to classify and verify agentic traffic using CloudFront Functions, Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore, and AWS WAF Bot Control, then serve tiered responses without touching origin. Hear how you can serve AI-powered personalization on every page in about a millisecond by encoding decision-tree models in KeyValueStore, fed by an Amazon Bedrock pipeline. Discover battle-tested patterns for your next cyber week.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Sagar Desarda (Solutions Architecture Leader - Retail, AWS)
Andrew Templeton (Chief Technology Officer, CSC Generation)

title: Level up your bot defense for mobile apps and web with AWS WAF SDK
abstract: In this session, we'll dive into advanced bot mitigation using the AWS WAF SDK and label evaluations. Learn how to go beyond basic rule-based blocking to implement dynamic, data-driven defenses that adapt to evolving threats. We'll explore programmatically managing WAF rules, leveraging labels for granular request inspection, and integrating SDK workflows to automate threat response across mobile app, JavaScript, and API traffic integrations. Through real-world scenarios, you'll see how to distinguish legitimate traffic from sophisticated bots, reduce false positives, and maintain application performance across surfaces. Bring your questions and learn how to implement scalable, intelligent bot protection at the edge.
speakers: Tzoori Tamam (Principal Solutions Architect Specialist, Amazon Web Services)
Harith Gaddamanugu (Sr.Solutions Architect- Edge Services, AWS)

title: A practitioner’s guide to migrating from 3rd-party CDN and WAF to AWS
abstract: Considering migrating from a third-party CDN/WAF provider to AWS services? In this chalk talk, we’ll walk through the migration phases together: defining success criteria, running low-risk proof of concepts, designing your target architecture with Amazon Route 53, Amazon CloudFront, AWS WAF, and edge compute, executing the DNS cutover, and managing post-migration operations. Most of this session is open discussion: you bring your questions and stories, and we’ll share what we’ve learned running these migrations in production.
speakers: Etienne Munnich (Snr Edge Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Achraf Souk (Principal Solutions Architect, Edge Services, AWS)

title: AI agents are crawling your website? Identify, optimize, rate-limit, & monetize them
abstract: AI agents are the new web visitors, but how do you protect your content while unlocking new revenue? In this code talk, we deploy a Single Page Application on CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, and Bedrock, then progressively secure and monetize AI agent traffic. We integrate AWS WAF Bot Control to identify agents via the WBA protocol, implement intelligent routing in CloudFront Functions to serve optimized content per visitor type, and enforce rate limits by bot identity and actual resource consumption. Finally, we enable AI Traffic Monetization in WAF and demonstrate end-to-end paid content access using the x402 payment protocol with a Bedrock AgentCore.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: RISHU GUPTA (Senior Cloud Support Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Philon Terving (Specialist SA, Edge Services, AWS)

title: AI agents are crawling your website? Identify, optimize, rate-limit, & monetize them
abstract: AI agents are the new web visitors, but how do you protect your content while unlocking new revenue? title: Building searchable live sports with AWS Elemental and Amazon CloudFront
abstract: Live sports fans no longer watch one feed and wait for the recap. They expect every angle live and every key play instantly findable. In this session, see how you turn live sports into searchable fan moments on AWS. Using AWS Elemental inference, the platform generates highlight clips in real time and pairs them with conversational AI powered by Amazon Bedrock, so fans can ask for "the catch in the third quarter" and get it in seconds instead of hours. Then go deeper into the delivery workflow: composing multi-view experiences so viewers follow simultaneous matches and camera angles, enriching clips with AI-generated titles and captions, and delivering live feeds and clips globally through a single Amazon CloudFront architecture.
speakers: John Councilman (Edge Solutions Architect, Amazon AWS)
Brian Bedard (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: The AWS network I would build today: Identity over topology (sponsored by Tailscale)
abstract: Modern AWS environments can grow from a handful of VPCs into complex regional and global routing topologies. This session explores a different model: keeping VPC networking local and predictable while using identity-aware connectivity between users, workloads, and networks. See how Tailscale connects AWS environments and resources, including those that cannot run an agent, and explore an experimental integration with AWS Gateway Load Balancer and GENEVE. Attendees will learn the tradeoffs, where native AWS networking remains the right choice, and how identity-aware networking can reduce connectivity complexity without sacrificing control. This presentation is brought to you by Tailscale, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Lee Briggs (VP, Customer Engineering, Tailscale)

title: Extending your cloud network with Amazon Leo satellite connectivity
abstract: Your cloud network doesn't have to end where fiber does. In this interactive whiteboard session, you'll design hybrid network architectures that combine Amazon Leo's low-earth orbit satellite connectivity with AWS networking services including VPN, Transit Gateway, and Cloud WAN. We'll start with Leo's real-world performance characteristics: latency, throughput, and availability. Then, we'll work through three architecture patterns: first-day connectivity for new sites, primary connectivity for remote locations, and satellite-based redundancy for existing terrestrial links. You'll leave with reference architectures you can adapt to your environment and a clear understanding of how the constellation fits in your network design.
speakers: Catalina Villegas (Technical Program Manager, Amazon Leo)
Camden Forgia (Principal Product Manager Tech, Amazon Leo)

title: Innovations in Elastic Load Balancing and application networking
abstract: Discover the latest innovations in application networking. This session covers new capabilities in Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) and simplified application delivery across all compute environments. Learn how new approaches to application networking help you save time and money. Whether you're building microservices, modern application architectures, or AI agent workloads, see what's next for application networking on AWS.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater

title: AI innovations across network monitoring and operations
abstract: Join us to explore how AI is transforming network monitoring and observability. This session dives into new capabilities for traffic analysis, network health monitoring, and faster issue resolution that shows how intelligent, automated tooling helps you move from reactive troubleshooting to proactive insight. Whether you want to cut time-to-resolution or get a clearer, real-time pulse on your network's health, come see what's new and what's on the horizon.

title: Innovations in Secure Service Edge architectures on AWS
abstract: Join us to learn about the latest innovations and capabilities in Secure Service Edge (SSE) and cloud networking. Whether you're simplifying your security stack or scaling secure connectivity, see what's new across SSE architectures.

title: Building hybrid satellite and cloud networks with Amazon Leo
abstract: Learn how low-earth orbit (LEO) satellite connectivity is changing the way organizations build hybrid networks. This session explores how Amazon Leo satellite constellations integrate with AWS networking services to extend cloud connectivity to remote and hard-to-reach locations. We cover new innovations in space-based networking, including how to add network resiliency and architect hybrid satellite-cloud networks. Whether you're looking to improve coverage for distributed operations or exploring new connectivity options, come learn how satellite networking fits into your cloud network strategy.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater

title: Innovations in DNS and Amazon Route 53
abstract: Join us to learn about the latest innovations in Domain Name Systems (DNS) and Amazon Route 53. This session covers new capabilities in DNS resolution and new approaches to private and public domain resolution. Join us for architecture patterns and best practices that simplify DNS at scale.

title: DDI Architecture Patterns: DNS, DHCP, and IPAM at AWS
abstract: Join us to explore architecture patterns for DDI - DNS, DHCP, and IP Address Management (IPAM). This session covers approaches for resolving DNS across hybrid and multicloud environments, managing private and public domains, and unifying address management for consistent governance and visibility. Walk away with best practices that simplify DDI operations at scale.

title: DDI Architecture Patterns: DNS, DHCP, and IPAM at AWS

abstract: Join us to learn about the latest innovations in Domain Name Systems (DNS) and Amazon Route 53. room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater

title: Innovations in network security on AWS
abstract: Join us to learn about the latest innovations in network security on AWS. This session covers new capabilities in traffic protection and new approaches to securing internet traffic across your environment. Join us for architecture patterns and best practices that simplify network security at scale.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Code Talk

title: Innovations at the Edge on AWS
abstract: Modern applications demand networks that are fast, flexible, and built to scale. Join us for a practical look at architecture patterns that help you deliver high-performance, low-latency connectivity across your AWS environment. We'll cover approaches for optimizing network performance, supporting demanding workloads, and designing for resilience - giving you a toolkit of patterns you can apply to your own network.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater

title: Owning atoms to bits: How AWS accelerates network innovation at scale
abstract: At AWS, we design everything within our infrastructure networks, from buildings to fiber, routers to protocols. This atoms-to-bits ownership lets us move at breakneck speed: the moment we spot an opportunity to improve customer performance or resilience, we drive it into production. In this talk, Senior Principal Engineers cover how they applied this pattern to develop the random graph fabrics reshaping data center topologies and highly available systems for machine learning at planet scale. Learn what it takes to continually refresh, upgrade, and re-architect live infrastructure without ever interrupting a single customer workload.
speakers: Stephen Callaghan (Senior Principal Network Engineer, AWS)
Giacomo Bernardi (Sr. Principal Technologist, Amazon)

title: Connect everything, everywhere: AWS global connectivity
abstract: Point solutions don't scale globally. Stitching together and managing dozens of them creates gaps. In this session, discover what's new in AWS Cloud WAN and AWS Direct Connect: simplified hybrid connectivity, smarter segmentation, and real-time visibility across global traffic. See how AWS Cloud WAN's policy engine and AWS Direct Connect's latest capabilities combine to deliver seamless connectivity from anywhere to anywhere. Discover patterns to build a borderless, resilient global network.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Shridhar Kulkarni (Principal Product Manager, Amazon)
Sidhartha Chauhan (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Chaos engineering: Network fault injection with Gateway Load Balancer
abstract: Your application works perfectly in the lab, but what happens with 45ms latency and 0.1% packet loss? In this session, deploy a transparent network fault simulator using AWS Gateway Load Balancer and Linux Traffic Control (TC) on Amazon EC2. Inject delay, jitter, packet loss, and bandwidth constraints into live traffic, then observe how a tightly coupled application degrades in real time. Use the results to set SLA thresholds, validate AWS Direct Connect failover behavior, and justify architectural decisions. Leave with a reusable, parameterized emulator pattern deployable via AWS Systems Manager.
speakers: Gonzalo Escarrá (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Harold Morales (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazno Web Services)
Anuj Saxena (Technical Account Manager, Amazon.com)
Elshan Hasanov (Senior Technical Account Manager, AWS)
Rob Fulton (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Managing and monitoring AWS Direct Connect at scale: customer lessons
abstract: AWS shares customer best practices for managing and monitoring AWS Direct Connect at hyperscale. Network teams discusses how they operate one of the world's largest Direct Connect footprints, spanning multiple regions and supporting AI training workloads that serve billions of users. We deep-dive into new monitoring capabilities: Amazon CloudWatch metrics for BGP session health and prefix counts, VIF rate limiters that prevent bandwidth contention across shared connections, and Network Synthetic Monitor for proactive path-level health diagnostics. Attendees will learn strategies for alerting, capacity planning, and building unified dashboards for cross-Region network visibility.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Dave Gadling (Production Engineer, Meta)
Robin Rodriguez (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Pratik Mankad (Sr SA, Networking, AWS)

title: EFA deep dive: Architecture, evolution, and scaling with OpenAI
abstract: We built EFA to deliver multi-tenant, elastic, high-performance networking with portability across every instance type and accelerator through Libfabric. The architecture that followed, such as multipath packet spraying, out-of-order delivery, and encryption of every byte in transit, has scaled from HPC workloads to the backbone of today's largest AI training clusters. Now it's evolving again to support disaggregated inference and expert parallelism. OpenAI joins to share how they adapted their production inference stack to EFA on EC2 UltraServers, covering Reliable Datagram semantics for GPU-to-GPU collectives, NCCL tuning, and topology-aware communication patterns that unlock new performance.
speakers: Brian Barrett (Senior Principal Technologist, Amazon Web Services)
Sujith Katakam (Head of Supercomputing, OpenAI)
John Pangle (Principal Product Manager - Tech, Amazon)

title: Innovations across the AWS Backbone
abstract: In this session, we explore how AWS innovates on the backbone and improves the customer experience. We cover new capabilities that help deliver higher performance and reliability for mission-critical workloads. Learn about the challenges and innovations throughout this multi-year journey to improve network availability across the AWS backbone.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: From AI proof of concepts to enterprise-grade production systems on Ubuntu (sponsored by Canonical)
abstract: AI stacks are complex, interdependent, and high-stakes. Spinning an AI prototype is easy while making it enterprise-ready is much more challenging. Most organizations can’t keep track of their dependencies within their AI projects, leading to solutions that fail security checks and break easily. How do you move to a robust, secure AI solution that is built to last? Learn how to architect, secure, and maintain a resilient enterprise-grade AI infrastructure on Ubuntu, without sacrificing speed. This presentation is brought to you by Canonical, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Aaron Whitehouse (Public Cloud Product Manager, Canonical)

title: Observe me that: Easy OpenTelemetry monitoring for your systems (sponsored by Dash0)
abstract: OpenTelemetry is the de-facto open-source standard for vendor-neutral traces, metrics, and logs. But, if you are not an OpenTelemetry expert, the learning curve to add it to your systems can be intimidating. This session covers how to bring OpenTelemetry with zero-code/no-touch instrumentation in applications running on AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2, ECS and EKS, as well as how to bring into your OpenTelemetry pipelines telemetry from various AWS managed services and how to use agentic skills to level up the quality of your instrumentations and get better value out of your telemetry backends, coding agents, and AI tools. You will leave this session with a concrete map to get your OpenTelemetry journey started with tangible results in minutes. This presentation is brought to you by Dash0, an AWS Partner.

title: Governing AI assets at scale with MCP Gateway and Registry
abstract: As enterprises onboard AI assets (MCP servers, Agents, Skills) they face a governance problem: no unified way to discover, authenticate, or observe them. MCP Gateway and Registry is an open source control plane with centralized registration, OAuth2 auth, semantic tool discovery, and end-to-end telemetry. Walk through the project's architecture, pluggable auth and storage backends, and deployment patterns on Amazon EKS. An AI/ML platform VP shares their production rollout, governance patterns that scaled across business units, and lessons learned contributing back upstream.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Sabeena Shafaq (VP of AI & Analytics Platforms, Expedia Group)
Amit Arora (Principal Solutions Architect - AI/ML, AWS)

title: Rethinking the AWS SDK for Python: Async, streaming, and more
abstract: If you've ever wrapped boto3 in asyncio, juggled thread pools for concurrent AWS calls, or wished for proper streaming support, this session is for you. With the new AWS SDK for Python, async is native, concurrent calls no longer require thread-pool workarounds, and bidirectional streaming enables use cases like live transcription and speech-to-speech that go beyond what's available in boto3 today. Follow along as we put those capabilities to work with clean concurrent calls, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Transcribe streaming, and a practical path to migrating your own code to the new SDK.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Jonathan Gaytan (Software Engineer, AWS)
Alessandra Romero (Software Development Engineer, AWS)

title: Beyond chatbots: Event-driven AI agents on Apache Flink
abstract: Most AI agents wait for a prompt. Apache Flink Agents flips that—agents react autonomously to live event streams as Flink operators, with exactly-once guarantees, durable state, and millisecond latency. Learn how this event-driven foundation differs from request-response frameworks, then see an ops agent detect a failing Flink job, diagnose it with an LLM on Amazon Bedrock, retrieve a runbook, and remediate—no human in the loop. Hear from Flink committers on production agents at Alibaba and LinkedIn, and from AWS contributors building Bedrock and other AWS integrations upstream.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Weiqing Yang (Senior Staff Software Engineer, LinkedIn)
Mayank Juneja (Senior Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Observability for AI agents: Strands, OpenTelemetry, and Langfuse
abstract: You're running AI agents in cloud ops, but can you see inside them? In this hands-on workshop, deploy a Strands Agents SDK agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, then wire up full observability using Strands' built-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation and Langfuse (open-source) as the backend. Trace every LLM call, tool invocation, and reasoning step. Debug failures, analyze token costs, version prompts, and score output quality — all with open source and open standards.
speakers: Smruti Tripathy (Systems Development Engineer II, Amazon Web Services)
Kien Tran (Principal Cloud Support Engineer, Amazon)

title: Agents need names too: Open standards for agent discovery
abstract: As AI agents proliferate, the internet needs a decentralized way to name, discover, and trust them. This session explores how AWS contributes to open source projects like DNS-AID (IETF/Linux Foundation) and AI-Catalog (Linux Foundation) to define the agent discovery layer atop existing DNS infrastructure. We'll walk through the specs — SVCB records, W3C DIDs, Verifiable Credentials, HTTP Message Signatures — and show how anyone can resolve and verify an agent with off-the-shelf libraries and a single DNS query. No vendor lock-in. Standards in, standards out.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Bhargav Talluri (Senior Manager, Product Management Technical, Amazon Web Services)
Jeffrey Damick (Principal SDE, AWS)

title: AWS CDK - Contributing AI safety tooling to the IaC ecosystem
abstract: AI agents generate infrastructure-as-code that looks correct but fails 38% of the time at deployment. The open source Agent Toolkit for AWS provides skills for validation, linting, and security checks that any MCP-compatible AI tool can consume before deploying. This chalk talk covers how we contributed these capabilities as open source tooling that works across cfn-lint, Checkov, and cdk-nag, improving first-deploy success from 62% to 82%. Attendees discuss how to build similar validation layers for their own IaC tools and the tradeoffs between blocking vs advisory checks in agent workflows.
speakers: Praneeta Prakash (Sr. Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build multi-agent workflows with Strands Agents SDK on AWS
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, build a multi-agent system using the Strands Agents open source SDK. You will create specialized agents with distinct roles, connect them via MCP for tool access, implement agent-to-agent delegation patterns, and add memory for stateful conversations. Deploy and test your multi-agent workflow end-to-end. Walk away with working code and reusable patterns for orchestrating collaborative AI agents using open source tooling.
speakers: Arun Kumar Selvaraj (Senior Delivery Consultant, Amazon Web Services)
Daniel Lorch (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: The Neuron Stack: Enabling open source ML solutions on AWS Trainium
abstract: The Neuron software stack has evolved into an open source-first architecture. Developers can read, modify, and contribute to the components that compile, optimize, and execute ML workloads on Trainium. This session covers how Neuron enables open source ML solutions on Trainium. We show what's open source, how it integrates with upstream projects like PyTorch and distributed training frameworks, and how developers use these tools without modifications. Attendees leave understanding the Neuron stack, which parts are open source, and how to use and contribute to them.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Maen Suleiman (Head of Neuron Product Management, Annapurna Labs)

title: Defense in depth for Strands AI agents with Cedar, AgentCore, and Rex
abstract: AI agents that generate and execute code on remote systems need more than a single permission check - they need policy enforcement at every trust boundary. In this builders' session, you’ll configure Cedar policies at two distinct enforcement points for a Strands pre-built operations agent : AgentCore Policy on AgentCore Gateway and Trusted Remote Execution (REX) on the target remote host. You’ll see why both are necessary, how they compose, and how the agent gracefully adapts when it hits either boundary.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Trevor Schiavone (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))
Abdu Mahmoudi (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Nadhya Polanco (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Matt Eglin (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Emre Alptekin (Sr Specialist TAM - Security, AWS)

title: CLI Agent Orchestrator: Open source multi-agent AI for developer CLIs
abstract: Complex projects outgrow a single AI agent's context and capability. CLI Agent Orchestrator (CAO), an awslabs open source project, coordinates 8 CLIs including Amazon Kiro CLI, Claude Code, and Codex into a multi-agent powerhouse via the Model Context Protocol and tmux. It provides a centralised harness with shared skills, memory, and integration with OpenClaw and Hermes Agent. In this builders' session you'll install CAO, launch a supervisor and specialist agents, and put the team to work on a real change in a sample repo. You'll walk away with a multi-agent workflow to drop into your projects.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Haofei Feng (Senior Cloud Architect, AWS)
Anil Kumar (Sr SDE, Amazon)
Stan Fan (Solution Architect, AWS)
Augusto Dias (Deliver Consultant, AWS)

title: What's new with OpenSearch: AI-native search, agents & observability
abstract: "The OpenSearch project has shipped its most transformative year ever. From agentic search with autonomous relevance tuning and persistent memory, to GPU-accelerated vector search with 58% throughput gains, to a reimagined observability stack with Prometheus and Apache Iceberg support, the 3.x release train delivers capabilities builders can use today. OpenSearch Ambassador Dotan Horovits and TSC Chair Andrew Ross walk you through what's new, what it means for your architecture, and how to put it to work, whether you're building RAG pipelines, deploying monitoring, or creating AI agents."
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Dotan Horovits (Sr. Developer Advocate, Amazon Web Services)
Andrew Ross (Principal Engineer, AWS)

title: Hugging Face on AWS: AI Model Deployment at Scale
abstract: AWS and Hugging Face collaborate on open source Deep Learning Containers, optimized inference frameworks, and Neuron integrations that make deploying community models production-ready. This session covers the open source stack - from Transformers library optimizations for Graviton and Trainium to TGI container contributions - that enables customers to serve Hugging Face models at 50% lower cost. Learn deployment patterns used by enterprises running open weight LLMs at millions of requests per day.
speakers: Saurav Mohanty (Technical Account Manager, Amazon)
Prajwal Nag Ramesh (Sr Technical Account Manager, AWS)

title: Building Production Graph Pipelines with Nodestream and Amazon Neptune
abstract: Nodestream is an open source declarative framework for building, maintaining, and analyzing graph data, built collaboratively by engineers at Intuit and AWS. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Nodestream connects data sources like Apache Kafka, APIs, and files to graph databases with automatic schema migrations and zero database-specific code. We'll dive into the Amazon Neptune plugin, discuss how declarative pipelines eliminate brittle ETL, and share lessons learned from real world customer scenarios. Bring your graph data challenges and we'll solve them live.
speakers: Kelvin Lawrence (Senior Principal Architect, AWS)
Taylor Riggan (Principal Graph Architect, Amazon Neptune, Amazon Web Services)

title: Kiro Crew: Architecture of an open source AI coding agent built on Kiro
abstract: Kiro Crew is an open source AI coding workspace built on Kiro CLI that grew from a side project to 39,000 users and nearly 500 contributors inside Amazon. Unlike single-session assistants, Kiro Crew combines multi-step task orchestration, tool-use planning, and a shared context layer for real engineering workflows. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through how Kiro Crew decomposes complex tasks, selects and chains tools, manages execution state, and integrates with existing developer environments. We'll discuss the design trade-offs that enabled rapid adoption and our journey to open source.

title: Bootstrapping GitOps on Amazon EKS with Argo CD, ACK, and kro
abstract: Deploying an application to Kubernetes is straightforward. Provisioning its AWS resources, IAM roles, policies, and supporting infrastructure is more complex. Separate infrastructure and application toolchains create fragmented workflows and increase the risk of drift. In this session, we'll build a GitOps platform using EKS Capabilities, Argo CD, AWS Controllers for Kubernetes (ACK), and kro. See how kro packages Kubernetes workloads and their AWS dependencies behind a single, self-service custom resource. Learn how Argo CD continuously reconciles the entire application stack from one Git repository. Finally, watch several microservices deploy, with their cloud resources provisioned and continuously managed alongside their workloads.

title: Powertools for agent DevOps: Debug reasoning, not just exceptions
abstract: Your agent returned the wrong answer — no exception, no alarm, it just reasoned poorly. Traditional monitoring catches crashes, not bad decisions. In this builder session, you'll use Powertools for AWS Lambda to build agent observability: Logger with log buffering to capture decision context only on failure, Tracer with annotations for confidence scores and tool selections, and Metrics tracking token cost and reasoning steps. Wire OTEL with Strands SDK for end-to-end traces across the agent loop. You leave with dashboards that answer "why did the agent decide this?" - not "did it crash?"

Andrea Amorosi (Senior AI Engineer, AWS)

title: Performance tuning for streaming ingestion with Apache Iceberg
abstract: Unlock real-time streaming into Apache Iceberg with advanced performance tuning. Learn how to optimize ingestion pipelines using Apache Kafka and Apache Flink for fraud detection, IoT monitoring, and real-time analytics. This session covers throughput optimization through partitioning, parallelism, write distribution, batching, and checkpoint tuning. Discover techniques to reduce small file issues with compaction, minimize write amplification with deduplication, and maintain low-latency ingestion at scale, turning raw streaming data into actionable insights with efficiency and reliability.

title: Expedite model loading times on Kubernetes using kro and ACK - from storage to GPU
abstract: LLM inference on Kubernetes is bottlenecked by loading multi-gigabyte model weights through the storage → network → CPU → PCIe → GPU path. In this chalk talk we benchmark four approaches to accelerating model delivery to GPU memory: SOCI for lazy-loading container image layers, s5cmd parallel downloads, Mountpoint for Amazon S3 CSI streaming, and Run.ai Model Streamer for direct S3-to-GPU pipelining. We walk through when each technique shines, how they compose together, and the tradeoffs platform teams face when optimizing inference cold starts on Amazon EKS. Learn how kro and ACK enable declarative provisioning of optimized storage pipelines, allowing platform teams to compose reusable stacks.
speakers: Ramesh Mathikumar (Principal Consultant, Amazon Web Services)
Kumudhan Cherarajan (Senior Delivery Consultant - Devops, Amazon Web Services)

title: Apache Iceberg V4: Fast commits, smart metadata, and portable tables
abstract: Apache Iceberg V4 is the biggest architectural evolution of the format, shifting from batch-first to real-time ready. Explore how single-file commits eliminate metadata bottlenecks for streaming ingestion, how Parquet-based metadata and redesigned content statistics accelerate query planning, and how relative paths make tables portable across regions and clouds without costly rewrites. We'll walk through what's changing under the hood and what it means for the way you design and operate lakehouses. Discover how V4 delivers the speed and flexibility modern lakehouses demand.

title: Reduce LLM inference costs up to 80% through caching with Valkey
abstract: LLM inference depends on limited GPU memory, and a KV cache lets agentic AI applications reuse computed intermediate states across prompts to reduce latency and costs. In this talk, we explain how KV caching works and walk through a production architecture using Valkey as a high-performance datastore, LMCache for KV reuse at inference, and llm-d for cache-aware routing. You will leave with practical implementation guidance and a framework for evaluating when a KV caching tier is the right choice to reduce costs for your AI applications.
speakers: Kevin McGehee (Principal Software Engineer, Amazon)
Jeff Duffy (Product Manager, Amazon ElastiCache, Amazon Web Services)

title: Cut token costs by 50%: Building context efficient agents with Strands
abstract: AI agents degrade as conversations exceed context windows. You need retrieval strategies, compression policies, and adaptive storage backends. This code talk covers the three-tier context cache hierarchy of AWS's open source Strands Agents SDK. We'll discuss context management as composable primitives with extension points for custom backends, compression, and retrieval. We'll explore trade-offs between framework and agent-controlled context, how plugins compose without coupling, and where abstractions break under extreme workloads. For developers building or extending agent frameworks.

title: Kubernetes-native agentic AI on Amazon EKS with open source primitives
abstract: Production agentic AI needs a scalable runtime, governed LLM access, persistent memory, observability, tool discovery, and secure code isolation. In this workshop you'll build all six on Amazon EKS using native Kubernetes primitives and open source projects. Tackle all six end-to-end or take individual modules home. Deploy LiteLLM as a multi-model gateway, Mem0 for user-scoped memory, Langfuse for observability into reasoning and tool calls, an MCP registry for tool discovery, and sandboxes for hardware-level code isolation. title: Connect agents across frameworks live using the A2A open protocol
abstract: Agents built on different frameworks need to talk to each other. In this session we will build two agents on Strands and LangGraph, then wire them together using the A2A protocol hosted at the Linux Foundation. You will see the full handshake: AgentCard publication for discovery, task negotiation, streaming artifact exchange, and multi-turn collaboration between agents that share nothing except the protocol. We will deploy both sides on AgentCore Runtime and demonstrate cross-framework interoperability working live. You will leave with the patterns to make any framework's agents collaborate over a standard wire.

title: Turn PQC readiness into the trust story your board needs
abstract: Organizations planning post-quantum cryptography (PQC) migrations face the same three questions: where do I start my migration plan, which workloads do I prioritize, and how do I get buy-in from leadership? See how DXC built a cryptographic asset intelligence and orchestration platform on AWS to discover and correlate assets across AWS and enterprise PKI, automate certificate lifecycles, and assess post-quantum readiness. We will demystify the present state and future trajectory of PQ authentication. We discuss the updated CNSA 2.0 dates when RSA and EC will no longer satisfy authentication requirements and the uncertainty around PQ public certificate formats and Merkle Trees in non-browser scenarios.

title: Intent-Based Access Control for AI Agents that Actually Do Things (sponsored by WorkOS)
abstract: Agent permissions offer two bad options: approve every action manually, or skip permissions and trust the prompt. Auto-approve protects your laptop; it won't stop an agent from deleting a thousand CRM records. Roles and scopes suit static users, not agents whose next action depends on the last prompt. This session introduces Intent-Based Access Control (IBAC), where the agent's intent, not a pre-assigned role, is the unit of permission. WorkOS built Airlock on it: mission-bound tokens, every call evaluated against intent, decisions resolving to allow, deny, or escalate. Live demo across Gmail and Linear, including a blocked exfiltration and real-time human approval. This presentation is brought to you by WorkOS, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater

But with this level of autonomy, zero-day vulnerabilities can propagate across your stack faster than ever. Staying resilient requires shifting security directly into the agent’s execution loop. Through live demos and an interview with Capita CISO, Luke Beeson, on their rapid AWS adoption, discover how to embed guardrails directly into agentic IDEs. Learn to catch vulnerabilities and overscoped tool permissions as code is written, and walk away with a battle-tested framework to ship agentic AI at full velocity on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Wiz, an AWS Partner.

FanDuel handled adjustments by hand for years, until attackers started moving faster than the tuning backlog. Join FanDuel and Datadog to see detection rebuilt around automation: SIEM logic as code, orchestrated enrichment and triage, vulnerability workflows in the same pipeline. Attendees will leave with practical patterns for scaling detection engineering, reducing analyst toil, and knowing where AI helps and where it creates new work. title: Agents can delete your data lake. Can you recover it? (sponsored by Rubrik)
abstract: AI is multiplying the identities and agents that can change your AWS data. One over-scoped role or runaway agent can delete or overwrite the data your models depend on, in an S3 lake or Iceberg lakehouse. Replication copies a bad write, versioning is often off. How do you recover without a valid backup? Learn where recovery breaks across S3, Glue Data Catalog, S3 Tables, and databases and pipelines around them, then how Rubrik recovers petabytes in hours, restoring only what changed, critical data first, within your RTO. Resilience spans your estate. Hear how TGS built a ransomware-resilient platform with Rubrik. This presentation is brought to you by Rubrik, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
