Jérôme Cousin (VP Enterprise IT, TGS)

title: Outpace AI attacks: Auto-recover AWS apps at machine speed with Rubrik. (sponsored by Rubrik)
abstract: Abstract: AI-driven attacks move at machine speed, and your AWS application is an interconnected system of code, infrastructure and data. Rebuilding by hand is a nightmare, if it’s even possible. Join us to see how an AI attack unfolds, and how Rubrik brings your business back by recovering the whole application in one automated motion. Rubrik discovers your application's dependencies, flags structural drift before it becomes an incident, and recovers it all together. Hear how Just Eat is moving from manual to validated, isolated recovery on AWS. Outpace AI-speed attacks with machine-speed recovery: less downtime, no manual rebuilds. This presentation is brought to you by Rubrik, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Kalyan Akella (Distinguished Engineer, Rubrik Inc.)

title: Reinvent cloud security with runtime and AI (sponsored by Upwind)
abstract: This session explores the evolution of cloud security and why traditional approaches fall short in the era of ephemeral compute and agentic AI. While legacy CloudSec relied on static scanning for visibility, today’s environments are dynamic, real-time, and increasingly autonomous, resulting in blind spots, excessive noise, and incomplete protection. We’ll examine how AI-driven and hybrid cloud architectures introduce new challenges across visibility, protection, and validation, from cross-provider gaps to real-time attack vectors and model vulnerabilities. To address this, Cloud and AI security must move beyond static analysis to a unified, runtime-driven approach. By continuously monitoring activity across the environment and embedding security throughout the SDLC, including production, organizations gain real-time context, better prioritization, and proactive threat mitigation. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

title: Go Hack Yourself. With AI. (sponsored by Horizon3.ai)
abstract: Defenders often drown in noise while attackers move at machine speed. To truly secure your environment, you must adopt an attacker’s perspective. Horizon3 CEO Snehal Antani shares insights from 250,000+ autonomous pentests across 6,000+ environments, demonstrating how AI hackers find exploitable paths that scanners miss, such as credential theft and domain compromise without CVEs. You’ll learn why vulnerable doesn’t mean exploitable, how to validate controls through a Hack-Fix-Verify loop, and where AI belongs in offense and defense: tool for scale and proof, not a black box. This presentation is brought to you by Horizon3.ai, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater

title: Building Trust into Agentic AI on AWS in the Age of Autonomous Agents (sponsored by Check Point)
abstract: AI agents are evolving from assistants into autonomous systems that call APIs and take actions on behalf of users. Traditional perimeter controls aren't enough; threats now emerge from prompt injection, excessive permissions, and unmonitored tool use. In this session, we'll show how Check Point's AI security intelligence integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to enforce real-time guardrails at the agent runtime layer inspecting intent, validating actions, and preventing policy violations before they execute. Walk away with a practical framework for securing agentic AI on AWS with Check Point. This presentation is brought to you by Check Point, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Dhanil Parwani (Principal Partner Solutions Architect, Networking and AI Security, AWS)
Shahar Tal (Head of Agentic Security Innovation, Check Point)

title: Extend AWS WAF to the APIs your AI agents call (sponsored by Wallarm)
abstract: Network and edge controls stop the traffic patterns they were built to recognize. AI agents introduce a different pattern: authenticated requests, at machine speed, against business logic rather than known vulnerabilities. Teams running AWS WAF often find these requests pass inspection because nothing about them is malformed. In this session, examine how agent-driven traffic reaches APIs, which risks fall outside signature and rate-based inspection, and what an additive API security layer contributes. Learn how teams instrument existing AWS WAF deployments for API-level visibility, apply real-time redaction to sensitive data in responses, and enforce without adding latency. This presentation is brought to you by Wallarm, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Tim Erlin (VP Product, Wallarm)

title: When agentic AI meets critical infrastructure (sponsored by IBM)
abstract: Agentic AI can transform how utilities serve customers, manage infrastructure and respond to operational events. Join IBM Consulting and industry leaders to see how organizations are putting agentic AI to work on AWS across complex operational workflows. Through real client stories, explore how modern platforms, trusted data and secure software foundations help teams improve service, strengthen resilience and move AI into production with confidence. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater

title: Move AI agents from prototype to production with 1Password (sponsored by 1Password)
abstract: Giving an AI agent real work means connecting it to real systems without exposing their credentials. For developers, platform engineers, and security teams, this lightning talk demonstrates how 1Password, AWS Strands Box with AWS Credentials Daemon can give sandboxed agents access to the services they need while keeping secrets outside the agent. We’ll show how developers connect credentials managed in 1Password, how Box injects them into permitted requests, and how local policies restrict what the agent can do. We’ll also explore the path to centrally managed authorization, approvals, and time-limited access across local and cloud deployments. This presentation is brought to you by 1Password, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: Agentic AI Meets ‘Human-Guided-Autonomy’ (sponsored by Terra)
abstract: AI is accelerating how fast code ships and how fast attackers find exploitable weaknesses, and annual pentests cannot keep pace. This session looks at what it takes to make security validation genuinely continuous rather than just more frequent, tracking what changed instead of retesting everything from scratch. Self-driving cars, robotic surgery, and other sensitive actions all became viable the same way: not by removing the human, but by defining exactly which actions the machine takes on its own and which ones need a hand on the controls. This talk will cover the delegate balance between autonomy, safety and control in Offensive Security. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater

title: Securing the AI-Native Cloud (sponsored by Upwind)
abstract: In this session, we will demonstrate how AI is redefining cloud security by moving beyond static posture management to real-time, context-aware protection. The session will showcase how organizations can gain continuous visibility across their environments and respond to threats as they emerge. Attendees will see how AI-driven analysis of runtime behavior enables faster detection of anomalies, prioritization of real risks, and automated response across dynamic, multi-cloud infrastructures. The session will highlight how security teams can reduce noise, strengthen security processes, and proactively respond to threats before they escalate. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

title: From Confirmed Exploit to AWS WAF Rule in Minutes (sponsored by Terra)
abstract: A confirmed exploit still needs a code fix, and that fix often takes days or weeks. The exploit path stays open the whole time. This session shows how Terra Security turns a validated pentest finding into a scoped virtual patch inside the application's existing AWS WAF: matched to the specific attack, not a site-wide block, activated by a human on your team, and checked against both the exploit and normal traffic before you trust it. You will leave with a clear picture of how the integration works and a model for closing the gap between proof and fix without breaking the app you are protecting. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Spencer Chin (Senior Director of Solutions Engineering, Terra Security)

title: Continuous Attack Chains Across Every Surface (sponsored by Terra)
abstract: Most security tools score vulnerabilities in isolation, but attackers do not think in isolation. This session shows how Terra continuously chains signals into real attack paths across web applications, APIs, AI systems, and network infrastructure using agentic AI, the same way a human adversary would pivot from one weak point to the next. Every proposed chain is validated by an expert human pentester before it becomes a finding, turning a pile of low severity noise into a small number of confirmed, exploitable risks. Learn how continuous, cross surface attack chaining changes what a security team should actually prioritize first. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Ofek Haviv (AI Security Researcher, Terra Security)

title: Inside the Architecture: Building Secure AI Applications on AWS (sponsored by TrendAI™)
abstract: AI is rapidly moving from experimentation to production, creating new challenges for developers, architects, and security teams. In this technical session, explore the real-world architectures enterprises use to build and secure AI applications on AWS. Learn how organizations leverage Amazon Bedrock, EKS, ECS, Security Lake, CloudTrail, and cloud-native automation to protect AI workloads, monitor risk across multi-account environments, and streamline security operations. Through practical deployment patterns and lessons learned from large-scale AWS environments, discover how to build AI applications that are secure, scalable, and production-ready. The session draws on deployment patterns described for TrendAI Vision One on AWS, including AI workload protection, cloud telemetry integration, and AWS-native architecture approaches. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.

title: One Control to Rule Them All: Guardrail Automation for Every Identity (sponsored by Sonrai Security)
abstract: Separate guardrails for humans, machine identities, and AI agents get messy, and rewriting every IAM policy takes forever. SCPs deployed at scope are easy to write. What follows is not. Nobody can say what a policy will break, so it never deploys. Someone gets blocked and the fix becomes a two hour hunt. The tenth control behaves nothing like the first. New accounts inherit none of it. This lightning talk answers all four using only AWS Organizations, SCPs, and RCPs. See how usage data makes a default deny safe, how access returns in seconds, and how least privilege holds. This presentation is brought to you by Sonrai Security, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Ian Weyenberg (Sr. Mgr Cloud Architecture, NetDocuments)

title: Smoking on Airplanes: Rethinking How Enterprises Trust Software (sponsored by Glow)
abstract: Every day, employees install browser extensions, IDE plugins, and open-source packages with powerful access to corporate devices, code, credentials, and data. AI coding agents are accelerating this practice by recommending and installing software to complete tasks. Yet much of it enters the enterprise without comprehensive security review. We've normalized a practice that may someday seem as unthinkable as smoking on airplanes. In this session, we'll expose hidden risks in plugin and package ecosystems, show why traditional application controls miss this rapidly changing software layer, and explore what security teams must rethink as AI makes software adoption faster and increasingly autonomous. This presentation is brought to you by Glow, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: SAST Is Dead: Program Analysis for AI Agents (sponsored by Semgrep)
abstract: LLMs didn't kill security testing, they exposed tools that guess at context they don't have. This talk explains what we learned by reinventing program analysis for new end users: builders and agents. We had to develop benchmarks and add determinism with program slicing to better control costs and deliver the optimal price per true vulnerability detected. This presentation is brought to you by Semgrep, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: From Signals to Action for Sempra: AI-Powered Cybersecurity on AWS (sponsored by Accenture)
abstract: AI is reshaping cybersecurity, but security teams must act faster without adding complexity. Sempra Energy, AWS, and Accenture deployed Accenture Cyber.AI on AWS to create a unified view of cyber risk and identify the highest-priority actions across the enterprise. Learn how the team integrated existing security investments, addressed governance and architecture requirements, and operationalized AI-driven risk management. Speakers will share key design decisions, implementation lessons, and practical guidance for using AI to improve cyber resilience, strengthen security operations, and maintain control of data and infrastructure in cloud environments. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: JONATHAN HOLT (Enterprise Technology Architecture Science Associate Director, Accenture)
Ben Gordon (SVP, CIO & CDO, Sempra Energy)

title: Regulation to Innovation: A Global Enterprise Guide to Digital Sovereignty (sponsored by Accenture)
abstract: Digital sovereignty is a growing priority for global enterprises operating across Europe as they navigate regulatory requirements, geopolitical uncertainty, and increasing demand for cloud and AI innovation. Organizations must balance data residency, compliance, resilience, and business agility without slowing transformation. Learn how leading enterprises are using AWS European Sovereign Cloud as part of a broader cloud strategy to meet sovereignty requirements while continuing to adopt modern cloud services and AI. Accenture will share practical approaches to assessing sovereignty needs, designing compliant architectures, and integrating sovereign cloud capabilities into enterprise environments. Attendees will leave with actionable guidance for balancing trust, resilience, compliance, and innovation at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Emanuele Baldassarre (Managing Director, Accenture)

title: Who’s Pulling the Strings? Securing GitHub from Rogue AI Agents (sponsored by Zscaler)
abstract: With the rise of autonomous AI agents like Devin, Cursor, and Amazon Q, the security boundary has shifted from the network perimeter directly to the developer's workspace. These AI tools and automated integration pipelines establish dynamic, encrypted connections straight to GitHub, third-party repositories, and cloud workloads—creating blind spots that legacy firewalls cannot see. Join us as we map out this highly interconnected AI developer ecosystem and showcase why traditional security fails. We will share a unified, proxy-based Zero Trust architecture that inspects encrypted developer traffic, secures access to critical repositories, and isolates untrusted AI actions. You’ll leave with an actionable blueprint to protect your code, APIs, and AI integrations while maintaining peak developer velocity. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Mrigank Singh (Sr. Director, Product Management, ZScaler Inc.)

title: Build Secure AI Agents on AWS: XAA, Bedrock AgentCore and the AI Blueprint (sponsored by Okta)
abstract: Building AI agents is easy, but securing enterprise data access without slowing development is hard. Teams often rely on static, over-privileged credentials, creating major security risks. But there’s a solution. This session explores how to secure agentic workflows with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Okta. We’ll introduce the Blueprint Alliance, of which AWS and Okta are founding members, and cover how standards like Cross App Access (XAA) and SCIM for Agents transform AI identity. You'll learn how replacing static keys with dynamic, delegated permissions enables real-time policy evaluation at every tool call, empowering developers to build scalable, trusted AI agents that operate strictly within verified boundaries. This presentation is brought to you by Okta, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Wayne Smiley (Principal Solutions Architect, Okta)
Steven Tamm (SVP, Okta)

title: Ghost agents: Governing ephemeral AI & machine access in real-time (sponsored by SailPoint)
abstract: Ephemeral AI agents and cloud workloads spin up, access resources, and vanish in minutes, never landing in traditional identity registries. How do you govern what you can’t track? The answer lies in securing the non-human identities (NHIs) they leave behind. Join SailPoint for a live demo on governing ephemeral agent behavior. We’ll show you how to untangle NHI ownership, expose over-privileged access, and establish real-time governance over transient machine identities before they expose your cloud. Walk away with a blueprint to manage non-human access risk at cloud scale. This is clarity you can act on. This presentation is brought to you by SailPoint, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater
speakers: Stephen Cortese (Principal Agentic Technologist, SailPoint)

title: EU operational autonomy in action: AWS European Sovereign Cloud
abstract: The AWS European Sovereign Cloud is built on fully isolated infrastructure within the EU, operated exclusively by EU-resident staff, with no access from outside Europe. In this lightning talk, learn from the AWS European Sovereign Cloud Managed Operations team what independent operations means in practice and how it works day to day.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Zoltan Albrecht (Director ESC Managed Operations, AWS)

title: Demystifying AWS KMS authorization: building key policies that scale
abstract: Authorization to your key involves a mix of key policies, IAM policies, grants, SCPs, and VPC endpoint policies — each playing a distinct role in access decisions. This talk demystifies how these policies are evaluated in the context of AWS KMS, then applies that understanding to create a scalable policy design. You'll learn about ABAC, using grants for dynamic delegation, and AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) which offers a simpler yet scalable way to share keys in your organization. You'll leave with the mental model to predict outcomes and reusable patterns that grow with your organization.
speakers: Kevin Kevin (Sr. Product Manager - Technical, AWS)
Patrick Palmer (Principal Security Specialist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Can You Stop ALTERED SPIDER? A Live AWS Cloud Breach Challenge (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
abstract: The breach is underway. Watch CrowdStrike Experts put cloud detection and response into action during a live, audience-driven investigation of a simulated AWS intrusion. They will uncover evidence, determine the next move, and capture flags hidden across identities, workloads, and cloud activity. Get briefed on cloud-focused adversary ALTERED SPIDER, then connect the clues, contain the threat, and stop the attack. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Allie Barnes (Sr. Technical Marketing Manager, Cloud Security, CrowdStrike)
Jay Flora (Sr.Technical Marketing Manager, CrowdStrike)

title: Secure by design: the AWS foundation for your AI applications
abstract: As organizations put AI and agents into production, leaders need confidence that their cloud provider is secure by design. This session explains how AWS foundational security extends into AI services and which AI security capabilities build on that foundation. You see the controls customers use to protect their most critical AI workloads.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Maitreya Ranganath (Principal Security Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc)
Josh Du Lac (Enterprise Security Strategist, AWS)

title: Automate and Scale Cloud Operations with Purpose-Built AI Agents (sponsored by Datadog)
abstract: Engineering teams lose time correlating telemetry, triaging alerts, investigating threats, and turning findings into fixes. This session explores how Datadog’s purpose-built AI agents can reduce that operational burden by applying organizational context and production telemetry to focused developer, SRE, and security workflows. Using the AWS Well-Architected Framework, we’ll examine where agents can improve operational excellence, reliability, security, performance efficiency, and cost optimization. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater

title: Close the gap between alert and resolution without growing your security team
abstract: For most security teams, the delay sits in manual triage and tool switching after an alert. This chalk talk covers the newest AWS detection and response capabilities, including enhanced threat detection, automated vulnerability management, and AI-assisted security operations, and how they shorten the time between finding a risk and resolving it. We work through how to connect AWS security services across AWS and your other clouds so the team you already have can resolve findings faster.
speakers: Ryan Holland (Sr Manager, GuardDuty, AWS)
Himanshu Verma (Worldwide Security Specialist Leader, AWS)

title: Close the gap between alert and resolution without growing your security team
abstract: For most security teams, the delay sits in manual triage and tool switching after an alert. This chalk talk covers the newest AWS detection and response capabilities, including enhanced threat detection, automated vulnerability management, and AI-assisted security operations, and how they shorten the time between finding a risk and resolving it. We work through how to connect AWS security services across AWS and your other clouds so the team you already have can resolve findings faster.
speakers: Himanshu Verma (Worldwide Security Specialist Leader, AWS)
Ryan Holland (Sr Manager, GuardDuty, AWS)

title: Governance foundations for AI workloads that grow into autonomous agents
abstract: Agentic workloads are reaching production, and governance has to keep up without slowing teams down. This session shows how to build a governance foundation for AI with AWS Control Tower, AWS Config, AWS Organizations, and automatic evidence collection, then extend it to autonomous agents. You apply preventive and detective controls to Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker, automate compliance evidence, and map controls to frameworks such as ISO 42001. The same controls hold whether the workload is a single model call or a fleet of agents acting on their own.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Rodolfo Brenes (Principal WW Security Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)
Nivas Durairaj (WW Governance Specialist, AWS)

title: Network security innovations for agentic workloads
abstract: AI agents plan and execute actions autonomously, at machine speed, with real-world consequences. Unlike traditional automation that follows pre-defined network paths, agent traffic is non-deterministic, calling different APIs and chaining different services each time it runs. In this session, we cover the network security capabilities AWS has built for this shift. You'll see how to inspect and control autonomous traffic at every layer, from DNS resolution to application-layer filtering, enforce least-privilege connectivity for agents, and detect anomalous behavior in machine-to-machine communication.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Sofía Aluma (WW Security Network Security GTM Lead, AWS)
Brandon Carroll (Senior Security PMM, AWS Village - Network Security)

title: Find and Fix Exploitable Code at Machine Speed with AWS Continuum
abstract: In this hands-on builders' session, you integrate AWS Continuum into your development workflow, where a frontier agent scans and remediates code before it leaves your IDE. Write code with intentional vulnerabilities, run context-aware code reviews that go beyond pattern matching, review prioritized findings with structured evidence, and use Kiro to fix issues in real time. Leave with three controls you can reuse: a pre-commit scan, a pull request gate, and a context-aware pentest you can revalidate.
speakers: Shweta Shrestha Thapa (Senior Security Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Lily Ashidam (Security Solutions Architect, AWS)
Poornima Venkatesan (Senior Security Consultant, AWS)
Kafayat Adeyemi (Senior Security Services SA, AWS)
Meriem SMACHE (Security Specialist Solution Architect, AWS)

title: Malware Protection: hands-on detection and response for malicious files
abstract: In this one-hour builder session, get hands-on with the core capabilities of Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection. Configure on-demand S3 scanning using the SendObjectMalwareScan API, set up automated EBS volume scanning for EC2 instances, and build event-driven response pipelines that quarantine infected objects before they spread. Walk through real malware samples triggering findings, interpret scan results, and integrate with Security Hub for centralized visibility. Leave with a working malware detection and response workflow deployed in your own account.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Omner Barajas (Security Specialist SA, AWS)
Anthony Harvey (Sr. Security Specialist SA, AWS)
Fabian Serrano Morales (Security Solutions Architect, AWS)
Shay Grinberg (Product, AWS)
Pedro Gadelha (Security Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Build your controls strategy org-wide to accelerate innovation
abstract: AWS Organizations policies drive governance through native service integrations. In this session, explore service control policies and resource control policies for data perimeters. Use declarative policies to enforce resource configurations, such as Amazon S3 public access restrictions, and centralize AWS Security Hub settings org-wide. Deploy AWS Config organizational rules and conformance packs for continuous compliance, leverage multi-party approval, enforce best practices via the AWS Control Tower controls catalog, and explore automated compliance assessments. Leave with a governance architecture driven by policy integrations.
speakers: Oscar Diaz Cordovez (Sr Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build your controls strategy org-wide to accelerate innovation
abstract: AWS Organizations policies drive governance through native service integrations. In this session, explore service control policies and resource control policies for data perimeters. Use declarative policies to enforce resource configurations, such as Amazon S3 public access restrictions, and centralize AWS Security Hub settings org-wide. Deploy AWS Config organizational rules and conformance packs for continuous compliance, leverage multi-party approval, enforce best practices via the AWS Control Tower controls catalog, and explore automated compliance assessments. Leave with a governance architecture driven by policy integrations.
speakers: Oscar Diaz Cordovez (Sr Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: How SCHUFA strengthened security operations with AWS Security Hub
abstract: Across complex cloud environments, security teams must sift through a growing volume of signals to prioritize the risks that matter most. AWS Security Hub correlates these signals across AWS and multicloud environments to surface critical attack paths and help you respond at scale. Hear firsthand from SCHUFA, Germany's main credit scoring agency, on how they adopted Security Hub to streamline security operations under strict regulatory requirements. We'll also dive into the latest capabilities, including multicloud visibility, enhanced risk correlation, AI-powered detections, and visibility into AI workloads.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Scott Ward (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build a KMS key lifecycle dashboard with usage and cost insights
abstract: Determining which KMS keys are actively in use and which can be safely retired has historically required manual CloudTrail log analysis, and meanwhile, unused keys accumulate as operational clutter. In this hands-on builders session, you'll use the GetKeyLastUsage API to identify which keys are protecting production workloads and which are candidates for retirement. You'll configure policy conditions that prevent accidental deletion of active keys, and build a Amazon Quick dashboard that surfaces usage and cost optimization opportunities across accounts. You leave with a working multi-account key lifecycle solution you can recreate in your organization.
speakers: Jeremy Stieglitz (GM AWS Digital Asset Vault (DAV), AWS)
Tobias Nickl (Delivery Consultant - Security, AWS)
Alex Goff (UKI Area Security Lead, AWS)
Svenja Moehring (Area Security Ldr, DEU Central, Amazon Web Services)
Jonas Buecker (Engagement Security Consultant, Amazon)

abstract: Determining which KMS keys are actively in use and which can be safely retired has historically required manual CloudTrail log analysis, and meanwhile, unused keys accumulate as operational clutter. In this hands-on builders session, you'll use the GetKeyLastUsage API to identify which keys are protecting production workloads and which are candidates for retirement. You'll configure policy conditions that prevent accidental deletion of active keys, and build a Amazon Quick dashboard that surfaces usage and cost optimization opportunities across accounts. You leave with a working multi-account key lifecycle solution you can recreate in your organization.

Jeremy Stieglitz (GM AWS Digital Asset Vault (DAV), AWS)
Jonas Buecker (Engagement Security Consultant, Amazon)
Svenja Moehring (Area Security Ldr, DEU Central, Amazon Web Services)
Tobias Nickl (Delivery Consultant - Security, AWS)

title: Network firewall deployment without the guesswork: codify, deploy, done.
abstract: In this workshop, you deploy AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall into a realistic multi-VPC environment using reusable Terraform modules. You start by adding egress and east-west traffic inspection, then get hands-on with recent launches including container-aware rules, domain category filtering for visibility into AI traffic, and managed threat intelligence. You leave with reusable patterns for adding network traffic inspection to your own infrastructure.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Pål-Magnus Slåtto (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Lawton Pittenger (WW Network Security Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
David Fowler (Principal EAE, Amazon Web Services)
Preetkumar Shah (Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Network firewall deployment without the guesswork: codify, deploy, done
abstract: Level up your firewall policy operations at scale in this hands-on workshop. Learn to integrate AWS Network Firewall into an existing AWS environment using Terraform. Starting with a realistic multi-VPC setup with AWS Transit Gateway, you will deploy Network Firewall and configure routing, inspection, and logging in minutes using reusable modules. You will then implement the latest Network Firewall features such as web category filtering, JA4 fingerprinting, and EventBridge automation. By the end of this session you will have both practical experience adding Network Firewall to existing environments and reusable patterns ready for your own infrastructure.
speakers: Pål-Magnus Slåtto (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Lawton Pittenger (WW Network Security Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
David Fowler (Principal EAE, Amazon Web Services)
Preetkumar Shah (Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Building production-ready agents securely: lessons from AWS at scale
abstract: Most AI agent demos work on stage but break in production. Real enterprise agents need multi-layer guardrails, tenant identity isolation, graceful degradation, and continuous evaluation. In this code talk, we share patterns from shipping two production security agent systems on AWS: one that investigates incidents across customer accounts, and one that helps security practitioners author threat detections. We cover practices that any team can adopt such as prompt injection defense, tenant-scoped sessions, circuit breakers, observability, and eval-driven improvement.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Hardik Thakkar (Sr. Security Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Max Tybar (Security Engineer, AWS)

title: Closing the loop: using frontier agents for continuous governance
abstract: Wire two AWS frontier agents into an automated find-and-fix security loop aligned to the Well-Architected Framework. AWS Security Agent pen-tests a web application and flags a privilege-escalation vulnerability. You author a DevOps Agent skill that queries findings through AWS Continuum MCP Server on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, correlating the operational symptom to the vulnerability in your codebase and generating a GitLab merge request, with human approval at every gate. Trigger the exploit, approve the fix, watch AWS Continuum revalidate it closed, and update your pipeline to block similar vulnerabilities before they reach customers. Automated detection, investigation, remediation, verification, and ongoing prevention closes the loop and provides continuous governance.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Ryan Dsouza (Principal Solutions Architect, AMAZON)
Peter Grainger (Senior Technical Account Manager, AWS)
Emir Ayar (Sr. AI Architect, AWS)
Charles Roberts (Senior Delivery Consultant, Amazon Web Services)
Cameron Smith (Sr. Security Engineer, FDE, AWS Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE))

title: Use AWS Continuum to move from annual pentesting to continuous security
abstract: AI coding tools can make developers 10–20x more productive and yet many organizations may only be able to pentest critical apps once a year. The rest need to go untested entirely. In this builders' session, use AWS Security Agent (now part of Continuum) to run an on-demand penetration test against a live application. You'll triage findings by exploitability, validate real-world impact, and apply automated code remediations. Leave with prescriptive next steps to scan your own applications using a frontier AI agent that secures workloads from design through deployment. You must bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Jeremy Schiefer (Pr. Security SA, AWS)
Cameron Smith (Sr. Security Engineer, FDE, AWS Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE))

title: Hands-on with the AWS Network Firewall proxy for secure egress
abstract: AWS Network Firewall now gives you the flexibility to act as an explicit forward proxy for outbound traffic on the firewall you already run. Clients connect to it directly by its proxy FQDN, so no route-table changes are required. The proxy attaches to a NAT gateway and terminates each client connection, letting one firewall consolidate egress for multiple VPCs regardless of overlapping CIDRs. In this builders session you'll get hands-on deploying the proxy and building layered egress controls, up to and including outbound TLS inspection. You'll leave knowing when and how to use the firewall proxy to centralize and enforce egress controls for private workloads.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Anvesh Koganti (Specialist SA, Networking, Amazon Web Services)
Rahi Patel (Technical Account Manager, Amazon)
Preetkumar Shah (Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Geoff Sweet (Sr Security Specialist SA, Amazon, Inc.)
Hunter Chilcote (Security Services SA, AWS)

title: Hands-on Network Defense with AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 DNS Firewall
abstract: In this workshop, you'll build a comprehensive network security architecture using AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall. You'll configure egress and VPC-to-VPC traffic inspection, IDS/IPS filtering, and container-aware rules for dynamic workload protection. Explore DNS-layer defenses, including DNS tunneling detection, and gain visibility into AI service traffic through domain category filtering. Through real-world scenarios, you'll cover the most common use cases and leave knowing how these services work together to defend your network. This workshop is for security and network engineers who are comfortable with Amazon VPC networking and AWS Transit Gateway.
speakers: Lawton Pittenger (WW Network Security Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Brian Westmoreland (Sr. Delivery Consultant - CIA, AWS)

title: Advanced AWS network security: defending against emerging threats
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, master AWS network security techniques using AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall. Gain practical experience configuring URL category filtering to detect unauthorized AI service usage, and explore recent feature improvements for container workload protection and advanced DNS-layer defenses. Through real-world scenarios, you'll implement IDS/IPS filtering, east-west traffic controls, and domain-based policies using fully managed AWS services. Leave equipped to build resilient network defenses that address both traditional and emerging threats.
speakers: Lawton Pittenger (WW Network Security Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Brian Westmoreland (Sr. Delivery Consultant - CIA, AWS)

title: Crypto escape room: race to migrate to quantum resistance
abstract: The migration to post-quantum cryptography is underway and here's a chance to hone your skills. In this gamified builders' session, each team races a countdown clock through different cryptographic migration challenges: TLS endpoint migration, ML-DSA key for code signing, quantum ready PKI, and an audit of your PQ posture. Teams complete quests using the AWS Key Management Service (KMS), AWS Private Certificate Authority, and AWS Secrets Manager services. A live leaderboard tracks progress across teams. Leave with new skills and the confidence to build quantum-resistant cryptographic infrastructure.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Jay Viera (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Phoebe Sorkin (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Arun Krishnaswamy (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Shankar Rajagopalan (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: Cryptographic computing on AWS: homomorphic encryption in practice
abstract: What if you need to process sensitive data without exposing it to the system performing the computation? In this hands-on workshop, use fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) to evaluate selected ML models while inputs remain encrypted and only the data owner decrypts the results. Work through encrypted inference for medical images, spam messages, and financial transactions in Amazon SageMaker Studio, then deploy a validated FHE model bundle to an AWS Lambda serving path. Examine the architecture, trust boundaries, performance constraints, and operational trade-offs that determine where FHE is practical today. Leave with concrete AWS patterns for privacy-sensitive and regulated workloads.
speakers: Jonathan Herzog (Principal Security Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Ruben Merz (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Preventing unintended access: a practical guide to data perimeter controls
abstract: Are you looking to prevent unintended access to your data and mitigate data exposure risks? This hands-on session demonstrates how data perimeter controls implemented through service control policies (SCPs), resource control policies (RCPs), and VPC endpoint policies help keep corporate data within organizational boundaries. You'll build data perimeter policies for real-life security scenarios and validate their effectiveness using an assessment tool. By the end, you'll have practical knowledge on how to help ensure only trusted identities access trusted resources from expected networks.
speakers: Sowjanya Rajavaram (Sr PMT-ES, AWS)
Nitin Kulkarni (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Manas Chhabra (Software Development Manager, AWS)
Vaibhav Chowla (Sr. PMT, Amazon Web Services)

title: Securing AI coding agents: defense in depth across the development lifecycle
abstract: AI coding agents optimise for task completion, not security, generating code and PRs faster than humans can review. This chalk talk presents a defense-in-depth framework spanning five pillars - pre-generation, authoring, PR, pipeline, and deployment - with three lines of defense at each: deterministic controls, AI screening, and human judgment. We cover author-time techniques (steering, specs, scoped MCP, hooks) and build-time gates (SAST, SCA, IaC scanning, AI-assisted review, approval) using Kiro, AWS Security Agent, CodePipeline and more. Leave with a layered model you can apply on Monday.
speakers: Mac Stevens (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Alex Waddell (Principal Security Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)

title: Securing AI coding agents: defense in depth across the development lifecycle
abstract: AI coding agents optimise for task completion, not security, generating code and PRs faster than humans can review. This chalk talk presents a defense-in-depth framework spanning five pillars - pre-generation, authoring, PR, pipeline, and deployment - with three lines of defense at each: deterministic controls, AI screening, and human judgment. We cover author-time techniques (steering, specs, scoped MCP, hooks) and build-time gates (SAST, SCA, IaC scanning, AI-assisted review, approval) using Kiro, AWS Security Agent, CodePipeline and more. title: Investigating Threats to AI: Incident Response to Compromised AI Workloads
abstract: As organizations adopt generative AI on AWS, security teams need to extend their investigation capabilities into the AI layer. In this hands-on workshop, participants work through a realistic multi-phase incident — tracing a compromised credential from initial exposure through privilege escalation into Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases and AI agents. Using GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, and Athena, you'll reconstruct the full attack chain and walk away with the skills to detect, investigate, and respond when threat actors pivot from traditional cloud resources into generative AI workloads.
speakers: Kyle Shields (Security Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Steve de Vera (Senior Security Engineer, AWS)

title: Assume breach, prove recovery: a ransomware resilience workshop
abstract: Most organizations have backups. Few can prove clean recovery after ransomware, and regulators now demand exactly that proof. In this hands-on workshop, you configure a resilient backup architecture on AWS using vaults and immutable storage. You then experience a simulated ransomware event, validate that your recovery infrastructure held, restore to an isolated clean room environment, and scan recovered resources for attacker persistence using GuardDuty Malware Protection. You leave with a recovery validation approach and an understanding of why least privilege, vault lock, and validation are non-negotiable.
speakers: Danny Wright (Principal Technical Account Manager, AWS)
Christopher Strug (Senior Technical Account Manager, Amazon)

title: Assume breach, prove recovery: a ransomware resilience workshop
abstract: Most organizations have backups. Few can prove clean recovery after ransomware, and regulators now demand exactly that proof. In this hands-on workshop, you configure a resilient backup architecture on AWS using vaults and immutable storage. You then experience a simulated ransomware event, validate that your recovery infrastructure held, restore to an isolated clean room environment, and scan recovered resources for attacker persistence using GuardDuty Malware Protection. You leave with a recovery validation approach and an understanding of why least privilege, vault lock, and validation are non-negotiable.
speakers: Christopher Strug (Senior Technical Account Manager, Amazon)
Danny Wright (Principal Technical Account Manager, AWS)

title: Not all bots are bad: building a secure perimeter with AWS WAF
abstract: Your edge traffic is a mix of customers, AI agents, scrapers, and attackers. Treat them the same and you lose either security or revenue. In this workshop, you turn AWS WAF into a decision layer that classifies traffic in real time and routes it. Legitimate users get a fast lane, suspicious traffic goes to deception environments that waste attackers' time and reveal their intent, and AI agents get their own treatment that opens the door to new ways of charging for access. None of it requires changes to your origin logic.
speakers: Manuel Pata (Sr. TAM, AWS)
Eitav Arditti (Senior Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: What's new in Application Security: Securing applications at machine speed
abstract: AI is accelerating your release cadence. AWS application security capabilities help engineering teams ship secure applications faster, including AI-powered workloads. In this session, learn how AI-driven services enforce organizational guardrails before code is written, perform threat modeling, review code for vulnerabilities, generate fixes automatically, and enable on-demand penetration testing. See how to codify these into paved pathways that give developers room to build with AI while maintaining consistent security standards. Leave with a clear plan for embedding AWS application security into your platform, from design through continuous validation.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Christopher Rae (Principal, Worldwide Security Specialist, AI Security, Amazon Web Services)
Joao Melo (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Daniel Santana (CISO, Itau Unibanco SA)

title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Multi-agent systems create a larger attack surface than single-agent deployments: prompt injections that propagate across agent boundaries, identity spoofing, tool-chain escalation, and data exfiltration through natural-language covert channels. In this chalk talk, we threat-model this risk using the OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, then whiteboard defense-in-depth patterns for validating inter-agent messages, enforcing least-privilege orchestration, and detecting anomalous behavior before it cascades. Leave with a set of recommendations and architectures that demonstrate how to layer security controls in a multi-agent system.
speakers: Kunle Adeleke (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Daniel Wells (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Enforce AI guardrails across your organization without the friction
abstract: Your security team defines the controls, and your product teams build and deploy AI applications across dozens or hundreds of AWS accounts. This chalk talk shows how to enforce AI guardrails centrally without making your security team the bottleneck. We walk through an architecture for applying Amazon Bedrock Guardrails through controls at the AWS Organizations, account, and AI infrastructure layers. You see how controls inherit across those layers, which limitations to plan for, and how tiered governance lets teams tailor controls to their applications while the organizational baseline stays enforced.
speakers: Rob Whitelocks (Snr Specialist Solutions Architect - Security, AWS)
Michael Ingoldby (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Enforce AI guardrails across your organization without the friction
abstract: Your security team defines the controls, and your product teams build and deploy AI applications across dozens or hundreds of AWS accounts. This chalk talk shows how to enforce AI guardrails centrally without making your security team the bottleneck. We walk through an architecture for applying Amazon Bedrock Guardrails through controls at the AWS Organizations, account, and AI infrastructure layers. speakers: Michael Ingoldby (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Rob Whitelocks (Snr Specialist Solutions Architect - Security, AWS)

title: Security leverage at AI velocity: the operating model shift
abstract: The speed AI gives your developers is also available to attackers, so AI investment is now a security decision as much as an engineering one. This session covers three changes to how security teams work when engineers pair with frontier agents. Agents carry application context across design, code, and pen testing, so security coverage keeps pace with development. When an agent builds a working proof of exploit for a finding, or shows that an existing control already blocks it, the security team no longer has to argue over whether the finding is real, and the false-positive queue shrinks. Agentic development environments also let you put preventive controls on what agents generate. We cover how to adopt these practices and which signals show they're working.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Ram Ramani (Principal Security AWS, AWS)

title: Authenticating workloads to the outside world
abstract: Your workloads and agents authenticate to external systems today mostly via individual OAuth implementations, secrets in config files, and custom refresh logic owned by separate teams. In this chalk talk, we'll explore patterns for centralizing how workloads obtain, manage, and govern credentials for non-native services. We'll diagram a reference architecture covering control, data, and governance planes, walk through real-world authentication flows and discuss how to design policies that control which workloads can access which external credentials.
speakers: Fei Yuan (Principal Engineer, AWS Identity, Amazon Web Services)

title: Protect workloads with AWS Certificate Manager
abstract: Discover how to automate and manage TLS certificates using AWS Certificate Manager. In this chalk talk, we'll discuss automation opportunities for certificate issuance, export, distribution, and renewal across diverse environments. By attending, you'll gain the skills to eliminate manual certificate management tasks and minimize the risk of certificate-related outages in your organization.
speakers: Michael Slaughter (Principal Software Development Engineer, AWS)

title: Conquer Suricata: simplify rule writing on AWS Network Firewall
abstract: Writing and maintaining firewall rules at scale can be complex. In this code talk, join AWS Network Security experts as they walk through practical techniques, and new capabilities, to simplify rule-writing experience with AWS Network Firewall. Through live examples, learn to structure rule groups to meet common use cases and deploy according to best practices. This session will dive deep to keep policy writing easy to manage as your environment grows. Walk away with hands-on patterns you can apply immediately to tame rule complexity and ship changes with confidence.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk

title: Faster root cause analysis for IAM access denied errors
abstract: When an IAM request is denied, teams can spend valuable time finding the root cause. Now, access denied error messages go beyond surfacing the policy type or ARN that blocked a request—they tell you the exact reason access was denied. In this session, we'll walk through how the feature works, how to put it to use, and considerations for larger AWS environments where different policy types are owned by different teams.
speakers: Matt Luttrell (Principal Security Engineer, Amazon)
Matthew Heck (Senior Software Development Manager, Amazon)

title: Fix a Security Hub finding once with four layers of controls
abstract: You remediate a finding today and see the same class of finding next week. This chalk talk shows how to break that cycle. You take a real AWS Security Hub finding category and work through four control layers. An SCP stops the misconfiguration, an AWS CloudFormation Guard rule catches it before deployment, an AWS Config rule detects existing violations, and AI-generated auto-remediation corrects drift. Each finding you remediate this way becomes a rule that keeps it from coming back.
speakers: Todd Kudlicki (Speciality Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Maitreya Ranganath (Principal Security Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc)

title: Crossing the Kill Chain: Detection and Response When Attackers Pivot Between Clouds
abstract: When an attacker gains a foothold in one cloud and pivots into another, the kill chain crosses boundaries that no single-cloud tool follows on its own. Detecting it starts before the incident, with the preparation that makes the cross-cloud seam visible: centralizing and normalizing telemetry across your estate. In this chalk talk, we work through how to prepare for, detect, and respond to cross-cloud lateral movement together. Using real attack sequences, we showcase how to build the detection and response using AWS Security Hub, Amazon CloudWatch, and multicloud telemetry sources. You'll leave with an alerting framework and correlation patterns you can run against your own environment.
speakers: Ameya Paldhikar (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Geoff Sweet (Sr Security Specialist SA, Amazon, Inc.)

title: Managing software vulnerabilities in the agentic world
abstract: Vulnerability management is evolving beyond detection. As AI agents generate and deploy code at machine speed, security teams need a fundamentally different approach to identifying, prioritizing, and resolving software vulnerabilities. In this session, explore how AWS thinks about the future of vulnerability management — from contributing to open source vulnerability databases and detecting malicious packages before they reach your pipeline, to enforcing remediation at scale without slowing development velocity. Learn how to shift from reactive CVE chasing to a proactive posture that accounts for AI-generated code, autonomous deployments, and the expanding software supply chain.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Anthony Verleysen (Sr. Product Manager Technical - External Services, AWS)
Nirali Desai (Principal Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: The security you inherit: how the AWS platform protects your workloads by default
abstract: Every organization has finite security resources. The more the platform handles, the more your team can focus on securing what is unique to your application — your data, your logic, your users. In this session, we explore the security capabilities built into the AWS platform that work before you write a single IAM policy. From threat intelligence that blocks malicious actors at the network edge, to Nitro's zero operator access architecture that eliminates an entire class of insider risk, to automated reasoning that mathematically proves your policies behave as intended — these are protections you inherit just by running on AWS. We also cover PrivateLink for eliminating public internet exposure, default encryption, and S3 Block Public Access. Understand what the platform already handles so you can direct your security investment where it matters most: the application layer.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Matt Meck (WW Security Specialist, AWS)
Marshall Jones (Security Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: One query across every signal: centralized security investigations at scale
abstract: When an alert fires, your first question is "what else happened?" Answering it means correlating API calls, network flows, DNS queries, and application logs, often across dozens of accounts and regions. In this session, we show how security practitioners centralize every signal into a single queryable layer using Amazon CloudWatch unified data store, then investigate incidents with faceted queries that span all telemetry types at once. We walk through building always-on visibility dashboards, running cross-account investigations without switching tools, and using AI-assisted analytics to surface context before you need to go looking for it. You leave with a reference architecture for turning centralized logs into faster investigations and clearer security posture.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Abeetha Bala (Senior Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Marshall Jones (Security Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Threat technique catalog for AWS: practical controls for real TTPs
abstract: Threat actors are evolving faster than ever, leveraging AI-generated exploits and automated attack tooling to move at machine speed. AWS CIRT sees these techniques firsthand across customer incidents of all sizes. The Threat Technique Catalog for AWS (TTC), extending the MITRE ATT&CK framework, documents these recurring TTPs with detection and mitigation guidance specific to AWS. This session covers how to turn observed attacker patterns into an advantage: build actionable detections and mitigations into your security operations before the next incident hits.
speakers: Shannon Brazil (AWS Security Engineer, Manager, AWS)
Cydney Stude (Sr. Security Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: AI-assisted incident response: preparing for AI-assisted offensive
abstract: The tools to raise the bar on incident response are here. AI can handle the volume so your team can focus on the nuance. But making that shift in practice, earning trust, building feedback loops, securing the tools themselves, is where we have seen teams get stuck. In this chalk talk, AWS Customer Incident Response Team (CIRT) leaders share exactly how we made that transition and what we learned along the way. We'll diagram the pipeline live, simulate an investigation, and spend real time working through your scenarios at the whiteboard.
speakers: Robert Saul (General Manager Customer Incident Response Team, AWS)
Lindsey Henry (Head of AWS CIRT, AWS)

title: AI-assisted incident response: preparing for AI-assisted offensive
abstract: The tools to raise the bar on incident response are here. AI can handle the volume so your team can focus on the nuance. But making that shift in practice, earning trust, building feedback loops, securing the tools themselves, is where we have seen teams get stuck. In this chalk talk, AWS Customer Incident Response Team (CIRT) leaders share exactly how we made that transition and what we learned along the way. speakers: Robert Saul (General Manager Customer Incident Response Team, AWS)
Lindsey Henry (Head of AWS CIRT, AWS)

title: Living Off the Agent: Detecting and Preventing Lateral Movement in Agentic AI
abstract: "Living off the land" (LOTL) attacks use native OS tools to evade detection. In 2026, techniques evolved to "Living off the Agent" (LOTA), compromising enterprise AI agents through subtle prompt injections to exfiltrate data, escalate privileges, and move laterally. Red team studies identified vulnerabilities in production AI agents with distinct LOTA patterns. This chalk talk explores the LOTA taxonomy, detection strategies, and architectural containment patterns. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we'll whiteboard defenses together.
speakers: Emmanuel Isimah (Senior Solutions Architect, amazon web services)
Victor Okonyia (Senior Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Cut through the noise: risk-based prioritization for your security findings
abstract: Security Hub prioritizes critical security risks and helps you respond at scale. By correlating threats, vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations across AWS and multicloud environments, it surfaces attack paths and prioritizes what needs attention first. In this chalk talk, we deep dive into how exposures work, how risk prioritization scores are calculated, and how to operationalize the findings in your environment.
speakers: Michael Davis (Manager Security Engineering, AWS)
Nicholas Jaeger (Principal, Security Specialist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Cut through the noise: risk-based prioritization for your security findings
abstract: Security Hub prioritizes critical security risks and helps you respond at scale. By correlating threats, vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations across AWS and multicloud environments, it surfaces attack paths and prioritizes what needs attention first. In this chalk talk, we deep dive into how exposures work, how risk prioritization scores are calculated, and how to operationalize the findings in your environment.
speakers: Michael Davis (Manager Security Engineering, AWS)
Nicholas Jaeger (Principal, Security Specialist, Amazon Web Services)

title: Automated forensics at scale with generative AI
abstract: Forensics is one of the hardest, most manual parts of incident response, and it usually requires a specialist. In this code talk, we work through a realistic Kubernetes cluster compromise where an Amazon GuardDuty finding kicks off the forensics investigation. We watch as an AI agent identifies injected code, and reconstructs the attack chain. Then we tackle the real problem. Forensic evidence needs determinism and a defensible chain of custody, and generative AI is not deterministic. We show the techniques that close that gap, so an AI-driven investigation produces evidence you can defend.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Barry Conway (Sr. Security Solution Architect, AWS)
Chris Lamont-Smith (Sr. AI/ML Security Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services Australia)

title: Automated forensics at scale with generative AI
abstract: In a live demo, we deploy malware built from APT41 tradecraft onto a Kubernetes cluster and watch an AI agent autonomously investigate the forensic evidence — acquiring volatile memory, identifying injected code, and tracing the attack chain without human intervention.In a live demo, we deploy malware built from APT41 tradecraft onto a Kubernetes cluster and watch an AI agent autonomously investigate the forensic evidence — acquiring volatile memory, identifying injected code, and tracing the attack chain without human intervention.
speakers: Chris Lamont-Smith (Sr. AI/ML Security Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services Australia)
Barry Conway (Sr. Security Solution Architect, AWS)

title: Good fences make good neighbors: a network perimeter approach to data perimeters
abstract: How do you secure that which has no network? AWS services such as S3, SQS, and DynamoDB help teams build and scale faster but come with a different set of security implications than services that live in your VPC. In this session, you'll learn about best practices and architectural patterns for building secure networks on AWS using network features like DNS firewall, and Network firewall and layering them with AWS IAM policies like VPC endpoint policy, and Resource Control Policy to help ensure that your resources that live outside of your network behave like they are in your network.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Swara Gandhi (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Jesse Lepich (Security SA, AWS)

title: Build layered defenses for agentic AI from prompt to tool execution
abstract: Attendees build a defense-in-depth security architecture for an AI agent. You start with a pre-deployed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with Lambda tools, then run adversarial test scenarios to observe how gateway and tools respond without controls. You layer defenses from Bedrock Guardrails for prompt-attack detection, through AgentCore Policy Engine with Cedar policies-based tool authorization, including Dogwood temporal policies, and finally native rate limits paired with CloudWatch anomaly detection. By progressing through each scenario again, you verify how each protection aligns with a layered security pattern you can apply to your agentic workload.
speakers: Reetesh Surjani (Delivery Consultant - Security, AWS)
Anshu Bathla (Sr. Lead Consultant - Security, AWS)

title: When security, speed, and trust all matter: Lessons from Project Glasswing
abstract: In 2026, a frontier AI model demonstrated it could discover and chain software exploits at machine speed. This new reality forced the industry to confront an entirely new class of offensive capability. In this session, learn how AWS Security's Office of the CISO engaged executive customers and partners to build playbooks to help assess AI-era vulnerability management and remediation. We share the lessons implemented with customers, the internal changes AWS made to operate as a more secure AI-first organization, and practical steps every security team can take now.
speakers: Clarke Rodgers (Office of the CISO, Amazon Web Services)
Hart Rossman (VP, Security, AWS)

title: From MCP poisoning to defense: securing the agent tool supply chain
abstract: MCP is becoming the standard for connecting AI agents to tools, but MCP servers are packages that present supply chain risk. In this builders session, you will observe a live MCP tool poisoning attack, then build three defense layers hands-on: gateway validation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy to restrict tool actions, a pre-deployment integrity scanner that detects silent tool definition changes, and runtime monitoring that flags anomalous tool behavior. Leave with a working understanding of how MCP supply chain attacks work and how to defend against them.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Trevor Schiavone (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))
Markus Rollwagen (Senior Solution Architect, AWS)
Abdu Mahmoudi (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Joe Rudd (Sr. Technical Acount Manager, AWS)
Desiree Brunner (Security Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Zero trust for non-human identities: IAM for autonomous agents
abstract: Agents access tools, call APIs, and delegate to other agents. They need layered identity controls at every stage. In this builders' session, apply zero trust principles to a multi-agent environment using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll configure agent identities with OAuth providers, enforce least privilege via OBO token exchange, differentiate agents from humans with IAM MCP condition keys, and set Gateway rules blocking unauthorized access. Then, you stress test your setup using cross-chain access, privilege escalation, identity spoofing to see each blocked by a different layer you built.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Yaniv Cadosh (Startup Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Shimi Rokah (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Brendan Paul (Security Services SA Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Future-proof your keys: HSMs to AWS KMS in the post-quantum era
abstract: Cryptography is changing fast. The dedicated HSM you rely on today, whether AWS CloudHSM or an on-premises appliance, carries operational overhead that will only grow as the industry moves toward post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and stricter digital sovereignty requirements. AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now covers most workloads that once required dedicated HSMs, with the same FIPS 140-3 Level 3 security, lower cost, and zero infrastructure management, while giving you a clear on-ramp to PQC and the sovereignty controls to keep your keys and data under your control. In this chalk talk, bring your architecture and we'll work through it together: we'll assess your workload, map signature and encryption migration paths, and show how moving to KMS puts you on the fastest path to post-quantum readiness. Meet the AWS Cryptography team and leave with a plan and concrete next steps.
speakers: Kevin Kevin (Sr. Product Manager - Technical, AWS)
Derek Tumulak (Principal Product Manager, AWS)

title: Securing OpenClaw deployments on AWS
abstract: In this session, we introduce the OpenClaw architecture, compare the major variants and their security posture differences, and then map the threat landscape for AWS-hosted deployments. Drawing on years of experience helping customers deploy, we cover the infrastructure and runtime threat landscape. You will leave with a reference architecture that applies defense-in-depth principles to such OpenClaw deployments on AWS, minimizing risk without sacrificing capability.
speakers: Maxim Raya (Specialist SA Security, AWS)
Itay Meller (Security Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Agentic AI for Security: How AWS CIRT reduced triage time to minutes
abstract: When a security event hits a customer account, every minute counts. Learn how AWS CIRT built an agentic AI system using Amazon Kiro that performs investigation workflows autonomously: ingesting case data, baselining environments, analyzing indicators, and producing triage assessments. We cover architecture decisions for AI agents with live AWS API access, evaluation frameworks measuring accuracy against expert answer keys, and guardrails keeping humans in the loop. Leave with patterns for applying agentic AI to operational workflows where accuracy is non-negotiable.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Joshua McKiddy (Security Engineer, Amazon)
Brian Poole (Senior Security Engineer, AWS)

title: Policy to Proof: govern deployments at machine speed
abstract: When agents and automated pipelines deploy at machine speed, manual sign-off can't keep up, so the proof has to be built into the pipeline itself. Developers want to ship fast, governance teams want controls enforced, and compliance teams want evidence. In this builder session, you'll build a CI/CD pipeline that satisfies all three: cfn-guard validation against policy rules, CloudFormation deployment, Config evaluation after deployment, and a compliance report generated as a pipeline artifact. The full policy-to-proof loop in one pipeline. You leave with a working pipeline where every deployment validates governance rules and produces audit evidence on its own.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Welly Siauw (Principal Partner SA, AWS)
Jerry Peter (Senior PMT, Amazon)
Jean Velez Torres (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Vinicius Elias (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Pujah Goviel (Technical Account Manager, AWS)

title: How to Govern an agent fleet: auto-approve the routine, escalate the ambiguous
abstract: Your teams are building agents faster than anyone can review them by hand, and that creates operational and security risk along with the visibility problem. In this workshop, you build a layered controls stack for an agent fleet. You enforce content and business-logic boundaries with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, apply an evaluator pattern for policy validation, and track compliance posture with AWS Config conformance packs. Then you connect these into an operating model that approves routine actions automatically and sends only the ambiguous ones to a person, so you can deploy more agents than your team could review individually.
speakers: Matej Macek (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL)
Ganesh sedhai (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Shared judgment: security culture for the agentic era
abstract: Your agents are reviewing PRs, shipping code, and answering messages. They communicate on your behalf, surfacing every weak relationship in your org. Soft skills have never mattered more. Shift Left and Shift Down brought security in as automation to build trust in systems. Agents have moved the question to trust between humans. Security teams have historically operated at a remove: by org chart, tooling, and reputation. That distance becomes a liability when agents reduce the time between decision and consequence. This session is about building a security function whose core output is shared judgment with the engineers it serves.
speakers: Jonathan Jenkyn (Snr Security and Compliance SA, AWS Security Assurance Services)
Samantha Wylatowska (Security Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Shared judgment: security culture for the agentic era
abstract: Your agents are reviewing PRs, shipping code, and answering messages. They communicate on your behalf, surfacing every weak relationship in your org. Soft skills have never mattered more. Shift Left and Shift Down brought security in as automation to build trust in systems. Agents have moved the question to trust between humans. Security teams have historically operated at a remove: by org chart, tooling, and reputation. That distance becomes a liability when agents reduce the time between decision and consequence. This session is about building a security function whose core output is shared judgment with the engineers it serves.
speakers: Jonathan Jenkyn (Snr Security and Compliance SA, AWS Security Assurance Services)
Samantha Wylatowska (Security Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Centralized governance for multicloud environments
abstract: When AI agents and automated pipelines ship changes across AWS, Azure, and other providers in minutes, governance that runs on separate toolchains can't keep pace. You end up with disparate security findings along with mis-aligned operational metrics, and a team that spends its time reconciling dashboards instead of actually reducing risk. In this session, see how to collapse multicloud governance into a single operating model across AWS and Azure, leveraging Amazon CloudWatch unified telemetry for centralized observability and AWS Security Hub for aggregated findings into a single surface.You'll walk through a deployable architecture that gives one analyst a unified view across clouds, so your governance moves at the same speed your engineering teams already do.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Craig Edwards (Sr. Technologist, AWS)
Simone Pomata (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall
abstract: Teams deploying AI agents inherit two exposures. Any client reaching the endpoint can invoke the agent, and it can reach any destination its tools name. In this builders' session, learn to close both gaps with AWS managed controls. Put AWS WAF Bot Control in front of your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to classify callers and admit only the classes you choose, then route the agent through AWS Network Firewall and use domain category filtering to decide which destination categories it may reach. Run each control in count or alert mode, then enforce it and verify the allowed and the refused path. Leave with a two-boundary pattern you can apply to your own agent deployments.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Pedro Rosinholi (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Alin Scurtu (, AWS)
Leonardo Azize (Solutions Architect, AWS)
PRAVEEN HOSUR NARAYANA GUPTA (Specialist Solutions Architect - Edge Services, AWS India)
Prabhu G (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall
abstract: AI agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore accept untrusted input and make outbound API calls, creating both ingress and egress attack surfaces. In this session, learn how to defend both paths using AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall. See how WAF authenticates callers, enforces rate limits, and blocks prompt-injection payloads before they reach your agent, while Network Firewall applies managed threat-intelligence categories to drop egress traffic to malicious destinations without maintaining custom deny lists. Walk away with a deployable defense-in-depth boundary pattern for your agentic AI workloads.
speakers: Alin Scurtu (, AWS)
Leonardo Azize (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Pedro Rosinholi (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Prabhu G (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
PRAVEEN HOSUR NARAYANA GUPTA (Specialist Solutions Architect - Edge Services, AWS India)

title: Building resilient authentication with Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication
abstract: Authentication is the front door to your app, and if that's unavailable, everything is unreachable. Amazon Cognito is the managed CIAM service that handles sign-up, sign-in, federation, and threat protection at scale. In this chalk talk, learn how Cognito's new multi-Region replication (MRR) unlocks resilient authentication across Regions. We'll whiteboard reference architectures for B2C, B2B, and M2M workloads, cover implementation considerations like customer managed keys and in-Region dependencies, and walk through failover strategies. Leave ready to architect authentication that keeps customers connected.
speakers: Edward Sun (Sr Security Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Abrom Douglas III (Sr. Security Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: A day in the life of a SPIFFE SVID
abstract: Workloads across AWS, on premises, and other clouds need verifiable identity without long-lived secrets, and SPIFFE provides it. In this lightning talk, we show how to issue SPIFFE SVIDs and how they flow into AWS. You follow one SVID through SPIRE attestation, cross-cloud federation, exchange for STS credentials through IAM Roles Anywhere or AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, and presentation to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity for AI agent tool access.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Brendan Paul (Security Services SA Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Design your cedar authorization model with AI coding agents
abstract: Your identity provider handles authentication, but how do you design the authorization model that follows? In this chalk talk, learn how to use OIDC token claims from providers, including Amazon Cognito, with a Cedar-based authorization model. We'll walk through implementing RBAC, ReBAC, and ABAC patterns locally or in Amazon Verified Permissions, and show how to use AI coding agents (Kiro, Claude) to generate your schema and policies. Bring your use case for this interactive session. You'll leave with a repeatable approach to designing fine-grained authorization from scratch.
speakers: Julian Lovelock (Principal Product Manager Technical, Amazon)
Kevin Hakanson (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Quantum-proof your IoT fleet: migrate devices to Post-quantum cryptography OTA
