abstract: NIST has announced post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards and CNSA 2.0 requires quantum-resistant algorithms by 2027. IoT devices deployed today operate for 10–20 years, so they need to be quantum-resistant from day one. In this workshop, migrate a real ESP32-S3 SoC from classical TLS to post-quantum cryptography over the air with zero physical access required. Connect to AWS IoT Core, trigger an OTA delivering ML-KEM and ML-DSA with quantum-safe certificates from AWS Private CA, and watch your device reboot into PQC-secured MQTT. No embedded experience needed. You leave with the ESP32-S3 and open-source code to quantum-proof your fleet at scale.
speakers: Pravin Nair (Sr. Security Strategy SA, Amazon Web Services)
Samuel Waymouth (Senior Compliance Specialist, AWS)

title: Proving your defenses work: validating GuardDuty runtime detection
abstract: Your board wants to know your detections work and auditors want evidence. The only way you find out today is when something real hits. In this code talk, you;ll see us build a detection validation program that answers the question before it gets asked. We'll live-code realistic attack scenarios mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, generate the correlated signals that trigger GuardDuty runtime findings, scope detection rules to specific accounts, and interpret findings as they fire. You'll walk out with a repeatable framework your team can run after every GuardDuty update to prove coverage, not assume it.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Muhammad Wasiq (AWS) (Principal Security Engineer, Amazon (AWS))
Bryan Van Hook (Sr. Security Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)

title: From static to dynamic - modernizing bidirectional federation
abstract: Static credentials remain the most common source of identity-related security incidents, yet many workloads still rely on them across trust boundaries. AWS now eliminates them in both directions. Humans and workloads outside AWS can use OIDC, SAML, or X.509 certificates to federate in and obtain temporary AWS credentials. Conversely, IAM outbound identity federation lets AWS workloads exchange IAM identities for short-lived JWTs when calling external clouds like Azure and Google Cloud, AI providers like OpenAI or Anthropic, SaaS platforms like Databricks and Snowflake, and your own applications. This session covers how to configure trust, scope credentials, and enforce authorization controls.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Ram Maharajapuram (Sr. Manager - Software Development, Amazon Web Services)
Mohamed Keshk (Sr. Product Manager, Amazon (AWS))

title: Innovation in identity security: how we protect the cloud & help you do it too
abstract: Learn how AWS approaches identity as the foundation of cloud security - both protecting AWS infrastructure and enabling customers to operate securely at scale. Explore how AWS innovates in access management and develops prescriptive, service-specific guidance helping organizations adopt services confidently, drives secure-by-default authorization across 300+ services, and ensures IAM policies work predictably. Millennium Partners will share how they use AWS guidance and threat modeling to evaluate new services, strengthen their security posture, and give developers freedom to innovate faster.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Ilya Epshteyn (Director, Identity Security & Solutions, AWS)
Kristen Haught (Sr. Security Engineering Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Alan Garver (Head of AWS Platform Engineering, Millennium Management)

title: Closing the compliance loop when agents change your infrastructure
abstract: AI agents and automated pipelines now change your infrastructure faster than any review can keep up, and not every change comes through CloudFormation. In this workshop, you'll close the compliance loop end to end: author a CloudFormation Hook that enforces encryption and tagging before deployment, then extend the same logic into an AWS Config custom rule with CloudFormation Guard so out-of-band changes get caught continuously. You'll build auto-remediation with SSM Automation, package it into a Conformance Pack for org-wide reach, and use Resource Timeline to trace drift. You leave able to keep compliance closed however fast change arrives.
speakers: David Sokolik (Senior Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
JaQuan Thompson (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Authentication, authorization, and audit for agentic AI on AWS
abstract: In this session you will learn how to secure identities and permissions for AI agents across your agentic workflows. Using Strands SDK, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, Cognito, and Verified Permissions, you implement user and machine authentication, fine-grained authorization, consent management, and permission delegation for agents, tools, and LLMs. The session follows a "choose your own adventure" format so you focus on the scenarios most relevant to you, whether that is agent-to-agent delegation, human-in-the-loop consent, or least-privilege tool access. You leave ready to apply these patterns to your own agentic AI systems.
speakers: Meric Degirmenci (Security and Compliance Specialist, AWS)
Rickard Löfström (Specialist SA, Security & Compliance, Amazon Web Services)

title: Stop threats at DNS: what's new in Route 53 DNS Firewall
abstract: DNS is where threats are first visible and Amazon Route 53 DNS Firewall is turning that visibility into defense. This session explores how Route 53 DNS Firewall's evolving security capabilities help you resolve, inspect, and protect egress DNS query traffic to the internet across global, multi-account environments. See how deeper integration with other AWS security services, expanded DNS threat detection, wider visibility, and a growing partner ecosystem come together to strengthen your first line of defense. Whether you run a single VPC or a global network across AWS and hybrid networks, you'll leave with a clear picture of how DNS security for egress traffic is advancing and how to put it to work.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Adhish Bhobe (Principal Product Manager - Tech, Amazon Inc.)
Jesse Lepich (Security SA, AWS)

title: Securing software and AI supply chains with Network Firewall at Coupang
abstract: Coupang, South Korea's largest e-commerce platform, runs millions of daily transactions on AWS. At that volume, each open source library, container base image, and AI model weight pulled from the internet is a supply chain risk. This session goes deep on the AWS Network Firewall architecture and its newer capabilities, including centralized management and container-aware egress inspection. Coupang shows how it built egress control that scales automatically across a container-first fleet, automates allowlist management, and limits exposure to rogue AI dependencies and dynamic payloads without slowing developers down.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Sang Won Kim (Senior Security Engineer, Coupang)
Amish Shah (Sr. Product Manager Technical, Amazon Web Services)
Andrew (Kyungshik) Shin (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Control what goes out: egress security for AI workloads
abstract: Most AWS workloads send traffic out in two ways, DNS queries and network connections, and attackers can abuse both to exfiltrate data. This session shows how to lock down both paths. We cover DNS Firewall enhancements for the DNS path, Network Firewall improvements for outbound connection control, and how running DNS Firewall and Network Firewall together gives you one view of DNS security. We also cover URL and domain categories, managed threat intelligence, and extending egress protection to containerized and AI workloads.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Sofía Aluma (WW Security Network Security GTM Lead, AWS)
Bashuman Deb (Principal Software Development Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Akshay Choudhry (Principal Product Manager, Amazon)

title: Designing security governance for your AWS multi-account foundation
abstract: AWS gives you flexibility to design your multi-account environment, but customer needs guidance choosing the right security services to deploy, where, and how to validate the deployment against AWS best practices. This session shows how the AWS Security Reference Architecture provides a prescriptive security blueprint you layer on top of your account governance foundation. Using whiteboarding, you cover OU design, service prioritization, centralized vs. distributed placement, design considerations, validation with SRA Verify, and deployment acceleration. You leave with a tailored governance model ready for implementation.
speakers: Ishai Shvartz (Sr. Mgr, PMT, Accounts, Amazon)
Avik Mukherjee (Sr. Security SA, Amazon Web Services)

title: Map once and prove everywhere across multiple compliance frameworks
abstract: Regulatory frameworks like SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and the EU AI Act each demand separate assessments, yet a significant portion of their requirements overlap. You spend time collecting duplicate evidence for controls you already have. This chalk talk introduces the control inheritance approach and shows how a single AWS Config rule or organizational policy can satisfy requirements across multiple frameworks. You walk through real examples of framework overlap, automation patterns that eliminate duplicate evidence collection, and a governance approach you can implement immediately.
speakers: Brian Stucker (Pr. Security Specialist SA, Amazon)
Kevin Donohue (Sr Security Compliance Engineer, aws)

title: Architecting firewalls on AWS: a layered defense strategy
abstract: With automated traffic now more than half of the web, a single firewall layer can't separate good bots from L7 attacks. This chalk talk covers how AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall work together. We cover deployment patterns for internet-facing apps, outbound controls, and workload segmentation, including firewall patterns attached to AWS Transit Gateway. Then we dig into the tradeoffs, including centralized versus distributed inspection, cost versus latency, and when one service can carry the load and when you need both. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we whiteboard a design for your environment.
speakers: Patrick Duffy (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Jonathan Woods (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: Land migrated workloads with controls already in place
abstract: Most migrations add governance controls after workloads land on AWS, and that creates rework. This chalk talk shows how to build guardrails into your AWS Transform migration workflow with AWS Organizations, IAM Identity Center, AWS Config, and AWS Security Hub so workloads arrive with controls in place. Bring your migration challenges, and we design a secure-by-default landing together that carries governance through each phase of the migration.
speakers: Jakob Altevolmer (Delivery Consultant, AWS)
David Piet (Worldwide Principal Specialist Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Navigating mergers and divestitures across multiple AWS organizations
abstract: Enterprises go through mergers, face divestitures, and inherit multiple AWS Organizations, each with its own structure and identity provider. Consolidating or separating these environments is complex. This interactive session covers patterns for merging AWS organizations, managing multiple organizations in parallel, and splitting organizations cleanly. You dive into the identity challenge of migrating between Microsoft Entra ID, Google, and Okta when each entity brings its own IdP to AWS. You leave with practical patterns and lessons learned engagements with customers like you.
speakers: Nivedita Tripathi (Sr. Product Manager Technical ES, Amazon)
Alex Torres (AWS) (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Stop troubleshooting your AWS network from memory and stale diagrams
abstract: Your network grew faster than your documentation. Routes were added in a sprint, VPC attachments stacked during migrations, and somewhere along the way, your team lost the full picture. When something breaks, you're troubleshooting from memory and stale diagrams. In this session, learn how to turn that around in hours instead of months. See how to point AI-assisted tooling at your live environment to map every resource, trace every traffic path, and surface misconfigurations before they become incidents. Then take it further: modernize what you find with current AWS network security capabilities. Walk out with a repeatable workflow you can run against your own network this week.
speakers: Neil Yajnik (Sr. Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Kartik Ganesh (Sr Security Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Stop troubleshooting your AWS network from memory and stale diagrams
abstract: Your network grew faster than your documentation. Routes were added in a sprint, VPC attachments stacked during migrations, and somewhere along the way, your team lost the full picture. When something breaks, you're troubleshooting from memory and stale diagrams. In this session, learn how to turn that around in hours instead of months. See how to point AI-assisted tooling at your live environment to map every resource, trace every traffic path, and surface misconfigurations before they become incidents. Then take it further: modernize what you find with current AWS network security capabilities. Walk out with a repeatable workflow you can run against your own network this week.
speakers: Neil Yajnik (Sr. Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Kartik Ganesh (Sr Security Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Governing hundreds of accounts in seconds: agentic AI meets Landing Zone operations
abstract: When you manage hundreds of AWS accounts, governance can fall behind. Drift accumulates, controls take days to propagate, and problems go undetected until something breaks. We demonstrate Landing Zone Accelerator 2.0 with built-in AI that lets operators use natural language to apply organizational changes in minutes, if not seconds. We deploy org-wide security controls, provision accounts, and enforce encryption through a Bedrock-powered interface supporting CloudFormation and Terraform. An AI agent generates each change plan, and before anything is applied, an org-wide preview catches conflicts and policy violations. Issues are surfaced up front instead of discovered after a break. Attendees learn how we built LZA 2.0 with Kiro spec-driven development and Rust, and how to design pre-deployment previews that keep multi-account operations safe.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Randy Domingo (Sr. SDM, AWS)
Bo Lechangeur (Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: AWS and Nu: Building scalable architecture using IAM Account access manager
abstract: As organizations grow across teams, AWS accounts, and countries, workforce access often becomes a bottleneck. This is especially true when you depend on existing IAM roles you don't want to re-engineer. Learn how IAM account access manager helps you assign your existing IAM roles to users and groups in IAM Identity Center, give native AWS CLI access to your workforce, and carry each user's identity into every role session, all on a resilient architecture. Then see how Nu, the largest digital bank in Latin America, modernized a decade-old authorization model across 11 organizations and hundreds of AWS accounts to securely scale for more than 140 million customers.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Hugo Feijó (Lead Software Engineer, Nubank)
Laura Reith (Sr. Identity Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Tim Kosanke (Software Development Manager, AWS)

title: How Moeve turned natural language into enforced governance controls
abstract: Translating compliance requirements such as GDPR or NIS2 into enforceable controls usually means writing policy by hand. Moeve built a Governance Control AI Assistant on Amazon Bedrock to change that. You see how engineers ask questions in natural language and the system turns their intent into SCPs, hooks, and AWS Config rules assigned at OU and account scope, validated through CI/CD and GitOps. Moeve shares the architecture and what it learned running the assistant in production.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Rayco Martínez Hernández (Head of Cloud Center of Exellence, MOEVE)
Luis Rodriguez Montilla (Sr. CloudOps Specialist SA, AWS)
Nicole Klatt (WW Specialist, AWS)

title: How to build an autonomous compliance environment auditors trust
abstract: Auditors require evidence of compliance on demand. Learn how to keep your AWS environment audit-ready at all times, continuously producing the proof auditors need, without manual intervention. Across services such as AWS Config, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Security Hub and more, we walk through an architecture that automatically collects evidence, maps it to your control frameworks, checks whether the collected evidence meets control requirements, identifies gaps and delivers prescriptive guidance to close each gap. We finish with how AI agents now investigate findings, draft remediations, and defend evidence to auditors, moving compliance from continuous monitoring to continuous resolution.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Kristine Harper (Senior Practice Manager, AWS Security Assurance Services, LLC)
Suchita Verma (Principal Product Manager, Amazon)

title: Orchestrate GuardDuty and Network Firewall to prevent exfiltration
abstract: Compromised workloads and AI agents share a common path: outbound channels that most teams barely monitor. From CVE-driven RCE on EC2 to prompt injection on agentic systems, both threats end with unauthorized data leaving your environment. In this session, dive deep into a layered egress architecture combining AWS Network Firewall, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, VPC endpoint policies, SCPs, RCPs, GuardDuty, and IAM Access Analyzer. We'll trace concrete attack scenarios through each control and show how to orchestrate them to prevent data exfiltration.
speakers: Maxim Raya (Specialist SA Security, AWS)
Meriem SMACHE (Security Specialist Solution Architect, AWS)

title: Protect EKS and ECS workloads without chasing pod IPs
abstract: Pod IPs in Kubernetes change constantly as containers scale and restart, making IP-based firewall rules brittle and hard to maintain. In this lightning talk, learn how container attribute-based rules in AWS Network Firewall let you write policy using native attributes like namespaces, cluster names, and labels instead of ephemeral IPs. We'll show how a container association auto-discovers matching pods, refreshes IP mappings in near real-time, and enriches alert logs with container context for faster troubleshooting and audit. Bring the same Layer 7 inspection, FQDN filtering, and managed IDS/IPS protections you already trust to your Amazon EKS and ECS workloads.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Bongkyoon Choi (Security Sales Specialist, Amazon Web Services)
Amish Shah (Sr. Product Manager Technical, Amazon Web Services)

title: Inside the frontier: What builders are creating at OpenAI
abstract: How are builders at OpenAI turning big bets into systems and new products used across the company? Through demos and firsthand stories, go behind the scenes of ambitious projects with the people who built them. Discover the problems they’re tackling, the frontier capabilities that made their ideas possible, and what they’ve learned putting them into practice. Leave with practical lessons for bringing your own ideas to life with OpenAI.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Teri Yu (Multimodal Product, OpenAI)

title: From containers to containment: trust the boundary, not the agent (sponsored by Docker)
abstract: For a decade, teams have trusted containers to run the same way everywhere. Coding agents raise the stakes: the thing inside now installs packages, accesses credentials, and acts on its own. In this session, see how the idea that made containers the standard becomes containment for agents: a Docker sandbox that limits what an agent can reach, hardened images beneath what it builds, and a record of what it was allowed to do and what was stopped, under policies set once for every developer. The agent gets room to work; the boundary gets the trust. That is what running on trust means. This presentation is brought to you by Docker, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Partner Advantage Theater

title: When AI Moves Money: Secure the Agentic Future of Financial Services (sponsored by TrendAI™)
abstract: Organizations are racing to adopt AI, but many struggle to balance innovation, governance, and security. In this session, learn how Discover how technology leaders are enabling AI innovation while reducing operational risk and complexity. enterprises are using TrendAI Vision One on AWS to accelerate AI initiatives, gain visibility across complex cloud environments, and reduce operational risk without slowing the business. Discover real-world deployment patterns, lessons learned, and the architectural principles that help security teams move from reactive defense to proactive risk management while enabling AI at scale. Built on AWS-native services and integrated across the cloud ecosystem, this approach helps organizations simplify operations, improve threat detection, and confidently embrace the next wave of transformation. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: Automated compliance evidence from day one
abstract: Your compliance team spends weeks collecting evidence manually before every audit. Automated evidence collection eliminates that burden from day one. In this builders' session, you'll learn how to leverage AWS GRC services, including AWS Config, AWS Organizations, AWS CloudTrail, and Control Catalog, to configure automated evidence collection, map controls to your target framework, use the AI compliance agent to validate both technical controls and procedural policies, and build continuous drift detection that alerts you before your next audit finds the gap.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Nicole Klatt (WW Specialist, AWS)
Pal Patel (Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Marc Luescher (Senior Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))
Bill Ohlson (Enterprise Technologist, AWS)
Desiree Brunner (Security Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Mitigating prompt injection with structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Prompt injection works because LLM outputs are unconstrained. Structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock compiles a JSON Schema into a grammar and enforces it during decoding so every token the model emits is a valid position in the schema. In this code talk, we live-code defense schemas for sentiment analysis, intent classification, and SQL validation, then attack them with real injection payloads. We cover provider differences between Claude and open-weight models, strict tool use for agentic workflows, and how to combine grammar enforcement with input validation for defense in depth.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Aswath Ram A Srinivasan (Sr. WW Specialist Solutions Architect- Bedrock, Amazon Web Services)
Mac Stevens (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Network policy across hundreds of accounts with AWS Network Security Manager
abstract: Once an organization grows to hundreds of accounts, managing network security policies by hand becomes a liability. AWS Network Security Manager deploys AWS WAF, AWS Shield, and soon to come AWS Network Firewall across a multi-account environment from a single policy definition. This session covers how to build defense in depth with Network Security Manager, and how to keep centralized network security manageable as you add accounts.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Ian Olson (Sr. Specialist SA Security, Amazon Web Services)
Robert Albach (Principal Product Manager, AWS)

title: Securing applications at machine speed in the frontier model era
abstract: Frontier AI models discover code vulnerabilities in minutes. Security teams still take days or weeks to validate, prioritize, and fix them. AWS Continuum closes that gap with one continuous workflow: discover risks in your code, prioritize by real exploitability, validate in a sandbox with reproduction steps, and remediate at machine speed within guardrails you define. In this session, we walk through how Continuum operates end-to-end: building a security context graph from your infrastructure, identity, and code to determine what is reachable, confirming exploitability through sandboxed proof-of-concept, and generating validated fixes. You see graduated trust in action, starting with human approval and promoting to autonomous remediation as confidence builds. You leave understanding how to move from manual triage to continuous discovery, validation, and remediation.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater

title: Turn autonomous agents into accountable ones
abstract: Your AI agents pass the demo but struggle in production because of limited accountability and controls. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard a governance framework that closes the loop. You get governed agent accounts with AWS Control Tower, hard API boundaries with AWS Organizations policies, and runtime tool-access controls and behavior scoring in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. AWS Config detects drift from policy and triggers automated rollback. You leave with a repeatable, observe-score-remediate pattern for keeping AI agents operating within your policies."
speakers: Vijay Shekhar Rao (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Michael Tschannen (Sr. Specialist SA Security, Amazon Web Services)

title: How to use AI to develop and deploy controls from your internal policies
abstract: You maintain internal security policies but turning them into implemented, risk-prioritized controls could be manual and slow. This lightning talk demonstrates how to use Kiro to develop and deploy controls at scale across three layers. Preventive controls that block non-compliant actions, detective controls that identify violations and trigger remediation, and proactive controls that validate configurations before deployment. You leave with a practical approach to using AI to accelerate the entire control lifecycle from policy to enforcement.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Pujah Goviel (Technical Account Manager, AWS)

title: How to solve for multicloud identity lifecycle management
abstract: Organizations operating in multiple clouds face a compounding multi-cloud identity lifecycle governance challenge. How do you provision, manage, audit, and decommission identities when each cloud provider enforces different authorization models, attribute schemas, and lifecycle hooks? In this session, the National Institutes of Health (NIH), a federal research organization, describes how it uses a centralized identity governance platform to provision identities and entitlements across AWS and Microsoft Azure. You will learn how to avoid governance divergence and design identity lifecycles where access reviews, birthright provisioning, and decommissioning work consistently, regardless of which cloud the identity lands in.
speakers: Joshua Stultz (Chief, Cloud Services, National Institutes of Health)
Phillip Spies (Snr Solutions Architect, aws)
Rodney Underkoffler (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Secure Coding Agents for Regulated Environments with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (sponsored by Act Security)
abstract: Learn how HUB International, a top-five global insurance broker, partnered with AWS and Act Security to securely bring autonomous coding agents into a regulated enterprise environment, without giving the agents standing credentials or expanding the attack surface. The team transformed the local Claude Code experience into a secure, per-user cloud sandbox on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, preserving the familiar IDE and terminal workflow while moving execution to the cloud. See how OIDC authentication through the corporate IdP, per-call token minting through AgentCore Identity, and Cedar-based authorization for tools exposed through AgentCore Gateway enforce per-user, per-action access. Finally, discover how Act Security sustains least privilege over time and enforces narrower policies - whether you are deploying AgentCore for the first time or hardening an existing environment. This presentation is brought to you by Act Security, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: Offir Levy (Field CTO, Act Security)

title: How Woodside handed SOC monitoring to AWS SIR to focus on threat hunting
abstract: Routine monitoring and alert triage leave security teams stretched thin. In this session, hear how a global energy company worked with AWS Security Incident Response to change what its SOC spends time on. The company handed eyes-on-glass monitoring and incident response operations to AWS, which freed its security staff for proactive threat hunting. You see how integration with existing ITSM workflows made adoption straightforward, and how the combined team sped up detection, containment, and resolution during a real supply chain attack.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Philip Winstanley (Principal Security Engineer, AWS)

title: Securing your AI-accelerated software supply chain with AWS Well-Architected
abstract: Modern software depends on open-source packages from npm, PyPI, and Maven. AI assistants pull them into your codebase faster than ever, sometimes suggesting packages that don’t exist or shouldn’t be trusted. Attackers exploit this through “slopsquatting.” Supply chain incidents show registries targeted via credential compromise, typosquatting, and token farming at scale. This workshop builds a layered defense aligned to the AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar. You replace long-lived credentials with OIDC, sign artifacts with AWS Signer, and govern dependencies with CodeArtifact package groups. You scan AI-generated and human-written code with Amazon Inspector, then detect threats with GuardDuty and Security Hub. You leave with a defense-in-depth blueprint that scales with AI-accelerated development across your environment.
speakers: Anshu Bathla (Sr. Lead Consultant - Security, AWS)
Rohit Verma (DELIVERY CONSULTANT - SECURITY, AMAZON AWS)

title: Your Agent Is in Production. Can You Explain What It Did? (sponsored by Datadog)
abstract: Your team shipped an agent to production last quarter. It works, mostly. When it doesn't, nobody can explain why. This session covers what changes when non-deterministic systems enter your stack: which signals actually matter for agentic workloads, how to trace a multi-step agent across tools and models, and where AI agents can safely take action in your own operations. Live examples from Datadog LLM Observability, the Agent Console, AI Guard, and Bits AI. You'll leave with an instrumentation checklist. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Andrew Krug (Head of Security Advocacy & Research, Datadog)

title: How Badger Meter unified customer identity with Amazon Cognito
abstract: Badger Meter provides smart water solutions for utilities that run critical infrastructure. Its applications used to rely on fragmented authentication, including password hashes, siloed SAML integrations, and custom JWT schemes. Managing identity across those platforms stopped working as the portfolio scaled to 4,000+ tenants. Learn how Badger Meter migrated to Amazon Cognito to centralize authentication, improve authentication experience, and onboard new tenants faster. This session covers multi-tenant architecture, AWS Lambda triggers for token enrichment, SAML and OIDC federation, and managed login.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Howie Li (Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Jarred Kohout (Software Engineer, Badger Meter)
Pranab Bora (Software Engineering Manager(SaaS), Badger Meter)

title: Find, prove, and fix code vulnerabilities with AWS Continuum
abstract: Frontier AI models discover code vulnerabilities in minutes. Security teams still take days or weeks to validate, prioritize, and fix them. In this builders' session, use AWS Continuum to close that gap end to end on a live application. You build a security context graph from your infrastructure, identity, and code to determine what is actually reachable, confirm exploitability through a sandboxed proof-of-concept, and generate a validated fix. You will see graduated trust in action, starting with human approval and promoting to autonomous remediation as confidence builds. Leave able to move your team from manual triage to continuous discovery, validation, and remediation.
speakers: Pat Gaw (Principal Security Engineer, AWS)

title: Securing APIs with AWS
abstract: Teams want visibility into their API landscape and find that traditional controls may miss attacks targeting API-specific vulnerabilities. In this session, learn how AWS is thinking about the modern API security challenge, from discovering unknown and unmanaged endpoints to detecting the kinds of authorization, authentication, and abuse issues that appear normal request by request. We'll explore common patterns behind recent industry incidents, why API visibility and runtime protection matter, and how a native, integrated AWS approach can help you reduce risk and respond faster.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: The latest innovations in multicloud agent security
abstract: AI agents are showing up everywhere your teams work, and security teams also want to keep pace. In this session, explore the latest innovations in securing AI across multicloud environments. See how AWS is thinking about the challenges security teams face as AI is used by teams, and the direction it is taking to help them stay ahead. Walk away with a clearer picture of where AI security is heading and practical ways to get ahead of it in your own organization.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: Maintain accountability when using IAM federation
abstract: Many enterprises access AWS through IAM federation with providers like Okta and Microsoft Entra ID. But if your analysts share an IAM role, downstream services do not distinguish who has assumed that role making per-user access controls and audit more challenging. In this chalk talk, we'll explore considerations when using federated environments, discuss why it matters for compliance and security, and examine what it takes to maintain individual accountability without overhauling your existing federation setup.

title: Winning the DDoS Game: defend your app under real-time attack
abstract: Compete in a team-based environment where you face real-time threats aimed at your web application. Use the latest capabilities in AWS WAF and AWS Shield to mitigate HTTP floods, web exploits, and malicious bots that disrupt your customers. This risk-free event puts teamwork to the test as you work under pressure. Watch a real-time scoreboard as your team works through each level. Whether it's volumetric attacks or the new wave of AI-driven traffic hitting your APIs, you'll leave prepared to defend against what's coming next. The most effective team earns a prize!
speakers: Julian Garcia (Senior Technical Account Manager, AWS)
Jonathan Woods (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: Red team CTF: when auth and guardrails aren't enough
abstract: The best way to secure an AI agent is to think like the attacker. In this CTF-style session, you start with a production-realistic agent - AgentCore runtime, Bedrock Guardrails, Cognito authentication, and three MCP tools - and you systematically exploit it. Across 6 challenges, you poison trusted data sources, bypass prompt-level access control, jailbreak an authenticated session, compromise a third-party MCP server, exfiltrate data through authorized channels, and burn the inference budget. After each breach, you enable the real fix and verify the attack fails. You will compete on a live leaderboard and leave with a fully hardened agent and a defense-in-depth playbook.
speakers: JaQuan Thompson (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Mac Stevens (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Ship permissions faster: IAM policy tools in your CI/CD pipeline
abstract: Build a complete permissions pipeline that identifies IAM policy issues at code review. In this session, we build the pipeline stages: validate policies at pull request time with Access Analyzer, simulate critical access paths before deployment, preview Service Control Policies (SCP) impact against real CloudTrail data, and automatically triage Access Denied errors in production using IAM's new debugging API and autofix recommendations. We'll write commit gates that block overly permissive policies, integration tests that ensure operational permissions, and auto-triage that turns production denials into automated remediation commits.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Todd Kudlicki (Speciality Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Siva Rajamani (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Moumita Saha (Sr. WW Specialist SA Identity, Amazon Web Services)
Kevin Shanley (Principal Solutions Architect - Identity, AWS)
Diana Yin (Senior Technical Product Manager, AWS)

title: From vulnerability to exploit to fix: closing the loop with AWS Security Services
abstract: You start with a deployed e-commerce web application containing OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities like SQL injection and SSRF, hardcoded credentials, and a dependency CVE. Using Amazon Inspector and AWS Continuum (formerly AWS Security Agent), you discover and validate existing flaws, reproduce the exploit chain, and push Continuum-generated fixes through CI/CD. When Amazon GuardDuty detects the active exploitation, including credential theft and prompt injection against an AI assistant, you isolate the compromised instance and harden it. Walk away with a repeatable closed-loop workflow: Inspector finds it, GuardDuty catches it, Continuum fixes it.
speakers: Jason Schamp (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Aliaksei Ivanou (WW Security & Identity Sr. PSA, Amazon Web Services, Inc.)
Travis Rocco (Security Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Kiran Dongara (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Navigating the inter-workings of an agentic SOC & threat hunting analyst
abstract: Security analysts face an expanding attack surface with finite time and attention. In this session, we show how analysts can leverage AI-powered agents to accelerate their core workflows — from automated triage and log correlation to proactive threat hunting across CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and threat intelligence feeds. Walk through real investigation scenarios where AI handles the repetitive evidence gathering while analysts focus on judgment calls: scoping impact, deciding containment actions, and validating findings. You will see how to configure trust boundaries so agents act within your approved scope, how source attribution ensures every AI-surfaced claim traces back to a specific log, and how to evaluate whether the AI is actually making your team faster.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Moumita Saha (Sr. WW Specialist SA Identity, Amazon Web Services)
Chris Elmore (Sr. Manager Security Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)
Gopinath Jagadesan (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Michael Leighty (Security Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Jonathan Nguyen (Principal AI Security Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Constrain AI agents with permissions boundaries and Cedar in AgentCore
abstract: Your AI agents need permissions to be useful, and unconstrained permissions lead to unintended consequences. In this workshop, you build defense-in-depth governance for agentic workloads. You create scoped IAM execution roles with permissions boundaries, enforce mandatory Amazon Bedrock Guardrails through IAM policy, validate agent policies with IAM Access Analyzer, and add deterministic Cedar enforcement in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The result constrains what agents can do while still letting legitimate actions through.
speakers: Ravid Glam (Technical Account Manager, AWS)
David Sokolik (Senior Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Constrain AI agents with permissions boundaries and Cedar in AgentCore
abstract: Your AI agents need permissions to be useful, and unconstrained permissions lead to unintended consequences. In this workshop, you build defense-in-depth governance for agentic workloads. You create scoped IAM execution roles with permissions boundaries, enforce mandatory Amazon Bedrock Guardrails through IAM policy, validate agent policies with IAM Access Analyzer, and add deterministic Cedar enforcement in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The result constrains what agents can do while still letting legitimate actions through.
speakers: David Sokolik (Senior Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Ravid Glam (Technical Account Manager, AWS)

title: Build a container pipeline that blocks tampered images at the gate
abstract: What if you want to prove cryptographically that every container in your environment is untampered and fully inventoried? In this builders' session, you build exactly that. Dive deep into the AWS Signer cryptographic model: KMS-backed keys, ECDSA P-256, COSE_Sign1 envelopes, and notation trust policies. Implement ECR managed signing, generate SBOMs with Amazon Inspector, slim images to reduce attack surface, and enforce admission on EKS with Kyverno. Then stress test it with attack simulations against the pipeline you just built.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Builders' Session 1
speakers: Michael Tschannen (Sr. Specialist SA Security, Amazon Web Services)
Andre Baumeier (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Desiree Brunner (Security Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Andrea Rossi (AWS Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Build a container pipeline that blocks tampered images at the gate
abstract: What if you want to prove cryptographically that every container in your environment is untampered and fully inventoried? In this builders' session, you build exactly that. Dive deep into the AWS Signer cryptographic model: KMS-backed keys, ECDSA P-256, COSE_Sign1 envelopes, and notation trust policies. Implement ECR managed signing, generate SBOMs with Amazon Inspector, slim images to reduce attack surface, and enforce admission on EKS with Kyverno. Then stress test it with attack simulations against the pipeline you just built.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2
speakers: Andre Baumeier (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Andrea Rossi (AWS Solutions Architect, AWS)
Desiree Brunner (Security Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Michael Tschannen (Sr. Specialist SA Security, Amazon Web Services)

title: Threat detection and IR in AgentCore workloads
abstract: Step into an AWS environment where command-and-control callbacks from agent tools, exfiltrated credentials, and disabled safety guardrails occurred across AgentCore workloads. Your mission: detect, investigate, and respond. Using Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub alongside CloudWatch and AgentCore Observability, you'll triage findings, correlate security events with application traces, map entity relationships, isolate compromised resources, and build automated remediations. You'll leave with practical skills to secure AgentCore systems you can trust.
speakers: Nima Fotouhi (Delivery Consultant, Amazon)
Mike Saintcross (Sr. Security and Compliance Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: AWS Security Incident Response Challenge: Defend the Cake
abstract: The Magic Unicorn Cake recipe needs defending, and the Grumpy Cats are on the move. In this hands-on workshop, you become an AWS Security Engineer protecting critical assets. Working in teams, you strengthen security posture, establish continuous monitoring, and execute incident response playbooks while a live threat actor works to exfiltrate the recipe. A live leaderboard tracks every scored action. Through this immersive experience you learn threat modeling and the detection and response methodologies the team behind AWS Security Incident Response applies daily. Practical techniques that translate directly to your own environment. Bring your laptop.
speakers: Ben Fletcher (AWS SIReT EMEA Operations Lead, AWS)
Geroen Joris (Security Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)

title: Processing PII without exposing it using AWS Nitro Enclaves for confidential computin
abstract: How do you process PII data at scale without giving your data pipeline access to the plaintext? In this workshop, you combine AWS Nitro Enclaves for confidential computing with Amazon EMR on EKS to build a high-assurance screening system. AWS Nitro Enclaves provides isolated compute environments within EC2 instances to protect highly sensitive data. Encrypted records are sent to an enclave, where data is decrypted only after AWS KMS verifies the enclave's cryptographic attestation. Screening rules are applied and only the decision is returned. Plaintext never leaves the enclave boundary. The pattern generalizes to any workload processing highly sensitive data at scale.
speakers: Sathish Kumar Prabakaran (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Webservices India Pvt. Ltd)
Abhishek Jawali (Sr Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services India Private Limited)

title: Secrets rotation patterns for agentic pipelines at scale
abstract: Autonomous agents provision, consume, and rotate credentials without a human in the loop. In this chalk-talk, work through how to build a secrets lifecycle for multi-step agentic workflows: issue dynamic secrets using AWS temporary credentials and leverage AWS Secrets Manager for secrets rotation, Scope each agent with resource policies and VPC endpoint conditions to enforce a data perimeter, and apply AWS KMS envelope encryption so ephemeral secrets never persist in plaintext. Leave with deployable templates for zero-standing-privilege secret delivery across chained agent invocations.
speakers: Enrico Bonaccorsi (Principal Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Francesc Sala (Principal TAM, AWS)

title: From rules to reasoning: Build an intelligent tagging compliance agent with AgentCore
abstract: AWS Config rules detect missing tags, but what about resources where the correct tag value isn't obvious? In this builder session, you'll create an AI agent using AgentCore that goes beyond detection to intelligent remediation. Your agent analyzes resource context, account ownership, VPC placement, creator identity, naming patterns to infer correct tag values, and handles ambiguous cases by requesting human input. Start where Config rules end: not just "is it tagged?" but "what should the tag be?"
speakers: Avi Harari (Sr. Technical Account Manager, AWS)
Gautam Bhaghavatula (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Francesco Provino (Sr TAM (EMEA-ISV), L6, AWS)
Nour Shlian (Snr. Technical Account Manager, Amazon)
Ibrahim Cesar (Well-Architected Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: Orchestrating AI agents for continuous code security hardening
abstract: Agentic AI is increasing the rate at which organizations discover and fix security vulnerabilities — and the rate at which findings arrive faster than anyone can act on them. In this workshop, you'll build an agentic security hardening pipeline using Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore: deterministic scanners fan out across code, dependencies, secrets, and infrastructure; reviewer and triage agents correlate and rank what comes back; and policy-as-code gates decide on demonstrated evidence rather than on agents agreeing. You'll learn how to decompose a security audit into parallelizable agent tasks, and how to keep a human holding every consequential decision before changes reach production.
speakers: Trevor Schiavone (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS))
Owen Hawkins (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: OAuth delegation patterns for AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
abstract: AI agents act on behalf of users and systems, and delegating the right access without over-permissioning is hard. In this chalk talk, we use code examples to work through authorization delegation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity. We cover the OAuth grant flows that matter for agents, including authorization code for user-delegated access, client credentials for machine-to-machine calls, token exchange for on-behalf-of propagation, and Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) for fine-grained permission scoping. For each flow, you see which agent scenario it fits and when to choose it over the others.
speakers: Jeff Lombardo (Principal Security Specialist, AWS)
Fei Yuan (Principal Engineer, AWS Identity, Amazon Web Services)

title: Visualizing agent identity privileges to monitor multi-agent behavior
abstract: If one of your AI agents quietly gained admin-level access right now, would you know? In multi-agent systems, each handoff between agents can widen permissions, and traditional monitoring won't catch it. In this code talk, we build a real-time graph answering three questions: who are my agents, what can each one do, and what can they reach through each other? We connect IAM roles, Cedar policies, and CloudWatch data into one visual map, then add alerts that fire the instant any permission chain exceeds what you defined. You leave with the tool that catches it first.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Alex Waddell (Principal Security Specialist SA, Amazon Web Services)
Meg Peddada (Principal FSI Security Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Architect resilient, multi-region workforce access on AWS
abstract: Most AWS workforce access hinges on a single Region and a single identity provider. When either one goes down, everyone who signs in is affected—developers can't ship, DevOps engineers can't deploy, and administrators may be locked out just when they need access most. This session applies defense in depth across four layers: IAM Identity Center multi-Region replication, direct IAM federation through AD FS, Regional AWS STS endpoints, and break-glass IAM users. You learn how to decide which layers your environment needs, the order to fail over in, and how to test the full path without disrupting production.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Prashob Krishnan (Principal Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Laura Reith (Sr. Identity Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Alex Milanovic (Sr. Product Manager Technical, Amazon Web Services)

title: A deep dive on IAM policy evaluation
abstract: Every API call in AWS passes through IAM policy evaluation, but few truly understand what happens in that moment between request and access decision. In this chalk talk, we go deep into the weeds of how IAM actually evaluates your policies: how the request context is assembled, how each policy type interacts in the evaluation chain, where implicit and explicit denials come from, and why some evaluation scenarios behave in ways that may be surprising. We will work through real scenarios, common gotchas, and edge cases live.
speakers: Matt Luttrell (Principal Security Engineer, Amazon)
Khaled Sinno (Senior Principal Engineer, AWS)

title: A deep dive on IAM policy evaluation
abstract: Every API call in AWS passes through IAM policy evaluation, but few truly understand what happens in that moment between request and access decision. In this chalk talk, we go deep into the weeds of how IAM actually evaluates your policies: how the request context is assembled, how each policy type interacts in the evaluation chain, where implicit and explicit denials come from, and why some evaluation scenarios behave in ways that may be surprising. We will work through real scenarios, common gotchas, and edge cases live.
speakers: Khaled Sinno (Senior Principal Engineer, AWS)
Matt Luttrell (Principal Security Engineer, Amazon)

title: From proofs to production: Neurosymbolic AI and provable security
abstract: AWS has spent a decade proving the correctness of critical infrastructure, from IAM policy evaluation to cryptographic implementations and network isolation. This session traces the evolution from early automated reasoning tools to today's neurosymbolic AI, where formal verification and large language models converge. We examine how mathematical proof engines like Lean, combined with reinforcement learning and agentic workflows, enable provable security guarantees at scale. Attendees will learn how specification-driven development, whole-service data flow analysis, and Bedrock Guardrails' automated reasoning checks are moving the industry beyond "test and hope" toward mathematically verified trust.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Byron Cook (VP/Distinguished Scientist,  Agentic AI Leadership, Amazon)

title: How AWS Continuum validates security findings across the SDLC
abstract: AWS Continuum embeds security expertise at every stage of the software development lifecycle: AWS Continuum reviews architecture documents, AWS Continuum scans pull requests and full repositories, and AWS Continuum can pentest deployed applications. In this chalk talk, we dive deep into how AWS Continuum coordinates multiple analysis passes with built-in safety guardrails and multi-step validation to deliver high-confidence findings. Bring your questions about integrating security into CI/CD pipelines and scaling AppSec across multiple teams.
speakers: Jeremy Schiefer (Pr. Security SA, AWS)

title: Threat modeling the agentic SDLC: from user story to deployment
abstract: "Threat modeling the agentic SDLC with ThreatForest Agentic development is speeding up, and traditional threat modeling assumes a person makes the decisions. In this code talk, you follow one process end to end. You threat model a user story with the autonomous threat modeling built into AWS Continuum, carry it through the developer workflow, and take it to deployment. You see how ThreatForest, an agentic tool built on the Strands framework, generates attack trees and MITRE ATT&CK mappings on its own, and how to build a mitigations catalog your organization can reuse. We also show where traditional threat modeling can be used for agentic systems."
speakers: Brad Dispensa (Pr. Security and Compliance Specialist, Amazon)
ionut ionescu (Security Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Tenant-isolated agent memory: one IAM policy for AgentCore Memory
abstract: Managing memory for hundreds of tenants in SaaS shouldn't require hundreds of IAM policies — yet most products scaling multi-tenant agents on AWS end up there: a namespace per tenant-agent pair, a policy per tenant, deployment times that climb with every customer. In this chalk talk, learn how to isolate both layers of agent memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — short-term session events and long-term extracted records — with one Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policy backed by AWS Security Token Service (STS) session tags. We cover the actorId and namespace conventions, the Token Vending Machine that mints per-tenant credentials, and the anti-patterns that break isolation as you scale. Leave with the reference architecture and the IAM policy template you can use on Monday.
speakers: Daniel Wirjo (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Nihilson Gnanadason (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Tenant-isolated agent memory: one IAM policy for AgentCore Memory
abstract: Managing memory for hundreds of tenants in SaaS shouldn't require hundreds of IAM policies — yet most products scaling multi-tenant agents on AWS end up there: a namespace per tenant-agent pair, a policy per tenant, deployment times that climb with every customer. In this chalk talk, learn how to isolate both layers of agent memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — short-term session events and long-term extracted records — with one Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policy backed by AWS Security Token Service (STS) session tags. We cover the actorId and namespace conventions, the Token Vending Machine that mints per-tenant credentials, and the anti-patterns that break isolation as you scale. Leave with the reference architecture and the IAM policy template you can use on Monday.
speakers: Daniel Wirjo (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Nihilson Gnanadason (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Multi-tenant isolation with IAM: ABAC, session tags, and token vending machines
abstract: Multi-tenant SaaS has two isolation options: application-layer filtering or IAM enforcement. Filtering requires every query and API call to add tenant scoping — one missed filter leaks data. IAM enforcement holds even when code has a bug, and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes it work without per-tenant policy explosion. We cover the stack: ABAC session tags, a Token Vending Machine minting tenant-scoped STS credentials, IAM condition keys for DynamoDB/S3 partition boundaries, and a credential-caching model that keeps latency acceptable at millions of requests per second across thousands of tenants. Leave with a deployable reference architecture and policy template.
speakers: Nicholas Tunney (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Dave Roberts (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Multi-tenant isolation with IAM: ABAC, session tags, and token vending machines
abstract: Multi-tenant SaaS has two isolation options: application-layer filtering or IAM enforcement. Filtering requires every query and API call to add tenant scoping — one missed filter leaks data. IAM enforcement holds even when code has a bug, and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes it work without per-tenant policy explosion. We cover the stack: ABAC session tags, a Token Vending Machine minting tenant-scoped STS credentials, IAM condition keys for DynamoDB/S3 partition boundaries, and a credential-caching model that keeps latency acceptable at millions of requests per second across thousands of tenants. Leave with a deployable reference architecture and policy template.
speakers: Nicholas Tunney (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)
Dave Roberts (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Network Firewall deployment models: pros, cons, best practices
abstract: One firewall, many ways to deploy it, and each mode unlocks a different architectural superpower. This session maps your options: distributed, centralized, multi-endpoint, explicit proxy, and the newest firewall modes. Through real architectures, you'll see where each one shines, how they scale, and the patterns that make your network security clean, flexible, and future-ready. Whether you're protecting a single VPC or a global multi-account estate, you'll leave knowing exactly which mode fits your environment and why. If you route traffic through AWS, this is the map that gets you there faster.
speakers: Brian Westmoreland (Sr. Delivery Consultant - CIA, AWS)
Luke Notley (Senior Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Secure your CI to operate at machine speed (sponsored by Chainguard)
abstract: AI agents are changing how software is built, introducing new security challenges across the software supply chain. CI environments are particularly vulnerable, with access to sensitive credentials and elevated permissions. We’ll explore how Chainguard's trusted artifacts, isolated build environments, and integrations with AWS can reduce risk from development through deployment and what securing software delivery looks like when AI agents are doing more of the work. This presentation is brought to you by Chainguard, an AWS Partner.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater

title: Firewall policy management for mixed regulated and legacy workloads
abstract: Your firewall policy now has to cover new workloads on modern tech stacks alongside legacy systems still running Windows. Some of them fall under financial regulations, and others under privacy controls. In this code talk, we show how new firewall management features help you write policy elements your team can understand and maintain, avoid policy sprawl, and spend less time preparing for audits.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Dario Goldfarb (Security & Networking Leader LATAM, Amazon Web Services)
Ian Olson (Sr. Specialist SA Security, Amazon Web Services)

title: Leverage the power of MCP servers for resource inventory and compliance
abstract: AI agents can now interact with AWS services through the Model Context Protocol. In this code talk, we live-build a governance agent that uses MCP to query AWS Config for resource configurations. You'll see how to construct compliance checks, detect configuration drift, and trigger automated remediation using natural language all powered by Config's recording and advanced query capabilities. We explain the architecture decisions and trade-offs so you can adapt this pattern to your own governance workflows.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Code Talk
speakers: Pal Patel (Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Francisco (Chico) Ferreira (Senior Software Development Manager, AWS)

title: Tokenomics of attacks: how AWS defends you from AI-powered threats
abstract: AI isn't just transforming how we build, it's transforming how attackers exploit. In this session, AWS threat researchers share the intelligence they observe in real time: the prompts adversaries feed into AI systems, the tokenomics that make AI-powered attacks devastatingly scalable, and the shrinking window between vulnerability disclosure and weaponized exploitation. We'll share first-hand threat intel from MadPot, AWS's globally distributed honeypot network, and show how AWS protects AI-based workloads. You'll learn how AWS Active Threat Defense capabilities proactively block malicious infrastructure before it reaches your workloads, so you can innovate with AI confidently while staying ahead of emerging threats.
speakers: Paul Bodmer (Threat Research Team Manager, AWS)
Alexandra Lee (Principal Engineer, AWS)

title: Next-gen threat detection: GuardDuty advanced security capabilities
abstract: Amazon GuardDuty protects millions of accounts using AI and ML models purpose-built for cloud security, and the detection engine keeps getting smarter without requiring action from you. In this session, the lead scientist behind GuardDuty's detection engine takes you inside the research. Learn how the team designs models for security inference at scale, uses distillation and reinforcement learning to keep detection cost-efficient without sacrificing accuracy, and distinguishes normal from anomalous behavior without using customer data for training. See how these advances translate into expanded coverage, faster detection of sophisticated threats, and deeper investigation workflows. You leave with an understanding of the engineering tradeoffs behind AI-native threat detection at AWS scale and how to operationalize the latest capabilities.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Baris Coskun (Sr. Principal Scientist, AWS)
Justin Criswell (AWS Security Services Specialist SA Leader, AWS)

title: A leader's guide to predicting and proving AI value
abstract: Every organization faces the same AI questions: How do we predict and manage costs? How do we prove value when outcomes are hard to measure? How do we move fast without losing control? Two finance leaders, one advising enterprise executives and one managing AI economics at scale inside Amazon, share what is working, what is not, and where teams go wrong. Learn how to measure AI cost and value in terms finance and technology leaders agree on, which guardrails to set as investment grows, and how to make the case for AI value to your board.
speakers: Chris Hennesey (Executive in Residence, AWS)
Lindsey Drake (VP, Applied AI Solutions Finance, Amazon)

title: A leader's guide to the AI you haven't seen yet
abstract: Most AI strategy is built for the AI leaders can see. The models in production today are the constrained ones, gated by capacity and cost, and that gate is lifting. When it lifts, a dozen breakthrough applications becomes a million, and AI systems get as cheap and as common as a website. Progress has stopped being predictable too: capability arrives in step changes that can obsolete a year of work in a quarter. This session asks what you would build if AI were free and never made a mistake, and how to tell a durable bet from a disposable one.
speakers: Ishit Vachhrajani (Executive in Residence, Amazon Web Services)
Matt Wood (Chief AI & Technology Officer, AWS)

title: A leader's guide to advanced teams models in an agentic world
abstract: Agents made execution cheap. The work did not disappear. It moved into deciding what should exist, checking what agents produce, and owning it when something breaks. Most team designs were not built for that. This session gives you four questions to ask of any piece of work: what is it for, what does it touch, how will we check it, and whose name is on it. Then we walk through the team models leaders reach for, what each gets wrong, and where the pager and the name should sit. You leave knowing who does what now.
speakers: Jonathan Allen (Executive in Residence, AMAZON WEB SERVICES)
Carrie Wood (Director, AWS Senior Talent & Transformation, Amazon)

title: A leader's guide to how AI is changing Amazon’s ways of working
abstract: AI is changing how Amazon hires, builds, manages, and deploys teams across every function to innovate and deliver on behalf of customers. This session shares Amazon's emerging framework: the mental models fueling transformation, a state model for understanding where teams are on the AI journey, and real case studies of teams that have crossed from AI-enhanced to AI-native and beyond. We'll walk through the implications, share the questions we're still wrestling with, and offer practical recommendations for leaders navigating the same transition. First-person data from an organization at scale, shared with candor.
speakers: Stephen Brozovich (Executive in Residence, Amazon Web Services)
Ian Wilson (VP, Sr Talent & Transformation, Amazon)

title: A leader's guide to escaping proof-of-concept purgatory
abstract: Drawing on 1,000+ customer conversations about building competitive advantage with data and AI, Rahul Pathak, VP of AWS Data & AI GTM, shares what separates organizations getting real value from agentic AI from those stuck in pilots. When everyone has the same models, your data is the only differentiator. Rahul covers how to set goals worth deploying against, why working backwards from outcomes matters, why cross-functional teams outperform centralized AI functions, what governance must exist before agents reach production, not after, and how to create urgency without a mandate. Field notes from 1,000+ rooms, and a playbook for Monday morning.
speakers: Rahul Pathak (VP, Data & AI GTM, Amazon Web Services)

title: A leader’s guide to governing AI, on behalf of humans
abstract: AI deployments can reason, problem-solve, and act with increasing agency. Leaving governance models built for deterministic software no longer sufficient. AWS Executive in Residence Ryan Seaman and Dr. Bernadette Han, organizational psychologist at the American Psychological Association (APA), bring technology and human behavior into one governance conversation. As AI interacts with people, influences decisions, and takes actions, governance must address not only what AI can do, but how it behaves with people and what happens as a result. Bernadette introduces the EEI-AI Behavioral Architecture™, translating psychological science into behavioral requirements organizations can design for, test, observe, and govern responsibly.
speakers: Ryan Seaman (Executive in Residence, Amazon)
Dr. Bernadette Han (Head of APA Learn, American Psychological Association)

title: A leader's guide to the AI speed trap
abstract: Your developers are faster with AI. Your organization isn't. AI tools accelerate individual teams, but organizational outcomes depend on what happens between teams: coordination, dependencies, and end-to-end value streams that extend far beyond code. Most productivity metrics miss this entirely because they stop at the team boundary. In this session, we present real patterns from startups, scaleups, digital natives, and large organizations, introduce measurement frameworks that capture what matters at the organizational level, and share practical approaches for turning team-level acceleration into outcomes your customers will notice.
speakers: Matthias Patzak (Executive in Residence, Amazon Web Services)
Laura Tacho (Senior Principal Technologist, AWS)

title: A leader's guide to how Amazon built its data foundation for agents
abstract: Organizations racing to put AI agents on top of their data keep hitting the same walls: security, privacy, scale, and data they can't trust. In this session, Anas Fattahi (VP, Amazon Business Data Technologies) and G2 Krishnamoorthy (VP, AWS Databases) share how years of foundational investment positioned Amazon to move quickly when the agentic AI moment arrived, and where the hard problems still live. You'll hear which bets paid off, what's working now, what they're still building, and how to inspect your own setup against what they've learned.
speakers: Anas Fattahi (VP, Business Data Technologies, Amazon)
G2 Krishnamoorthy (VP, Database Services, AWS, Amazon)

title: A leader's guide to why agentic AI just made your data problem urgent
abstract: The data problem you tolerated for years just became an emergency. Agents do not politely work around missing metadata. They guess confidently, and you find out three weeks later. Enterprises assumed they could solve AI first and data second. They can't. You get the framework that separates compounding value from programs that never finish. AWS Marketing built an agentic system over thousands of warehouse tables. It worked. Its first output: an inventory of every undocumented decision in the warehouse. That exposure was worth more than the answers. You leave knowing what to fix first, and why analytical demand climbs.
speakers: Tom Godden (Executive in Residence, AWS)
Karolis Urbonas (Director, Applied Science, AWS)

title: A leader's guide to what your board must know about AI (and shouldn't)
abstract: Your board is asking about AI — and that's a good thing. Their curiosity is the opening you need. But that attention can create more heat than light: dashboards and benchmarks that generate activity without moving the organization forward. The real opportunity is to channel that interest — show AI's true potential and turn your board into a genuine partner for a transformation that needs their conviction to succeed. In this session, assess where your board sits, understand the personas at play, and learn proven tactics to move them from curiosity to conviction.
speakers: Taimur Rashid (Managing Director, Frontier AI Engineering & Services, Amazon Web Services)
Mario Thomas (Head of Applied AI & Emerging Technology Strategy, Amazon Web Services)

title: A leader's guide to modernizing systems for AI, with AI
abstract: Every enterprise faces the same sequencing problem: "Before we can deploy AI, we need to fix our legacy systems." This is technology's most expensive false binary. Organizations that made real progress rejected that sequence. They use AI to understand undocumented code, decompose monoliths, and rebuild the very systems blocking deployment. One airline uses AI to comprehend reservation logic only three people understand. Another enterprise uses agents to reverse-engineer decades of business rules into microservices. The recursive unlock: the technology you want to deploy removes what blocks it. This session covers the funding, sequencing, and organizational decisions that make it work.
speakers: Matthias Patzak (Executive in Residence, Amazon Web Services)
Sree Ratnasinghe (Director, Customer Solutions, AWS Strategic Accounts, Amazon Web services)

title: A leader's guide to moving from AI investment gridlock to acceleration
abstract: Fund the platform or the use case? Demand proof before investing, or invest to generate the proof? These decisions determine whether AI compounds or stalls, and can't wait for the annual budget cycle. To move at the pace of AI, the CIO and CFO must be in lockstep. Two former operators share how the best pairs manage AI like a venture portfolio: bets in the face of uncertainty, recycling of wins into the next ones, and governance that scales across the portfolio rather than project by project — plus the key questions every pair should answer before their next AI investment.
speakers: Chris Hennesey (Executive in Residence, AWS)
Paul Krebs (Executive in Residence, AWS)

title: A leader's guide to scaling AI adoption without losing control
abstract: I gave the organization AI tools — why did adoption stall? Most enterprises equip teams with AI and expect transformation to follow. It doesn't. Amazon scaled agentic AI to thousands of production deployments not by mandate, but by investing in what surrounds the model: governance that guards what truly matters — customer trust, privacy, security, and cost — while loosening its grip everywhere else, a culture where experimentation and oversight coexist, and upskilling that turns casual prompters into confident builders. This session names the structural bets that move adoption, the debts you're quietly acquiring, and why losing control isn't the failure — over-constraining is.
speakers: Daniel Slater (Executive in Residence
Worldwide Head, Culture of Innovation, Amazon Web Services, Inc.)
Erin Kraemer (Senior Principal Technical Product Manager, AWS)

title: A leader's guide to reimagining complex business processes with agents
abstract: Most enterprises use AI as an assistant, automating individual tasks for incremental 20% gains. The leaders unlocking profound productivity gains are doing something different: reimagining entire business processes from the outcome backward, so every step hands forward context, confidence, and decision authority, not just data. This session shows what it takes to transform your most strategic operations with agentic AI and scale them, then Thomson Reuters walks through the lessons of rebuilding its M&A process end-to-end. You leave knowing which processes to reimagine and how to move them into production, where value compounds.
speakers: Helena Yin Koeppl (Director, Executive in Residence, Amazon Web Services)
Romeo Romeo (VP, AI Ventures and Tech M&A, Thomson Reuters (UK))
Simone Zucchet (Head of UKI SA - Advertising, Publishing and Information Services, Amazon Web Services)

title: A leader's guide to what separates AI leaders from the rest
abstract: In early 2026, the Reimagine research program interviewed senior technology leaders under conditions of candor: off-the-record, non-attributable, no marketing follow-up. What they said contradicts the prevailing conference narrative. Nobody is running agents autonomously, not one. The most advanced organizations are carrying the most technical debt. The AI generating real value looks nothing like the demos. This session synthesizes the patterns that emerged when executives stopped performing confidence and started sharing reality.
speakers: Tom Godden (Executive in Residence, AWS)

title: A leader's guide to security at the speed of AI, powered by Mythos
abstract: As AI capabilities advance, so do the capabilities of those who attack software. The pace of modern development has outgrown point-in-time security reviews, leaving vulnerabilities exploitable longer than any leader should accept. Periodic snapshots cannot keep up when code changes constantly, so security has to become continuous, evaluating posture as the code itself evolves. Amazon used frontier-model capabilities, through Mythos, to make security continuous at its own scale, finding issues and guiding builders to fix them as they work. This session explores that shift. Senior leaders will learn how to secure their organizations at AI speed.
speakers: Sarah Davenport (Director, Security Engineering, Amazon)
Rush Carskadden (Director, Security Engineering, Amazon)

title: Running SAN workloads on Amazon EBS
abstract: Amazon EBS delivers the performance, durability, and enterprise features that mission-critical SAN workloads depend on. In this session, learn how the latest EBS capabilities map to what you run on premises today, which workloads are the best fit, and how customers are moving databases and enterprise applications off storage arrays and onto EBS. Leave with practical guidance to get started.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater

title: Persistent memory, shared context, instant discovery. Solving storage for AI agents
abstract: Production AI agents need to remember what happened yesterday, share work with other agents today, and find the right data in milliseconds. Most storage wasn't built for this. This session introduces the S3 stack purpose-built for agentic workloads. S3 Files provides a shared file system for multi-agent artifact handoff. S3 Vectors stores embeddings as long-term semantic memory that persists across sessions and restarts. S3 Metadata makes every object discoverable by tag, time, or custom attribute without scanning. Learn reference architectures for coordination, checkpointing, least-privilege access patterns, and framework integration.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Claire Edgcumbe (Sr. Software Development Manager, Amazon)
Jordan Dolman (Principal Product Manager, AWS Storage, Amazon Web Services)

title: Choosing the right AWS storage service
abstract: AWS storage spans block, file, and object services alongside purpose-built storage for vectors, tables, and migration, each optimized for distinct access patterns, latency requirements, and cost profiles. Choosing the most efficient option can help you reduce complexity, over-provisioning, or rearchitecting later. In this chalk talk, AWS storage experts walk you through a decision framework based on workload characteristics, not product names. Bring your architecture questions and work through real scenarios interactively. You will leave with a clear mental model for matching workloads to storage services and the confidence to make the right decision as your requirements evolve.
speakers: Christian Smith (Head of WW Specialists - Storage, AWS)
