Hiren Chandiramani (Sr. Manager, GTM Specialist - S3, Amazon)

speakers: Christian Smith (Head of WW Specialists - Storage, AWS)
Hiren Chandiramani (Sr. Manager, GTM Specialist - S3, Amazon)

title: How A+E Global Media Manages Storage Sprawl and Optimizes Cost (sponsored by Datadog)
abstract: As data-intensive and AI workloads drive continued growth in cloud infrastructure and storage, the complexity of understanding usage, ownership, and cost is increasing. In this session, we'll walk through how A+E Global Media gained visibility into the drivers behind rising S3 spend, connected costs to application owners, and established stronger FinOps governance. Attendees will walk away with best practices for architecting cost-efficient systems with Datadog by identifying inefficiencies and connecting cost, storage, and operational context to drive continuous optimization. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Purple Theater

title: How Bayer simplified their genomics pipeline with Amazon S3 Files
abstract: Bayer's genomics and research teams relied on a patchwork of workarounds to support specialized software, user scripts, and ad-hoc analysis on cloud-stored data. AWS DataSync and Storage Gateway handle high-throughput data uploads to S3, but downstream access meant managing multiple data copies, manual downloads, and unstable FUSE mounts, adding cost and operational overhead. Bayer shares how adding S3 Files to their architecture eliminated these access workarounds by providing a simple, mountable file interface directly on their S3 data. Learn how their team reduced data duplication and gave researchers access to petabyte-scale genomics datasets without changing their existing tools or workflows.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Builder Theater
speakers: Ben Gonzalez (Senior Cloud Engineer, Bayer)

title: Cost optimization techniques for Amazon EBS
abstract: Learn about the latest Amazon EBS capabilities and how they help you optimize your storage volumes. We cover new features, use cases, and guidance for getting started.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: Design for resiliency in Amazon EBS
abstract: Learn about new Amazon EBS capabilities and how they help you build resilient architectures. We cover new capabilities, relevant use cases, and guidance for getting started.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Red Theater

title: From Risk Signal to Recovery: Building Agentic Resilience with MCP (sponsored by Commvault)
abstract: AI agents are changing cloud operations from human-led workflows to machine-speed decisions and actions. But when agents can access, modify, and move critical data, resilience must become part of the operating model, not a recovery step. Join experts from Commvault, Wiz, and AWS to explore an architecture where MCP connects security context, data intelligence, and recovery capabilities. We'll demonstrate how security signals can guide protection and recovery decisions across Amazon S3 and other cloud services, turning risk insights into governed actions. Learn the guardrails, controls, and architectural patterns behind the workflow, and leave with practical insights for bringing these capabilities into your own cloud-native environments. This presentation is brought to you by Commvault, an AWS Partner.
speakers: Akshay Joshi (Vice President, Product Management, Commvault Systems Inc.)
Lawrence Chang (Chief Engineering Officer of Clumio, Commvault Systems Inc.)

title: Scale data for RAG and AI agents cost-effectively with Amazon S3 Vectors
abstract: Discover how S3 Vectors transforms retrieval workloads for AI agents and RAG pipelines with native vector storage and query capabilities. This session explores recent enhancements that deliver deeper, more comprehensive search results per query while dramatically reducing costs at scale, reducing the need for multiple round trips while running large-scale RAG, semantic search, and AI workloads. Learn architecture best practices, performance optimization techniques, and diverse vector use cases, from semantic search to large-scale RAG implementations.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Venkata Sistla (Sr. Worldwide Specialist SA - AI/ML, Amazon Web Services)
Dhanika Sujan (Sr. Product Mgr - Tech, Amazon)

title: Deep dive on S3 Files with use case architectures and best practices
abstract: What if every application, AI agent, and team in your organization could access S3 data as a shared file system? With S3 Files, connect thousands of compute resources to your data in S3 through a high-performance file interface that scales to multiple terabytes per second. Stop duplicating data between object and file storage. Stop building staging workflows just to read a file. In this session, you'll see how S3 Files turns S3 into the shared file system your workloads already expect, and how customers are replacing copy-heavy pipelines with direct file access today.
speakers: Smitha Sriram (Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Jimmy Zuber (Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Amir Levy (Senior Product Manager, Amazon)

title: Maximizing block storage performance for high-intensity workloads
abstract: Amazon EBS handles over 222 trillion I/O operations daily. Performance matters, a lot, but it’s not just about average performance, it’s about stable low latency that minimizes outliers or tail latency. io2 Block Express volumes are designed for that purpose with consistent sub-millisecond latency and 99.999% durability for critical applications such as SAP HANA, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and more. Learn about how its performance characteristics optimize compute utilization, leading to cost efficiency and the success of many performance-demanding use cases.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Marc Olson (Senior Principal Engineer, AWS)
Jody Gibney (Director, Amazon)

title: Data protection and resilience with AWS storage
abstract: Risks to data availability are intensifying, and the cost of getting recovery wrong is rising. Recovering well means recovering deliberately, not reactively, with a strategy built for the unpredictability of what can go wrong. In this session, you'll learn how the 3-2-1-1-0 defense-in-depth framework provides that structure, guiding you from failure scenario analysis through recovery objective planning to layered protection across local, cross-region, and immutable isolated copies. The result is a playbook for how AWS storage services bring each layer to life, from native replication and disaster recovery to centralized backup with immutable isolated vaults for cyber recovery.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Danny Johnston (Data Storage Specialist | Global Financial Services, AWS)
Stuart Lupton (Sr Specialist SA - Storage, Amazon Web Services)

title: Amazon S3 Tables: A deep dive into storage built for Apache Iceberg
abstract: Amazon S3 Tables are setting a new standard for Apache Iceberg data lakes: fully managed, open, and AI-ready. In this session, learn everything you need to know about S3 Tables, from how we continuously optimize Iceberg tables as your data scales, to support for ingestion, migration, data protection, cost-efficiency, and performance. We’ll explore how S3 Tables make it easy for AI agents to build on Iceberg tables and dive into the latest re:Invent announcements. Hear real-world customer stories and walk away equipped to bring S3 Tables to your organization.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Amy Yu (Senior Product Manager - Tech, Amazon Web Services)
Yuri Zarubin (Principal Engineer, AWS)

title: Deploy AI agents on containers with Amazon S3 Files and S3 Vectors
abstract: Build a multi-agent architecture on Amazon EKS using S3 Files as the shared workspace and S3 Vectors as persistent semantic memory. Mount an S3 file system across agent containers using standard POSIX file I/O. Agents read, write, and hand off artifacts without custom SDKs or message brokers. A background process generates embeddings stored in S3 Vectors, giving agents long-term memory they query semantically. Deploy a self-managed orchestrator that spawns agents, routes tasks via file system events, and retrieves vector history. Fine-tune synchronization, monitor with CloudWatch, and establish DR with cross-Region replication. Walk away with a production-ready, self-managed multi-agent system.
speakers: Samyak Kathane (Sr. WW Specialist SA Storage, Amazon Web Services)
Kiran Chukkala (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Deploy AI agents on containers with Amazon S3 Files and S3 Vectors
abstract: Build a multi-agent architecture on Amazon EKS using S3 Files as the shared workspace and S3 Vectors as persistent semantic memory. Mount an S3 file system across agent containers using standard POSIX file I/O. Agents read, write, and hand off artifacts without custom SDKs or message brokers. A background process generates embeddings stored in S3 Vectors, giving agents long-term memory they query semantically. Deploy a self-managed orchestrator that spawns agents, routes tasks via file system events, and retrieves vector history. Fine-tune synchronization, monitor with CloudWatch, and establish DR with cross-Region replication. Walk away with a production-ready, self-managed multi-agent system.
speakers: Samyak Kathane (Sr. WW Specialist SA Storage, Amazon Web Services)
Kiran Chukkala (Senior Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Accelerate data migrations with AWS DataSync at any scale
abstract: Long migration windows, limited visibility, and complex source environments can slow your data migrations to AWS, whether you are transferring data from on-premises file servers, Hadoop clusters, or multicloud object storage. In this chalk talk, AWS storage experts show you how AWS DataSync Enhanced mode's parallel pipeline simultaneously lists, prepares, transfers, and verifies your data to dramatically reduce those timelines. You will learn how to configure for maximum throughput, design endpoint connectivity for secure and efficient data movement, and use richer metrics and monitoring to gain full visibility into your transfer pipeline.
speakers: Sravan Rachiraju (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Tugba Goksel (Sr. Migration Specialist, AWS)

title: Accelerate data migrations with AWS DataSync at any scale
abstract: Long migration windows, limited visibility, and complex source environments can slow your data migrations to AWS, whether you are transferring data from on-premises file servers, Hadoop clusters, or multicloud object storage. In this chalk talk, AWS storage experts show you how AWS DataSync Enhanced mode's parallel pipeline simultaneously lists, prepares, transfers, and verifies your data to dramatically reduce those timelines. You will learn how to configure for maximum throughput, design endpoint connectivity for secure and efficient data movement, and use richer metrics and monitoring to gain full visibility into your transfer pipeline.
speakers: Sravan Rachiraju (Sr. Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Tugba Goksel (Sr. Migration Specialist, AWS)

title: Shared file storage for containers, serverless, and Lambda
abstract: Containers spin up and disappear. Your application state needs to outlive them. Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx, and Amazon S3 Files give your containerized and serverless workloads durable, shared file storage. We'll break down when to choose each service based on access patterns, performance, and cost. You'll see how real teams run stateful microservices using EFS on ECS/EKS, leverage FSx for high-performance file system workloads, and unlock POSIX capabilities to S3 object data for analytics and AI workloads with S3 Files.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Eric Heinrichs (Worldwide Storage Specialist, Amazon)
Jacob Strauss (Principal SDE, AWS)
Samyak Kathane (Sr. WW Specialist SA Storage, Amazon Web Services)

title: Accelerating AI inference with Amazon EBS
abstract: As organizations optimize AI workflows to keep GPUs highly utilized, Amazon EBS plays a distinct role in the AI pipeline where key business data is close to compute. In this session, learn how EBS minimizes pre-staging time for model weights with low latency, accelerates data preparation and checkpoints on high-performance EBS volumes, and reduces response times by serving vector embeddings at sub-millisecond latencies during inferencing, all while delivering elasticity and configurability in storage and performance. Leave with architecture patterns, volume configurations, and a framework for extending your storage architecture with EBS for AI/ML workloads.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Sooraj Prasannan (Director of Product Management, Amazon)
Joe Stubenrauch (Product Manager, AWS)

title: Build your AI data pipeline to Amazon S3 and Bedrock
abstract: Agentic AI applications are only as good as the data supporting them, and that data often lives across on-premises systems, other clouds, and distributed AWS storage. In this workshop, you'll build an end-to-end pipeline that moves data from these sources into Amazon S3 and connects it to Amazon Bedrock to build agentic applications. You'll configure data movement services including Storage Gateway, DataSync, and Transfer Family, establish secure transfer patterns, and integrate your migrated data into a gen AI workflow. Leave with a working architecture pattern for scalable data lakes that feed AI applications, grounded in real-world migration and processing scenarios.
speakers: Cy Hopkins (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Allyn Henderson (Storage SA, AWS)

title: Unlock your S3 data for AI agents
abstract: You’ve built a rich data lake in Amazon S3. Now how do your AI agents actually find and use that data? In this chalk talk, explore patterns for connecting AI agents to S3 resources, including S3 Tables, S3 Metadata, and annotations, with real-time, governed access. Learn how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit for AWS help agents discover and operate on your data, how the AWS Context knowledge graph surfaces relationships agents can reason over, and how curated skills handle common data lake and analytics workflows. Bring your questions as we discuss permission boundaries and practical integration patterns.
speakers: Majisha Namath Parambath (Principal Software Development Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Harsha Battapady (Sr. Product Manager - Tech, Amazon Web Services)

title: Unlock your S3 data for AI agents
abstract: You’ve built a rich data lake in Amazon S3. Now how do your AI agents actually find and use that data? In this chalk talk, explore patterns for connecting AI agents to S3 resources, including S3 Tables, S3 Metadata, and annotations, with real-time, governed access. Learn how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit for AWS help agents discover and operate on your data, how the AWS Context knowledge graph surfaces relationships agents can reason over, and how curated skills handle common data lake and analytics workflows. Bring your questions as we discuss permission boundaries and practical integration patterns.
speakers: Majisha Namath Parambath (Principal Software Development Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Harsha Battapady (Sr. Product Manager - Tech, Amazon Web Services)

title: Scaling agent memory with Amazon S3 Vectors and S3 Files
abstract: Persistent, scalable memory is foundational to production AI agents. In this session, learn how the combination of S3 Vectors and S3 Files provides a unified memory layer for agents by using S3 Vectors for embedding-based semantic recall and S3 Files for low-latency, mutable working memory and shared state across agent sessions. We’ll cover architecture patterns for short-term and long-term memory, multi-agent memory sharing, and managing memory lifecycle and cost as usage grows, including how recent S3 Vectors enhancements improve retrieval economics at scale. Leave with patterns for memory architectures that scale to millions of agent interactions.
speakers: Samyak Kathane (Sr. WW Specialist SA Storage, Amazon Web Services)
Venkata Sistla (Sr. Worldwide Specialist SA - AI/ML, Amazon Web Services)

title: Bring your S3 data to your compute with S3 Files
abstract: S3 Files makes the data in your S3 buckets available to your compute as a high-performance file system, so any POSIX-based tool or workload can work with S3 objects in place. We will work through the two ways customers use it: giving established file-based applications direct access to data already in S3, and giving agents and other short-lived compute a durable, isolated file workspace they can leave behind. We'll whiteboard the decisions that matter: connecting compute to S3 Files across VPCs, accounts, and on-prem; tuning for price and performance; and securing access with IAM, POSIX permissions, and encryption.
speakers: Prabir Sekhri (Sr Mgr Specialist SA, AWS)
Andrew Peng (Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

Andrew Peng (Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Under the hood with Amazon EBS: Achieving sub-millisecond latency
abstract: Amazon EBS powers mission-critical applications with consistent sub-millisecond latency across millions of volumes. This session offers a behind-the-scenes look at the architectural innovations and engineering practices that make this possible. Learn how EBS leverages the AWS Nitro System, purpose-built hardware, and advanced I/O path optimizations to deliver reliable low-latency performance at hyperscale. Gain insights into how these capabilities translate into performance benefits for databases, analytics platforms, and latency-sensitive workloads.
speakers: Kirill Davydychev (Pr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Swapnil Dinkar (Sr. Software Developer, Amazon)

title: Optimize performance and cost of Amazon EBS at massive scale
abstract: Managing production workloads across multiple regions while weighing cost and risk requires optimal strategy. With block storage, operating at scale can mean different things, including delivering high IOPS or I/O bandwidth to applications, managing and monitoring millions of volumes, or protecting petabytes of data with stringent RPO and RTO requirements. In this talk, learn best practices for scaling and managing your Amazon EBS environment, including automation, monitoring at scale, and cost-optimization techniques using cloud-native tools to meet your business needs.
speakers: Nasan Tsengeg (Sr. Product Manager - Technical, Amazon Web Services)
Santhosh Arunuri (Solutions Architect, AWS)

With block storage, operating at scale can mean different things, including delivering high IOPS or I/O bandwidth to applications, managing and monitoring millions of volumes, or protecting petabytes of data with stringent RPO and RTO requirements. In this talk, learn best practices for scaling and managing your Amazon EBS environment, including automation, monitoring at scale, and cost-optimization techniques using cloud-native tools to meet your business needs.
speakers: Santhosh Arunuri (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Gaining insights with S3 Metadata and annotations
abstract: Learn how S3 annotations let you attach rich, structured context (JSON, XML, YAML, or plain text) directly to your objects without re-uploading them. In this session, you will configure annotations on a live dataset, build an enrichment pipeline that attaches AI-generated summaries on ingest, query annotation payloads at scale through S3 Metadata's Apache Iceberg table in Athena, and wire an AI agent that discovers and retrieves objects using annotation-based search. You leave with patterns for zero-read agentic discovery and metadata architectures that scale to billions of objects.
speakers: Sumaja Kapa (US, Specialist SA, Amazon)
Bimal Gajjar (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon)
Lee Kear (Sr. Manager Solutions Architecture - S3, AWS)
Fabio Lattanzi (Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build AI photo discovery with Amazon S3 Vectors
abstract: Learn how S3 Vectors turns millions of untagged images into a semantically searchable collection without standing up a separate vector database. In this builders' session, you will generate multi-modal embeddings from photo assets, store and index them in S3 Vectors with metadata predicates for filtered search, and wire an AI agent that discovers images using natural language queries. You will explore index configuration, batch ingestion throughput, and cost patterns at scale. You will leave with a working prototype and production patterns for building vector-native search directly on S3.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Builders' Session 2

title: Build a fully managed data lake with Amazon S3 Tables
abstract: Data lakes have evolved from raw Parquet files with Hive-style partitioning to fully managed Apache Iceberg tables. In this hands-on workshop, you'll understand that evolution, then build a working analytics data lake with Amazon S3 Tables in under two hours. You'll create an S3 table bucket, ingest real-world data, migrate data into the bucket, and query it with Amazon Athena. You'll also learn how to connect third-party tools like DuckDB for interactive exploration. Along the way we’ll cover the benefits of fully managed Iceberg tables and when to use Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation for open data architectures.
speakers: Ran Pergamin (Senior Solution Architect Data and Storage, Amazon Web Services)
Sumaja Kapa (US, Specialist SA, Amazon)

title: Build AI agents on Amazon S3 Files
abstract: S3 Files is the first cloud object store with fully-featured, high-performance file system access to your data. In this hands-on session, you'll create an S3 file system, attach it to an Amazon EKS cluster, and build an AI agent that loads model weights and processes data directly from S3 via standard file I/O. No SDK rewrites, no data duplication, just native POSIX access. You'll fine-tune synchronization behavior between S3 and the file system, controlling how data flows between object and file interfaces. Finally, you'll configure cross-Region replication to establish a disaster recovery strategy for your production workloads.

title: Accelerate database protection, recovery, and testing with Amazon EBS
abstract: Protecting your data and troubleshooting issues are essential for running production self-managed databases on AWS. This builders’ session tackles both. Get hands-on with EBS Snapshot Lock for immutable backups, Recycle Bin for accidental deletion recovery, and Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager for automated, application-consistent snapshots. Learn Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization for predictable restore throughput and use EBS Volume Clones to create virtually instant point-in-time copies without impacting production. You will leave with a practical playbook to improve your database resilience. Bring your laptop to participate.

James Kuhlke (Principal solutions architect, Amazon)

title: Architecting vector-driven AI applications with Amazon S3 Vectors
abstract: Vector search is the engine behind intelligent AI, transforming data into meaning-driven insights that power smarter search, recommendations, and generative experiences. In this session, discover how to combine cost-optimized, fully elastic vector storage delivered by Amazon S3 Vectors with multimodal embedding models in Amazon Bedrock to extract and index text and image semantics at scale. Learn how to leverage S3 Vectors with popular AWS AI services to power AI-driven applications that can efficiently search through large vector datasets. Whether you’re building media search applications or search-enabled AI, you’ll learn how to optimize your use of S3 Vectors.

title: Build an AI-powered AWS Backup analyst and remediate with AgentCore
abstract: Few teams have the capacity to continuously audit their backup posture across accounts and regions. AI agents can do that work and recommend fixes while keeping you in control. In this builders' session, you'll construct a multi-agent system that analyzes your AWS Backup environment across four dimensions: coverage gaps, ransomware resilience scoring, vault security, and cost optimization. You'll build an MCP server exposing backup APIs as agent tools, wire specialist subagents into an orchestration graph, and run a remediation agent with human-in-the-loop approval on AWS Bedrock AgentCore Harness. The system runs in your own environment after the session.

title: Amazon S3 security: Implementing access controls, policies & audits
abstract: Amazon S3 provides security settings and granular access controls to suit virtually any workload. In this workshop, learn how to manage access and define scalable user and resource-based policies using Amazon S3 access management tools. Learn techniques for monitoring and auditing data to find out who is accessing what data, from where, and when. Through practical scenarios, learn how to apply various S3 security tools and capabilities to meet diverse security requirements. Gain expertise in implementing robust security measures, from basic access controls to advanced audit systems, suitable for any workload complexity. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.
speakers: Erick Dame (Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Christie Lee (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build and optimize data transfers with AWS DataSync Enhanced mode
abstract: When you're moving petabytes from on-premises file servers and multicloud object stores into AWS, transfer speed and operational visibility are equally critical. In this builders session, you'll configure AWS DataSync Enhanced mode to move data from diverse source environments into AWS using its parallel pipeline for high-throughput transfers. Enhanced mode generates detailed task reports and transfer logs as it works. You'll then use Amazon Bedrock to analyze that data, surfacing performance bottlenecks and generating optimization recommendations. Walk away with reusable patterns for fast data movement and AI-powered transfer visibility.
speakers: Phani Surampalli (Sr Storage Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Shaguna Awasthi (Solutions Architect II, Amazon Web Services)
Santhosh Arunuri (Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Simplify secure file sharing with Transfer Family no-code web apps
abstract: Traditional file transfer solutions often require complex client software, custom scripts, or technical expertise, creating barriers for business users who need to share data. Learn how AWS Transfer Family web apps enable secure, browser-based file transfers that automatically trigger data processing workflows. We'll show you how to build automated pipelines that process files upon upload while maintaining enterprise-grade security through AWS IAM Identity Center for your workforce or Amazon Cognito for external users. Discover how to streamline file ingestion, kick off validations, and orchestrate downstream processing, starting with a simple drag-and-drop interface for your end users.
speakers: Emma Harrison (Solutions Architect, AWS)
Madhukumar Adavi (Sr Storage Specialist Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc)

title: Protect, recover, validate: Data resiliency for AWS storage
abstract: Data protection strategies today must span workloads and prove recovery works before an incident demands it. In this workshop, you'll implement recovery and data protection strategies for Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, and Amazon EBS with AWS Backup. Using a financial services application architecture, you'll configure protection mechanisms for ransomware and insider threats and execute step-by-step recovery procedures against simulated cyber threats. Recover across multiple services, validate restored data integrity, and walk away with patterns to strengthen your own recovery capabilities. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.
speakers: Rucha Kiwlekar (Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Allyn Henderson (Storage SA, AWS)

title: Improving your database agility with Amazon FSx
abstract: Customers self-manage databases on AWS to maintain full control over architecture, functionality, availability, and performance. Amazon FSx provides the high-performance, highly available storage they need to do this at scale. This workshop will whiteboard production architectures for self-managed databases on Linux and Windows using Amazon FSx for OpenZFS, NetApp ONTAP, and Windows File Server. Learn how to architect for high performance and high availability, implement zero-copy snapshots and clones for rapid database refresh, and accelerate backup and recovery. Whether you run Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, or PostgreSQL, bring your architecture questions.
speakers: James Kuhlke (Principal solutions architect, Amazon)
Andrew Peng (Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Amazon S3 cost optimization: when to tier, and when not to
abstract: Moving data to a colder storage class is the obvious way to cut Amazon S3 costs, but sometimes it makes your bill go up. Learn about the full cost model behind storage-class decisions: transition requests, minimum billable object sizes, per-object overhead, minimum durations, and retrieval. See why small objects, high-churn datasets, and request-heavy workloads are frequently cheaper left where they are, and how to spot them. Using S3 Storage Lens, S3 Inventory, and S3 Metadata, diagnose where you're spending and leave with clear guidance on when to tier, when to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and when to do nothing.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Eric Jones (Principal Product Manager, AWS, AWS)
Mark Twomey (Sr. WW Specialist SA Storage, Amazon Web Services)

title: Amazon S3 performance: Architecture, design, and optimization
abstract: Go behind the scenes of Amazon S3 performance architecture while learning practical optimization strategies for today's most demanding workloads. Explore how internal systems for S3 manage massive throughput, handle concurrent requests, and balance loads across its distributed infrastructure. From request routing and partitioning strategies to multipart transfers and byte-range fetches, understand the technical foundations that power real-time analytics, AI/ML training, and high-frequency data pipelines. Then see how S3 Express One Zone extends these capabilities with consistent single-digit millisecond latency through directory buckets and compute co-location. Walk away with patterns to maximize performance at every tier.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, White Theater
speakers: Greg Benjamin (Principal Engineer, Amazon)
Jonathan Wong (Sr. Product Manager Technical (S3), Amazon Web Services (AWS))

title: Beyond the GPU: Optimizing AI performance with storage architecture
abstract: When AI workloads need scale or speed, the instinct is to add more compute, but GPU speed only pays off when the data keeps pace. From training to inference, storage architecture shapes performance at every stage: optimizing checkpoints for uninterrupted training, reducing model load times, extending context windows beyond GPU memory, and accelerating retrieval for RAG and inference workloads. Learn how Amazon FSx for Lustre, FSx for OpenZFS, and Amazon S3 Express One Zone give you those levers.
room: Level 2, Ballroom F, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Edward Naim (GM, Amazon)
Randy Seamans (Principal Storage  Solutions Architect, AWS)
Aditi Garg (Sr Product Manager - Technical, Amazon Web Services)

title: AWS Backup: Centralized data protection for your cloud environment
abstract: Managing data protection across a growing cloud environment requires a centralized strategy. AWS Backup was designed around this principle, giving more than 150,000 organizations a fully managed service to automate backup operations, enforce protection policies at scale, and safeguard 20+ AWS services from a single console. From human error to infrastructure failures to targeted attacks, AWS Backup helps ensure you can recover the right data, at the right time, with confidence. In this session, learn how AWS Backup works, how you can use it to protect mission-critical workloads, and hear directly from customers about their implementation strategies and operational outcomes.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Bisman Sethi (Sr Product Manager, Amazon)
Heather Munoz (World Wide GTM - Storage, AWS)
LeelaVinod Bandla (Principal Software Engineer, Warner Bros. Discovery)
Mathew Patrick (Director of Cloud Engineering, Capital One)

title: Secure petabyte-scale data transfers with AWS DataSync
abstract: Organizations moving data across AWS regions or into AWS need transfers that are fast, secure, and manageable at petabyte scale. In this session, learn how AWS DataSync helps you accelerate large-scale migrations and automate ongoing data movement. We'll show how capabilities like DataSync Enhanced mode help you move data faster with less operational overhead, then hear from Snap about how they moved billions objects and petabytes of data across AWS Regions in weeks. We'll close with best practices for maximizing performance and cost efficiency in your own DataSync deployments.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Sachin Gupta (Sr. PM-T ES, Amazon Web Services)
Manchun Yao (Staff Software Engineer, Snapchat)
Christie Lee (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: What's new with Amazon S3... and now files!
abstract: Twenty years of redefining storage, and Amazon S3 continues to evolve beyond objects to serve you wherever you are and however you work with data. This session highlights that evolution, led by the convergence of object and file storage with the launch of S3 Files, delivering full file system access to your S3 data without sacrificing scalability or economics you expect from S3. We also explore S3 Vectors for AI workloads, S3 Metadata for richer data discovery, and S3 Tables for managed Apache Iceberg data lakes. Come see what’s launched, what’s next, and how to put it all to work.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Orange Theater
speakers: Shakhi Hali (Senior Manager, Product Management, AWS)
Ben Grubin (Director, Storage and Insights, AWS)

title: Know your data: discovery, context, and AI agents in Amazon S3
abstract: Organizations store billions of objects in Amazon S3 but struggle to answer basic questions: What do I have? Where did it come from? Is it still relevant? Learn how S3 Metadata and annotations turn your storage into a searchable, context-rich data estate. See how to attach business meaning directly to objects, query metadata at petabyte scale through managed Apache Iceberg tables, and drive governance workflows from metadata signals. Then discover how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit give AI agents governed access to your data, and how AWS Context lets them reason over relationships across your S3 data.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Monica Vyavahare (Senior Product Manager - Tech, Amazon Web Services)
Harsha Battapady (Sr. Product Manager - Tech, Amazon Web Services)

title: Designing performant and cost-effective data lakes on Amazon S3 Tables
abstract: Apache Iceberg data lakes that aren't thoughtfully planned can accumulate small files, excessive metadata, and redundant snapshots, ultimately degrading query performance and inflating costs. In this session, we dive into the design and maintenance choices that determine whether your Iceberg lake stays fast and cost-efficient or slowly deteriorates, including compaction strategies, snapshot expiration, and partition design. For each, we'll walk through the trade-offs, what happens when you get it wrong vs. right, and how Amazon S3 Tables can automate the heavy lifting for you. Leave with actionable strategies to balance performance and cost at scale.
speakers: Ankit Kalyani (Senior Technical Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Choosing the right AWS storage for low-latency workloads
abstract: Not all latency-sensitive workloads have the same storage requirements. From AI/ML training checkpoints to real-time analytics and high-frequency data pipelines, choosing between Amazon S3 Express One Zone, Amazon FSx for Lustre, and instance storage depends on access patterns, throughput needs, and cost constraints. In this chalk talk, we break down the decision framework for selecting low-latency storage across common workload types. Bring your architecture questions as we compare directory buckets, parallel file systems, and caching strategies side by side. Leave with a clear mental model for matching your performance requirements to the right AWS storage tier.
speakers: John Mallory (GTM Specialist, Amazon Web Services)
Mike Houle (Head of Engineering, AWS FSx, Amazon Web Services)

title: A practical guide to Amazon S3 data protection
abstract: Learn step-by-step methods to protect your critical Amazon S3 data against accidental deletion, ransomware, and corruption, even at billion-object and petabyte scale. This chalk talk provides hands-on guidance for implementing essential safeguards through S3 Versioning, Replication, Object Lock, and Resource Control Policy guardrails, plus techniques for recovering from unwanted changes across large datasets. We also cover how GuardDuty Malware Protection for AWS Backup lets you verify data is malware-free before restoring. Whether you’re meeting compliance requirements or ensuring business continuity, leave with actionable steps from basic backup policies to advanced immutability and malware-scanning controls.
speakers: Ed Gummett (Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS)
Denton He (Senior Product Manager (Technical), Amazon Web Services)

title: Monitoring and optimizing Amazon S3 with observability tools
abstract: As your S3 data estate grows across buckets, tables, and directory storage, operational visibility becomes critical for cost control, performance tuning, and security investigations. In this chalk talk, learn how to build a comprehensive observability strategy for Amazon S3. We will introduce S3 Storage Lens for organization-wide metrics and recommendations, server access logs for request-level diagnostics, CloudWatch metrics for real-time alerting, and S3 Metadata for storage analytics. We will walk through use cases for each tool, including when to reach for one over another, and deep dive into Storage Lens for optimizing at scale. Bring your monitoring questions as we work through real scenarios for identifying cost anomalies, diagnosing latency issues, and auditing access patterns across multi-account environments.
speakers: Mario Kiessling (Principal Software Engineer S3, amazon.com)
Roshan Thekkekunnel (Product Manager, AWS)

title: Optimize performance and cost for archival data with Amazon S3
abstract: Not all data needs frequent access, but it still needs the right retrieval strategy when called upon. In this chalk talk, learn how to design a cost-effective archival storage strategy using Amazon S3 Glacier storage classes. We cover how to analyze access patterns to identify archival candidates, automate data movement with S3 Lifecycle policies and S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and design restore workflows using S3 Batch Operations and S3 Event Notifications. Whether you're retaining compliance data for years or staging cold datasets for periodic analytics, leave with a practical framework for balancing retrieval performance against long-term storage costs.
speakers: Howard Kang (Sr. Storage Specialist Technical Account Manager, AWS)
Amita Marconda (Senior Software Development Manager, Amazon)

title: Optimize HPC with storage for throughput and IOPS
abstract: High-performance computing workloads demand storage that keeps pace with thousands of compute nodes processing data in parallel. Amazon FSx for Lustre delivers sub-millisecond latencies and high throughput without the operational burden of managing a parallel file system. Amazon FSx for OpenZFS adds high IOPS with consistent low-latency response for latency-sensitive workloads. Explore how to select the right deployment type based on your workload profile, leverage native S3 integration for data pipelines, and right-size performance independently from capacity. Bring your questions about CFD (computational fluid dynamics), genomics, semiconductor design, weather modeling, and other compute-intensive workloads.
speakers: Vandana Rungta (Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Mitch Becker (Sr. Storage Specialist, AWS)
Tom McDonald (Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Migrating petabytes of data: Real-world strategies with AWS DataSync
abstract: Learn how to plan, build, and implement the migration of 10 petabytes of on-premises data with AWS DataSync. Through interactive discussion and whiteboarding, explore effective approaches for data categorization and creating transfer job manifests that map directly to cost-optimized S3 storage classes. Discover how this data migration architecture accelerates the migration of client data to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP. This chalk talk provides practical insights and best practices for executing large-scale data migrations to AWS.
speakers: Wali Akbari (Principal AI Infra Specialist, Amazon Web Services)
Ameen Khan S (Sr. GTM Spec. SA Storage, AWS)

title: From CSV to Iceberg: Understanding open data formats on Amazon S3
abstract: Building a data lake on Amazon S3 and need to decide between Parquet, Hive, and Iceberg – or understand how your team already did? In this session we develop the mental model for storing structured data on Amazon S3 and trace how it evolved. Understand formats from CSV to Parquet that accelerate analytic queries, walk through the evolution of table and partition schemas that organize data at scale, and learn how open table formats like Apache Iceberg bring database-like capabilities to your data lake. Leave with a clear picture of each and how Amazon S3 Tables bring it all together as a fully managed experience.
speakers: Ran Pergamin (Senior Solution Architect Data and Storage, Amazon Web Services)
Danny Jones (Software Development Engineer, AWS)

title: Accelerate database protection and testing with EBS Snapshots and clones
abstract: Teams that rely on backups alone risk slow dev cycles, compliance gaps, and prolonged recovery times. Learn how Amazon EBS Snapshots and Volume Clones solve these challenges together. See how Snapshots deliver incremental, cross-region data protection with automated lifecycle policies for compliance, while Volume Clones create instant local copies for development and testing. We'll compare cost, performance, and architectural tradeoffs. You'll leave with a decision framework for when to snapshot, when to clone, and how to combine both in production architectures.
speakers: Shibin Michaelraj (Sr Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Santhosh Arunuri (Solutions Architect, AWS)

speakers: Shibin Michaelraj (Sr Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Inside Zeta Global's open lakehouse architecture on AWS
abstract: Are you building a data lakehouse and wondering how others have approached the same challenges? Go behind the scenes of a real AWS customer data architecture. Zeta Global's AI Marketing Platform serves thousands of clients using 245 million consumer profiles, but multi-hour data lag times and rising per-tenant costs were limiting growth. Learn how Zeta built an open streaming lakehouse with Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon EMR, and Amazon MSK that processes 10 TB daily across 10,000+ Apache Iceberg tables, cutting time-to-insight from hours to minutes while maximizing multi-tenant infrastructure efficiency at scale.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Global Impact Theater
speakers: SOUMIL SHAH (Lead Software Engineer, Zeta Global)
Shivam Patel (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc.)

title: Migrate your NAS to the cloud: Building AI-ready file storage
abstract: Enterprises store vast amounts of business-critical data on NAS systems, but aging hardware and rising costs are only part of the story. Legacy file storage also locks data away from modern AI workloads. Learn proven strategies for migrating NAS environments to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, then connecting that data to AWS analytics and AI services, including options like S3 Access Points, Amazon Bedrock, and SageMaker. We cover assessing your NAS estate, executing migrations with minimal disruption, and choosing the right path to unlock your data for modern workloads. You leave with a practical framework for modernizing file storage.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Red Theater
speakers: Luke Miller (Principal Technical Product Manager, FSx, Amazon Web Services)
Andrew Crudge (General Manager, Amazon FSx, AWS)

title: Ransomware resilience with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
abstract: Ransomware does not wait for a scheduled backup window, and neither should your defenses. In this chalk talk, learn how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP's built in Autonomous Ransomware Protection uses machine learning to catch abnormal file activity and automatically create protective snapshots before damage spreads. We cover configuring detection policies, integrating alerts with AWS security services, locking down recovery points with SnapLock, and building automated response workflows. Bring your questions as we design a defense in depth strategy together, one that gets your file data back fast when an attack happens, not just one that flags it.
speakers: Jay Horne (Pr. Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Break free from on-premises NAS: Migrating to AWS
abstract: Learn how Amazon FSx storage simplifies the migration of on premises workloads to the cloud while keeping the compatibility and performance your apps depend on. With fully managed, block and file storage that eliminates operational overhead, see real-world migration patterns for user file shares, high-performance applications, enterprise databases like Oracle, SAP, and SQL Server, and VMware migration with AWS Transform and FSx for ONTAP. Discover how organizations are reducing costs and accelerating innovation.
topics: amazon fsx for windows file server
speakers: Saurav Majumder (Sr. Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Eugene Kiliar (Sr. Product Mgr - Tech, Amazon)

title: Best practices for cost optimization with AWS Backup
abstract: AWS Backup protects workloads across more than 20 AWS services, and each resource type brings its own cost profile. In this chalk talk, learn practical approaches to managing your data protection TCO by tailoring your AWS Backup strategy to each workload. We'll dig into full versus incremental backups, lifecycle policies, cold storage tiering for S3 and other resource types, and backing up direclty to logically-air-gapped-vault to protect data from ransomware without maintaining multiple copies. Then we'll cover how to build cost observability using AWS Backup reporting and monitoring to track and optimize spend.
speakers: Lakshmi Nair (Sr. Product Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Samreen Taj K P (TECHNICAL ACCOUNT MANAGER, Amazon Web Services)

title: Modernizing VMware workloads with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
abstract: Migrating VMware workloads to AWS often means rethinking storage, but it doesn't have to. In this chalk talk, we explore how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides a storage foundation built for VMware migrations. Learn how FSx for ONTAP delivers multi-protocol support, enterprise data management, and ONTAP compatibility that VMware administrators already know. We'll discuss real world migration patterns, cost optimization through deduplication and compression, and high availability with Multi-AZ and zero RPO. Bring your questions and join us to design a migration strategy that minimizes disruption and maximizes your existing ONTAP investments.
speakers: Satya Vandrangi (Principal Product Manager, AWS)
John Jamail (Head of Engineering, Transform for VMware, AWS)

title: Storage decisions when you're building a multi-tenant business
abstract: When your business delivers cloud services to your customers, how you map tenants to storage is one of the earliest architectural choices, and it shapes everything that follows: onboarding automation, billing boundaries, isolation guarantees, and how accounts, users, and data relate to each tenant. Your workload mix adds another dimension, because data types using object, file, or block storage drive the handling of tenancy differently. In this chalk talk, we walk through silo, bridge, and pool deployment models, examining how workload profile, tenant count, and business requirements drive the choice. Bring your architecture and we'll work through it.
speakers: Dave Roberts (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
David DeLuca (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: Architecting video search at trillion scale with Amazon S3 Vectors
abstract: Storing and querying 1.5 trillion vectors demands rethinking traditional vector database architecture. Join this talk to learn how Bright Data built its video search retrieval layer on Amazon S3 Vectors, covering index partitioning across massive collections, embedding storage layout for sub-second nearest-neighbor queries, and cost/latency trade-offs versus dedicated vector databases at this scale. Bright Data walks through its approach to sharding, metadata filtering, and query routing, with benchmarks comparing throughput and cost per million queries. You'll leave with concrete architectural patterns for evaluating S3 Vectors in large-scale search, RAG, or embedding retrieval systems.
room: Level 2, Hall B, Expo, Industry Theater
speakers: Ran Pergamin (Senior Solution Architect Data and Storage, Amazon Web Services)

title: Connect NetApp FSx for ONTAP File Data to AI Apps with S3
abstract: Your AI workloads need enterprise data including documents, datasets, and unstructured content already sitting in ONTAP. The usual answer is to copy it to S3, build a sync pipeline, and hope nothing drifts. There's a better option. This session shows how to use FSx for ONTAP file shares directly via the S3 API so Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker can read them in place with no migration, no pipeline. Your existing access controls and data management policies stay intact. We'll cover the architecture, configuration steps, and how to pair ONTAP's data management capabilities with S3-based AI/ML services.
speakers: Beerinder Mann (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS)
Sean Phuphanich (Principal Technologist, Amazon)
Nava Ajay Kanth Kota (Sr Partner SA, Storage, AWS)
Virgil Ennes (Sr Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: AWS Backup: Architecture deep dive
abstract: Dive into AWS Backup architecture with AWS experts, including how new capabilities fit into your design. We work through deployment strategies, backup storage options, restore scenarios, and security posture. Bring your questions, leave with a plan.

title: What's new with AWS Backup
abstract: Learn about the latest AWS Backup capabilities and how they can help you simplify and strengthen your data protection strategy. We cover new features, use cases, and guidance for getting started.

title: Modernizing file transfer with AWS Transfer Family
abstract: Legacy file transfer platforms are costly to maintain and fragile under pressure. When outages and bottlenecks start compounding, patching isn't enough. In this session, learn how AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed foundation for secure file exchange that scales with demand. We'll cover core capabilities including managed SFTP servers, connectors, browser-based web apps, and event-driven automation. A customer joins to share how they replaced a failure-prone platform with a modern, AWS-native architecture on Transfer Family and S3.
speakers: Ulili Nhaga (Principal Architect, NVIDIA)
Madhukumar Adavi (Sr Storage Specialist Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services Inc)
Randy Boutin (Software Dev Manager, AWS)

title: Speed up latency-sensitive workloads with Amazon S3 Express One Zone
abstract: For data-intensive workloads such as ML training, analytics, and AI search, every millisecond spent waiting on data costs money without advancing the work. When workloads make millions of small, random reads and writes, low-latency storage keeps compute productive without provisioning for peak demand. S3 Express One Zone brings this low latency to Amazon S3, with single-digit millisecond data access up to 10x faster than S3 Standard. In this session, we walk through the design patterns customers use in production to add low-latency performance to data already in S3, and how to tell whether your workload is a fit.
room: Promenade South, Octavius 4, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Mallory Gershenfeld (Senior Product Manager, AWS)

title: Building resilience against ransomware using AWS Backup
abstract: To counter evolving cyber threats, organizations must fortify their backup infrastructure for recovery resilience. This session applies threat modeling to design a multi-account AWS Backup architecture across three pillars: immutability with isolation, integrity validation, and guaranteed accessibility. Walk through a phased reference architecture using logically air-gapped vaults for tamper-proof backups, restore testing and GuardDuty malware scanning for integrity assurance, and multi-party approval for secure recovery during account compromise. Learn how to define your minimum viable company to sequence recovery priorities, distinguish cyber RPO from operational RPO, and align your strategy to NIST CSF 2.0 for recovery resilience and business continuity.
room: Level 3, Chairman's 363, Content Hub, Blue Theater
speakers: Palak Desai (Sr. Manager, Product, Amazon)
Sabith Venkitachalapathy (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)
Ivan Velickovic (Senior Software Engineer, Amazon)

title: Build a real-time data lakehouse with CDC streams on S3 Tables
abstract: Learn how to build a real-time transactional data lakehouse using Amazon S3 Tables with Apache Iceberg. In this hands-on session, you will ingest CDC streams from Amazon MSK into a medallion architecture, transform batch and streaming data into business-ready gold layer tables with Amazon SageMaker, and query the results through Amazon Quick. You'll configure S3 Tables maintenance policies per layer and compare binpack, sort, and z-order compaction strategies to optimize query performance. You will leave with production patterns for continuous ingestion, incremental processing, and low-latency analytics at scale.
speakers: Lee Kear (Sr. Manager Solutions Architecture - S3, AWS)

title: Advanced S3 performance engineering: From multipart to resilience
abstract: Master advanced Amazon S3 performance optimization techniques across storage classes, including S3 Standard for general purpose storage and S3 Express One Zone for the highest performance needs. This expert-level workshop focuses on implementing sophisticated data transfer patterns using multipart uploads and Transfer Manager. Design and deploy resilient applications with advanced retry strategies and robust error handling mechanisms. Through technical exercises, build high-performance solutions for large-scale data transfers across different S3 storage classes. Learn to optimize your applications for specific performance requirements, from cost-effective general storage to ultra-low latency implementations. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.
speakers: Mark Twomey (Sr. WW Specialist SA Storage, Amazon Web Services)
Bob Holmes (Solutions Architect, Amazon)

title: Deploying mission-critical applications with Amazon EBS
abstract: Millions of customers run their performance-intensive enterprise applications and databases on AWS. In this workshop, explore deploying a high-performance application on Amazon EC2 and Amazon EBS for optimized availability, resiliency, and cost performance. Discover and choose the ideal Amazon EC2 instance types and Amazon EBS volume types for various workloads. Learn about on-demand storage flexibility and performance using Elastic Volumes. Monitor and optimize Amazon EBS using Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and observe how AWS DevOps Agent autonomously investigates and helps remediate storage performance issues. Build resilience and fault tolerance using AWS Fault Injection Service. You must bring your laptop to participate.
speakers: Vicky Dewani (Sr Cloud Support Engineer, Amazon Web Services (AWS))
Saurabh Bindoo (St. Technical Program Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Build ransomware recovery with AWS Backup air-gapped vaults
abstract: When ransomware compromises your account, your backups are the last line of defense. The question is whether they're isolated, verified, and accessible when you need them most. In this workshop, you'll work through a simulated account compromise using AWS Backup logically air-gapped vaults. You'll configure vault isolation policies to put backups out of reach, validate their integrity through restore testing, and orchestrate recovery when primary credentials are compromised. Backup Audit Manager ties it together with compliance monitoring to prove your posture holds. You'll finish with a tested recovery playbook built against a live compromise scenario. Participants must bring a laptop.
speakers: Santosh Setty (Storage Specialist SA, AWS)
Ameen Khan S (Sr. GTM Spec. SA Storage, AWS)

title: Build ransomware recovery with AWS Backup air-gapped vaults
abstract: When ransomware compromises your account, your backups are the last line of defense. The question is whether they're isolated, verified, and accessible when you need them most. In this workshop, you'll build ransomware recovery capabilities using AWS Backup logically air-gapped vaults, restore testing, and Backup Audit Manager. Working through a simulated account compromise scenario, you'll implement protection across three pillars: immutability with isolation, integrity validation, and predictable availability. Configure vault isolation policies, validate backup integrity, orchestrate recovery when primary credentials are compromised, and walk away with a tested recovery playbook. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.
speakers: Santosh Setty (Storage Specialist SA, AWS)
Ameen Khan S (Sr. GTM Spec. SA Storage, AWS)

title: Find and fix storage bottlenecks for self-managed OLTP on EC2 with EBS
abstract: ​​When you run a self-managed OLTP database on Amazon EC2, the storage bottleneck is rarely where you assume. This hands-on session teaches a repeatable method for finding and fixing it. Use Flexible IO tester and a PostgreSQL/pgbench workload to connect storage metrics to database symptoms. Measure latency, IOPS, throughput, and queue depth; determine whether the limit is the volume, instance bandwidth, or I/O pattern; then tune the right EBS volume configuration. Validate every change with EBS detailed performance statistics and CloudWatch. Leave with a proven sizing-and-tuning method for database workloads on EC2.
speakers: Shiju Purushothaman (Senior Cloud Support Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Anthony Thunyin (Technical Account Manager, Amazon Web Services)

title: Amazon S3 security and access control best practices
abstract: As organizations consolidate critical data in Amazon S3 across accounts, teams, and workloads, security and access control decisions multiply. Which identity model scales without becoming brittle? Where do you enforce encryption policy? How do you detect misconfigurations? This session walks you through a layered security framework for S3: perimeter controls that prevent unintended public exposure, identity and attribute-based access that scales across organizational boundaries, encryption options that satisfy compliance without adding operational friction, and monitoring that continuously validates your posture. You will learn how these layers compose into a cohesive strategy and which controls matter most as your environment grows.
room: Level 1, Forum 120, Content Hub, Purple Theater
speakers: Sam Parmett (Principal Engineer, Amazon)
Will Cavin (Principal Product Manager - Technical, Amazon Web Services)

title: Optimizing containerized applications with shared file storage
abstract: Containerized workloads can face unpredictable latency spikes, throughput bottlenecks, and runaway costs as they scale. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through techniques for identifying these issues and solving them in production environments. Bring your use cases, performance questions, and architecture challenges as we tune Amazon EFS, Amazon S3 Files, and Amazon FSx for real-world EKS and ECS deployments. We'll cover IO profiling, throughput vs. latency tradeoffs, cost-optimization strategies, multi-attach EFS configurations, FSx volume sizing, and POSIX-compatible pipeline design on S3 Files. You'll leave with practical insights you can apply to your environment immediately.
speakers: Eric Heinrichs (Worldwide Storage Specialist, Amazon)
Jacob Strauss (Principal SDE, AWS)

title: Advanced vaulting: Ransomware resilience with AWS Backup
abstract: Bad actors increasingly target backups alongside production data, and organizations need a vaulting strategy that puts them out of reach. Isolation, immutability, and encryption form the pillars of that strategy, and this session dives deep into how to implement all three with AWS Backup. We'll cover logically air-gapped vault architecture, including how backups are stored in isolated, immutable infrastructure by default, encryption with AWS-owned and customer-managed keys, and durable recovery pathways with Multi-party approval. We'll also cover how these vaulting patterns feed into recovery workflows so that what's protected stays recoverable.
speakers: Vivek Mishra (Sr. Product Manager, Amazon)
Fathima Kamal (Sr SA manager, Amazon)

title: AWS Backup clean room recovery: Comprehensive resilience framework
abstract: Having an isolated vault is only half the battle. When a cyber event hits, you need confidence your backups are clean and recoverable. In this chalk talk, learn how to design an Isolated Recovery Environment using AWS Backup that validates and restores data in a secure space separate from production: reducing blast radius, breaking the kill chain, and proving recoverability on demand. We'll cover immutable air-gapped copies, automated restore testing with malware scanning, and Multi-party approval to control recovery access during account compromise. Leave with a framework for building recovery confidence into your backup strategy.
speakers: Wali Akbari (Principal AI Infra Specialist, Amazon Web Services)
Sabith Venkitachalapathy (Principal Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: The multi-account AWS Backup playbook: centralized data protection
abstract: Deploying AWS Backup across hundreds of accounts brings challenges that a single-account setup never surfaces: centralized policy enforcement, cross-account and cross-Region copy, delegated administration, and consistent compliance evidence across the organization. This chalk talk walks through the patterns that hold up in large AWS Organizations - backup policies at the OU level, delegated administrator setup, cross-account vaults, and monitoring that scales. Bring your toughest multi-account backup questions; we'll whiteboard the architecture and trade-offs together.
speakers: Stuart Lupton (Sr Specialist SA - Storage, Amazon Web Services)
Mark Choi (Sr. PMT-ES, Amazon Web Services)

title: Protecting hundreds of accounts from one place with AWS Backup
abstract: Protecting a single workload is straightforward. But when every team owns their own accounts, organizations need a centralized approach to enforce consistent data protection across all of them. We'll dig into how to build backup architectures that scale across your entire AWS estate, covering Organizations backup policies to enforce protection standards across accounts, cross-account and cross-region copy strategies, and Backup Audit Manager for compliance monitoring and audit evidence. Whether you're onboarding new accounts or tightening controls on existing ones, we'll walk through patterns for centralized data protection you can prove.
speakers: Stuart Lupton (Sr Specialist SA - Storage, Amazon Web Services)
Mark Choi (Sr. PMT-ES, Amazon Web Services)

title: AWS Transfer Family: SFTP meets agentic AI workflows
abstract: Learn how to build enterprise-grade file transfer solutions using AWS Transfer Family and extend them into agentic AI workflows. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through building secure SFTP servers, integrating with enterprise identity providers like Okta and Azure AD, and automating file processing using Terraform. We'll explore how event-driven architectures handle malware scanning with GuardDuty, and how AI agents via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore take over downstream tasks like data extraction and fraud detection. Bring your questions. We'll dig into how each layer connects so you can extend your own Transfer Family deployment the same way.
speakers: Prabir Sekhri (Sr Mgr Specialist SA, AWS)
Matt Boyd (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: AWS Transfer Family: From SFTP to Agentic AI Workflows
abstract: Learn how to build enterprise-grade file transfer solutions using AWS Transfer Family and extend them into agentic AI workflows. We'll explore how event-driven architectures handle malware scanning with GuardDuty, and how AI agents via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore take over downstream tasks like data extraction and fraud detection. Bring your questions. You'll walk away with practical patterns for evolving traditional managed file transfer into intelligent, agentic processing pipelines.
speakers: Prabir Sekhri (Sr Mgr Specialist SA, AWS)
Matt Boyd (Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)

title: Inside Amazon S3 Vectors: architecture and cost optimization for vector search
abstract: Vector embeddings power everything from semantic search to RAG, but running them at scale often means high infrastructure costs and operational overhead. In this session, go inside the architecture of Amazon S3 Vectors to see how it delivers vector search at up to 90% lower cost than specialized alternatives, with support for up to 2 billion vectors per index. We'll whiteboard the indexing approach that makes this possible, then explore recent enhancements, including a 100x increase in the per-query search result limit and reduced query pricing, and what they mean for your application's performance and cost.
speakers: Dmitri Pavlichin (Principal Applied Scientist, AWS)
Bryan Wilkinson (Principal Engineer, Amazon)

title: Advanced security patterns on Amazon S3
abstract: Amazon S3 security settings and access controls suit virtually any workload, but as data estates grow to millions of buckets across organizational boundaries, standard policy approaches hit limits. In this chalk talk, equip yourself with proven patterns for managing access at scale: optimizing policy evaluation with access points and access grants, scaling beyond IAM policy limits with cross-account structures, implementing attribute-based controls that adapt as teams and datasets grow, and securing your data lake perimeter with resource control policies. Join the S3 security team for a structured discussion of the patterns that solve the hardest multi-account access problems at scale.
speakers: Kavitha Viswanathan (Software Development Manager, Amazon Web Services)
Mourya Gudladona (Sr. Systems Development Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: Need for Speed: The journey to high EBS performance on EC2 instances
abstract: Achieving consistent, low-latency block storage at cloud scale requires rethinking every layer of the IO stack. In this session, we walk you through the architectural evolution of Amazon EBS, and show how a series of innovations reduced hypervisor overhead, slashed network latency, and enabled higher block storage IOPS and throughput on your EC2 instances. We will also discuss how Nitro enabled specific EBS features such as Instance bandwidth Configuration, Torn Write Protection, and detailed performance statistics via NVMe logs. Bring your questions and leave with an understanding of how EBS delivers high performing block storage for your mission-critical applications.
speakers: Kirill Davydychev (Pr. Solutions Architect, AWS)
Shyam Rajagopal (Principal Engineer, Amazon)

title: Dive deep into resilience architectures for Amazon EBS
abstract: Learn about new Amazon EBS capabilities for resilient architectures and how they work. We cover how to plan your approach and optimize your block storage. Bring your questions.
speakers: Barak Pinhas (Principal Engineer, Amazon EBS, AWS)

title: Building your first event-driven application
abstract: A customer places an order. Inventory updates. Payment processes. Notifications fire. In a monolith, one failure cascades through everything. In this builders' session, build a retail order system where each step runs independently using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. Through guided exercises, you'll publish and subscribe to events, handle failures in one service without breaking others, and trace event flows across your system. No prior event-driven experience required—you'll leave with a working application and the core patterns for decomposing synchronous workflows into resilient, asynchronous systems. Bring your laptop.

abstract: You want to build web applications on Lambda without changing how you write code. Lambda Web Functions make that direct. In this builders' session, deploy a full-stack web application with AWS Lambda Web Functions. Working in small groups with AWS experts, run an HTTP server on Lambda, serve static assets alongside application routes, render a DynamoDB-backed product catalogue, and stream live activity with Server-Sent Events. title: Building interactive web applications on AWS Serverless
abstract: Web applications need fast responses, server-side rendering, and real-time updates, but managing origin servers, CDN configurations, and scaling infrastructure pulls you away from building features. In this builders' session, deploy a full-stack web application entirely on AWS Serverless. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll configure routing and static asset delivery, implement server-side rendering with consistent low latency, and add real-time interactivity. Walk away with a working application and deployment patterns for production web workloads. Bring your laptop.

title: Building lightning-fast web apps
abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this lightning talk, hear how a customer built a full-stack web application entirely on AWS Serverless services, from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. They cover architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical takeaways for production-ready serverless web development.

title: Modernizing your compute stack with Lambda's new execution models
abstract: You're running workloads across Lambda, EC2, and containers because no single service handled orchestration, always-on compute, and isolated execution. Lambda's new execution models change that: durable functions add checkpointed orchestration, Managed Instances provide always-on compute at EC2 economics, and MicroVMs offer hardware-level sandboxes with persistent state. In this breakout, we discuss the operational decision tree: which execution model to standardize on for each workload class, how to manage mixed-model deployments, monitoring differences across models, and when to migrate workloads between them. Bring your workload portfolio. We'll help you build an operational playbook for multi-model Lambda.
speakers: Chris McPeek (WW Tech Lead - Serverless, AWS)
Eric Johnson (Principal Developer Advocate, Amazon)

title: How AI-native startups run untrusted agent code on Lambda MicroVMs
abstract: AI agents increasingly generate and execute untrusted code that needs a safe, isolated place to run. A growing set of AI-native startups and ISVs are converging on one pattern: one MicroVM per agent session, spun up on demand, torn down when the work is done. In this session, see how [Customer] built production agent sandboxes on Lambda MicroVMs, walking through the full lifecycle that delivers hardware-level isolation per session. See how they scale to thousands of concurrent sandboxes and the operational tradeoffs they navigated to get there.
room: Upper Convention Promenade, Cristal 2, Content Hub, Lightning Theater
speakers: Ayush Kulkarni (Senior PMT, Amazon)
Shotaro Kohama (Staff Software Engineer, AI Platform, Snorkel AI)

title: Everything your web app needs in one place

Built on open source, runs on AWS. Easy to start, built to last.

abstract: Processing large-scale data shouldn't require provisioning clusters or managing batch infrastructure. In this builders' session, design and deploy a distributed data processing pipeline using AWS Step Functions Distributed Map, AWS Lambda, and Amazon S3. Working in small groups, you'll implement fan-out patterns that process thousands of objects in parallel, handle partial failures gracefully, and optimize for cost and throughput. Learn when Distributed Map is the right choice versus other parallelization strategies, and walk away with a reusable pipeline template. Bring your laptop.

title: Production-ready Lambda: Security and performance patterns
abstract: A Lambda function that handles traffic well in prototype isn't necessarily production-ready—there's a gap between "works" and "hardened." In this builders' session, take a working Lambda function and add the security and performance layers that production demands. You'll implement least-privilege IAM policies, add request validation and secrets management, reduce cold start duration with SnapStart and right-sized memory, and configure reserved concurrency for predictable performance under load. Each change includes the trade-off: what you gain, what it costs, and when to skip it. Bring your laptop.

title: Reducing Lambda cost with Graviton and managed instances
abstract: Lambda's default x86 pricing works fine until your steady-state workloads make the per-invocation model expensive at scale. In this builders' session, start with a baseline workload and apply two cost levers: migrate to ARM64 (Graviton) for better price-performance, then deploy on Lambda Managed Instances for EC2 economics with multi-concurrency on steady-state traffic. You'll measure before-and-after cost and performance data at each step, evaluate when each approach makes sense versus default Lambda pricing, and leave with a repeatable migration playbook. Bring your laptop.

title: Integrating AI agents with event-driven architectures
abstract: Most multi-agent systems start with direct API calls between agents—then debugging becomes impossible, one slow agent blocks the chain, and replaying a failed workflow means re-running everything. In this chalk talk, discuss why event-driven patterns solve these coordination problems and how to design multi-agent systems using EventBridge for routing, human-in-the-loop controls that pause and resume agent actions via events, and compute selection—such as Lambda, Fargate, or AgentCore—based on your agent's execution profile. Bring architecture questions; we'll whiteboard patterns for decoupling agents across domains without sacrificing observability.

abstract: Production incidents at 2 a.m. don't wait for your team to wake up. You'll inject common production issues—such as Lambda throttling, timeout cascades, DynamoDB throughput exceeded, and SQS dead-letter queue buildup—then configure the agent to perform root cause analysis, propose remediation, and apply fixes. You'll tune detection sensitivity, set approval gates for automated actions, and evaluate where autonomous remediation is safe versus where human oversight is required. Bring your laptop.
speakers: Parnab Basak (Sr. Solution Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Itziar Olivera Goicolea (TAM, AWS)
Jay Colodner (Technical Account Manager II, Amazon Web Services)
Sahithi Ginjupalli (Cloud Support Engineer, Amazon Web Services)
Udit Parikh (Sr. Cloud Support Engineer, Amazon Web Services)

title: Orchestrating agentic workflows: Step Functions & durable functions
abstract: AI agents need orchestration that handles long-running tasks, human approvals, and recovery from partial failures. In this chalk talk, compare AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions for agentic workloads, and learn when to choose code-first, replay-based recovery versus visual state-machine semantics. We’ll whiteboard how durable functions checkpoint progress and resume after failures, how Step Functions handle branching and parallel tool calls, and where Lambda MicroVMs fit for sandboxing agent-generated code execution. Bring your architecture questions—we’ll design hybrid patterns that combine both orchestrators based on your workload shape.
speakers: Rohan Mehta (Worldwide Serverless Specialist Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Dan Ronald (Senior Manager, Product Management, AWS)

title: Building agentic apps with serverless: Lambda as your agent's toolbox
abstract: Agents need tools—functions they can call to retrieve data, take actions, and interact with external systems. Lambda is well-suited for this, but designing functions as agent tools requires different thinking than traditional API backends. In this chalk talk, discuss design principles for agentic Serverless: single-responsibility tools with clear input/output schemas, MCP-compatible interfaces for universal agent consumption, and multi-tenant isolation that keeps workloads secure. We'll whiteboard the trade-offs that matter—provisioned concurrency versus on-demand cold starts, cost per invocation at agent scale, and where Serverless fits versus where you need different compute.
speakers: André Stoll (Sr. Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services)
Uri Segev (Principal Serverless Solutions Architect, AWS)

title: Distributed transactions with Step Functions and durable functions
abstract: Distributed transactions across microservices break in ways monoliths never did: partial failures, inconsistent state, rollbacks that don't roll back. In this builders' session, build a payment processing using saga pattern that orchestrates multiple serverless microservices using AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions. You'll implement compensation mechanisms that handle partial failures, compare orchestration approaches for short-lived versus long-running transactions, and monitor transaction flows across distributed services. Walk away with working saga patterns and the observability setup to troubleshoot them in production. Bring your laptop.
